description: Left navigation shell. Input: the current route. Output: a nav rail rendering exactly three entries labelled Operational Picture, Hypotheses, Scenario Control, with the entry matching the current route marked active and exposed as the current page to assistive tech. Constraints: exactly three entries, no fourth; drill-down tables and system health are not entries. Failure case: rendering a fourth nav entry, or rendering zero active entries when the route matches a known screen, fails the spec. Refs: FR-701, FR-709, US-A1, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.7. Amended 2026-09-13, before tests, after scn-004 landed a screen nothing could reach. Six decisions. First, the current route is the URL hash: not a router library, and not component state. A library is a dependency taken on for three destinations with no nesting and no parameters; component state makes the URL a lie, so a reload returns the analyst to a screen they did not choose and no screen can be linked to or named in a bug report. The hash costs nothing, survives a reload, and makes each entry a real link -- which is what puts aria-current=page on an anchor where assistive technology expects it, rather than on a button pretending to be one. An empty or unrecognised hash resolves to the Operational Picture rather than rendering nothing. Second, all three destinations render something and two of them exist. Operational Picture is unchanged. Scenario Control renders scn-004's screen. Hypotheses has no screen yet, so its destination says exactly that: FR-701 fixes the rail at three entries, and an entry that renders a blank page is worse than one that names what is missing. Third, the Scenario Control destination states that its runs are a fixture rather than the database. api-006 does not exist, so that table lists the mock -- real seeds from a real batch, but not what the database holds -- and api-003 already settled the principle this turns on: example data presented as though it were the system's own is the failure this project exists to argue against. The screen already carries a note when nothing is wired to its controls, and that note names the table too. Fourth, the poll runs only while the Operational Picture is mounted. App calls api-003's hook unconditionally today; with three destinations that keeps a five-second poll running against an endpoint nobody is looking at. The hook moves into the destination that uses it, which leaves api-003's seam where it was -- one place that knows the picture is fetched rather than passed in. Fifth, the three screens are declared once, in one list, and the rail is a dumb component over it. Exactly-three is then assertable at the source as well as in the DOM; two lists would be two places to add a fourth. Sixth, the rail carries no system-health strip and no drill-down entries. Health is a strip in the shell rather than an entry (FR-709), and it is not this item's. Failure cases added: an unrecognised hash rendering no screen at all; and the Scenario Control destination presenting fixture rows with nothing on screen saying they are fixture rows. Scope: a route list, the rail, the App wiring, and one sentence added to scn-004's note. It builds no Hypotheses screen and wires no scenario endpoint. Refs adds: scn-004, api-003, api-006, FR-714. Superseded in part 2026-09-13 by api-010, recorded here rather than left as a silent divergence. The third decision above put a sentence on screen saying the listed runs were a fixture, which was true for exactly as long as api-006 did not exist. The runs now come from GET /api/v1/scenario/runs, so that sentence would be false and the note carrying it is gone, together with the test that asserted it. The principle the decision expressed is unchanged and is now enforced from the other side: api-010 asserts the word fixture is absent from the screen once the rows are real, and that no fixture row is ever rendered while the list has not been read. The fourth decision -- the poll belonging to the screen that needs it -- is unchanged and now holds for two screens rather than one; its test counts picture requests by path, because a bare call count rises for the scenario poll as well.

System-health status strip in the nav footer. Input: a system-health value from the operational-picture contract. Output: a compact strip in the navigation footer showing the health state as a categorical label. Constraints: it is a strip, not a screen and not a nav entry; state renders as a categorical label only. Failure case: rendering health as a percentage such as 98% uptime, or promoting health to a fourth nav entry, fails the spec. Refs: FR-702, FR-715, ui-001, nav-001. Amended 2026-10-03, before tests. **The input named above does not exist, and the one this strip wants now does.** `operationalPicture.scenario.health` is HARD-CODED to `unknown` in the payload builder, with a comment saying no health monitoring exists -- so a strip reading it would render `unknown` on every screen forever, which looks like a fault rather than a gap. It is also the wrong KIND of value: it is a property of one run, while this strip is in the rail and is therefore on all three screens, and reading a picture field there would need the picture's poll on every screen -- `nav-001` deliberately scoped that poll to the picture. `api-014` removes the field. What exists instead, and did not when this item was written, is `ops-005`: the service's own health route stopped being a liveness stub and now reports whether the database is at the revision the code expects. That is a service-level fact, available on every screen from one cheap request, and it is what the design's own panel asks for -- Connectivity and Service rows, neither of them about a run. Input becomes GET /api/v1/health. Output: two rows, and the split is `ops-005`'s own three states one layer out rather than a decoration. CONNECTIVITY is whether the request reached the backend at all -- the browser-to-service link. SERVICE is what the backend said about itself -- the service-to-database link: healthy at the expected revision, REFUSING when the schema has drifted (the 503, which is the state that cost a day of a screen returning 500 while the container reported healthy), and CANNOT TELL when the backend answered but could not reach its database, because an outage is not a misconfiguration. Collapsing the two into one would lose exactly the distinction `ops-005` was built to make. Constraints. Categorical only and **never a percentage** -- the item's original failure case, and worth noting that the design reference itself renders `99.9% UPTIME` in this panel, so the failure case is not hypothetical and the design is not gospel here (FR-715, AC-11). Still a strip and not a screen and not a fourth nav entry (FR-701, FR-702, nav-001). It survives `nav-003`'s collapse: at 56px the two labelled rows do not fit, so each becomes a state dot with its row name and state in the accessible name, and neither row is dropped -- `nav-003`'s rule is that collapsing hides labels, never entries. It polls on its OWN interval, slower than the picture's five seconds, because what it reports changes only when somebody runs a migration or the database goes away, and because `ops-005` reads the database's revision on every single probe by design -- so the picture's cadence here would be a database round trip every five seconds per open screen for a value that cannot change that fast. Failure cases, replacing the original rather than adding to it. Rendering health as a percentage. Promoting it to a fourth nav entry. Reading the picture payload rather than the health route, so the strip is blank or stale on two of three screens. Collapsing REFUSING and CANNOT TELL into one state, which makes a misconfigured deployment indistinguishable from an outage -- the conflation `ops-005` exists to end. A 503 from the health route being treated as the request having failed, which would report the connectivity row as down when the request in fact arrived and was answered. And either row dropped when the rail collapses. Refs adds: ops-005, api-001, api-014, nav-003, AC-11.

Operational Picture status bar. Input: operationalPicture.scenario. Output: a top bar showing the scenario name badge and a persistent data-mode badge reading SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA. Constraints: the data-mode badge is unconditional and cannot be dismissed or collapsed; it renders even when scenario data is absent. Failure case: the data-mode badge missing, or hidden behind a loading or empty state, fails the spec. Refs: FR-703, NFR-303, US-A7. Amended 2026-10-03, before tests, and the amendment is a split rather than a widening. **This item was one badge doing two jobs.** FR-703 requires a data-mode badge on EVERY screen and NFR-303 requires every screen to present the system as a prototype running on synthetic and replayed data; this item is scoped to one screen, and so the requirement has been unmet since the shell was built with nothing reporting it -- no screen carries a badge at all today, the Operational Picture printing the bare word `mixed`, which is not a badge and does not say the environment is simulated. The two jobs are: (A) THIS SYSTEM IS NOT LIVE, which is true on every screen regardless of what is loaded and needs no input of any kind; and (B) THIS HOUR IS MADE OF synthetic RF and replayed tracks, which is true only of the hour on screen and changes per hour. Separating them is what makes (A) satisfiable: it needs no payload, so it lives in the NAV RAIL -- the one component present on all three screens -- without dragging the picture's five-second poll onto screens that do not need it, which `nav-001` deliberately scoped to the picture. (A), the standing badge. Rendered in the rail, on all three screens, from NO input: unconditional in the strongest available sense, having nothing that could be absent -- a failed poll, an empty store, a screen with no data and a backend that is down all leave it in place. Reads **SYNTHETIC & REPLAYED DATA**, in the requirement's own words rather than this item's original `SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA`: FR-703 itself says 'synthetic or replayed' and NFR-303 says 'synthetic and replayed', while the corpus's aircraft tracks are real recorded ADS-B, so a badge claiming the whole environment is synthetic understates their provenance in the other direction. It survives `nav-003`'s collapse, which this item already requires ('cannot be dismissed or collapsed') and which the 56px rail makes a real constraint: the collapsed form reads **NOT LIVE** -- the claim itself rather than an abbreviation of the words, because an abbreviation of the words is cryptic and the claim is what must not be lost -- with the full wording kept as the accessible name in both states. (B), the per-hour readout. Stays on the Operational Picture, LABELLED, and renders the data mode in words rather than as the payload's token: synthetic RF and replayed tracks together for `mixed`, each alone for `synthetic` and `replayed`, and for `unknown` what it actually means -- the hour holds no observations -- since that value is produced by a run with nothing stored against it and not by any uncertainty. The scenario name badge is unchanged and is already rendered as the run's own label (`api-012`). Failure cases, replacing the original one rather than adding to it. The standing badge absent from any of the three screens, which the original item could satisfy while two screens carried nothing. The standing badge derived from any payload, poll, or fetched value, so that a backend failure can remove it. The standing badge hidden, truncated to nothing, or dropped when the rail collapses. The per-hour readout rendering the payload's token verbatim, so the screen still reads `mixed`. The per-hour readout rendering `unknown` as uncertainty rather than as an hour with no observations. And the two merged back into one: a single badge that reads the payload would fail both jobs at once, being absent when the payload is and wrong about the hour when it is not. Refs adds: FR-703, FR-701, NFR-303, nav-002, nav-003, api-012, api-014, op-009.

Active hypothesis cards in the right rail. Input: operationalPicture.hypotheses. Output: one card per active hypothesis showing title and confidence as a Low/Medium/High pip; activating a card navigates to that hypothesis on Hypothesis Detail. Constraints: confidence renders via the ui-001 primitive; an empty list renders an explicit no active hypotheses state rather than a blank rail. Failure case: an empty hypothesis list rendering an empty rail with no message, or a card rendering confidence as a number, fails the spec. Refs: FR-707, FR-715, ui-001, hyp-001, US-A4.

Detection summary panel. Input: operationalPicture.detectionSummary. Output: anomaly counts per category plus an overall severity rendered as Low/Medium/High. Constraints: counts are integers and may be shown as integers; severity is categorical only; no anomaly score, signal integrity, or confidence figure is rendered as a percentage or decimal. Failure case: rendering a severity of 0.82 or 82% fails the spec. Refs: FR-707, FR-715, ui-001, NFR-203. Amended 2026-10-03, before tests. Three additions, and the first changes the shape of the work. **(1) THE VOCABULARY, AND IT IS SHARED WITH op-006.** The payload carries each finding type **verbatim** -- `possible_interference_zone` -- which is `api-011`'s rule and deliberate: the backend sends facts and never prose, so the screen composes copy where the rest of that screen's copy lives. The screen never composed any, so the panel prints the system's internal names at an analyst. What makes this more than a panel's problem is that `op-006`'s timeline carries the SAME verbatim type in its `event` field -- run 207's single event reads `possible_interference_zone` -- so copy written inside this panel would need a second copy in the timeline, and one conclusion would then have two sentences on one screen with nothing to notice when they drift. **The copy is therefore one module both panels read**, and that is a constraint on this item rather than a convenience. **(2) THE SET IS CLOSED, AND THE COPY IS HELD TO IT.** A copy map that misses a finding type prints a raw token, which is the defect being fixed -- so it must be impossible rather than unlikely. The reportable finding types reach the frontend as a **union type** in `operationalPicture.ts`, parity-checked against the register `anom-008` declares, following the two unions `api-012` already holds that way and the five scenario type ids before them. A copy map that does not cover the union is then a type error, so **a new detection rule forces its copy to be written** rather than appearing on screen as a token. Note where that test lives: in the BACKEND suite, because the TypeScript parser exists once and on that side -- the distinction between where a file lives and which suite guards it, recorded as the fifth hazard's second form in `measurements/README.md`. **(3) THE TYPED ABSENCES STAY EXACTLY AS BUILT**, and are specified here because they were `api-012`'s and this item renders them. A built rule that found nothing renders **0**; a rule that does not exist renders a **dash and never 0**, a zero there quoting the absence of a rule as the accuracy of one; `not-persisted` renders the same way. Only **reportable** counts are listed: a quiet run genuinely holds ~138 intermediate findings, and an analyst shown those as anomaly counts reads a correct non-detection as a storm. The two levels render through `ui-001` rather than inline. Failure cases, replacing the original rather than adding to it. A finding type reaching the screen as its raw token. The same finding type worded differently in this panel and in the timeline. A finding type with no copy being dropped, or falling back to the token. A rule that does not exist rendering 0. An intermediate finding counted as an anomaly. A level rendered without going through `ui-001`. And the union drifting from the register in either direction. Refs adds: api-011, api-012, anom-008, op-006, op-009, FR-904.

Tabbed exception panel. Input: the operational-picture payload for the current view filter (op-007, api-007). Output: one panel with three tabs labelled RF (n anomalous), Tracks (n degraded), Events, listing the rows the current filter admits, with a footer reading +n nominal hidden and a View all link. Constraints: the default filter state is Anomalous only, so nominal rows are absent from the first render; the hidden count comes from the suppressed-count metadata on the response, not from counting the payload, because server-side filtering means the excluded rows never arrive; n in the tab label equals the number of rows shown. Failure case: a nominal RF sensor appearing while the filter is Anomalous only, or the footer count being derived from the payload and therefore reading zero whenever the backend filtered, fails the spec. Refs: FR-708, FR-716, FR-809, US-A1, op-007, api-007, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.7. Amended 2026-10-06, before tests, on reading the design reference beside the payload. Four changes, and three of them are about what a tab must say when it has nothing to list. (1) THE THREE TABS DID NOT HAVE THREE PRODUCERS. RF had one (`rfSensors[].health`); Events had one and it was already on screen; Tracks had NONE -- `AircraftTrack` carries no degradation at all, so *Tracks (n degraded)* would have put an invented number in a tab label, which is `api-002`'s producer-less field reaching an analyst rather than sitting empty. `api-016` gives it one, and this item's wording moves to match it: the tab reads **Tracks (n interrupted)**, because the finding is that an aircraft's reporting broke and *degraded* is a judgement about the aircraft that nothing makes. The label follows the producer; the producer is not renamed to fit the label. (2) THE EVENTS TAB ABSORBS `op-006`'s TIMELINE rather than sitting beside it. They are one list rendered twice, which is the drift the single copy module exists to prevent, one layer up: the rail is left with the hypothesis cards and the detection summary, which is what FR-707 asks for, and the screen loses a panel. `op-006`'s guarantees travel intact -- oldest first by event time and never by array order, simulated time and never wall clock, the source beside the conclusion, and an explicit sentence when there is nothing. (3) AN EMPTY TAB SAYS WHAT IT FOUND, which is `op-003`'s correction at a third site. The default filter is *Anomalous only*, so on a quiet hour every tab is empty -- and a table with no rows and a footer reading *+7 nominal sensors hidden* states the hidden count twice and the finding not at all. Each tab renders a sentence instead: all seven receivers measured nominal; no aircraft's reporting broke. The hidden count stays in the footer and remains `api-007`'s metadata rather than a count of the payload. (4) THE PANEL SITS UNDER THE MAP AND NOT IN THE RAIL, following the design reference, which gives the screen a reading order worth stating: WHERE (the map), WHAT IS EXCEPTIONAL (this panel), WHAT IT MEANS (the rail's summary and hypotheses), WHY (`op-010`'s evidence). Failure cases add: a tab label counting rows it invented a property for. An empty tab rendering an empty table. The timeline rendered in two places. A tab count that disagrees with the rows beneath it. Amended 2026-10-07, before tests, on reading the item against what `api-016`, `api-007` and `op-007` built. Six changes. (1) THE TAB LABEL'S WORD FOLLOWS THE VIEW. The number is the rows the tab shows and the word names what those rows are: Anomalous only reads RF (n anomalous) and Tracks (n interrupted); Nominal only reads RF (n nominal) and Tracks (n nominal); All reads RF (n) and Tracks (n). On an unexamined hour (`view.examined` false) no state word appears under any view, because nothing has a state. Events carries its count too, Events (n), so a conclusion cannot sit behind an unopened tab uncounted. (2) THE FOOTER NAMES THE HIDDEN ROWS BY WHAT THEY ARE, from `view.suppressed` for the open tab: Anomalous only, +n nominal hidden; Nominal only, +n anomalous hidden on RF, +n interrupted hidden on Tracks, +n conclusion(s) hidden on Events; an unexamined hour, +n hidden and that the hour has not been examined; nothing withheld, Nothing hidden by this view. The View all link renders DISABLED WITH A REASON (decided 2026-10-06): the drill-down tables are `op-005` and not built. (3) THE RECEIVER GRID BECOMES THE RF TAB, on this item's own argument for the timeline -- one list rendered twice. The map box keeps a placeholder sentence until `map-001`; `op-007`'s empty-grid and empty-timeline sentences move into the RF and Events tabs. (4) COLUMNS ARE THE PAYLOAD'S FIELDS ONLY. The design reference shows Last Signal, Noise Floor and Severity, none of which has a producer, and filling them would be `api-002`'s invented field reaching an analyst. RF: receiver, station, band, state. Tracks: aircraft pseudonym, altitude in feet, position, state; an absent altitude reads 'not reported', never a dash. Events: `op-006`'s guarantees unchanged. (5) THE TABS ARE A TABLIST, RF open first; the open tab persists across polls, hours and views and is not stored across a reload. (6) TESTS THAT PINNED THE OLD PLACES ARE RE-POINTED, NOT DELETED: `op-006`'s and `op-007`'s tests that read a Timeline region or the receiver grid open the tab first and keep their assertions. Failure cases add: a tab label naming a state its rows are not in. A footer calling withheld rows nominal on an unexamined hour. A column for a field nothing produces. The receivers listed twice. The open tab lost on the next poll.

Drill-down tables. Input: activation of the View all link in an exception panel footer (op-004). Output: a full table over the same contract data, showing nominal and anomalous rows: full RF observation stream from the RF tab, full track inventory from the Tracks tab. Constraints: reachable only from panel footers, never from the nav; it is a view over the same data, not a new data source. Failure case: adding a nav entry for a drill-down table, or a drill-down fetching from an endpoint the panel does not use, fails the spec. Refs: FR-709, FR-701, nav-001, op-004.

Timeline strip. Input: operationalPicture.timelineEvents. Output: a horizontal strip rendering each event with its label and time, ordered oldest to newest. Constraints: ordering is by event time and independent of array order in the input; an empty list renders an explicit empty state. Failure case: events supplied out of order rendering out of order, or an empty list rendering a bare strip with no message, fails the spec. Refs: FR-710, hyp-001. Amended 2026-10-03, before tests. Four additions. **(1) The event label is the same finding type this screen's summary panel renders, and it uses the SAME copy module** (`op-003`, amended). Named rather than reimplemented: the payload carries the type verbatim in `event` by `api-011`'s rule, and a second copy map here would give one conclusion two sentences on one screen. This is the constraint that made `op-003` and this item one piece of work. **(2) The strip carries the event's SOURCE** -- which receiver the claim was made at, already in the payload as `source` -- because a time and a conclusion with no place is the thinnest useful form of this strip and the field is served. **(3) Times are SIMULATED time and never wall clock.** The events are instants in a replayed 2022 hour; the run was generated in 2026. Rendering a relative time, or formatting against the viewer's clock, states the wrong thing -- `anom-009`'s recorded mistake, and the same one `api-013`'s hour labels had to avoid. **(4) The ordering requirement is a GUARD rather than a correction, and is kept for that reason.** `api-012` already serves the reportable claims oldest first, so sorting here changes nothing today. It is specified because the alternative is a screen whose order silently follows a backend's, and the item's own failure case -- events supplied out of order rendering out of order -- is then untestable without changing the backend. The test supplies them out of order directly. Failure cases adds: an event rendered as its raw finding type. The same type worded differently here and in the detection summary. An event time formatted against the viewer's clock or as a relative time. An event rendered with no source when the payload carries one. Refs adds: api-011, api-012, anom-009, op-003, op-009. Amended 2026-10-06, before tests. THE STRIP MOVES INTO `op-004`'s EVENTS TAB and stops being a panel of its own. Nothing about what it renders changes -- every constraint above holds, and the copy still comes from `op-003`'s one module -- but it is one list and it was about to be rendered in two places, which is exactly the drift that made `op-003` and this item one piece of work. The rail is then the hypothesis cards and the detection summary, which is what FR-707 asks for. Failure case adds: the strip left in the rail beside the Events tab, so one conclusion appears twice on one screen with nothing to catch a divergence.

View filter control. Input: analyst selection of Anomalous only, Nominal only, or All. Output: the selection is sent to the backend as the view parameter (api-007), and the returned payload drives the map (map-003) and the exception panel (op-004) together, so the two always agree about what is shown. Constraints: default state is Anomalous only, preserving US-A1; the selection persists across polls rather than resetting on each refresh; drill-down tables stay unfiltered, since they are the show-everything view by definition. Failure case: the map showing all entities while the panel still shows only anomalous ones, or the filter resetting to the default on the next poll tick, fails the spec. Refs: FR-716, FR-809, US-A1, US-A9, op-004, map-003, api-007. Amended 2026-10-07, before tests, on reading the item against the screen `api-007` serves. Four changes. (1) WHAT THE CONTROL DRIVES TODAY, AND WHAT EACH SAYS WHEN THE VIEW EMPTIES IT. Neither the map (`map-003`) nor the panel (`op-004`) exists; what the selection governs now is the receiver grid standing in for the map and `op-006`'s timeline, both read from the one filtered payload. Each states what the view withheld, from `view.suppressed` and never from counting rows: an empty receiver grid on an examined hour reads that no receiver is out of nominal and how many nominal ones the view hides; a timeline emptied by the view reads how many conclusions the view hides rather than that there are none; on an unexamined hour (`view.examined` false) either says the hour was not examined, never that it is clean. `op-004` inherits these sentences when the panel replaces them. (2) THE ROWS ARE LABELLED BY THE VIEW THEY WERE SERVED UNDER. Between a click and the response that answers it, the rows on screen belong to the previous view; the screen names what it shows from `view.selected` on the payload and marks the change as pending until the two agree, and never labels rows by the control's own state. (3) THE SELECTION LASTS AS LONG AS THE SCREEN. It persists across polls and across pinning or following an hour -- the hour and the view are independent -- and is not stored across a reload or put in the URL, so every visit starts at Anomalous only (US-A1). Choosing a view refetches at once rather than waiting for the next tick. (4) TWO REFERENCES WITH NOTHING BEHIND THEM YET. Drill-down tables do not exist, so 'unfiltered drill-down' is carried to `op-005`; 'drives the map' means the receiver grid until `map-003`. Failure cases add: an empty receiver grid with no sentence. A timeline reading 'no conclusions' while the view withholds one. An unexamined hour's hidden rows read as a clean hour. Rows from the previous view labelled with the new one. The view lost when an hour is pinned.

Playback transport control. Input: a scenario run's simulated-time window and analyst interaction with play, pause, speed, and scrub. Output: a playback cursor in simulated time driving the map render (map-004), with the current cursor position displayed. Constraints: the transport operates over simulated scenario time, never wall clock, consistent with anom-009; scrubbing to any point in the window is permitted, including backwards; pausing holds the cursor rather than resetting it. Failure case: playback speed altering the reported simulated time of a rendered position, so that the same cursor shows different data at 1x and 4x, fails the spec. Refs: FR-717, US-A10, anom-009, map-004, api-008, scn-004.

Confidence and severity rendering primitive, the global no-fake-precision invariant. Input: a confidence or severity value. Output: a rendered Low, Medium, or High label or pip. Constraints: the accepted input domain is exactly Low|Medium|High; the component never formats a number into a percentage or decimal; every screen renders confidence and severity through this primitive rather than inline. Failure case: passing 0.87 or 87 renders nothing and surfaces a development-time error rather than displaying 87%. Refs: FR-715, NFR-203, AC-11, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.5. Amended 2026-10-03, before tests. Two additions. **(1) The four call sites, named.** `detectionSummary.anomalyLevel`, `detectionSummary.signalIntegrity`, and a hypothesis card's `confidence` and `severity`. All four render as bare inline strings today. The item says every screen renders confidence and severity through this primitive; the two detection levels are in that class and are spelled differently, so they are named here rather than left to a reading of the word *severity*. **(2) A compile-time union is not the guard, and this is why the item exists.** The contract already declares `Level` as exactly `Low | Medium | High`, so TypeScript refuses a number at the call site -- and the payload is **cast** from JSON (`as OperationalPicture`), so a backend regression delivers `87` at runtime with nothing between it and the screen. The refusal is therefore a runtime one. What the refusal does, specified because *renders nothing and surfaces a development-time error* admits a reading that would be worse than the defect. It renders **no value at all** -- so no number, percentage or decimal reaches an analyst in any form -- leaves the surrounding label in place, so the row reads as visibly incomplete rather than silently absent, and reports the offending value through `console.error`. It **never throws**: a primitive that raises during render takes down a whole screen over one bad badge, which is a larger failure than the one being prevented. The audience for the error is a developer, not an analyst -- an invalid level is a defect upstream and not a state the system is allowed to be in -- which is why it is a console error and not a sentence on screen, and is the one place this project deliberately does not compose copy for an absence. It does **not** render the typed absences `op-003` carries: a missing count is a dash and a rule that does not exist is a dash, and both are facts about a producer rather than levels. Collapsing them into this primitive would make *no rule exists* and *the backend sent a number* render identically. Failure cases adds: a number rendered in any form, including as a rounded or truncated string. A level rendered inline at any of the four call sites rather than through this primitive. The primitive throwing rather than refusing. An invalid level leaving no trace at all, so the defect is invisible to the developer who caused it. And the primitive being given a typed absence to render. Refs adds: api-012, op-003, op-006, op-002.

MapView adapter boundary. Input: aircraft tracks, RF sensors, and anomaly zones from the operational-picture contract. Output: a rendered map with a marker layer per entity kind. Constraints: MapView is the only module in the repo importing MapLibre GL JS or any map library, so it can be mocked wholesale in tests; no other component imports map types or calls map APIs. Failure case: a second module importing maplibre-gl fails the spec, and a repo-wide import check must assert this. Refs: FR-704, FR-705, US-E2, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10. Amended 2026-10-03, the basemap decision. The adapter owns basemap configuration and ships TWO sources, not one: the DEFAULT is the self-hosted vector archive covering the corpus bounding box and requires no network, no API key and no third-party account (NFR-105, AC-07); SATELLITE is an optional raster source that does require network and is a documented opt-in. Constraints: the satellite source is off unless explicitly configured, nothing falls back to it, and nothing falls back FROM it to the default on a failed tile fetch without saying so on screen -- a silent substitution would make the two indistinguishable, which is the whole point of separating them; selecting it is an explicit analyst action; the two sources are not of equal standing and the write-up says so (the vector default is subordinated to the overlays by design, satellite is an orientation view that cannot be styled at render time). With no source configured at all, map-002's placeholder is the behaviour. Failure case: the default basemap issuing a request to any host other than the one serving the frontend bundle fails the spec, and an import-or-request check must assert it rather than the absence being assumed. A second: shipping one basemap source and treating the satellite option as a later concern fails the spec, because it is the decision that determines whether this adapter has one tile source or two. Refs adds: NFR-105, AC-07, docs/thesis_notes.md 'The map gets two basemaps'. Amended 2026-10-07, before tests, with the decisions the user took that day and what reading the stack found. (1) THE DEFAULT BASEMAP IS A PROTOMAPS CUT OF THE CORPUS BOX, 3-11E 49-54N, TO ZOOM 10: 86 MB by a dry-run extract of build 20261006 (zoom 9 was 27 MB, 11 was 219 MB, 12 was 529 MB). The map still zooms past 10; it stops gaining detail. (2) DOWNLOADED ONCE AGAINST A PINNED CHECKSUM, NOT COMMITTED. A `make basemap` target, Docker only like every other target (ops-003), cuts the archive and fetches the glyphs and sprites into `frontend/public/basemap/` (gitignored), and verifies each against SHA-256 values recorded in a committed manifest with the source URL, build date, licence (ODbL) and the attribution text. A checksum mismatch stops the target and leaves nothing half-written. (3) GLYPHS AND SPRITES ARE SELF-HOSTED with the archive, a subset of the Protomaps basemap assets at a pinned commit -- a default style points both at a CDN, and that hosted dependency would come back with the map still rendering perfectly. (4) THE REQUEST CHECK IS ON THE STYLE. Every URL the default style carries -- the vector source, glyphs, sprite -- is same-origin (a path beginning with a single '/'), asserted on the style the adapter builds, so the check needs no WebGL. (5) A CONFIGURED BASEMAP WHOSE FILE IS MISSING IS ITS OWN STATE: the adapter reads the archive header before creating the map, and an unreadable archive renders a labelled message naming `make basemap`, never a blank pane and never the satellite source. (6) THE SATELLITE SOURCE IS CONFIGURED, NOT CHOSEN IN CODE: an XYZ tile URL and its attribution in frontend environment variables, both required for the option to be offered; nothing in the repo names a provider. While satellite is selected, failing tiles are stated on screen and the default is not substituted. (7) ATTRIBUTION is rendered on the map for whichever basemap is showing (OpenStreetMap contributors and Protomaps for the default; the configured text for satellite). (8) SCOPE: the adapter renders receivers and aircraft from the filtered payload, a layer per kind; INTERFERENCE ZONES ARE DEFERRED to their own item because the payload carries no zone shape. (9) The adapter is `frontend/src/components/map/MapView.tsx` and is the only module importing `maplibre-gl`, `pmtiles` or `@protomaps/basemaps`; pure helpers it exports (config reading, style building, GeoJSON) are tested directly, and every other test mocks it. Failure cases add: a glyph or sprite URL pointing off-origin. A missing archive rendering a blank map. A satellite option offered with only one of its two variables set. A provider URL committed to the repo. Amended 2026-10-08, before tests, after the user reviewed the first build in the browser. (10) LIGHT BASEMAP: the default style is the Protomaps 'light' flavour with its own sprite (sprites/v4/light), self-hosted and checksummed like the rest; the dark sprite leaves the manifest. This reverses the dark choice argued in thesis_notes.md (a dark vector map kept the overlays salient); the entity markers now carry that job with darker fills and a white outline (map-003). (11) A EUROPE OVERVIEW UNDER THE BOX: a second archive, europe-overview.pmtiles, beside the first, cut from the same build to -11..30E, 35..61N at zoom 0-6 (6.2 MB by dry run), recorded in the manifest (overviewBbox, overviewMaxzoom) and fetched and verified by `make basemap`. The style carries both sources: the overview draws everywhere at every zoom (overzoomed past 6, with its labels only below zoom 7) and the detailed box draws over it from zoom 7, so there is ONE background layer. The camera's maxBounds is the overview box. The adapter reads both archive headers before making a map, and either one unreadable is map-002's missing-archive state. (12) MARKERS, NOT LAYERS: receivers and aircraft are HTML markers created inside MapView -- an antenna icon and an aircraft icon about 24 px -- each a focusable button with an accessible name (map-003), which also makes them testable without WebGL. The aircraft icon has a fixed orientation: the payload carries no heading and the icon does not imply one. Markers follow the payload: added, moved and removed as rows arrive and leave, and kept across a basemap switch. Before passes is set, panning under the All view (~430 aircraft) is measured in a browser; if it stutters, aircraft move to a canvas layer and the user is asked. Failure cases add: a grey area anywhere inside the overview box; the overview fetched from anywhere but this origin; a second background layer; a marker left on the map for a row the payload no longer carries.

MapView graceful placeholder. Input: absent or empty tile-source configuration. Output: a labelled placeholder region showing entity counts and a message that no tile source is configured. Constraints: no crash, no blank region, no thrown error, no network request attempted; the surrounding screen renders normally. Failure case: an unset tile-source env var producing a blank pane or an unhandled exception fails the spec. Refs: FR-705, NFR-102, map-001. Amended 2026-10-03, alongside map-001's basemap decision. The placeholder is the behaviour the offline guarantee rests on, so what triggers it is now stated precisely: an absent or empty DEFAULT tile source produces the placeholder, and an absent SATELLITE source does NOT -- the satellite option is simply not offered, because the default is available and showing a placeholder for an unconfigured opt-in would report a working map as broken. Failure case adds: an unconfigured satellite source producing the placeholder, or the satellite option being offered when no satellite source is configured, fails the spec. Refs adds: map-001, NFR-105, AC-07. Amended 2026-10-07, before tests. The placeholder is now one of THREE labelled non-map states, each with its own sentence and the entity counts: no default basemap configured; a default basemap configured whose archive cannot be read (naming `make basemap`, map-001 (5)); and the map library failing to start, e.g. no WebGL in the browser. None issues a request, none throws, and with nothing configured the map library is not even loaded. Failure cases add: the missing-archive state worded as 'not configured', which would send someone to the wrong fix.

Anomalous items highlighted on the map. Input: tracks, sensors, and anomaly zones each carrying an anomalous or nominal state. Output: anomalous entities render visually distinct from nominal ones and carry a non-visual anomalous marker for tests and assistive tech; selecting one emits a selection event identifying the entity and any linked hypothesis. Constraints: distinctness is asserted through the entity state exposed in the accessible name, not through CSS classes; nominal entities are never highlighted. Failure case: an entity flagged anomalous in the contract rendering identically to a nominal one fails the spec. Refs: FR-706, US-A2, US-A3, map-001, hyp-001. Amended 2026-10-08, before tests, with the states the payload actually carries. (1) THREE LOOKS PER KIND, from the DESIGN.md tokens with a white outline so they read on the light basemap: ANOMALOUS (receiver fault or deviating, aircraft interrupted -- the set api-007's anomalous view admits) is orange; NOMINAL is the kind's own colour, dark blue for aircraft and dark teal for receivers; NOT EXAMINED (unknown) is grey and hollow and never the nominal look, the panel's rule that an unexamined hour is never read as nominal. (2) THE STATE IS IN THE ACCESSIBLE NAME, e.g. 'Aircraft AC-1, interrupted', 'Receiver RF-01 (Schiphol), fault', 'not examined' for unknown; tests assert the name and the look a pure helper returns for each state, never CSS classes. (3) SELECTING AN ENTITY OPENS ITS POP-UP (map-005). The original 'any linked hypothesis' is DEFERRED to the hyp-* items: the payload links no hypothesis to an entity, and showing one would invent the link. Failure cases add: an unexamined entity drawn in the nominal look; fault and deviating receivers drawn differently from each other as if one were not anomalous; a hypothesis named in a selection when the payload carries no link.

Track playback rendering. Input: buffered aircraft positions across a simulated-time window and the playback cursor from op-008. Output: aircraft rendered at their interpolated position for the cursor, each with a trailing path over a configured lookback, with anomalous track segments visually distinct from nominal ones and anomaly zones appearing and clearing as their windows enter and leave the cursor. Constraints: interpolation is client-side between buffered frames, so motion is smooth independently of the poll interval; all map work stays inside the MapView boundary per map-001. Failure case: a track whose buffer has not yet loaded must hold its last known position and be marked stale, not jump to a default coordinate or vanish. Refs: FR-717, FR-718, US-A10, map-001, map-003, op-008, api-008.

Entity pop-up and labels on the map. Input: the receivers and aircraft MapView already renders (map-001) with their states (map-003). Output: (1) A POP-UP: clicking or pressing Enter on a marker opens one pop-up for that entity, payload fields only -- a receiver's id, station, band, state and position; an aircraft's name, altitude ('not reported' when absent, the exception panel's wording), state and position. State words as map-003 names them ('not examined' for unknown). Escape, the pop-up's close button, or clicking the map closes it; opening another replaces it, so at most one is open. A poll that still carries the entity keeps the pop-up open with the new values; a poll or view change that drops the entity closes it. (2) LABELS: receivers always show their station; aircraft show 'name · altitude' when interrupted, and every aircraft is labelled from zoom 9. Where two labels would overlap the lower-priority one is hidden -- anomalous receivers, then receivers, then anomalous aircraft, then the rest -- so a dense view under All stays readable. Constraints: everything lives inside MapView (map-001); no field outside the payload, so no speed, no heading and no linked hypothesis (map-003 (3)). Failure cases: speed, heading or any value not in the payload appearing in a label or pop-up; a pop-up left open for an entity the payload no longer carries; two pop-ups open at once; a nominal aircraft's label hiding an anomalous one's. Refs: FR-706, US-A2, US-A3, map-001, map-003, op-004, docs/qa.md 154.

Health endpoint. Input: GET /api/v1/health. Output: 200 with a JSON body reporting service status. Constraints: no database dependency, so it answers before persistence exists; every route is mounted under the /api/v1 prefix by a single APIRouter, so the prefix is declared once and no handler hard-codes it; the route is tagged system for OpenAPI grouping; the backend owns the full path, so neither the nginx proxy nor the Vite dev proxy rewrites or strips /api. Failure case: returning 200 while the app has failed to start, requiring a database connection to answer, or serving the endpoint at an unversioned path such as /health, fails the spec. Refs: FR-801, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.8, docs/qa.md section 16. Amended 2026-10-03 by ops-005, in the output clause only. The output is now **200 or 503**: the endpoint reports whether the database's schema is at the revision the code expects and refuses when it has drifted, because this route is what the Compose healthcheck probes and it reported healthy for a day while /api/v1/operational-picture returned 500 against a database still at 0008. The failure case 'requiring a database connection to answer' is **unviolated** and the reading is narrower than it looks: the endpoint still answers without a database -- that is ops-005's *unknown* state, 200 with a note that it could not tell -- and it consults one when there is one. The clause exists so health stays truthful before persistence exists and so a degraded database does not present as an unreachable service; both still hold, the second being exactly why an unreachable database answers 200 rather than 503. No property this item asserts has been withdrawn.

Operational picture endpoint. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture. Output: 200 with a payload whose shape matches frontend/src/types/operationalPicture.ts exactly: scenario, hypotheses, detectionSummary, rfSensors, aircraftTracks, timelineEvents. Constraints: field names and nesting mirror the TypeScript contract; confidence and severity values are Low|Medium|High strings; a contract test asserts shape parity in both directions. Amended 2026-09-04, three additions. (1) The two detection-summary fields become Low|Medium|High strings, and anomalyScore is renamed anomalyLevel because it is no longer a score. The contract as committed declared them numeric and the screen rendered '74.2%' and '0.92', which violates FR-715 and fails AC-11. This item is the last cheap moment to fix it: its own deliverable is a parity test whose purpose is to make the shape hard to change, so a shape frozen here is a shape defended afterwards. The mock's confidence value 'Medium Confidence' becomes 'Medium' for the same reason. Removing the percentage and toFixed rendering from the screen is part of this item; routing those values through a shared primitive is ui-001 and stays there. (2) What is actually served, given that four of the six sections have no producer. scenario comes from the most recent scenario run whose completed_at is set, falling back to the most recent run when none has completed (db-007). aircraftTracks are the latest position per aircraft within that run's final window -- 412 aircraft in the corpus as replayed -- with altitude converted from stored metres to the contract's feet, and name carrying the pseudonymised aircraft identifier, never a source one (dal-004). hypotheses, rfSensors and timelineEvents are empty arrays and detectionSummary is neutral, because no detector, RF source or generator exists. An empty section is honest; a populated one would be invented data reaching an analyst through a system whose argument is that this must not happen. (3) Reads go through a repository function rather than the handler (FR-904), which is what makes db-006's structural check assert over a real route rather than an empty set. Parity is proved by a backend test that parses the TypeScript contract and compares field sets in both directions, with frontend/ mounted read-only into the test container as compose.yaml and the Makefile already are; the test raises rather than skips when the mount is absent, because a skip here is the failure it exists to catch one level up (ops-003, adp-007). Failure case: adding, renaming, or dropping a field on either side without the other changing fails the contract test. A second: any percentage or decimal score in the payload fails the spec, and the parity test asserts the type of those two fields rather than only their names. A third: a real icao24 or callsign appearing in a track fails the spec. A fourth: serving a run that is not known to have completed while a completed run exists fails the spec. A fifth: the parity test skipping, rather than failing, when the frontend contract is not mounted. Refs: FR-802, FR-715, FR-904, AC-11, ui-001, api-003, db-006, db-007, dal-004, docs/implementation.md Phase 5. Amended 2026-09-30, one finding, and it is about this item's own reasoning rather than its behaviour. The note above justifies the three empty collections and the neutral summary 'because no detector, RF source or generator exists'. The PRINCIPLE stands -- an empty section is honest and a populated one would be invented data reaching an analyst through a system whose argument is that this must not happen -- and the CONDITION has expired: there are now eight detection rules, the synthetic RF source, the generator, 103 stored evidence bundles and 155 stored hypothesis rows. Nothing noticed, and nothing could have, because three items consume these fields -- op-003 takes detectionSummary, op-006 takes timelineEvents, api-007 filters both -- and no item produced them. A producer-less field is invisible in a backlog: every consumer of it can be built and pass while the field stays empty for a reason that stopped being true. Filling them is api-012 and not an amendment here, because it is new behaviour with failure cases of its own; what is recorded here is that the reason above is now historical. Refs adds: api-012, anom-015. Amended 2026-10-02 alongside api-012, closing the record this item's previous amendment opened. Three of the four producer-less sections are now produced -- detectionSummary, rfSensors and timelineEvents -- and ONE REMAINS: hypotheses is still an empty list, and still for a reason that is true rather than expired. 155 hypothesis rows exist, so the condition that justified the other three has gone here too; what holds the field empty now is that serving a hypothesis raises questions this item cannot settle -- which arm's output an analyst sees, whether a row whose grounding check FAILED may be shown at all, and what db-002's three-valued NOT_CHECKED renders as. That is a decision with its own failure cases and so its own item, not a gap. Recorded here because the lesson of the previous amendment was that a producer-less field is invisible in a backlog, and the fix for that is to name the remaining one rather than to let three closures read as four. Refs adds: db-002.

Frontend data access via polling. Input: a poll interval and the backend base URL. Output: a single API module fetching /api/v1/operational-picture on an interval and handing the typed contract to the screen. Constraints: exactly one module performs the fetch; no WebSocket, EventSource, or push transport exists anywhere in the repo; on fetch failure the app falls back to the mock and surfaces a degraded-data indicator rather than blanking. Amended 2026-09-05, four additions. (1) Placement: src/lib/api.ts performs the fetch and nothing else does; src/hooks/useOperationalPicture.ts owns the interval, the fallback and the degraded flag; App.tsx stays the single seam and the screen keeps taking a typed prop, so no component learns where data comes from. (2) The interval defaults to 5000 ms, chosen by hand as NFR-503 requires rather than tuned, against the 0.40 s warm response measured for api-002. An interval shorter than the response time produces overlapping requests rather than fresher data, which is the specific way this gets got wrong. (3) The app reports itself degraded from first paint, before any response has arrived, because the mock it renders in that moment is example data and not the system's. The indicator clears on the first successful payload. On a failure after a success the last good payload is retained rather than replaced by the mock: stale real data behind a degraded indicator is more useful and more honest than reverting to invented data, and the mock stays the fallback only while nothing real has ever arrived. (4) The no-push-transport rule is checked in both suites, because neither container can see the whole repository: the frontend suite scans src/ and package.json, the backend suite scans app/ and pyproject.toml. The frontend check strips comments and string literals before matching, since parsing TypeScript would mean adding a dependency to a test; that is weaker than db-006's AST check and is mutation-tested both ways regardless, so a transport named in a comment does not fail and a real one does. Failure case: a 500 or network error clearing the operational picture, or any push transport appearing in the dependency tree, fails the spec. A second: a fetch issued from any module other than src/lib/api.ts fails the spec, since a second caller is how a screen quietly becomes coupled to the transport. A third: the degraded indicator absent while the mock is on screen fails the spec -- example data presented as though it were the system's is the failure this whole project argues against. Refs: FR-807, FR-718, US-E4, NFR-102, NFR-503, api-002, db-006, op-001.

Hypothesis read endpoints. Input: GET /api/v1/hypotheses and GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}. Output: a list of hypothesis summaries, and a full hypothesis with evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, generator, and status. Constraints: the detail payload includes the producing generator so the UI can satisfy ai-010; confidence is a Low|Medium|High string. Failure case: GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{unknown-id} must return 404 with a JSON error body, not 200 with null and not a 500. Refs: FR-804, FR-713, hyp-001, ai-010.

Analyst feedback endpoint. Input: POST /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}/feedback with a verdict of confirm, reject, needs-more-evidence, or false-positive, and an optional note. Output: 200 with the updated hypothesis status persisted. Constraints: verdict is validated against the enum before any write; status transitions follow New, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Inconclusive. Failure case: an unrecognised verdict returns 422 and leaves hypothesis status and the feedback table unchanged; an unknown hypothesis ID returns 404. Refs: FR-601, FR-602, FR-604, FR-805, fbk-001, fbk-002.

Scenario control endpoints. Input: POST /api/v1/scenario/start with scenario type, parameters, seed, and batch count; POST /api/v1/scenario/reset; GET /api/v1/scenario/runs. Output: a run record with its ID and status; a cleared run state; a list of recent runs with type, parameters, seed, and outcome. Constraints: start echoes back the seed actually used so a run is always reproducible from its record, including when the caller omitted one. Failure case: starting with an unknown scenario type returns 422 and creates no run row; reset while no run is active succeeds idempotently rather than erroring. Refs: FR-806, FR-201, FR-204, scn-001, scn-004. Amended 2026-09-13, before tests, after nav-001 made the screen reachable and scn-004 left its controls disabled. Four decisions. First, the scope narrows to two endpoints. POST /scenario/start and GET /scenario/runs are built; POST /scenario/reset is deferred to its own item and its control stays disabled with the reason on screen. The schema has no active-run concept -- a run is a row -- and db-007 records that nothing is ever deleted, so 'a cleared run state' has no honest meaning until a batch can be in flight and abandoned. Reset therefore belongs with cancellation rather than here. Inventing a destructive endpoint to fill the name, or a no-op one that returns 200 and changes nothing, are both worse than a control that says plainly it is not wired. Second, start returns 202 and the batch runs in the background while the screen polls. A batch is roughly 70 seconds and half a million rows, and the project has no task queue by scope. Blocking would make a 70-second request against an nginx whose default proxy read timeout is 60 seconds -- passing in development and failing in the container, which is the exact shape of defect this project keeps recording. A queued row with no worker to drain it ships a control that changes a row and produces no run, which is worse than the disabled button already on screen. A background task needs no dependency, and a process killed mid-batch leaves runs with a null completed_at, which db-007 already defines as not known to have finished rather than a new state to invent. The cost is that nothing can cancel a started batch; that is recorded rather than hidden, and it is why reset is deferred rather than dropped. Third, the response carries the base seed actually used and every seed derived from it. The constraint already on this item is that start echoes the seed so a run is reproducible from its record. With a background batch the response is the only thing the caller receives synchronously, so it carries the base seed -- drawn by the API when the caller omits one, never invented by the screen, which scn-004 settled -- and the per-run seeds, which a caller would otherwise have to wait for rows to discover. Fourth, a listed run carries its recorded parameters and ScenarioRunSummary does not gain them. The frontend contract's listed run is the summary's fields plus parameters, and replay cannot do without them. They are added on a listing model used by this endpoint alone rather than on ScenarioRunSummary, which api-002 also serves: the recorded parameters carry the incident's radius, elevation, offset and duration, and putting those on the operational picture would describe the staged incident to the analyst whose detectors are being measured against it. Ground truth is selected by neither. Failure cases added. A configuration whose incident begins at or after the run ends must be refused with 422 before any run row is opened: run_batch raises on it, but by then the request has returned 202 and the refusal survives only in a log, so the twenty mislabelled controls that guard exists for would be produced while the screen reported success. A run count outside the batch bounds must likewise be refused with 422 and open no run row. Start returning 200 with a completed batch summary fails the spec, because it would mean the request blocked. A listed run carrying ground truth, or ScenarioRunSummary gaining a parameters field, fails the spec and api-009. The route constructing the engine, the layout or the corpus window itself fails the spec: the batch launcher is injected, so the endpoint is testable without a corpus on disk or a database, and FR-904 keeps SQL out of handlers. Scope: two route handlers, a listing model, a repository function that lists runs, an injected batch launcher with one real implementation and a seam for tests, and the router registration. It wires no screen -- the frontend swapping its fixture for a fetch is a separate step, and until it happens the note on that screen still says the rows are a fixture. Refs adds: db-007, api-002, api-009, nav-001, scn-003, FR-904, NFR-503. Defect found 2026-09-13 by running it, after api-010 put the button on screen. The launcher called Pseudonymiser.from_environment directly, and inside the container the pseudonymisation seed arrives from compose as an empty string rather than as absent, so every batch died immediately with 'PSEUDONYM_SEED is not set' while the screen reported the batch accepted. The command-line entrypoints do not have this fault: both clear a present-but-empty variable and then read backend/.env, each with a comment explaining the trap. There were therefore two copies of the remedy and the launcher was a third site that needed it and did not have it, which is why the fix extracts the remedy into one function that all three call rather than adding a third copy. This is the third recurrence of the present-but-empty defect recorded in this project (adp-007 first, then the container's own environment) and the second recurrence of the more general one: the place the code runs is not the place the tests describe. The launcher's existing tests could not have caught it, because they substitute the pseudonymiser to avoid needing a seed at all. Added failure case: a batch launched in a process whose seed variable is present but empty must read the seed from the env file and run, rather than raising where only a log can see it. Recorded limitation, not fixed here: a batch that fails after acceptance is invisible to the analyst, because the response has already been sent and nothing writes the failure anywhere the screen reads. That needs its own item.

Server-side view filtering. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture with a view parameter of anomalous, nominal, or all. Output: a payload containing only the matching rfSensors, aircraftTracks, and timelineEvents, plus metadata carrying the suppressed count per collection. Constraints: filtering happens in the query, not by returning everything and discarding client-side, so the payload shrinks with the selection; the suppressed counts are what keep op-004's hidden footer truthful once rows stop arriving. Failure case: an unrecognised view value must return 422 rather than silently defaulting to all, and a filtered response omitting the suppressed-count metadata fails the spec. Refs: FR-809, FR-716, api-002, op-004, op-007. Amended 2026-10-06, before tests. Two things the item could not have known when it was written. (1) IT CANNOT FILTER `aircraftTracks` UNTIL THEY CARRY A STATE. `rfSensors` has `health` and `timelineEvents` are reportable claims by construction, but an aircraft track carries no property an *anomalous* filter could select on -- so `api-016` is a prerequisite rather than a companion, and this item's `view=anomalous` means `state != nominal` on that collection. (2) THE SUPPRESSED COUNTS ARE PER COLLECTION AND THE UNEXAMINED CASE IS NOT A COUNT. On a run no pass has examined, every receiver is `unknown` and every track is `unknown` (`api-012`, `api-016`), so *anomalous* admits nothing and *nominal* admits nothing either -- and a suppressed count of 432 beside an empty list would report an hour nobody examined as an hour found clean. The metadata therefore says how many rows were suppressed AND that the run was not examined, which is the same distinction `detectionSummary`'s nullability carries. Failure cases add: filtering tracks on a property that does not exist. An unexamined run whose suppressed counts read as a clean hour. Refs add: api-012, api-016. Amended 2026-10-07, before tests, on reading the item against the code `api-016` left. Four changes. (1) SERVER-SIDE, IN THE PAYLOAD BUILDER, AND NOT IN SQL. Two of the three collections have no query to filter in: the receivers are `scn-005`'s layout, and a track's state is `api-016`'s join done in Python. Writing *interrupted* again as a SQL predicate would give one state two definitions that can drift. The filter therefore runs where the payload is assembled, over the same state each row is served with; FR-809's requirement is *server-side*, the payload still shrinks with the selection, and what stays forbidden is returning everything for the client to discard. (2) WHAT EACH VIEW ADMITS, per collection, superseding the 2026-10-06 sentence that `view=anomalous` means `state != nominal` on tracks -- which contradicted that amendment's own point (2) by admitting `unknown`. `anomalous`: receivers whose health is `deviating` or `fault`, tracks whose state is `interrupted`, and every timeline event (they are reportable claims by construction). `nominal`: receivers and tracks whose state is `nominal`, and no timeline event. `all`: everything. A row in state `unknown` is admitted by `all` only. (3) AN ABSENT `view` MEANS `all`, which is what every request receives today, so nothing on screen changes until `op-007` sends a selection; the *Anomalous only* default belongs to the control that sends it. An absent parameter and an unrecognised one stay different cases: the second is 422. (4) THE METADATA IS A TOP-LEVEL `view` FIELD, declared in both halves of the contract and parity-checked: `{selected: 'anomalous' | 'nominal' | 'all', examined: boolean, suppressed: {rfSensors, aircraftTracks, timelineEvents}}`, each suppressed value the count of that collection's rows the selection withheld. `examined` is false exactly when `detectionSummary` is null, so a reader of the counts alone cannot take an unexamined hour for a clean one. `detectionSummary` is never filtered: it is the account of the whole run whatever the view. Failure cases add: a filter written twice, once in SQL and once in Python. An `unknown` row admitted by `anomalous` or `nominal`. An absent view filtered as if it were `anomalous`. A summary whose counts shrink with the view.

Time-windowed track query for playback buffering. Input: a scenario run ID and a simulated-time span. Output: aircraft positions across that span, ordered by time per aircraft, sufficient for the frontend to interpolate between frames. Constraints: the frontend buffers ahead of the cursor and issues one request per span rather than one per frame, so the request rate is decoupled from the frame rate per FR-718; the span is bounded server-side to cap payload size. Failure case: a requested span exceeding the bound must be rejected or truncated with the truncation reported, never silently served in full; a span outside the run's recorded window must return an empty series, not an error. Refs: FR-810, FR-718, US-A10, op-008, map-004, adp-001.

Ground truth is never exposed outside the evaluation harness. Input: any API response, canonical observation, anomaly, evidence bundle, or hypothesis. Output: none of them carry the injected ground truth for the run. Constraints: the generator records what it injected on scenario_runs.ground_truth and that column is read by the evaluation harness only; no adapter, DAL record, detector input, API response, or evidence bundle may carry it, whether as a field, a label, or an inferable artefact such as a scenario-type string on an observation; GET /api/v1/scenario/runs may report that a run has ground truth recorded but never its content while the run is scorable. Failure case: an /api/v1/operational-picture or /api/v1/anomalies response including the scenario type or the injected event for the active run fails the spec, because a detector or an analyst able to see the answer invalidates every metric computed from that run. Refs: FR-207, FR-806, NFR-604, US-R5, AC-04, scn-002, adp-002, evb-001, eval-002.

Core schema and migrations. Input: an empty PostgreSQL database, reachable through the Engine db-005 constructs. Output: alembic added to pyproject.toml and locked; tables observations, quarantined_records, anomalies, evidence_bundles, hypotheses, analyst_feedback and scenario_runs created by ordered Alembic revisions; geometry(Point,4326) on observations.location and geometry(Polygon,4326) on anomalies.affected_area, both GiST-indexed; NOT NULL on observations over the provenance fields dal-003 requires (scenario_run_id, data_mode, source_id, source_type), and NOT NULL on quarantined_records over scenario_run_id, field and reason, with source_id, source_type and observation_type nullable there because dal-002 states attribution is best-effort -- a record can fail precisely because it lacks the field that identifies it. Constraints: Alembic is the documented migration convention, with revisions written by hand and autogenerate disabled, because autogenerate does not understand PostGIS geometry columns and would emit a revision nobody has read; the convention and the command that applies it are documented in README.md and exposed as a root Makefile target (ops-003); migrations apply cleanly from empty; source-specific fields live in the observation payload as JSONB, so the canonical table stays stable as sources are added; the hypotheses table carries generator, model_id, generation_params and raw_response from this first revision rather than a later one, because raw_response is not retrofittable after a campaign has run (db-002); spatial columns are stored as geometry and cast to geography at query time, so db-004's distance is computed by PostGIS rather than by the application while the full geometry function set stays available to the Phase 6 spatial clustering; this item creates schema only -- no repository implementation, which is db-003's, so that a red test can distinguish a wrong column type from a wrong write. Tests run against a disposable database in the postgis Compose service, carry a database marker, and read TEST_DATABASE_URL rather than DATABASE_URL, skipping when it is absent, so db-005's guarantee that unit tests need no live database survives; the coverage gate omits modules requiring a live database exactly when those tests skip, so the 90 per cent gate is measured over what was actually exercisable, and the containerised run -- the only one with a database -- remains the authoritative number. Failure case: applying migrations twice from empty errors. A second failure case: a missing PostGIS extension is not reported at migration time and surfaces later as type geography does not exist at first query, which is the failure scripts/smoke-test.sh already guards for the container and this item guards for the schema. A third failure case: the schema accepts an observation with a null scenario_run_id, data_mode, source_id or source_type, which is the half of dal-003 that item defers to here, and the same for dal-002's quarantine attribution. A fourth failure case: hypotheses created without the four reproducibility columns, which passes every test that exists today because nothing writes to that table yet, and is discovered only after a campaign has run. A fifth failure case: a module omitted from the coverage gate in both the native and the containerised run, so it is measured nowhere -- the omission must be conditional on database availability rather than unconditional, otherwise the exclusion that keeps the native gate honest becomes the hole that hides an untested repository. Amended 2026-08-29, before tests were written, on two counts that the item's own text got wrong. First, a seventh table: the six named here and in docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9 have nowhere to put a QuarantineRecord, whose shape is (source_id?, source_type?, scenario_run_id, observation_type?, field, reason) and carries no timestamp, no location and no payload, because those are what failed validation. Storing it in observations would require those three columns to become nullable, which would remove the NOT NULL guarantee dal-003 defers to this item -- so the item would delete the assertion it exists to add. The ERD in section 9 predates dal-002 and has been amended to match. Second, the skip signal: this text said database tests skip when DATABASE_URL is absent, which was true when written and was falsified a day later by tests/conftest.py, which sets DATABASE_URL for every test so that db-005's engine tests have a value that resolves but does not connect. It is therefore never absent. A separate TEST_DATABASE_URL is the signal instead, which is also a safety boundary rather than only a naming choice: this item's tests create and drop schema, and keying them on whatever DATABASE_URL happens to hold would eventually run a DROP against a development database. Refs: FR-901, FR-902, FR-906, dal-002, dal-003, db-002, db-003, db-004, db-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9, docs/qa.md section 34.

Hypothesis persistence and reproducibility. Input: a generation result from any arm (ai-003's envelope) and the identity of the evidence bundle it explains. Output: one stored row carrying the whole ai-001 hypothesis plus generator (template|local|hosted), model_id, generation_params and verbatim raw_response. Constraints: the four reproducibility columns exist from the first migration and do -- what 0001 could not know is the field vocabulary ai-001 later settled, so title, uncertainty and alternatives are RENAMED to hypothesis_title, evidence_against_or_uncertainty and alternative_explanations rather than mapped, because a mapping layer is a permanent place for two vocabularies to drift silently and the table holds zero rows, so the rename is free today and never again; summary and recommended_human_action have no column at all and gain one, which is the same class of defect as a late raw_response and has the same remedy cost after a campaign; grounding_passed becomes THREE-VALUED -- passed, failed, not yet checked -- because a hypothesis is written before ai-008 runs and a two-valued flag makes 'failed the check' and 'was never checked' identical, which is the typed-absence failure evb-001 exists to prevent and this repository has recorded three times; status gains the check constraint its neighbours generator and confidence already carry, over FR-602's five review states, and a new row starts at New; reading a stored bundle must yield its identity, since a hypothesis references one by id and evb-002's reader exposes none today, which is a blocker found by attempting the write rather than by reading the schema. model_id is a dated identifier and never a moving alias; raw_response is verbatim pre-parse output and never the parsed hypothesis re-serialised, because the difference only surfaces when somebody investigates a grounding failure months later and finds a record of what was understood rather than of what was said. The write goes through the repository, never SQL in a caller (FR-904). Failure cases: writing a model-arm row with model_id or raw_response null is rejected at the repository boundary -- a SECOND guard, ai-003 having already made such a result unconstructible, kept because this is the failure nobody can repair after a campaign and a boundary check holds against a row assembled some other way; a template row carrying a model id is rejected in the other direction; an unknown review status is refused by the database rather than stored. Refs: FR-508, FR-602, FR-903, FR-904, NFR-602, US-R3, US-R4, AC-06, ai-001, ai-002, ai-003, ai-008, db-007, evb-002, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 10. Amended 2026-09-27, two additions found by building the campaign that would consume this (ai-012), both in the class this item already calls the failure nobody can repair afterwards. (1) THE THREE-VALUED GROUNDING COLUMN HAS NO WRITER FOR TWO OF ITS THREE VALUES. save_hypothesis hard-codes 'not yet checked' and nothing updates it afterwards, so every row a campaign wrote would carry a verdict the campaign had in hand and never stored -- the typed absence built correctly and then never filled, which is worse than the two-valued flag it was built to avoid, because the column now looks capable of the distinction while the data never makes it. A repository function therefore records the verdict against one row id, taking ai-008's report rather than a bool so that 'flagged' and 'the check itself failed' cannot arrive as the same value; it refuses an unknown row id rather than silently affecting nothing, since a verdict written to no row is indistinguishable from a verdict written, and it refuses a move back to not-checked, because 'we looked and then stopped having looked' is not an event. (2) THE ROW CANNOT SAY WHICH ARM WAS ASKED, only which generator answered, and the campaign is the first caller where the two differ. When the model arm falls back, the stored template row is byte-identical to the template baseline's own row for the same bundle: a fallback is then invisible in the data, eval-005's per-arm counts are ambiguous at exactly the rows that matter most, and ai-010's screen indicator -- a fallback hypothesis must be visibly distinguishable from a primary-arm one -- is unbuildable on this schema rather than merely unbuilt. requested_generator is added NOT NULL over the same vocabulary and check constraint as generator, and generator != requested_generator is the DEFINITION of a fallback rather than a state to be refused, since ai-007 goes model-to-template and ai-006 goes hosted-to-local. The table holds zero rows -- nothing in app/ has ever written one -- which is the same free-today-and-never-again window the renames above used, and this is the second and last use of it. Failure cases added: a campaign row that does not say which arm was asked fails the spec; a grounding verdict recorded against a row id that does not exist is refused rather than counted as written. Refs adds: ai-010, ai-012.

PostGIS implementation of the DAL's repository port, the item that tests whether the port survived contact with a real database. Input: the ObservationRepository Protocol defined by dal-002, and canonical observations plus quarantine records produced by ingest_batch against the schema db-001 created. Output: a PostgreSQL/PostGIS implementation of that Protocol living in a repository module; a replayed window persists to observations and quarantined_records and is readable back; GeoAlchemy2 added to pyproject.toml and locked, and the geometry filterwarnings entry removed from pyproject.toml at the same time. Constraints: the Protocol's signature is the contract under test -- no storage-engine type may be added to it to make the implementation fit, so Location stays two floats and the WKB/ST_SetSRID conversion happens inside the repository; save_batch is one database transaction, so a failure part-way through leaves neither collection written; no caller-supplied primary key; all SQL and all spatial logic live here and nowhere else (FR-904, first half). The in-memory fake in tests/fakes.py is retained rather than replaced -- two implementations of one port is what makes the port meaningful, and it keeps the unit tier runnable with no Docker. No coverage omission: measured, the module sits at 53 per cent natively and the suite at 97.44 per cent, comfortably over the gate, and a 53 per cent reading is the honest signal that this module was not exercised here -- omitting it would make the native figure less informative rather than more. The containerised run remains authoritative and reports it at 100 per cent. Failure case: a batch of ten with three invalid must leave seven rows in observations and three in quarantined_records, and an induced failure between the two writes must leave zero of both -- seven observations with no quarantine trace fails the spec. A second failure case: an observation whose location round-trips to different coordinates, or is stored with an SRID other than 4326, fails the spec. A third: any change to the Protocol signature that introduces a session, an ORM model, a WKT or WKB string, or a caller-supplied identifier fails the spec, and if the implementation cannot be written without one, that is the finding and it is recorded in thesis_notes.md against the standing prediction (geometry and atomicity are the risks, identity is not) rather than worked around. Refs: FR-904, FR-901, US-E2, AC-02, dal-002, dal-003, db-001, db-005, db-004, db-006, docs/qa.md section 39.

PostGIS spatial query, the justification for the spatial database. Input: an RF anomaly zone geometry, a radius N in kilometres, and a time window.
