Output: the set of track discontinuities whose location falls within N km of the zone inside that window. Constraints: distance computed by PostGIS on geography, not by application-side arithmetic; the radius is a parameter, not a constant. Failure case: a discontinuity just outside N km must be excluded, and an empty result set must return an empty list rather than null or an error. Refs: FR-905, FR-305, anom-004, anom-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9. Amended 2026-09-15, before tests, on picking it up. Four things settled. First, this item is the proximity query and not the clustering one. FR-905 names 'track discontinuities within N km of an RF anomaly zone' and this item's own text describes exactly that, so the requirement and the item already agree. What disagrees is anom-004, whose text says its clusters are 'computed by the PostGIS query in db-004', and db-001's comment on the anomalies GiST index, which calls db-004 'the clustering query'. Two references to a query this item does not describe, neither noticed until now -- the same shape as FR-304 having no item at all, and found the same way, by reading the items rather than the phase heading. Second, clustering becomes db-009 rather than a note. It is real work that something must own, and leaving a needed capability described only in prose is exactly what FR-304 cost earlier in this phase; the correction is made by writing the item, not by recording that one is wanted. anom-004's reference is corrected when that item is picked up, and db-001's comment is left as it stands -- the revision is applied and its behaviour is right, so the comment is noted here rather than edited there. Third, the table read is detection_findings and not anomalies. db-008 created it because anomalies describes the reportable kind -- it requires a severity, a Polygon affected_area and a bundle link, none of which an intermediate finding has -- and it carries the GiST index on a Point location that this query is the reason for. Fourth, the input is any geometry with a radius rather than a polygon specifically. ST_DWithin on geography accepts either, and today the only producer of an RF zone is anom-001, which emits a point per sensor because an area needs corroboration from more than one; polygons arrive once db-009 clusters them. Requiring a polygon now would mean inventing one from a point, which is the coverage footprint this project has never modelled. Failure cases added. The boundary is bracketed rather than pinned at exact equality, and the reason is a measurement that contradicted this item as first amended. It claimed ST_DWithin is inclusive, so a finding exactly N km away would be inside; measured against PostGIS 3.5 on 2026-09-15, it is not. ST_Distance between two points returns 34338.94037894 m and ST_DWithin at exactly that value returns false, with no floating-point drift in the round trip through kilometres -- the operator itself excludes the boundary on geography. That was asserted here from documentation rather than from the database, which is the error this project keeps finding in its own reasoning. The specified behaviour is therefore that a finding one metre inside the radius is returned and one metre outside is not, which brackets the edge to metre precision without depending on an exact-equality semantics no real input ever occupies; exact equality is recorded as undefined and left to PostGIS. A query that computes distance on geometry rather than geography fails the spec, because degrees are not metres and the error varies with latitude -- at 52 degrees north a degree of longitude is about 69 km and a degree of latitude about 111 km, so a radius expressed in degrees is wrong by a different factor in each direction. Findings belonging to another scenario run must never be returned, whatever their location: every metric in eval-002 is computed per run, and a query that reaches across runs would silently fuse evidence from two different staged incidents. Refs adds: db-008, db-009, anom-001, eval-002. Further failure case, added 2026-09-15 while building: a radius of zero or less is refused rather than answered. It would otherwise return an empty result that is indistinguishable from 'nothing nearby', which is the silent wrong answer this project guards against everywhere else -- and unlike an empty result, it is always a caller error.

Database connectivity: engine, session, and configuration. Input: DATABASE_URL in the environment, in the form compose already passes to the backend and pipeline services. Output: sqlalchemy and psycopg added to pyproject.toml and locked; a single SQLAlchemy 2.x Engine created once during application startup and disposed on shutdown via the lifespan hook; a sessionmaker bound to it; and a FastAPI dependency yielding one Session per request that rolls back on exception and closes on completion. Constraints: the driver is psycopg 3, addressed as postgresql+psycopg://; the URL is read from the environment only, with no DSN, host, or credential literal in application source or in a fixture (NFR-401); exactly one Engine exists per process, so the connection pool is shared rather than rebuilt per request; engine construction is lazy and opens no connection, so unit tests need no live database and the live connectivity check stays in scripts/smoke-test.sh; GET /api/v1/health continues to answer without acquiring a connection, preserving api-001 so a degraded database cannot present as an unreachable service. Failure case: a missing or empty DATABASE_URL must fail loudly at startup rather than at first query; constructing an Engine inside a request handler fails the spec; and a request whose handler raises must leave no session open and no transaction uncommitted. Refs: FR-901, FR-904, NFR-401, api-001, db-001, db-003, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10, docs/qa.md section 18.

Route handlers hold no SQL, no session construction, and no spatial logic, the enforcement half of FR-904. Input: the route modules under app/api/. Output: a structural test asserting that no route module constructs a session, builds an Engine, issues SQL, or calls a PostGIS function; handlers obtain data only by calling a repository function. Constraints: the check parses the modules rather than matching source text, because a substring match is satisfied by an example in a docstring -- the defect that made an earlier absence test pass vacuously (docs/qa.md section 38, db-001). This item is split from db-003 deliberately: db-003 is the repository existing and being correct, this is nothing bypassing it, and the two fail at different times -- a broken repository fails at write time against a populated database, a leaked query fails review and nothing else. It cannot be proved before there is a data-serving route, so it lands with api-002 in Phase 5, not with db-003. Failure case: a raw SELECT, a session or Engine constructed in a handler, or a PostGIS function called from a route module fails the spec. A second failure case: the test passing against a handler that contains a violation written inside a comment or docstring means the check is matching text and fails the spec itself -- it is mutation-tested both ways before this item is set passing. Refs: FR-904, US-E2, db-003, api-002, docs/qa.md sections 38 and 39.

Scenario run completion, so a partial run is distinguishable from a finished one. Input: a scenario run created by any producer -- adp-007's replay today, scn-001's generator later -- and its outcome. Output: a second Alembic revision adding completed_at, a nullable timestamptz, to scenario_runs; a repository function that sets it; and replay setting it after its final batch has committed. A run whose completed_at is null is a run not known to have finished. Constraints: nullable with no server default and no backfill, because the column's whole meaning is that absence is informative -- a default would mark every existing row complete including the partial ones this item exists to find. Set after the last batch commits, never before and never in the same transaction as the first, since a flag written up front records an intention rather than an outcome. Nothing is deleted on failure: the rows a partial run wrote are kept, because they are evidence about what went wrong and a cascading delete over 133,634 observations is a surprising thing for a failure path to do. Three states -- running, failed, crashed -- are deliberately collapsed into one, because a process killed outright cannot record its own failure, so a status column with a 'failed' value would be reliable for caught exceptions and silently wrong for everything else; null honestly means 'not known to have completed'. Written as db-007 rather than folded into adp-007 or scn-001 because the column belongs to the schema and every producer of a run must set it, so it cannot live inside one producer. Why this exists: adp-007 chose one window as the unit of work rather than one run, so an interrupted replay leaves its committed batches in place. Combined with a new run being created on every invocation rather than resuming, the database accumulates partial runs that are indistinguishable from complete ones by inspection. Harmless while nothing reads runs; wrong the moment eval-001 counts them or a detector reads a window from one. Failure case: a replay that raises part-way through must leave completed_at null on its run, and must leave the batches it already wrote in place -- deleting them, or marking the run complete, both fail the spec. A second failure case: completed_at set before the final batch commits fails the spec, and is tested by observing the run's completed_at from inside the last save_batch and asserting it is still null. A third: the revision applied to a database holding rows must leave every existing completed_at null rather than backfilling it, since those rows are exactly the runs whose completion is unknown. A fourth: applying the revision twice from empty must not error, and downgrading must drop the column. A fifth failure case: completing a run id that is absent from scenario_runs must raise rather than update nothing, because an UPDATE matching no rows reports success over a run that was never marked, which is the silent completion this column exists to make impossible. Refs: FR-201, US-E1, AC-01, db-001, db-003, adp-007, scn-001, scn-003, eval-001, api-006, docs/qa.md section 40.

Detection finding persistence. Input: the findings one rule produced for one scenario run -- anom-001's RF deviation episodes or anom-010's track discontinuities -- with the run id and the rule that produced them. Output: rows in a detection_findings table carrying the run, the rule, the finding type, the subject the finding concerns, its simulated-time window, a Point location and the triggering readings as recorded references; plus a read-back returning the same models that went in. Constraints: every finding carries the run it belongs to, because eval-002 computes every metric per run against that run's recorded ground truth and a finding that cannot name its run cannot be scored; the location is a geometry column with a GiST index, because db-004 and anom-004 are spatial queries over exactly this table and an unindexed one fails as a performance claim rather than a correctness one, which is the kind of defect that survives every functional test; the write is per run per rule and replaces what was there, so re-running detection after a rule changes cannot leave a stale set behind to be counted twice; all SQL stays in the storage layer and nothing above it learns a storage type (FR-904). Failure cases: a finding naming a run that does not exist must be refused by the database rather than stored orphaned; a finding whose window ends before it begins must be refused; reading findings for a run that has none must return an empty list rather than null or an error; a second write of the same rule's findings for the same run must leave the count unchanged rather than doubling it. Refs: FR-905, FR-904, NFR-601, db-001, db-003, db-007, anom-001, anom-010, anom-004, anom-005, db-004, evb-002, eval-002. Written 2026-09-14, on picking up db-004 and finding it had nothing to query: the anomalies table exists, no code writes to it or reads it, and no item covered doing so. Five decisions. First, findings are stored in their own table rather than in anomalies. That table describes the reportable kind -- it requires a severity, requires a Polygon affected_area, and links to an evidence bundle. The two rules built so far produce neither a severity nor an area: anom-008's amendment made the first deliberate, and anom-001's ninth decision made the second, because an area needs corroboration from more than one source and inventing a radius would mean modelling a coverage footprint the project has never measured. Forcing findings into that table would mean three nullable columns and a polygon that misstates what was observed. Second, anomalies gains a scenario_run_id in the same migration. It has none today, so no anomaly can say which run produced it, and every metric in eval-002 is computed per run. That is a gap in db-001 rather than a change of design, and it costs nothing now and a data migration after a campaign. Third, one canonical finding shape whatever rule produced it. The detectors return different models -- an RF episode carries a cell and a peak deviation, a track discontinuity carries an aircraft and a shape -- and a storage layer knowing about both would gain a branch per rule, which is exactly the dependency dal-001 removed one layer down. The same argument holds here: one shape every rule becomes, with whatever is rule-specific carried in a details payload, so a third detector needs no change to the storage layer at all. This is the RQ1 extensibility claim made at a second seam, and it is worth measuring when anom-003 lands. Fourth, the write replaces rather than appends. Detection is deterministic and regenerable from the run's seed, so a finding is derived rather than historical, and db-007's rule that nothing is ever deleted does not reach it -- that rule is about runs, which are facts about what happened. Appending would be worse than deleting: after a rule changes, the old findings and the new sit together and every metric counts both, silently. Fifth, the location is a Point and the index is GiST, following db-001, whose comment on the anomalies geometry index names db-004 as its reason. The discontinuities db-004 and anom-004 query live in this table, so the index belongs here too. Scope: one migration adding the table, its index and its constraints plus the anomalies column; one canonical finding model with converters from each rule's output; and one storage module with a write and a read. It computes no distances and groups nothing -- db-004 and anom-004 are the queries and they are separate items. Recorded and deliberately not resolved here: db-004 and anom-004 describe different queries, db-004 a proximity test against a zone geometry and anom-004 a clustering of findings among themselves, while db-001's own comment calls db-004 the clustering query. Both queries are wanted. Which item owns which is settled when db-004 is picked up; this item provides the table they both read. Amended 2026-09-19, on the evb-002 traceability measurement. from_track_gap wrote the finding's window ends into evidence_refs, which is right for one of anom-010's two mechanisms and wrong for the other. evidence_refs is a citation field, and a citation must name a row: it therefore takes its timestamps from anom-010's new observed_at rather than from the window. The failure case is the measured one -- a frozen_position finding whose refs cite started_at resolves to zero rows and fails evb-002's build, 91 times in 1,021 citations. This is a change to what is written and not to the shape, so no column moves and no migration is owed: findings are derived and regenerable under this item's own replace-rather-than-append rule, and the stored corpus catches up the next time a rule runs. No figure measured before this date is threatened by it, because nothing read evidence_refs until evb-002 did. from_track_cluster is deliberately left alone and recorded here as a known non-resolver: its refs are {aircraft_id} with no timestamp at all, which as a coordinate matches every report that aircraft made rather than one, and anom-004 clusters are not reportable so no bundle cites them -- evb-002 must refuse that shape by name rather than match it loosely. Refs adds: evb-002, anom-004, anom-010.

PostGIS clustering of detection findings. Input: the findings of one scenario run for one rule, a cluster radius in kilometres, and a time window. Output: groups of findings that lie within the radius of one another, each with a representative centroid and a geometry covering its members, returned as an ordered, deterministic set. Constraints: grouping is performed by PostGIS on geography rather than by application-side arithmetic, for the reason db-004 gives -- degrees are not metres and the error varies with latitude; the radius is a parameter, not a constant; the same findings and radius always give the same groups, including the order they are returned in, because a run must be reproducible from its seed (NFR-601); a finding belongs to exactly one group. Failure cases: two findings separated by more than the radius, with nothing between them, must not be reported as one group; a single isolated finding must be returned as a group of one rather than dropped, because anom-006 needs to know a dropout happened alone; an empty input must return an empty list rather than null or an error; and groups whose member order depends on the order rows came back from the database fail the spec. Refs: FR-301, FR-305, FR-904, NFR-601, db-004, db-008, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9. Written 2026-09-15, splitting the clustering half out of db-004 on picking that item up. db-004 is the proximity query FR-905 names and its text describes; anom-004 and db-001 both refer to it as the clustering query, which it never was. Two decisions. First, the function is ST_ClusterWithin and not ST_ClusterDBSCAN. Scope v2 cut DBSCAN, and while the PostGIS implementation is a spatial function rather than a learned model, using it would put a method the scope names as excluded into the detection path and would need a minimum-points parameter that nothing in the project has a basis for choosing. ST_ClusterWithin is transitive-closure grouping on a single distance: deterministic, one parameter, and explainable in a sentence to an analyst, which is what this phase is for. Second, the transitive property is recorded as a limitation rather than discovered as a defect. Grouping by transitive closure means a chain of findings each within the radius of the next forms one group however far the chain runs, so a cluster can span far more than the radius that produced it. That is the correct behaviour for a spreading interference zone and the wrong behaviour for a line of aircraft on a single airway, and the project has no basis yet for preferring either. The measurement that would settle it -- whether the roughly 138 background discontinuities in a quiet run ever chain into a group large enough for anom-006 to raise a data-source issue on -- is owed as soon as this item and anom-004 exist, and is the open risk recorded when anom-010 landed. Amended 2026-09-15, before tests, on picking it up. Four things the item assumed turn out not to hold, all four found by asking the database rather than the documentation -- the error this project has now made twice, most recently in db-004's boundary case. First, ST_ClusterWithin has no geography variant. Both overloads in PostGIS 3.5's function catalogue take geometry and a plain double, and that distance is in the SRID's own units, which for 4326 is degrees. The constraint as written -- grouping performed on geography -- is therefore not satisfiable with the function this item chose, and the two halves of the item contradicted each other from the moment it was written. It is resolved by projecting to EPSG:3035, ETRS89-extended LAEA Europe, an equal-area metre projection covering the whole corpus box, clustering there, rather than by changing function. The substance of the constraint survives: the radius means metres and the database measures it. What changes is the mechanism named. Measured against PostGIS 3.5 on 2026-09-15 at the box corners and centre, a 5 km separation in LAEA differs from the geodesic distance on geography by at most 2.57 m, or 0.055 per cent, worst at 54 north 3 east; the alternative the constraint was written to forbid, a radius applied to raw degrees, is wrong by about 62 per cent between the two axes at 52 north. Three orders of magnitude separate the approximation accepted from the one rejected, which is what makes the amendment honest rather than convenient. The alternative that would satisfy the constraint literally -- a recursive transitive closure over ST_DWithin on geography -- was rejected: it is exact, and it buys 2.57 m of accuracy on a radius nothing in the project has a basis for choosing to within a kilometre, at the cost of the property this item selected ST_ClusterWithin for, which is being explainable to an analyst in one sentence. Second, the window variant is used and not the aggregate. ST_ClusterWithin returns an array of geometry collections and so loses row identity: every finding would have to be joined back to the collection containing it to learn which group it landed in. ST_ClusterWithinWin, verified present in PostGIS 3.5 and confirmed to chain transitively across a three-point chain at 5 km, returns a cluster id per row. Third, the cluster ids the database produces are never the order the groups come back in. ST_ClusterWithinWin numbers groups in its own internal order over rows that have no guaranteed order unless one is imposed, which is precisely the failure case this item already names. Ordering is derived from content instead: members within a group by started_at, then subject, then id; groups by their first member's key once sorted. Fourth, the centroid is computed in metres and the covering geometry in degrees, and the split is measured rather than tidy. A centroid taken in degrees is the arithmetic mean of coordinates, which underweights longitude because a degree of it is shorter; for a cluster spanning about 25 km at 52 north the two centroids lie 7.69 m apart, and the metre-space one is the correct areal centre. The covering geometry is computed in 4326 because its vertices are findings that are already stored exactly, and a round trip through 3035 does not return them unchanged -- longitude 5.0 comes back as 4.999999999999997 and latitude 52.0 as 52.000000000000014. The rule behind both is one rule: each value is computed in the space where that value is right. Two further failure cases. A radius of zero or less is refused rather than answered, for the reason db-004 gives -- an empty result would be indistinguishable from nothing clustering. And the covering geometry of a group of one is a point and of a group of two a line, not a polygon; that is recorded here rather than papered over, because a group of one has no observed extent and inventing a polygon would claim an area nothing was seen across. The anomalies table's Polygon affected_area is anom-004's problem to solve when it promotes a cluster to a reportable anomaly, not this query's. Refs adds: db-001, NFR-601.

Canonical observation model and required-field validation. Input: a source-specific record emitted by any adapter. Output: a canonical observation with source_id, source_type, observation_type, timestamp, location, data_mode, validation_status, provenance, and a typed payload. Constraints: one model for every source; payload typing is per observation type via Pydantic; validation runs before persistence. Failure case: a record missing timestamp or location must not produce a canonical observation and must route to quarantine per dal-002. Amended 2026-08-25: TrackPayload gains contact_staleness_s alongside position_staleness_s. The two are different measurements, and the distinction is a detection discriminator rather than a detail. Position staleness is time minus lastposupdate, the age of the coordinate carried inside a row; contact staleness is time minus lastcontact, the interval since any message was received from the aircraft. A row where both are stale means the aircraft is no longer heard from at all, which is scenario type 4's coverage gap. A row with fresh contact and a stale position means the aircraft is still transmitting while its position has stopped advancing, which is scenario type 2's GNSS degradation signature. Without the second field the canonical model cannot represent the difference, and the two scenario types are indistinguishable in the data the detectors read -- a confound built into the model rather than discovered in the results. The signal is present in quantity: 4,553 positioned rows of the current extract, 3.4 per cent, carry a position more than ten seconds older than their last contact, to a maximum of 1,552 seconds, and the distributions confirm the mechanism rather than merely suggesting it, since contact staleness caps at 299.97 seconds where OpenSky drops a state vector after roughly five minutes of silence while position staleness runs on to 1,561 seconds. The field is required rather than optional because lastcontact is present on every one of the extract's 133,634 rows, including all 500 null-position rows, so requiring it creates no quarantine that a null position does not already cause; position_staleness_s by contrast is absent on exactly those 500. This item returns to passes false until the added field is proven, because the description now claims a shape the model does not yet have. A second failure case: deriving contact staleness from lastposupdate, or position staleness from lastcontact, which silently collapses the discriminator and makes scenario types 2 and 4 look alike in every downstream rule. Refs: FR-101, FR-102, US-E2, dal-002, dal-003.

Quarantine of malformed records. Input: a batch of records where some fail required-field validation. Output: valid records persisted as canonical observations; invalid records persisted to quarantine with the failing field, the reason, and the source attribution; a per-run count of each. Constraints: nothing is silently dropped; no invalid record aborts the ingest run; persistence happens through a repository port -- an interface accepting canonical observations and quarantine records, with the storage engine behind it -- so this item is provable against an in-memory implementation and the PostGIS implementation lands with db-003, which requires that seam regardless of build order; the two writes are one unit of work, so a run that persists observations and then fails before writing quarantine records must leave neither. What this item proves is DAL behaviour, not database enforcement: the NOT NULL and foreign-key guarantees over the same fields are db-001's to prove, and passes: true here asserts the first claim only. Failure case: a batch of ten records with three invalid must persist seven observations and three quarantine rows and complete without raising; raising, or persisting seven with no quarantine trace, fails the spec. A second failure case: a port signature carrying a storage-engine type -- a WKT or WKB string, a session, an ORM model, a database-assigned identifier the caller is expected to supply -- fails the spec, because the DAL would then know about PostGIS and the seam db-003 exists to enforce would already be broken. Refs: FR-103, NFR-102, US-E3, AC-02, dal-001, dal-003, db-001, db-003, docs/qa.md section 26.

Provenance on every accepted record. Input: a validated record and its ingest context. Output: a canonical observation carrying source ID, source type, data mode, and scenario run ID. Constraints: provenance is attached at the DAL, not per adapter, so it cannot be forgotten by a new adapter; data_mode distinguishes replayed from synthetic. The guarantee is asserted twice, at different layers and at different times: the DAL must refuse to construct a record with provenance missing, which is what this item proves, and the schema must refuse to store one, which is db-001's NOT NULL constraints and is proven there. Marking this item passing therefore asserts the DAL half only, and the constraint half is outstanding until db-001 lands. Failure case: a canonical observation constructed with a null scenario run ID or an absent data mode fails the spec. A second failure case: provenance applied inside an adapter rather than at the DAL passes its own tests while leaving the next adapter free to omit it, which is the failure this item exists to prevent and is asserted by driving two different adapters through the same DAL entrypoint. Refs: FR-104, US-A7, US-E2, AC-02, dal-001, dal-002, db-001, adp-003, docs/qa.md section 26.

Aircraft identifier pseudonymisation at the DAL. Input: a source record carrying source-native aircraft identifiers (icao24 and callsign for the OpenSky adapter) and a pseudonymisation seed held as fixed project configuration outside the repository. Output: a canonical observation in which those identifiers are replaced by deterministic pseudonyms -- aircraft_id derived from icao24, flight_id from callsign -- with the source values discarded rather than retained alongside. A blank or absent callsign yields no flight_id rather than a pseudonym of the empty string, since OpenSky reports many of them and an empty callsign is missing data rather than an identity. Constraints: the substitution happens at the DAL, not per adapter, so a new adapter cannot forget it -- the same argument dal-003 makes for provenance, and enforced the same way, by refusing a payload that arrives with aircraft_id or flight_id already populated; the pseudonym is a deterministic function of the source identifier and the configured seed, so one aircraft maps to one pseudonym within and across runs and track continuity survives for the detectors; the two identifier namespaces are separated in the derivation, so an icao24 and a callsign that happen to share text cannot collide; no reverse mapping is persisted anywhere the application can read, so a pseudonym cannot be resolved back from the database or an API response; the pseudonym carries no source information, so airline prefixes encoded in a callsign and country blocks encoded in an icao24 allocation do not survive into it; the real identifiers remain in the local extract, which the licence permits, since the restriction is on publication and disclosure rather than on local use. The seed is separate from the scenario seed and is never drawn per run: the mapping is a property of the corpus, not of a run, because the extract is a single replayed hour and the same airframes recur in every run of a batch. One aircraft therefore carries one pseudonym across every run, and scn-001's byte-identical guarantee for a given type, parameters and seed is unaffected, since nothing about the mapping varies with those three values. The seed itself is NOT committed and is NOT written into the manifest. Amended 2026-08-21: the item previously required the seed to be recorded in the corpus manifest, which is committed. That is a defect rather than a detail. icao24 is a 24-bit space of roughly 16.7 million values, so a reader holding the seed and the derivation function reconstructs the entire mapping by exhaustive search in seconds -- a published seed is a readable reverse mapping, which this item forbids in the same sentence. The seed is therefore read from the environment, its key documented in backend/.env.example alongside the existing convention that secrets are never committed (NFR-401), and what the manifest records is the SHA-256 fingerprint of the seed rather than the seed. That preserves what recording it was for -- a seed change remains a detectable, recorded corpus-level event sitting beside the extract checksum, rather than a silent one -- without publishing the value. The consequence is a limitation to be stated rather than hidden: the mapping is machine-local, so a reader who rebuilds the corpus obtains different pseudonyms from the author's. Every reported metric still reproduces exactly, because nothing downstream reads a pseudonym's value -- it is an opaque grouping key, and detection, evidence bundling and scoring are invariant under relabelling. What does not reproduce is a specific label quoted in a thesis figure, which is the correct trade: a figure whose labels a reader could reverse is the disclosure the item exists to prevent. Failure case: a real icao24 or callsign appearing in an API response, an evidence bundle, a hypothesis, a hosted-provider request payload, or a rendered screen fails the spec, because OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(i) requires aircraft identifiers to be de-identified for any publication or other disclosure and section 3(iii) forbids making the data available outside the licensee's institute. A second failure case: the same aircraft carrying different pseudonyms in two runs against the same corpus, which breaks track continuity across a replay and makes a batch non-comparable; deriving the pseudonym from the scenario seed produces exactly this and fails the spec. A third failure case: retaining the source identifier in the observation payload beside the pseudonym, which satisfies the letter of the mapping while leaving the real value one query away. A fourth failure case: committing the seed, or writing it into the manifest, which makes every pseudonym reversible by exhaustive search over the icao24 space and reduces the whole item to theatre. A fifth failure case: truncating the digest far enough that two of the corpus's 1,445 distinct icao24 values collide onto one pseudonym, which merges two airframes into one track and corrupts every continuity rule downstream without raising anything. Refs: FR-111, NFR-405, NFR-401, FR-101, FR-104, US-E2, AC-02, dal-001, dal-002, dal-003, adp-001, adp-003, adp-004, evb-001, ai-004, docs/qa.md section 22, docs/qa.md section 26.

OpenSky replay adapter, a pure windowed reader over the archived extract. Input: the bounding-box-filtered OpenSky extract at data/opensky/opensky_extract.parquet, its committed manifest, and a bounded half-open window of source time. Output: source records in the DAL's source-record shape -- source_id, source_type, observation_type, timestamp, location, and a track payload carrying icao24, callsign, altitude_m, velocity_ms, heading_deg, vertical_rate_ms, on_ground, position_staleness_s and contact_staleness_s -- yielded in ascending time order and handed to ingest_batch, which converts them into canonical track observations. Amended 2026-08-23, three changes. First, the adapter holds no clock. The item previously took 'a replay position in simulated time', which put a replay cursor inside the adapter. It is now a pure windowed reader: given a half-open window over source time it yields the records falling in it and keeps no position between calls. The simulated clock belongs to the scenario runner, scn-001, because detection latency is measured in simulated scenario time from event onset to anomaly emission, and two components each holding a notion of now makes that measurement ambiguous at exactly the point it has to be defensible; it also keeps the adapter testable offline against a small fixture with no scenario machinery in scope. Second, the extract is not committed. The item previously described 'a committed Parquet file' and replay 'reproducible from a fresh clone with no download step'. Both were true when written and were falsified by adp-004's licence reversal: OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(iii) forbids making the data available outside the licensee's institute, so opensky_extract.parquet is gitignored. Reproducibility from a fresh clone now runs through adp-006 -- python -m app.corpus.build with explicit licence acceptance -- which re-downloads roughly 180 MB against the manifest's recorded checksum and re-filters. The adapter's own guarantee is unchanged and is the one that matters here: it reads from file only and never opens a socket. Third, a Parquet reader has to be written. read_rows in app/corpus/extract.py reads the raw tarball's gzipped CSV, not the extract, and write_parquet has no counterpart; the previous handoff recorded read_rows as already yielding the rows this item replays, which was wrong. The reader takes its types from the schema embedded in the artefact rather than inferring them or importing the writer's column list; verified against the real extract, ParquetFile.schema_arrow returns the writer's fields in the writer's order, so the file is asked rather than a shared constant. A reader that inferred types would silently disagree with the writer as soon as a column is entirely null within a window, and one that imported parquet_schema would restate what the artefact already carries and drift from it the moment the two disagreed. Scope, settled 2026-08-25: the item delivers app/adapters/opensky.py, a module that imports nothing from app.corpus -- the arrow must not point from the consumer of the artefact back to the build-time tool that downloads and filters it. Three functions. read_window is the pure reader: path and half-open window in, source records out, no DAL involvement and no state between calls. replay_window is thin wiring that drives read_window into ingest_batch and returns the IngestResult, taking the ingest context, the repository and the pseudonymiser as injected arguments and importing no concrete implementation of either. That wiring is in scope here rather than in scn-001 because this item's stated output is canonical track observations, and the claim is only provable end to end if something within the item crosses the adapter-DAL boundary; a reader alone would leave it asserted rather than demonstrated. available_window is the manifest's one job: it derives the extract's span from snapshot_hour, recorded as 2022-06-27T12:00:00Z, so a caller knows what time range exists without scanning the file. The manifest is deliberately not re-verified per window, because content_sha256 is computed over every row and checking it on each call would read the whole extract to serve a ten-second slice; checksum verification at build time is adp-006's, and it is already proven there. Constraints: reads from file only, never the network, so replays are deterministic, offline and repeatable; the window is yielded lazily rather than materialised, since the extract is 133,634 rows and a caller asking for the whole hour should not force it into memory. The adapter performs dialect translation and nothing else -- it attaches no provenance, derives no pseudonyms and persists nothing, per dal-003 and dal-004, and validate_record rejects a record arriving with provenance, aircraft_id or flight_id already populated, so an adapter doing the DAL's job fails loudly rather than passing its own tests. It emits real icao24 and callsign values, which is the precondition for dal-004's substitution rather than a breach of it: for the DAL to be the single place identifiers are replaced, the raw values have to reach it. Position staleness is the measured delta between time and lastposupdate, never an inferred or defaulted value. Records are emitted in ascending time order, which the extract already satisfies in file order, so continuity and inter-sample gap rules see samples in the order they were observed. The adapter drops nothing: a malformed row is passed through and quarantined by the DAL, because adp-004 deliberately retained 500 null-position rows so dal-002's quarantine path has real input and AC-02 is demonstrated on real data rather than on fixtures alone. Parquet is the archive format for this extract alone and is never a read path for observations, which are served from PostGIS. Altitude is decided against the corpus rather than by preference: altitude_m takes baroaltitude, falling back to geoaltitude only where baroaltitude is absent. Measured over the 133,134 positioned rows of the current extract, baroaltitude is null on 30,276 and geoaltitude on 34,777, and the null sets nest -- every row lacking a barometric altitude also lacks a geometric one -- so the fallback fires on zero rows and geoaltitude contributes nothing this corpus does not already have. Barometric is preferred because it is one consistent reference across the fleet, whereas geoaltitude is GNSS-derived and is therefore the field that the interference this project injects would itself degrade, and because TrackPayload carries a single altitude field with no way to record which reference a value came from. The consequence is that 30,276 positioned rows, 22.7 per cent, carry a null altitude_m; that is permitted by the model and must not be defaulted to zero or carried forward from the previous sample. Failure case: a row with a null lat or lon must quarantine rather than persist a track observation at a default coordinate. A second failure case: an adapter that falls back to fetching from the OpenSky API when the extract is missing, which silently reintroduces the network dependency the archive exists to remove. A third failure case: filtering null-position rows out inside the adapter, which satisfies the first failure case by never exercising it and removes the only real-data input dal-002 has. A fourth failure case: defaulting position_staleness_s to zero when lastposupdate is absent, which asserts a perfectly fresh position for a row that has none and suppresses the update-frequency rule the field exists to feed; such a row must quarantine. In the current extract lastposupdate is null on exactly the 500 null-position rows and present on every positioned row, so this path is not exercised by the corpus and must be proven by fixture. A fifth failure case: an empty or inverted window yielding the whole extract rather than nothing, the default-to-all bug, which hands 133,634 rows to a caller that asked for none. A sixth failure case: the adapter deriving aircraft_id or flight_id itself, or attaching provenance, which passes the adapter's own tests while relocating an obligation that must hold across every source into a place a third adapter's author need not look; this is the defect dal-001's original fixtures carried until dal-004 exposed it. A seventh failure case: replay_window importing a concrete repository, or constructing a Pseudonymiser from the environment itself, rather than receiving both as arguments -- which couples the adapter to a storage engine and to process configuration and breaks the seam db-003 requires. An eighth failure case: available_window derived by scanning the rows rather than read from the manifest, which reads the whole extract to answer a question the manifest already answers and makes the corpus span a property of whichever rows happen to be present rather than of the recorded artefact. A ninth failure case: computing either staleness from the other's source column -- contact staleness from lastposupdate, or position staleness from lastcontact -- which produces plausible numbers, raises nothing, and collapses the discriminator between scenario types 2 and 4 (dal-001). The fixtures give the two columns distinct values precisely so a transposition fails a test rather than passing one. A tenth failure case: dropping lastcontact on the floor, which is what this item did between the 2026-08-23 amendment and this one -- the column was read and discarded because TrackPayload had nowhere to put it. Refs: FR-105, FR-110, NFR-101, dal-001, dal-002, dal-003, dal-004, adp-004, adp-006, scn-001, anom-008, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources, docs/qa.md section 30, docs/qa.md section 31.

Synthetic RF adapter. Input: scenario type, parameters, and seed from the scenario generator. Output: RF source records on a sensor x channel x time grid, each carrying sensor ID, sensor location, timestamp, channel index, channel centre frequency, band, power, SNR, bandwidth, signal type, and baseline delta, converted by the DAL into canonical RF observations. Constraints: fully determined by scenario type, parameters, and seed; emits no data of its own accord outside a scenario run; every sensor reports on every channel at every interval, so a missing reading is a detectable gap rather than an ambiguous absence; carries no ground-truth field, per api-009. Failure case: two runs with identical type, parameters, and seed producing different RF observation sequences fails the spec. A second failure case: emitting a sparse grid in which a sensor silently omits channels it has nothing to report on, which makes a genuine dropout indistinguishable from a design choice. Amended 2026-09-11, before implementation, because this item is the body scn-003's batch executes and the decisions below are the ones that would otherwise be settled silently while writing it. Five of them. First, the module is app/adapters/synthetic_rf.py -- one module per source, beside opensky.py -- and it is a driver only: the stream is scn-001's emitter in app/scenario/emitter.py and stays there, so nothing that invents a number moves into the adapter layer. It mirrors replay_window's shape and takes its repository and pseudonymiser rather than constructing either, so the adapter/DAL seam RQ1 measures is the same seam on both sources rather than two different arrangements to compare a third against. Second, the unit of work is one run, not one window -- deliberately the opposite of adp-007's choice, and for a reason that only holds on this side: a synthetic run regenerates byte-identically from its seed, so all-or-nothing at run scale costs nothing to retry, whereas a replay that lost twelve committed batches would have to re-read the corpus. A run that fails part-way must therefore leave no observations at all, or scn-003's skipped run is a partial one that later counts as evidence. One run at the shipped layout is 5,040 records -- seven sensors x eight channels x ninety ten-second ticks over fifteen minutes -- comparable to one of adp-007's twelve replay batches, so the larger transaction that argument rejected does not arise here. Third, every observation this adapter produces carries data_mode SYNTHETIC, which is the field op-001's SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA badge reads; the badge is a property of the data rather than a UI constant, so a synthetic reading stored as replayed makes the interface lie about what the analyst is looking at. Fourth, the pseudonymiser is carried and unused: IDENTIFIER_RULES has no entry for RF, so substitute is a no-op on these payloads, and the argument is passed anyway rather than made optional at the DAL -- a single ingest entrypoint carrying a bypass for one source is no longer the architectural guarantee dal-002 and dal-003 rest on. Fifth, this adapter creates no scenario_runs row, records no ground truth and marks nothing complete. It is handed a scenario_run_id and writes observations under it; the run lifecycle belongs to the producer of the run, which is scn-003. Failure cases added by this amendment. A stored observation carrying data_mode replayed, or any value other than synthetic, fails the spec. A run whose stored observation count is not sensors x channels x ticks fails the spec, which is the dense-grid constraint above re-asserted against the database rather than against the in-memory stream -- a gap that only appears after persistence is invisible to every test scn-001 wrote. Observations surviving in the store from a run whose ingest raised part-way fails the spec, since the batch runner above would then skip a run that had already written half its grid. Accepted plus quarantined not equalling the number of records emitted fails the spec, which is dal-002's nothing-is-silently-dropped guarantee reduced to arithmetic at this level, as adp-007 reduces it at its own. Refs: FR-106, FR-108, FR-201, scn-001, scn-002, scn-003, scn-005, api-009, dal-001, dal-002, dal-003, dal-004, db-003, adp-007, op-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources.

Third source adapter, the extensibility measurement. Input: a simple additional source, for example a synthetic source-health feed. Output: canonical observations of a new observation type flowing through the unchanged DAL, plus a recorded measurement of files touched, lines changed, and hours taken. Constraints: the DAL, canonical model, and detection layer must require no modification beyond registering the adapter and its payload type; this is RQ1 evidence, not a feature, and is built late. Failure case: needing to alter the canonical observation model or a detection rule to accommodate the new source is a reportable negative result and fails the spec as written. Refs: FR-107, US-E2, US-R6, dal-001, docs/research_scope.md RQ1.

OpenSky corpus extraction and archive. Input: a locally downloaded raw OpenSky hourly state-vector file (states_YYYY-MM-DD-HH.csv.tar, wrapping one gzipped CSV member, from the anonymously readable data-samples bucket), a bounding box, and an output directory. Output: under data/opensky/ -- opensky_extract.parquet, the bounding-box-filtered Parquet extract, gitignored and never committed, plus a bounded sample of rows whose lat or lon is null, retained deliberately so the quarantine path has real input; manifest.json, committed, recording source URL, snapshot hour, download date, the licence and the required attribution text verbatim, the SHA-256 checksum of the original raw file, and a content checksum of the extract; and coverage.json, committed, the coverage report giving the per-icao24 inter-sample gap distribution against the 10-second cadence. Constraints: neither the raw file nor the extract may be committed, because the OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(iii) forbids making the data available to anyone outside the licensee's institute; reproducibility is carried instead by the committed manifest plus a fetch-and-filter entrypoint that re-downloads against the recorded checksum and re-filters, so a fresh clone reproduces the extract in one command once the reader accepts the same licence; download and filter are separate operations and the filter itself performs no network access, so it is testable offline against a small fixture; filtering is deterministic, so re-running against the same raw file and bounding box yields an extract with identical row content and column schema, verified against the recorded content checksum rather than by byte equality, since Parquet writers embed non-deterministic metadata; licence and attribution are captured at download time and stored verbatim, because the terms as published on that date cannot be reconstructed later; Parquet is the archive format for this extract alone and is never a read path for observations, which are served from PostGIS; the corpus lives under data/opensky/ rather than scenarios/, which is reserved for scenario fixtures -- this is replayed source data, not a fixture. A bounding-box test cannot be applied to a null coordinate, so a pure spatial filter would exclude every null-position row and leave dal-002's quarantine path exercised by fixtures alone and AC-02 undemonstrated on real data; the filter therefore also retains the first N rows with a null lat or lon in file order, N being configuration with its value and the resulting count recorded in the manifest. File order is used rather than a seeded sample so the retention needs no seed of its own and stays deterministic for a given raw file. Such a row can only ever reach quarantine, never a canonical observation, so retaining it adds evidence without any risk of contaminating the operational picture or a metric. The coverage report computes its gap distribution over positioned rows only, since a null-position row is not a coverage gap. Failure case: a filter step that downloads the snapshot itself when the raw file is absent fails the spec, because it reintroduces the network dependency the archive exists to remove and makes the filter untestable offline -- the same failure adp-001 guards against at replay time. A second failure case: opensky_extract.parquet or the raw file appearing in git fails the spec as a licence breach, and a manifest missing the original checksum, the licence, or the attribution text fails it because the artefact is then neither reproducible nor attributable. A third failure case: an extract containing no null-position rows at all, which silently removes the only real-data input dal-002 has and reduces AC-02 to a fixture claim. A fourth failure case: a coverage report whose natural gap distribution overlaps the gap durations the aircraft-coverage-gap scenario will inject must fail acceptance and force a different bounding box, never be waived, because genuine and injected dropouts would then be indistinguishable and the false-positive rate uninterpretable. Refs: FR-105, FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-601, AC-02, adp-001, scn-002, anom-008, docs/implementation.md Track 0, docs/qa.md section 21.

Fetch-and-verify entrypoint for the OpenSky corpus, the network half of the corpus tooling. Input: a source URL and expected SHA-256 read from the committed manifest, a destination directory, and an explicit licence acceptance. Output: the raw tarball downloaded to data/opensky/raw/ and verified against the recorded checksum, followed by the adp-004 filter, so one command takes a fresh clone to opensky_extract.parquet, manifest.json and coverage.json. Amended 2026-08-21: the command itself is adp-006. This item delivers the fetch-and-verify function; until adp-006 landed the one-command claim was met only by a multi-line python -c invocation, which is not a command. Constraints: this is the only module in the corpus tooling permitted to open a socket, which is what keeps the adp-004 filter network-free and testable offline; the checksum of the downloaded file is verified before the filter runs, not after, so a corrupted or substituted file never reaches the extract; the download writes to a temporary path and is moved into place only once verified, so an interrupted run leaves nothing that a later run would mistake for a complete file; a run whose destination already holds a file matching the recorded checksum skips the download rather than re-fetching roughly 180 MB; licence acceptance is an explicit act by the operator, not a default, and the licence and attribution are displayed at the point of acceptance, because the whole reason the extract is not committed is that acceptance belongs to the reader rather than being bypassed by handing them the bytes; every test mocks the transport and no test in the suite performs a real download. Failure case: a checksum mismatch that still produces an extract fails the spec, because the artefact would then be unattributable to the recorded source and the manifest would assert a provenance that does not hold; the run must abort and leave no extract, manifest or coverage report behind. A second failure case: a partially downloaded file left at the destination path, which a later run would accept as complete and filter into a silently truncated extract. A third failure case: downloading without explicit licence acceptance, which makes the tool take a licence action on the operator's behalf. A fourth failure case: any test performing a real network call, which makes the suite slow, non-deterministic, dependent on OpenSky's hosting, and quietly turns continuous integration into an unattended acceptor of someone else's terms. Refs: FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-601, AC-12, adp-001, adp-004, ops-003, docs/qa.md section 21, docs/implementation.md Track 0.

Command-line entrypoint for the corpus build, the operator surface over adp-004 and adp-005. Input: an invocation of python -m app.corpus.build carrying a data directory, an explicit licence-acceptance flag, an optional bounding-box override, an optional null-retention bound, and the pseudonymisation seed read from the environment, with backend/.env loaded by the entrypoint so the seed does not have to be exported by hand. Output: exit code 0 with opensky_extract.parquet, manifest.json and coverage.json written per adp-004, and a summary naming what was written, the row counts, the content checksum, and the seed fingerprint; a non-zero exit with a diagnostic naming the cause on every failure path. Constraints: this is the one command adp-005 promises, which until now was met by a multi-line python -c invocation -- not a command, not documentable in a README without inviting transcription error, and the vehicle for the download_date trap below. The bounding box defaults to the box recorded in the committed manifest rather than to a literal in code, so the manifest remains the single authority on what the corpus covers and a re-filter cannot silently apply a different box from the one that built the extract; an explicit flag overrides it, and overriding is what a deliberate box change looks like. download_date is derived rather than supplied: when adp-005 skips the download because the destination already matches the recorded checksum, the existing manifest's download_date is carried forward unchanged, and only an actual download records today's date. The recomputed content checksum is compared against the one already in the manifest before any artefact is overwritten, and a difference aborts the run with both values reported; proceeding requires an explicit flag, because replacing the corpus every recorded measurement was taken against is a deliberate act rather than a side effect of re-running a build. Licence acceptance is an explicit flag with no default and the notice is displayed before it is checked, per adp-005. The pseudonymisation seed is read from the environment and is never a command-line flag, because a flag is recorded in shell history and visible in process listings; a missing seed aborts before any file is written, per dal-004. Nothing derived from the seed other than its SHA-256 fingerprint is printed or written. Failure case: defaulting download_date to today on a run whose download was skipped, which writes a false provenance date into a committed artefact and is precisely the trap the manual invocation carried. A second failure case: overwriting the manifest when the recomputed content checksum differs from the recorded one, which silently replaces the corpus behind every measurement already taken and reported. A third failure case: a run that leaves a partial artefact set behind when a later step fails -- the manifest must not be rewritten unless the extract was written, the same all-or-nothing argument adp-005 makes for the download. A fourth failure case: exiting 0 on any of the above, since a command that reports success on failure cannot be used in a script or in CI. A fifth failure case: accepting the licence by default, or reading acceptance from an environment variable rather than from an explicit act by the operator. A sixth failure case: the seed appearing in a flag, in the summary output, or in the manifest, any of which discloses the key and makes every pseudonym reversible by exhaustive search over the icao24 space. Refs: FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-401, NFR-601, AC-12, adp-004, adp-005, dal-004, ops-003, docs/qa.md section 27, docs/qa.md section 28, docs/implementation.md Track 0.

Replay entrypoint, the operator surface over the adapter and the DAL. Input: an invocation of python -m app.replay carrying an optional window length in seconds, an optional start and end bounding the span replayed, and a data directory; DATABASE_URL and PSEUDONYM_SEED from the environment. Output: the archived extract driven through adp-001's reader, the DAL, and db-003's PostGIS repository into a live database; a scenario_runs row created for the replay; a summary on stdout reporting rows read, observations accepted, records quarantined, batches written, and wall time; a non-zero exit status when the replay fails. Also: a make replay target running it in a container, and PSEUDONYM_SEED passed through into the backend and pipeline compose services from the host environment as ${PSEUDONYM_SEED}, with no default of any kind. Amended 2026-09-04 during implementation: this item originally specified Compose's required form, ${PSEUDONYM_SEED:?}, so that an unset seed failed on the host. That was wrong. Compose interpolates the whole file for every command regardless of profile, so a required variable makes up, migrate, test and demo all demand a seed only replay needs -- and make demo on a clean machine is AC-12. Verified by running it: with the seed unset, docker compose config itself exits non-zero. The loud failure moved rather than being lost, to Pseudonymiser.from_environment, which raises before anything is written and names backend/.env.example. Constraints: this command constructs nothing the adapter should own -- replay_window already takes its repository and pseudonymiser, and this item supplies them. It calls init_engine() explicitly and disposes on exit, because db-005 made get_engine() refuse to build lazily and no FastAPI lifespan runs here. It loads .env, following app/corpus/build.py rather than app/main.py, so the two operator CLIs behave alike and main.py remains the single documented exception (docs/qa.md section 37). The seed is never committed and never defaulted (dal-004). Four decisions fixed 2026-09-04, before implementation, and recorded because each is a real constraint rather than a detail. First, this command creates its own scenario_runs row, with scenario_type 'replay-only', seed 0, empty parameters and null ground_truth: observations carries a NOT NULL foreign key to that table, no scenario generator exists yet, and a command requiring a run nothing can create would be unrunnable. scn-001 supersedes this, and the placeholder scenario_type is what makes such rows identifiable when it does. Second, the unit of work is one window, not one run -- so dal-002's all-or-nothing guarantee holds per batch and a run interrupted part-way leaves the windows already written in place. That is a deliberate weakening of what dal-002 promises at run scale and is stated here rather than discovered; a whole-hour single transaction was rejected as a 133,634-row write held open for the length of the replay. Third, it does not reuse the pipeline compose service, whose command points at app.pipeline, a module that does not exist -- make replay runs compose run --rm backend, mirroring migrate. Fourth, the summary exists to make the corpus figures reproducible: the wall time currently on record was taken with a throwaway script, measures the reader and the DAL against the in-memory fake rather than PostGIS, and is recorded inconsistently as 2.44 s in thesis_notes.md and 2.46 s in qa.md and the handoff. Re-taking it through this command and reconciling both documents is part of this item. Failure case: PSEUDONYM_SEED unset must fail before any row is written, and must not fall back to a default or to an empty seed -- a replay that silently pseudonymises under an empty seed produces a corpus whose identifiers cannot be reconciled with any other run. A second failure case: an unreachable database, a missing extract, or a window outside the corpus span must exit non-zero with a message naming which of the three failed; exiting zero over a replay that wrote nothing fails the spec. A third: a real icao24 or callsign reaching any persisted row fails the spec (dal-004). A fourth: the reported accepted and quarantined counts not summing to rows read fails the spec, because that is the arithmetic dal-002's nothing-is-silently-dropped guarantee reduces to at this level. Refs: FR-105, FR-104, NFR-101, US-E7, AC-02, AC-12, adp-001, adp-004, dal-002, dal-003, dal-004, db-003, db-005, ops-003, scn-001, docs/qa.md sections 37 and 39. Implemented 2026-09-04. Measured through this command against the full corpus, in containers, with the PostGIS repository: 133,634 rows read, 133,134 accepted, 500 quarantined, 12 batches of 300 simulated seconds, 14.25 s wall time -- against ~2.4 s for the same corpus through the in-memory fake, so persistence is about 5.8x the cost of reading and normalising. Cross-checks reproduced independently in the database: 30,276 observations with no altitude, 948 distinct aircraft, every geometry at SRID 4326, and zero rows mentioning icao24 or callsign. Two defects were found by running it and were unreachable from the test suite: DEFAULT_ENV_FILE was anchored to the repository root, which does not exist inside the container, and Compose passing an unset variable through as an empty string shadowed backend/.env because load_dotenv treats present-but-empty as present. Both now carry regression tests.

Injection-exclusion list for track perturbation. Input: the archived extract, the bounding box from the committed manifest, a minimum gap length, and the pseudonymisation seed. Output: data/opensky/natural_gaps.json, committed, naming every aircraft carrying a natural reporting gap while airborne and away from the box edges - identified by its DAL pseudonym rather than by icao24 - with each gap's start, end and duration, and the parameters the analysis ran under. Constraints: a gap counts only when it starts and ends inside the box with the aircraft airborne at both ends, because an aircraft leaving the box or parked on the ground produces an interval that is an artefact of the filter rather than a coverage failure; identifiers are pseudonyms so the artefact can be committed without carrying source identities (dal-004), and are therefore meaningful only against the seed whose fingerprint the manifest records; the analysis is deterministic and the artefact is regenerated by the same command that builds the corpus (adp-006). Failure case: reporting a gap distribution with no identifiers, which is what coverage.json already does and what leaves the exclusion unbuildable - the point of this item is the identity, not the duration. A second failure case: committing icao24 values, which would place source identities in the repository that dal-004 exists to keep out. A third failure case: counting a gap whose ends straddle the bounding box, which is the error the box sweep already made once and corrected. Refs: FR-202, adp-004, adp-006, dal-004, scn-002, anom-008, docs/thesis_notes.md.

Seeded reproducibility of scenario runs, landed with the smallest seeded emitter. Input: a scenario type, a parameter set, and an optional integer seed; the RF layout from scn-005; and a simulated start time and duration. Output: a run record carrying the type, the parameters and the seed actually used, and a stream of RF source records on the layout's sensor x channel x interval grid, one reading per cell, whose serialisation is byte-identical to that of any other run with the same three inputs. Constraints: no wall-clock time, no unseeded randomness and no process-dependent ordering may influence output, so each cell's values are derived from the seed and the cell's own coordinates - sensor, channel index, tick - rather than from the order draws are taken in, and derivation uses a stable digest rather than Python's per-process salted hash; the seed is always recorded, including when it was generated rather than supplied; the run row is written through the storage layer rather than by SQL in a command module, superseding adp-007's placeholder run row, and is marked complete per db-007. Scope: this item emits the unperturbed baseline only - injection is scn-002's and persistence through the DAL is adp-002's - and its records carry no scenario type and no ground truth, per api-009. Failure case: identical inputs producing different output, or differing seeds producing identical output, both fail the spec; the second is the trap, since a generator that ignores its seed entirely is trivially reproducible and useless. A second failure case: output that changes when PYTHONHASHSEED differs between two processes, a difference that is stable within a process and so survives every in-process test. A third failure case: a run whose seed was generated automatically rather than supplied and then not recorded, which can never be repeated. A fourth failure case: two runs with the same seed and different parameters producing identical output, since a parameter that controls nothing is the same defect as a seed that controls nothing. Refs: FR-201, US-E1, NFR-601, AC-01, api-006, api-009, scn-002, scn-003, scn-005, adp-002, adp-007, db-007.

The five scenario types. Input: one of normal-baseline, gnss-degradation, rf-sensor-fault, aircraft-coverage-gap, ambiguous-mixed-evidence, with parameters and a seed (scn-001). Output: the RF stream from scn-001's emitter with that type's injected component added per cell; for track-perturbing types, replayed track source records altered between the adapter and the DAL; and a ground-truth record written to scenario_runs.ground_truth at generation time, naming the type, the affected sensors, channels and aircraft, the simulated window, and the affected area. Signatures: normal-baseline injects nothing on either side; gnss-degradation raises the noise floor on the L1 channel alone or across all eight - spectral extent is a parameter, never a sixth type - and freezes the reported position of aircraft inside the affected area while their contact staleness stays fresh; rf-sensor-fault deviates one sensor while its spatial neighbours stay nominal, on a single channel or on all eight, since anom-007 must weight those differently; aircraft-coverage-gap suppresses replayed rows for chosen aircraft in a window; ambiguous-mixed-evidence stages a single-sensor RF deviation with a co-located contemporaneous coverage gap, so a sensor fault and genuine localised interference are both consistent with the evidence and the correct hypothesis is that they cannot be distinguished. Constraints: the injected component is a separately keyed derived quantity per cell, so adding it moves no baseline value a previous run produced (scn-001); ground truth is recorded at generation time, never inferred from detector output, and never leaves the run record (api-009); track perturbation sits between the adapter and the DAL rather than inside either, since adp-001 is specified as a pure reader and dal-003 owns provenance; aircraft chosen for any track-perturbing type exclude those carrying a natural interior airborne gap (adp-008), or a real dropout and an injected one become indistinguishable and the false-positive rate for that type is meaningless. Failure case: normal-baseline injecting any deviation at all fails the spec, because anom-008 and the false-positive rate depend on it being genuinely clean. A second failure case: adding a sixth scenario type for broadband interference rather than parameterising the existing one. A third failure case: an injected run whose readings differ from the same seed's normal-baseline run in cells the injection does not touch, which would mean the injection moved the noise rather than added to it. A fourth failure case: ground truth appearing on any observation, anomaly or API response for a scorable run. Refs: FR-202, FR-204, FR-108, AC-04, scn-001, scn-005, adp-001, adp-002, adp-008, anom-007, anom-008, api-009, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.2.

Batch execution. Input: a scenario type, a parameter distribution, a base seed, and a run count between 20 and 30. Output: N runs with distinct derived seeds, each with its own recorded parameters and ground truth, executed without manual intervention. Constraints: derived seeds are a deterministic function of the base seed, so the whole batch is reproducible from one value; a failing run is recorded and skipped rather than aborting the batch. Failure case: one run raising and terminating the batch, or two runs in a batch sharing a seed, fails the spec. Refs: FR-205, FR-1001, US-R2, scn-001, eval-001. Amended 2026-09-12, before tests, because the original text settles the loop and leaves every question about what one run of the loop does. Seven decisions. First, every run carries both halves: the synthetic RF grid through adp-002, and a window of the replayed corpus through adp-001 and the DAL under the same run id, with a TrackPerturber in front of it for the three types that stage on tracks. This is not confined to the track-perturbing types. rf-sensor-fault and normal-baseline stage nothing there and still need the stream present, because anom-005 fuses RF deviation with co-located track trouble and anom-006 fires on track trouble with a clean spectrum: in a run holding no tracks, 'no track trouble' is true by construction, so those rules stay silent for the wrong reason and the false-positive rate of the control measures the RF half alone. Second, per-run seeds are derived from the base seed by scn-001's keyed derivation rather than by advancing a sequence, so the batch is reproducible from one value and the derivation does not depend on how many runs preceded a given one. Measured 2026-09-12: thirty derived seeds from base 20220627 are all distinct and land on all seven layout receivers, between two and six runs each. Third, each run's simulated window is derived from that run's own seed and must lie inside the corpus span, because several runs in a batch necessarily share a zone centre -- there are seven centres and twenty to thirty runs -- and runs sharing both a centre and a window would be near-duplicates on the track side, differing only in invented noise. Fourth, the window and duration are written onto the run row with the parameters. RunSpec.as_parameters currently records the baseline and incident parameters and neither start nor duration_seconds, so scn-001's reproduction property holds in the test suite, where the window is a module constant, and not from the database. A batch claimed to be reproducible from one value whose rows cannot regenerate their own streams is not reproducible in the sense that matters. Fifth, the unit of work is deliberately one act per half rather than one per run, and this is a weakening stated here rather than discovered later: adp-002 commits a run's RF grid in a single act and the track window commits in its own, so a run that fails between the two leaves the first half behind. Nothing is deleted in response (db-007), the run is left with completed_at null, and every reader of runs filters on completion as api-006 already does. Making the whole run atomic would mean a third ingest path composing both sources into one call, bypassing both adp-002's entrypoint and adp-001's driver, which is a large structural cost to buy a guarantee the completion stamp already provides. Sixth, the batch reports per run: the derived seed, the type, accepted and quarantined counts for both halves, the number of aircraft actually staged, and whether the run completed. The staged-aircraft count is reported because detectability varies with it and the variation sits inside a batch: measured on the corpus over the default five-minute window, a 60 km zone holds 75 aircraft at Schiphol and 18 at Eindhoven, so the default 8% fraction stages about six aircraft in one and about one in the other, and aggregate recall over thirty runs would average a nearly undetectable run with an easy one and report a single number. Seventh, the operator surface is python -m app.pipeline, the module compose's pipeline service already names, taking a scenario type, a base seed, a run count and a data directory, with make generate passing a default through PIPELINE_ARGS as make replay passes REPLAY_ARGS; ops-003 is amended in the same change, since it currently records make generate as knowingly broken. It fails before it writes, as adp-007 does: a missing corpus, an out-of-range run count or a window outside the corpus span exits non-zero before an Engine is built. Failure cases added by this amendment. A run of any type whose observations contain no track records fails the spec, the quiet control included. A run row from which the run's stream cannot be regenerated -- no recorded window, or a recorded window that does not reproduce the stored readings -- fails the spec. A batch in which two runs share a derived seed, or in which every run shares one simulated window, fails the spec, the second because it makes runs sharing a zone centre near-duplicates on the track side. A failed run marked complete fails the spec, and so does a failed run that aborts the batch. A batch that reports only an aggregate and not a per-run outcome fails the spec, since a batch whose individual runs cannot be inspected cannot be reproduced selectively either. Known limitation, recorded rather than fixed: thirty fifteen-minute windows inside a single recorded hour overlap heavily, so track-side independence across a batch is bounded by the corpus rather than by the design. Refs additionally: adp-001, adp-002, adp-007, adp-008, db-007, api-006, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-008, ops-003, docs/qa.md sections 52 and 53.

Scenario Control screen. Input: the five scenario types and the recent-runs list from GET /api/v1/scenario/runs. Output: a scenario library, a run configuration form for parameters, seed, and batch count, run controls for start, pause, reset, and replay, a run status indicator, and a recent-runs table showing type, seed, and outcome. Constraints: the seed field is visible and editable, because this screen is the visible face of the evaluation harness; replay of a listed run reuses its exact recorded seed and parameters. Failure case: starting a run with no seed entered and no seed shown afterwards fails the spec, since the run would be unreproducible. Refs: FR-714, FR-201, US-E1, api-006, scn-001, nav-001. Amended 2026-09-13, before tests, because the original text names the screen's parts and settles none of the questions that decide what it may honestly claim. Eight decisions. First, the screen is built against the contract rather than the endpoint: api-006 does not exist, so a TypeScript contract file mirrors GET /api/v1/scenario/runs and POST /api/v1/scenario/start, a mock satisfies it, and the screen takes the value as a prop, exactly as operationalPicture.ts did before api-002 served it. A backend test parses that contract and compares field sets in both directions, as api-002's parity test does, so a field added on one side alone fails. This is not the case the phase-order amendment warns about: api-007's view filter and api-008's playback are server-side by specification, whereas everything this item is judged on -- the seed visible and editable, replay reusing a recorded run's seed and parameters, exactly five types, and the failure case below -- is client-side and provable today. The same seam was measured at Phase 5 at four files and 118 insertions with no data-consuming component changed. Second, the run controls render disabled, with the reason stated on screen, until a handler is supplied. A start button that posts nowhere claims a capability the system does not have; today a batch is started from the command line. Start, reset and replay are props; with none supplied the status indicator reads idle and the screen says why. Failure case: a control rendered enabled with nothing behind it fails the item, and so does hiding the controls rather than disabling them, since an unbuilt capability the screen conceals is the degradation NFR-204 requires to be visible.
