Third, the configuration form exposes exactly the dials the batch entrypoint accepts and no others: scenario type, base seed, run count between 20 and 30, per-run duration, and the five incident dials -- offset, duration, radius, elevation and spectral extent -- excluding --data-dir, which says where the corpus lives rather than what the run is. The design mockup shows noise amplitude, affected sensor count and gap duration; the generator accepts none of them, and a control that changes nothing is scn-001's fourth failure case in a different coat. Asserted by parity against app.pipeline's parser rather than by reading the form, so a dial added to either side alone fails. Fourth, the seed is rendered and edited as the decimal integer that is stored. The mockup shows 0xA4F2. A seed's only job is to reproduce a run -- pasted into PIPELINE_ARGS, or sent back by replay -- and a second representation is one more conversion to get wrong. Bounded by SEED_MAX, because a seed that does not round-trip through scenario_runs.seed cannot reproduce its run. Failure case: a seed rendered in a form the run record cannot hold. Fifth, the seed field may be left blank and the seed actually used comes back. The screen never invents one: scn-001 requires the seed to be recorded including when it was generated rather than supplied, and api-006 requires start to echo it. The item's stated failure case is restated as this -- a run started from this screen whose seed appears nowhere afterwards fails, whether because the field was blank or because the returned record was not rendered. Sixth, replay repopulates the configuration from the listed row rather than starting the form's current state under that row's seed, which would be reproducible in name only. RunSpec.from_record is the server-side half of the same guarantee and already refuses a row that cannot describe its own window. Failure case: replaying a run whose recorded parameters the screen silently drops. Seventh, pause is not built here and the divergence is recorded rather than left silent. FR-714 lists start, pause, reset and replay; FR-806 specifies start, reset and runs only, and generation has nothing to pause -- a batch is a loop of whole runs, each committing atomically in about three seconds, so the only coherent meaning is stop-after-the-current-run, a server-side lifecycle nothing specifies. Pause belongs to FR-717's playback transport over a recorded run's simulated time, which is op-008 on the Operational Picture. Revisit if api-006 gains a lifecycle. Eighth, the recent-runs table shows the scenario type and that is not an api-009 violation. api-009 forbids the answer key, and the type as a label, on observations, detector inputs, evidence bundles and the analyst-facing picture; this screen is the evaluation harness's own face and FR-714 requires the type on it. The table carries type, seed, start and an outcome derived from whether the run is marked complete (db-007), never the ground truth's contents, which ScenarioRunSummary has no field to hold. Scope: the screen, its contract and its mock. It adds no routing -- the screen becomes reachable when nav-001 lands -- and it does not implement api-006. Refs adds: api-009, db-007, scn-003, NFR-204, FR-717, op-008.

RF sensor and channel layout. Input: a layout configuration file, or the packaged default when none is given. Output: a validated layout of six to eight RF sensors at recorded geographic positions, each reporting on eight 2 MHz channels with centre frequencies 1567.42, 1569.42, 1571.42, 1573.42, 1575.42, 1577.42, 1579.42 and 1581.42 MHz, at a fixed interval of simulated time. Constraints: one channel is centred exactly on GNSS L1 at 1575.42 MHz, with four channels below it and three above, so frequency adjacency runs in both directions from L1; channel indices are contiguous from zero and centre frequencies strictly ascending, so adjacency by index is adjacency in frequency; sensor positions are discriminating at the layout's recorded radius, meaning every sensor has at least one other sensor within that radius and at least one beyond it, which is what makes the neighbour test in anom-007 non-vacuous and the spatial-coherence test in anom-005 non-trivial; the layout is configuration loaded and validated at run time, not hard-coded constants, so it can be varied without editing generator or detector code. Failure case: a layout with fewer than six sensors, or one in which some sensor has no other sensor beyond the radius - every sensor inside every plausible affected area - makes spatial clustering undiscriminating and must be rejected at load rather than accepted and detected later. A second failure case: a channel plan with no channel centred on L1, which removes the band the gnss-degradation scenario targets. A third failure case: silently accepting a malformed, incomplete or missing layout file, rather than failing loudly before any observation is generated. Refs: FR-108, FR-109, scn-002, adp-002, anom-002, anom-004, anom-005, anom-007, evb-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources.

Stage only on aircraft that are airborne in the run's window. Input: the corpus records a run replays, the staged zone from scn-002, and the run's window. Output: a target set containing only aircraft observed airborne inside the zone during the window, and a ground truth answer key naming exactly that set. Constraints: the airborne test is made where the targeting decision is made, not compensated for afterwards, following adp-008's precedent of keeping unsuitable tracks out of a run rather than correcting the metrics later; the target draw stays order-independent and derived from the run's seed, so a run remains reproducible per NFR-601; an aircraft airborne for part of the window and on the ground for the rest is eligible, because it is detectable for the part it was flying. Failure cases: an answer key naming an aircraft that is on the ground in every one of its reports fails the spec; a run whose eligible target set is empty must record that it staged nothing rather than staging on an ineligible aircraft; and a fix applied by filtering the answer key while still perturbing ineligible aircraft fails, because the perturbed records would remain in the run as unlabelled staged data. Written 2026-09-16, on measuring anom-011. The measurement that forces this item: across 77 staged runs of the three track-perturbing types, 381 aircraft were recorded as staged and only 172 were ever airborne -- 55 per cent of every injection lands on an aircraft parked for the whole run. The generator's zone test checks position against the radius and nothing else, so an aircraft parked at an airfield inside the zone is targeted like any other. anom-010 then refuses it correctly, because an aircraft on the ground stopped reporting when it was switched off and its stale position is indistinguishable from that. The consequence is that every parked target is a guaranteed false negative in eval-002's metrics for a reason that has nothing to do with detection quality. Measured effect on the recall figure: 25 per cent over all staged aircraft against 55 per cent over those that were airborne at any point, and for gnss-degradation 37 per cent against 74. The alternative considered and rejected was to keep the targeting as it is and exclude parked aircraft from the answer key instead. It produces the same recall arithmetic and leaves the perturbed records in the run, so a parked aircraft would carry a staged disruption that the ground truth does not mention -- unlabelled staged data in a corpus whose whole value is that its answer key is complete. A falsifiable prediction is recorded with this item and is the reason it is worth building before the fusion rules: anom-004 measured no separation between a staged run and its matched control at any radius from 5 to 60 km, and roughly doubling the detected staged findings per run may change that. It is to be re-measured after this item lands, and the result reported whichever way it falls. Refs: FR-304, FR-308, NFR-601, adp-008, anom-004, anom-008, anom-010, anom-011, eval-002, scn-002, scn-003.

Guarantee a minimum number of staged aircraft per run. Input: the eligible aircraft for a run -- airborne and inside the zone, per scn-006 and adp-008 -- the affected fraction, and a configured minimum count. Output: a staged set that is the larger of the fraction's draw and the minimum, chosen deterministically from the run's seed. Constraints: the selection stays order-independent and reproducible from the seed alone, which the current per-aircraft draw achieves by keyed derivation and which a draw-until-N loop would break; the intended implementation is therefore to rank the eligible aircraft by their derived value and take the lowest n, where n is the greater of the minimum and the fraction's expected count, so the fraction's behaviour is unchanged wherever the pool is large; a run with fewer eligible aircraft than the minimum stages all of them and records that it could not reach the floor, because silently staging fewer would reintroduce the empty answer key this item exists to remove. Failure cases: a run whose answer key names no aircraft while eligible aircraft existed fails the spec; and a selection that depends on the order the aircraft arrive in fails it, since scn-001 established that traversal order must never reach a number a run has to be reproducible from. Written 2026-09-17, unbuilt, and the measurement that forces it is on anom-006. Since scn-006 restricted staging to airborne aircraft the eligible pool shrank and the 8 per cent fraction now draws a mean of 1.7 aircraft per run, with 11 of 40 runs drawing none -- so a quarter of the coverage-gap arm has an empty answer key and is indistinguishable from its control by construction. scn-006 already recorded that the limiting quantity is how many aircraft a run stages on and named it the open question; this is that question as an item. The cost is that building it requires regenerating the batches, which invalidates every detection figure measured through them, exactly as anom-014 does -- and the two are now blocked on the same act, so when a regeneration happens both should land in it and every figure should be re-measured together rather than item by item. Refs: FR-202, NFR-601, scn-002, scn-003, scn-006, adp-008, anom-006, anom-011, anom-014, eval-002. Amended 2026-09-18, when the item was taken off the shelf to be built, and the amendment records something the original could not have known: the implementation it names cannot be done where the original assumed it would be. The item says to rank the eligible aircraft by their derived value and take the lowest n. Ranking needs the pool, and the perturber does not have one -- scn-002's seam is a per-record transform on a stream that the replay processes one window at a time, which is exactly why selection was made a pure function of the seed and the aircraft's own pseudonym in the first place. So the item needs a survey pass that does not exist yet: the run reads its corpus window once through adp-001's reader without ingesting anything, collects the pseudonyms that are eligible -- inside the window, inside the zone, airborne, not on adp-008's exclusion list -- ranks that set, and hands the chosen set to the perturber before the replay begins. The cost is one extra parquet scan per run over an extract of 133,634 rows, against a run that already ingests tens of thousands of observations, and it buys the property the original wording asked for: the selection is still a pure function of the seed and the pool, still order-independent, and still reproducible without replaying the run. Ties in the derived value are broken by pseudonym so the ranking is total. The perturber therefore gains an optional selection, and a perturber without one keeps the unbounded behaviour -- the fraction alone, with no floor -- which stays the honest description of what it does rather than a fallback pretending to be the new rule. Two further decisions. The run records what the survey found, not merely what it staged: how many aircraft were eligible, how many were asked for, and whether the floor was reached, all onto the answer key beside the aircraft themselves, because a run that staged two aircraft because only two were there is a different fact from a run that staged two because two were asked for, and eval-002 cannot tell them apart from the aircraft list alone. And the floor's value is NOT fixed here: it is measured by backend/measurements/corpus/scn007_floor.py, which asks how many staged aircraft it takes for a coverage-gap run's track-gap findings to separate from its own seed-matched control, and the default is set from that with the figure recorded beside it. Choosing it by eye would repeat the error anom-012's radius was reversed for.

RF threshold rule, rule ID RF-NOISE. Input: RF observations in a window and the baseline for the band from anom-002. Output: an anomaly of type rf_noise_deviation carrying severity, time window, affected area, and the observation IDs that triggered it. Constraints: the threshold is configuration, not a literal in the rule; the rule is deterministic, so the same observations always give the same anomaly. Failure case: observations at exactly the baseline must produce no anomaly, and observations one unit above threshold must produce exactly one. Refs: FR-301, FR-303, anom-002, evb-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, on picking it up after anom-002. Nine decisions. First, this item is a detector and not a writer: it takes readings and a baseline table and returns findings, touching no database, which is what lets it be tested without Docker and keeps FR-904's rule true one layer up. Persisting an anomaly needs its own item, and that item inherits a problem recorded here rather than discovered there -- the anomalies table's affected_area column is a NOT NULL polygon, and this rule produces no polygon, for the reason in the ninth decision. Second, the triggering readings are identified by their natural key -- sensor id, channel index, timestamp -- and not by a database id. CanonicalObservation has no id field at all, deliberately, and adding one would put storage identity on the model dal-001 keeps free of storage concepts. The natural key is unique because scn-005's grid is dense: every sensor reports every channel every interval, so the three values name exactly one reading. It is also the better artefact for this phase's purpose -- 'RF-03, channel 4, at 12:07:30' is a reference an analyst can check, and a bigint is not -- and evb-002 can resolve it against the database as readily as a surrogate id. Third, the comparison has a direction per metric and is not an absolute deviation. Raised power is the noise signature; falling SNR is the same event seen the other way round, because noise rising is what drives SNR down. An absolute deviation would report a channel quieter than baseline as noise, which is a different fault entirely and probably a dead receiver. Fourth, the threshold is an absolute offset from the baseline mean in the metric's own units, supplied as configuration. It is deliberately not a multiple of the baseline's standard deviation: that is anom-003, and keeping the two apart is what makes them independent evidence about the same reading rather than one detector counted twice in a bundle. Fifth, the comparison is strictly greater than, so a reading exactly at the threshold raises nothing. The item's existing failure case fixes the two ends and this fixes the boundary between them. Sixth, severity is Low, Medium or High and nothing else, per ui-001, derived from configured bands in the metric's units. The measured exceedance is carried on the anomaly for traceability and is never rendered as a score, which is the same arrangement anom-003 makes for its z value. Seventh, the unit of output is one anomaly per cell per contiguous episode of exceedance, not one per reading. A run emits 5,040 readings, so per-reading anomalies would produce thousands of findings describing one event, and evb-001's grouping would then be repairing damage this rule did rather than doing its own work. An episode carries its first and last exceeding reading as its window. Eighth, a cell whose baseline is insufficient is reported as unjudged rather than passed over in silence. This matters to anom-008 more than to this item: a detector that skips what it cannot measure would let 'zero anomalies on a clean run' be satisfied by not having looked, and the false-positive rate computed from that is meaningless. Ninth, the affected area of a single-sensor deviation is the sensor's own position, a point. An area requires corroboration from more than one sensor, which is anom-004's clustering and anom-005's fusion, and inventing a radius here would mean choosing a coverage footprint the project has never modelled. Following dal-001, no geometry type appears on the model: coordinates only. Failure cases added. A reading below its baseline by more than the threshold must raise no noise anomaly. A reading exactly at the threshold must raise nothing. A cell with no usable baseline must be reported unjudged and must not be counted clean. A run of consecutive exceeding readings in one cell must produce one anomaly and not one per reading. Refs adds: anom-008, ui-001, dal-001, scn-005, FR-904.

Rolling-average baseline engine. Input: observations from normal-baseline runs, a metric, and a window length. Output: a baseline value against which deviation is measured, computed per metric per sensor per channel for RF metrics and per metric per region for track metrics. Constraints: the baseline derives from normal-scenario data only; per-channel granularity is required so that a quiet channel and a noisy one on the same sensor are not averaged into a baseline that fits neither; a window with insufficient samples returns an explicit insufficient-data result, not a misleading average over one point. Failure case: computing a baseline from a window containing injected anomaly data, or returning a value from a single sample as if it were a baseline, fails the spec. A second failure case: pooling channels into one per-sensor baseline, which hides single-channel deviations inside the spread of the others. Refs: FR-302, FR-301, FR-108, anom-001, anom-003, anom-007, scn-002, scn-005. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, after the baseline data was measured rather than assumed. Against the twenty completed normal-baseline runs in the development database: 100,800 RF readings over 56 sensor-channel cells (seven sensors, eight channels), 1,800 samples per cell, cell means spanning 0.177 dB from -95.081 to -94.904 dBm, and per-cell standard deviations from 1.437 to 1.551 dB. The cells are statistically indistinguishable on quiet data, and that has a consequence this item must state rather than let a mutation pass discover: its second failure case -- pooling channels into one per-sensor baseline, hiding single-channel deviations inside the spread of the others -- cannot be demonstrated against baseline runs, because there is no between-channel variation for a pooled baseline to hide anything inside. An implementation replacing per-cell baselines with a pooled one would survive every test built from the quiet grid, which is the same defect shape as the api-010 tests that could not fail: a test distinguishing A from B must be built from values occurring in only one of them. The granularity is justified structurally, not empirically on clean data. It is what makes anom-007's single-channel-against-broadband discrimination possible once something is injected, and the cells are uniform only because scn-001's baseline emitter is uniform by construction. Added constraint: the test proving per-channel granularity is built from staged runs, or from a constructed series in which cells genuinely differ, never from normal-baseline data alone. Added failure case: a per-channel claim proved only against quiet runs fails the spec, because such a test cannot tell the implementation apart from the pooled one the item forbids. Refs adds: anom-007, scn-001, api-010. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, on starting to build it. Scope narrows to RF metrics. The item asks for a baseline per metric per region for track metrics as well, and that half is not built: no region concept exists anywhere in the project, and nothing consumes a track baseline -- anom-001, anom-003 and anom-007 all read RF baselines, and anom-010's staleness threshold is configuration by its own text rather than a deviation from an average. Building it would mean inventing a region definition to satisfy a signature nothing calls, and picking that definition badly before a consumer exists to judge it. The engine is therefore written per cell rather than per sensor-and-channel, with the RF cell being sensor id and channel index, so the track half is a second cell extractor plus a region decision rather than a rewrite. This is recorded as a narrowing rather than done silently; the track half needs its own item when something wants it. Three further decisions. First, the engine cannot tell for itself which runs are quiet, because an observation carries no scenario type at all -- api-009 forbids it, and dal-001 gives the model nowhere to put one. So the caller supplies the run ids the baseline may draw from and the engine refuses any observation from outside that set, which turns 'derives from normal-scenario data only' from a convention the caller is trusted to honour into this item's first failure case, enforced where it can be tested. Second, the window is a trailing duration evaluated at a point: observations outside [end - window, end] do not contribute, and the end defaults to the newest observation supplied. That is what makes it a rolling average rather than an average, and what makes 'a window with insufficient samples' a real state rather than a description of an empty input. Third, the sample standard deviation is carried on the baseline beside the mean and a zero one is flagged rather than hidden, because anom-003's own failure case is a degenerate baseline dividing by zero and it reads the baseline from here. Refs adds: anom-010, dal-001, api-009, FR-303.

Z-score deviation detector. Input: a metric series, its baseline mean and standard deviation from anom-002, and a z threshold. Output: anomalies for points whose absolute z-score exceeds the threshold, each carrying the computed z and the rule ID. Constraints: the z value is stored on the anomaly for traceability but is never rendered to the analyst as a score, per ui-001. Failure case: a series with zero standard deviation must not divide by zero; it returns no anomalies and records the degenerate baseline. Refs: FR-301, ui-001, anom-002, evb-002.

Spatial clustering of track discontinuities. Input: track-continuity anomalies in a time window and a cluster radius. Output: clusters of discontinuities with a representative centroid and affected-area geometry, computed by the PostGIS query in db-004. Constraints: clustering is spatial and deterministic; isolated discontinuities outside the radius form no cluster. Failure case: two discontinuities separated by more than the radius must not be reported as one cluster. Refs: FR-301, FR-305, db-004, anom-005. Amended 2026-09-15, before tests, on measuring the question this item was written to answer. Two defects corrected and two decisions forced by measurement. First defect: the clustering query is db-009 and not db-004. This item said 'computed by the PostGIS query in db-004', which is the proximity query FR-905 names and describes; db-001's comment on its GiST index repeats the same error. db-009 was written when db-004 was picked up and found to describe a different query. Second defect: this item's constraint that 'isolated discontinuities outside the radius form no cluster' contradicts db-009, which returns a lone finding as a group of one deliberately, because anom-006 must know that a dropout happened alone -- a source that goes quiet by itself is an infrastructure problem rather than an incident. The constraint is replaced: an isolated discontinuity forms a group of one, and it is the consuming rule that decides what a group of one means. First decision, and the one that changes this item's purpose: the output is an intermediate finding and cluster size is never on its own reportable. Measured 2026-09-15 over eight seed-matched triples from the stored batch, the largest cluster a staged run produces is identical to the largest cluster in its own matched control in all eight, at every radius from 5 to 20 km; at 30 to 60 km the difference is 0.12 to 0.25 clusters, with one or two triples of eight differing at all. Findings per run are 15.9 on staged runs against 16.0 on controls. The control is an rf-sensor-fault run at the same seed, not a normal-baseline run: no normal-baseline run in the batch shares a seed with a staged one, so it replays a different stretch of corpus and would confound the injection with the traffic, while rf-sensor-fault shares seeds and perturbs nothing on the track side -- its ground truth records zero staged aircraft against 2 to 11 in each matched staged run. Clustering track gaps alone therefore provably cannot distinguish a staged run from its own control, and a rule reporting on cluster size would be reporting background. Second decision: the radius is a parameter and is explicitly not fitted. The measurement covers 5 to 60 km and the separation is between zero and 0.25 clusters across all of it, so no value is chosen because it worked; the default is set to the scale of a staged incident, whose zone radius is 60 km, and this measurement is recorded beside it. A radius selected by searching for one that made a control go green would be fitted to eight triples of one batch. Failure cases added. A cluster radius of zero or less is refused rather than answered, per db-009. A rule raising a reportable anomaly on cluster size alone fails this spec. And the count of clusters on quiet runs is recorded alongside the reportable count, per anom-008's amendment, because it is the number that moves first if the corpus or the generator changes underneath the detectors. Refs adds: db-009, anom-008, anom-010, anom-011, eval-002.

Fusion rule, rule ID FUSION-SPATIAL. Input: RF noise anomalies from anom-001 and track-gap clusters from anom-004. Output: an anomaly of type possible_interference_zone when both occur in the same simulated time window and within the configured distance, carrying references to both contributing anomalies. Constraints: both conditions are necessary; the window and distance are configuration. Failure case: RF noise and track gaps in the same area but in non-overlapping time windows must not raise this anomaly, and neither must a co-occurrence with only one of the two present. Refs: FR-305, US-A2, db-004, anom-001, anom-004, evb-001. Amended 2026-09-16, after measuring the track side's discriminating power. The input changes from anom-004's clusters to anom-012's local rate excess, and the reason is that cluster size carries no signal: over 20 seed-matched pairs the largest cluster on a staged run beats its own control in 1 to 3 pairs at every radius from 5 to 60 km. The failure this fixes is not sensitivity but attribution. As written, this rule fires when an RF anomaly has any co-located track cluster, and a background cluster sits within the fusion radius on 70 per cent of the runs whose truth is a sensor fault -- so it would claim most of anom-007's runs and, being mutually exclusive with anom-006 for the same cluster, take them from that rule too. The excess at a 30 km radius fires on 10 per cent of those controls. A further observation recorded here rather than acted on: the track side may not need to carry the sensor-fault discrimination at all, because anom-007 separates a fault from an environmental cause using the RF pattern alone -- one sensor abnormal with clean spatial neighbours -- which is a far stronger signal than any track evidence measured so far. If anom-007 claims those runs first, this rule's threshold can be set for sensitivity rather than for specificity, and the trade-off curve in anom-012 is read at a different point. That ordering is worth establishing before either threshold is fixed. Refs adds: anom-012, anom-007, anom-011. Amended 2026-09-17, after anom-013 was built, and the decision it records is that this rule does NOT gate on the rate excess. That reverses the original constraint that both conditions are necessary, and the reversal is measured rather than argued. Five decisions. First, the question the trade-off curve answers is not the question this rule faces. Every figure quoted for anom-012 -- 26 of 40 staged against 15 of 40 controls at 60 km -- was measured over all runs of each type. Under anom-013 this rule never sees most of them. Measured over the 120 runs of batches 2 and 3 plus the 20 quiet runs, the zones actually reaching this rule are 40 of 40 gnss-degradation, 0 of 40 aircraft-coverage-gap, 0 of 20 normal-baseline and 1 of 40 rf-sensor-fault -- and that single leaked fault carries a zero-length window, so it cannot be measured at all. The population arriving here is 40 true interference zones and one unmeasurable leak. A gate on the excess at the pre-registered threshold would report 26 of the 40 and reject nothing false, because in this corpus there is nothing false here to reject. Second, and this is the finding that settles it rather than merely supporting it: the 14 zones a gate would lose are not zones where the track evidence was weak. They are zones where there was almost no air traffic to observe. Every one of the 14 holds 4 or fewer track findings in the disc across the whole 900-second run -- five of them hold none at all during the window, two hold none anywhere -- while the distribution over the 40 has a median ratio of 3.87 and a 75th percentile of 11.47. The gate would therefore reject an interference report on the grounds of low traffic density in the affected zone, which is a property of where the incident was staged and not evidence about whether it happened. Losing a report backed by an 8 dB radio signal because few aircraft happened to be nearby is the same error this project has now recorded three times in a different costume. Third, the trigger is therefore the RF pattern alone: an anom-001 anomaly that anom-007 declined as environmental, which is by construction a deviation reaching more than one receiver. Mutual exclusion with anom-006 survives intact and becomes cleaner, because the discriminator between the two rules is now the presence or absence of a co-located RF anomaly -- the strong signal -- rather than a threshold on the weak one. anom-013 enforces it. Fourth, the threshold is not discarded; it is demoted from a gate to a confidence boundary, so nothing measured is wasted and the cost of the gate is avoided. Confidence is Low, Medium or High (ui-001) and it is three-valued in the same shape anom-007 uses, for the same reason: High where the excess reaches the threshold on a disc holding enough findings to measure a rate, Medium where it is measurably below, and the third band where the disc holds too little traffic for a rate to mean anything. That third band must not read as absent corroboration. A disc with one finding in it is not a disc that showed no disruption, exactly as a neighbour with no baseline is not a neighbour reading nominally, and this is the third distinct place in the detection layer where silence had to be separated from evidence of absence. The count floor separating the second band from the third is to be measured when this rule is built -- the arithmetic constraint is that anom-012's smoothing term must not dominate the measured rate -- and it is not fixed here from the fourteen values above, because choosing it from them would be choosing from the sample it will be scored against. Fifth, the limitation, stated because the measurement above cannot support the stronger claim. The corpus contains no scenario producing a multi-receiver RF anomaly that is not interference, so what is measured is that the gate has no opportunity to help here, not that it would never help. A deployment could see multi-receiver anomalies from weather, a distant emitter, or two receivers failing together. The decision stands regardless, because a gate whose benefit is unmeasurable and whose cost is measured at 14 of 40 cannot be justified on this evidence -- but if a corpus arm is ever generated that stages such a cause, the question is reopened with data rather than settled by this entry. Refs adds: anom-007, anom-012, anom-013, ui-001. Corrected 2026-09-17, later the same day, before tests, and the correction is to the fourth decision of the amendment above. That decision said the excess threshold should become the anomaly's confidence boundary. It should not, and the reason is the argument this item has just spent three measurements establishing: letting a signal with a Youden's J near 0.3 grade a claim an 8 dB deviation establishes is the same error as gating on it, softened. A zone with strong radio evidence and no aircraft nearby would be reported at low confidence, which understates it for exactly the reason a gate would have suppressed it. Four decisions replace it. First, the excess sets a corroboration state and not the confidence, and the state is three-valued and carried as its own field: corroborated where the excess reaches the threshold, not corroborated where it is measurably below, and not measurable where the disc cannot support a measurement. The distinction lives in the evidence, where an analyst can see which way it went and why, rather than being compressed into a single word. Second, the floor between the second and third state is that both the window and its complement must hold at least one finding, and the justification is arithmetic rather than fitted. anom-012 adds a smoothing term of one finding per run span to both rates. A period holding no findings therefore has a rate consisting of nothing but that constant, so the ratio is not a comparison of two observed rates and its value is a function of the period lengths. A disc with nothing in it during the window is not a disc that showed no disruption, on the same argument anom-001 makes for a cell it could not judge and anom-007 for a neighbour it could not measure. Third, confidence has a floor of Medium that the track side cannot breach, and is High only when corroborated. The floor is the radio evidence: by the time this rule fires, anom-007 has declined the zone as environmental, which means a deviation past threshold on more than one receiver, and that is beyond five sigma against a baseline spread of about 1.5 dB. The track side can raise the claim and cannot lower it. This rule therefore never emits Low, which is recorded here rather than left as an unreachable branch. Fourth, confidence is not taken from the radio side's own gradations, because measured they do not vary. Over the 40 zones reaching this rule, the zone spans 2 receivers in 34 and 3 in 6, and the peak deviation runs from 11.9 to 15.9 dB with a median of 13.4, which anom-001 grades Medium in 35 and High in 5. A confidence mapping on either quantity would be very nearly constant and would carry no information, which is worth recording as a property of the generator: scn-002 stages one incident of one size, so the corpus cannot exercise a severity gradation at this layer at all. The corroboration states measured over those 40 zones, at the chosen 60 km radius and the pre-registered threshold: corroborated 6, not corroborated 9, not measurable 25. Refs adds: anom-001, scn-002. Built 2026-09-18, and two things were found by running the ladder over the corpus that the unit tests could not have shown. First, one event was being reported once per receiver. An incident spanning two receivers has both dismissed as environmental, each naming the other, so one zone per dismissal describes the same event twice: measured, 160 interference zones from 60 staged runs. The dismissals are therefore merged into events before any zone is emitted, grouped on anom-007's own finding of which receivers deviated together rather than by measuring distance a second time here. Membership chains, as db-009's grouping does, so a deviation reaching three receivers is one event even where the outer two never name each other. After merging the corpus yields 61 zones from 60 staged runs and one leaked fault -- exactly one per event. This also makes anom-013's cross-rule-only suppression safe: the ladder will not merge two claims from one rule, deliberately, so the rule must not produce two for one event. A merged zone is centred between its receivers rather than on whichever was assessed first, because that centre is what anom-012's disc is measured around and taking one end would measure a patch offset from the event by half its width. The window is the union of its members'. Second, merging changed the corroboration figures, and the merged ones are the honest ones because they are per event rather than per receiver. Over the 61 zones: corroborated 7, not corroborated 7, not measurable 47. The per-receiver figures recorded above -- 6, 9 and 25 over 40 runs -- were taken before merging and are superseded rather than withdrawn, since they were correct for the question then being asked. The consequence for this item's central decision is that the case against a gate is far stronger than the measurement that settled it suggested. Gating on corroboration would report 7 of 60 staged interference runs, not 26 of 40: 47 of 61 zones cannot have their track side measured at all, because the disc holds no finding in one of the two periods. The track side is not a weak second vote on this corpus. It is absent in three quarters of the cases and confirms in about one in nine. The ladder end to end over all 240 runs, which anom-013 shipped without: 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault decided as possible_sensor_fault, 60 of 60 gnss-degradation as possible_interference_zone, 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence as a sensor fault by the design recorded on anom-007, 75 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap correctly silent and 19 of 20 normal-baseline correctly silent. The 6 of 100 false reports on runs staging nothing on the RF grid are anom-001's own false positive rate promoted one layer, already recorded on anom-007 and owned by anom-014. Five gnss-degradation runs and one rf-sensor-fault run carry a second anomaly of the other type in a different zone; that is not a precedence violation, because anom-013 guarantees at most one answer per zone and never per run, and a run may genuinely hold a broken receiver in one place and interference in another. Re-measured 2026-09-18 on the regenerated corpus, and the gating decision is unchanged while both sides of its argument moved. What reaches step three is now 60 of 60 gnss-degradation and 0 of every other arm -- the single rf-sensor-fault leak is gone, because anom-014 removed the spurious episode that produced it, so nothing false arrives here at all and a gate still has nothing to catch. The cost of gating fell sharply: the excess now clears the threshold on 58 of 60 rather than 26 of 40, with a median of 9.61 against 3.87, and there are no unusable windows where there were seven. So a gate would now lose 2 runs rather than 14. The decision stands on the same reasoning it was made on -- an unmeasurable benefit against a measured cost -- and it is worth recording that the cost falling by a factor of seven does not change a benefit that is still zero. Corroboration also improved and remains the honest limitation: 18 of 60 zones corroborated against 7 of 61, 1 not corroborated against 7, and 41 of 60 still NOT MEASURABLE against 47 of 61. Two thirds of reported zones continue to have no measurable track side, so any claim about fusion must still be stated as the radio evidence with an occasional corroborating note.

Data-source issue rule, rule ID SOURCE-GAP. Input: track dropout clusters and the set of RF anomalies for the same window and area. Output: an anomaly of type possible_data_source_issue when dropouts are present and no co-located RF anomaly exists. Constraints: this rule is the discriminator that keeps a coverage gap from being reported as interference; it is mutually exclusive with anom-005 for the same cluster. Failure case: an aircraft-coverage-gap scenario producing possible_interference_zone instead of possible_data_source_issue fails the spec. Refs: FR-306, scn-002, anom-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Amended 2026-09-17, after measuring what this rule would have to detect, and the amendment records that it is NOT built and why. Six findings, in the order they were taken. First, the defensive half of this item's job is already done, by anom-013 rather than by anything here. The item's stated purpose is to be the discriminator that keeps a coverage gap from being reported as interference. Measured over 240 runs, 0 of 40 aircraft-coverage-gap runs reach anom-005 at all, because that type stages nothing on the RF grid and anom-005's trigger is an RF anomaly. The misattribution this rule exists to prevent can no longer occur, and it is prevented by the absence of a strong signal rather than by the presence of a weak one. What remains for this item is the positive claim: saying we are not hearing aircraft here when that is true. Second, that positive claim cannot be made on the current corpus, and the reason is the open question already recorded on scn-006 rather than anything about this rule. Since that fix a coverage-gap run stages a mean of 1.7 aircraft and 11 of 40 stage none at all, so a quarter of the arm has an empty answer key and is by construction indistinguishable from its control. Third, the effect that remains is real and unmistakable and far too small to act on. Over 40 seed-matched pairs against rf-sensor-fault controls -- same seed, same corpus window, same aircraft, nothing staged on tracks in 40 of 40 -- a coverage-gap run holds a mean of 16.1 track-gap findings against its control's 15.1, and never fewer: 23 pairs strictly greater, 17 tied, 0 lower. Zero discordant losses in 40 pairs is overwhelming evidence that the effect exists. It is also one finding in fifteen, and a detector sees one run without its control, so it cannot tell 16 from 15. Fourth, the zone-level design does not rescue it; it makes matters worse. Proposing zones by clustering the findings (anom-004) and scoring each by anom-012's rate excess, then taking the strongest zone per run, gives staged against control of 7 to 3 at a 20 km cluster radius, 5 to 4 at 40 km and 4 to 2 at 60 km, with the remainder tied. That is chance. The machinery destroys a signal that raw counting preserves, and the mechanism is visible in anom-005's measurement: a ratio taken over a disc holding one to three findings is dominated by anom-012's smoothing term, so taking the maximum across zones selects for small-sample noise rather than for effect. Fifth, building it as specified would be actively wrong rather than merely weak. The rule as written fires when dropouts are present and no co-located RF anomaly exists; a quiet run genuinely holds about 15 findings and no RF anomaly, so the rule would fire on every normal-baseline run in the corpus and destroy anom-008's zero-anomalies control. A discrimination threshold is therefore mandatory, and the measurements above say no threshold on the available quantities separates the arm from its control. Sixth, what unblocks it is a generator change and not a detector one, which is scn-007. This item stays specified and unbuilt until a corpus exists in which a coverage gap is a zone-level event, and the measurement above is then repeated before any threshold here is chosen. Recorded as a threat to validity in the meantime: the detection layer currently has no rule for the aircraft-coverage-gap arm, so that arm contributes only correct non-detections to eval-002 and must not be reported as though the system had been tested on it. Refs adds: anom-012, anom-013, scn-006, scn-007, eval-002. Re-opened 2026-09-18 on the regenerated corpus, and the reason is measurement rather than optimism. The item was closed as unbuildable on two findings: a run-level excess of one finding in fifteen, and zone-level scoring at chance (7:3, 5:4, 4:2 at 20/40/60 km cluster radii). With scn-007 putting a floor of five staged aircraft under every run, both were re-measured over 60 seed-matched pairs. The run-level picture is better and still not usable: 16.9 findings against the control's 14.2, 57 of 60 pairs won with 3 ties and 0 losses, and detected staged dropouts up from 1.07 to 3.05 per run -- but the excess of 2.7 sits against a control spread of 3.3, so it is 0.8 of a standard deviation and a detector seeing one run without its control still cannot tell 17 from 14. That was predicted on this item before the regeneration and the prediction held. The zone-level picture is the one that changed: 20 wins to 7 losses at 20 km, 14 to 8 at 40 km, 10 to 5 at 60 km, where every radius was previously indistinguishable from a coin. At 20 km, 20 against 7 discordant pairs is about one in fifty by sign test. That is a real signal in the machinery this rule would actually use, and it exists because five staged aircraft put enough co-located dropouts in one place for a cluster to form where 1.7 could not. The item is therefore buildable to try, NOT known to be buildable: a sign test on discordant pairs says the staged zone tends to beat its control, and says nothing about whether a threshold exists that separates them on a single run, which is the question a detector faces and which needs its own measurement before any threshold is chosen. Build it against that measurement, not against these figures. Refs: scn-007, anom-004, anom-012, anom-008, eval-002. Closed again 2026-09-18, on the threshold measurement this item asked for, and the item is now closed on a stronger basis than the first closure. The re-opening rested on a sign test over matched pairs (20 wins to 7 at a 20 km cluster radius) and recorded that it said nothing about whether a fixed threshold separates a staged zone from an unstaged one on a single run. That measurement has been taken, pre-registered in measurements/corpus/source_gap_threshold_prereg.md with its populations, its operating-point rule and its failure bar fixed in advance, and scored on a held-out base seed the threshold was not chosen on. Five findings. First, the answer is no: the best development operating point leaving anom-008's quiet arm silent is a 60 km cluster radius, a minimum zone size of four findings and an excess threshold of 11.53, giving 7 of 40 coverage gaps caught, and the held-out seed gives 3 of 20 with zero quiet-arm alarms. 0.15 against a pre-registered bar of 0.25. Second, and this is the finding that closes the item rather than merely failing it, the rule points the wrong way: at that operating point it fires on 6 of 20 gnss-degradation runs against 3 of 20 coverage gaps, twice as often on the arm it is not for as on the arm it is. anom-013 orders SENSOR-FAULT, SOURCE-GAP, FUSION-SPATIAL, so SOURCE-GAP outranks the interference rule and a firing there can take the zone before FUSION-SPATIAL is offered it. Building this rule would put the one arm the ladder gets right 60 of 60 at risk to catch a seventh of an arm it currently ignores. Whether those zones actually overlap is not measured, so the hazard is established and its size is not. Third, the ceiling is low everywhere and not merely at the zero-false-alarm constraint: the best Youden's J anywhere on the development sweep is 0.275, at a 0.38 quiet-arm rate anom-008 forbids outright, and anom-012 reported 0.23 to 0.40 on a curve this project already calls weak. Fourth, the mechanism is visible and is the one predicted when the item was first closed. The statistic saturates: at a size floor of one every arm reaches the same maximum ratio of 198.78 and the medians differ by 0.6, because taking the maximum across zones selects the noisiest small sample and every run has one. Separation appears only at a size floor of four or more, by which point the qualifying population has fallen to about two thirds of runs. Fifth, a population correction that outlives this item: ambiguous-mixed-evidence shares aircraft-coverage-gap's SUPPRESS mode and rf-sensor-fault perturbs tracks not at all, so at a shared seed the first pair and the second pair produce identical track findings, verified exactly. Any track-side figure quoting 120 negatives or treating the ambiguous arm as independent evidence is counting 60 seeds twice. The out-of-sample agreement was good, 0.17 development against 0.15 holdout, so this is a reliable measurement of a weak effect rather than a noisy one, and repeating it on more runs of the same corpus will not change it. What would change it is a generator change, as the first closure also concluded: a coverage gap must become a zone-level event distinguishable from a frozen one. The threat to validity recorded against eval-002 therefore stands unchanged and is now the settled position rather than a pending question: the detection layer has no rule for the aircraft-coverage-gap arm, its 60 of 60 correct non-detections are correct only because nothing judges that arm, and it must not be reported as though the system had been tested on it. Options not taken, recorded 2026-09-18 so the closure states what was declined and why rather than only what failed. Five were available and none is impossible. First, build it at a more sensitive operating point and accept the false alarms: declined because it breaks anom-008, a passing item, and because the arm it would falsely fire on is the one the ladder currently decides correctly 60 of 60, so a rule with an adverse likelihood ratio is worse than no rule. Second, build it as this item originally specified, firing on dropouts wherever no co-located RF anomaly exists: declined on the first closure's own measurement, since a quiet run genuinely holds about 15 discontinuities and no RF anomaly, so the rule fires on every baseline run. The RF side is a veto and not a discriminator. Third, change the statistic, summing or counting qualifying zones rather than taking the maximum: both ends of that family have now been measured and both fail, the run-level aggregate at 0.8 standard deviations and the zone-level maximum here, but intermediate forms were not tried and this is the cheapest untried option. Fourth, raise the staged fraction so a gap removes most aircraft in an area: possible with a mean eligible pool of 23.4, and declined because it changes what the scenario means -- removing most aircraft over a region is an outage rather than a coverage gap, and an easier problem than the one scoped -- and because it needs a third corpus generation that would invalidate every detection figure measured on v2. Fifth, change the generator so a coverage gap is a zone-level event by construction, suppressing a contiguous area rather than a selected set of aircraft: this is the option both closures identify as the one that would actually work, and it is declined on cost rather than on merit, needing a third regeneration, a re-measurement of the whole detection chapter and a re-derivation of scn-007's floor. Recorded as future work. Consequence for the corpus, and it is not confined to this item: with this rule absent, ambiguous-mixed-evidence and rf-sensor-fault are indistinguishable in the detection layer's reportable output, both decided possible_sensor_fault on all 60 runs. tracks.py gives the ambiguous arm the same SUPPRESS mode as the coverage-gap arm, so their track findings are identical at a shared seed, and fusion.py consumes only anom-007's environmental verdict, so on a single-receiver run that track evidence never reaches a claim. The arm built to present anom-013 with conflicting evidence therefore cannot produce a second bid. See anom-013 and eval-002, both amended with this.

Sensor fault rule, rule ID SENSOR-FAULT. Input: an RF sensor reporting abnormal readings, the readings of its spatial neighbours in the same window, and the readings of the frequency-adjacent channels on the sensor itself. Output: an anomaly of type possible_sensor_fault when the sensor is abnormal and its spatial neighbours are nominal, with the frequency-adjacency test recorded as a distinct piece of evidence rather than folded into the spatial one. Constraints: spatial neighbour selection is a spatial query with a configured radius, not a hard-coded sensor list; frequency neighbour selection is the adjacent channel indices on the same sensor. A real emission raises adjacent channels together, so an isolated single-channel deviation with clean neighbours is evidence about the sensor rather than the environment. Failure case: several adjacent sensors all reporting abnormal readings must not raise a sensor-fault anomaly, since that pattern indicates an environmental cause. A second failure case: a deviation spanning all eight channels on one sensor being reported with the same confidence as a single-channel one, since the broadband pattern is weaker evidence of a fault. Refs: FR-307, FR-108, scn-002, scn-005, db-004, anom-001, anom-002. Amended 2026-09-17, before implementation, after reading the layout and the threshold rule this consumes. Eight decisions. First, the input is anom-001's whole result and not only its anomalies. That rule reports the cells it could not judge alongside the ones it could, and this is the first consumer that would otherwise read that silence as cleanliness: a neighbour reporting nothing because it had no usable baseline is not a neighbour reporting nominal. The verdict is therefore three-valued rather than two -- a neighbour with an overlapping anomaly settles it as environmental, neighbours all judged and all clean settles it as a fault, and neighbours clean with any cell unjudged is recorded as undecided with the reason rather than as a fault. Positive evidence of an environmental cause outranks missing data, and missing data outranks inferring that nothing seen means nothing happened. Second, neighbour selection is by great-circle distance from the layout at a configured radius, defaulting to the layout's own discrimination radius, which scn-005 already validates as leaving every sensor at least one neighbour inside it and at least one beyond. A sensor with no neighbour inside the configured radius compares against nothing, and the vacuous case -- no neighbours, therefore no abnormal neighbours, therefore a fault -- would turn every RF anomaly in the layout into a sensor fault. That case is refused and recorded as undecided, which is this item's third failure case. Third, the unit of judgement is one sensor over one merged window and not one cell episode. A fault is a property of a receiver; per-episode output would report one broken box once per affected channel and leave any count of sensor faults reading as eight. Fourth, confidence is Low, Medium or High (ui-001) and it qualifies the attribution rather than the deviation. The size of the deviation is already carried by anom-001 as a severity, and the two are different quantities: how far past normal a reading went, against how strongly the pattern implicates the instrument. High is a single channel with both frequency neighbours clean; Medium is a deviation across some but not all of the plan; Low is every channel on the sensor, which is this item's second failure case -- a broadband elevation on one receiver is also what a wideband emitter parked beside it would produce. Fifth, the frequency-adjacency test is carried as its own field with its own list of the channels checked, not folded into the spatial verdict, because the two are evidence of different kinds and an analyst reading the bundle needs to see which one carries the argument. Sixth, episode overlap is inclusive at both endpoints. An anom-001 episode's end is its last exceeding reading rather than the first quiet one, so a neighbour whose episode ends on the tick this one starts genuinely overlapped it by one reading, and a strict comparison would call that neighbour clean. Seventh, this rule consults no track evidence, enforced by what it can be handed rather than by remembering not to: its input carries RF findings and a layout and has nowhere to put a track finding. anom-013 places it first for that reason, and the enforcement is what makes the ordering a property of the types rather than of the caller. Eighth, one thing this item cannot measure, stated rather than left silent: all 240 stored runs are narrowband, so the Low band exists in unit tests and has no corpus behind it. A broadband arm is a separate generation item, and the confidence ordering must not be quoted as measured until it exists. The measurement this item owes, and the reason it is built before anom-012's radius is fixed: anom-013's ordering assumes this rule claims the runs whose truth is a sensor fault, and that assumption is untested. To be recorded here once measured -- the catch rate over the 60 rf-sensor-fault runs, the false-fire rate over the 60 gnss-degradation and 20 normal-baseline runs, and separately the rate over the 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence runs, which stage a single sensor by construction and which this rule is therefore expected to claim. That last is a property of the scenario design rather than a defect in the rule, and it is reported rather than excluded. Refs adds: anom-013, anom-008, anom-012, ui-001, docs/phase8_detection.md. Corrected 2026-09-17, by the measurement this item owed, and the correction is a reversal of the first decision of the amendment above. Measured over 240 stored runs with the baseline built from the 20 quiet ones: the rule claims 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault runs, on the staged receiver and inside the staged window, which is the assumption anom-013 rests on and it holds without qualification. It also claimed 21 of 60 gnss-degradation runs on a staged receiver inside the staged window, which is a misattribution of the same class as the one anom-013 was written to remove, in the opposite direction. The cause is not the neighbour radius and not the layout. The injected elevation is 8 dB scaled per cell per tick by 1 + 0.25 of a standard normal draw, and anom-001's threshold is 6 dB, so about one tick in six falls short and ends the episode: a staged cell emits a median of six episodes where the incident is one. Two receivers loud through the same 300 s can therefore have fragments that never overlap, and each reads as isolated from the other. The defect is in reading the neighbour's nominality off another rule's episodes rather than off its readings, which is what the item asked for in its original wording -- the readings of its spatial neighbours in the same window -- and what the amendment above replaced with anom-001's findings. The original wording was right. The input is therefore the run's RF observations and the anom-002 baseline table alongside anom-001's findings: the findings say which of the subject's cells are abnormal and which cells nobody could judge, and the readings say whether a neighbour was nominal. Measured, over the 120 staged runs: a neighbour the incident also touched sits 2.51 dB above its own baseline at the 5th percentile and 4.46 dB at the median during a window this rule was about to call a fault, while a neighbour the incident did not touch sits at -0.05 dB at the median and 1.58 dB at the 95th. The populations separate, and a bar of 2 dB in the gap between them removes all 21 misattributions while leaving all 60 catches intact. The neighbouring bars are reported with it rather than only the chosen one: 1.0 and 1.5 dB also give 0 of 60, 3.0 dB gives 5 and 4.0 dB gives 7, so the choice sits on a plateau and not on a cliff, and the bar is a policy field with a measured default rather than a literal. The rejected alternative is recorded because it also works on this corpus and is cheaper: treating a neighbour episode within 30 s of the window as overlapping it gives 0 of 60 and 60 of 60 as well. It is rejected because it answers a different question -- whether the neighbour was anomalous recently, rather than whether it was nominal now -- and because it only works while the neighbour crosses anom-001's threshold somewhere nearby. The 8 dB elevation is the generator's choice, not a property of interference; a weaker emitter, or a neighbour further out, raises a neighbour by 3 or 4 dB and produces no episode at any tolerance, and the tolerance form would then read it as nominal for ever. The readings form sees it directly. Measured in support: of the 37 staged-neighbour measurements above, none exceeded anom-001's 6 dB threshold during the window in question, so every one of them was invisible to a test built on episodes. Consequences recorded rather than deferred. Nominality is judged in the direction the metric chooses -- power upwards, SNR downwards -- derived from the baseline table's own metric rather than configured, because a direction a caller can set wrongly is a silent wrong answer. A neighbour with no baseline or no readings in the window cannot be measured and is undecided, which is the same three-valued verdict as before with a more direct reason. A track observation handed in among the RF ones is refused rather than skipped, on anom-001's argument, which is also what keeps the no-track-evidence guarantee structural now that the rule takes observations at all. Two further results from the same measurement, neither of them about the neighbour test. First, anom-001 raises at least one anomaly on 13 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap runs and 1 of 20 normal-baseline runs, all of which stage nothing on the RF grid, and this rule promotes every one of them to a sensor fault at High confidence. Those 14 fires are all single-channel episodes of 20 s or less, which is anom-001's false-positive rate surfacing one layer up rather than a defect here; the rule has no minimum duration and a one-tick blip is not evidence about an instrument. A minimum-duration constraint belongs to anom-001 and is left to a separate item rather than patched here. Second, the rule claims 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence runs, at High confidence, with no trace of ambiguity in the output -- which follows from that type staging a single receiver by construction and from anom-013 offering a claimed zone to no later rule. That is a property of the scenario design meeting the ordering, it is reported rather than excluded, and it is a threat to the validity of any evaluation that treats the ambiguous type as a test of whether the system can express uncertainty. Re-measured 2026-09-17 on the rebuilt rule, same 240 runs, same baseline and same anom-001 policy, the only change being that nominality is read from the neighbours' readings. The rule claims 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault runs on the staged receiver inside the staged window, and 0 of 60 gnss-degradation runs, against 21 of 60 before. The window it reports now recovers the incident rather than a fragment of it: a median of 300 s against a staged duration of 300 s, where the episode-based version gave a median of 20 s, and the number of faults raised per sensor-fault run falls from about five to 1.13. The extension overruns slightly at the top -- 390 s at the maximum -- because a tick either side of the incident can still read above the 2 dB bar on ordinary noise, which is the cost of a bar set low enough to keep the window contiguous and is recorded rather than trimmed. Two residual behaviours, both reported rather than suppressed. Runs that stage nothing on the RF grid still raise a fault on 6 of 100 of them (5 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap and 1 of 20 normal-baseline), down from 14 of 100: these are anom-001 false positives promoted one layer up, and the residue survives because a short episode can still sustain a 2 dB mean across its own window. A minimum-duration constraint belongs to anom-001 and is left to a separate item. And the rule still claims 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence runs at High confidence, for the reason recorded above: that type stages a single receiver by construction. The new refusal this rebuild added, which is what removed most of the false positives: an episode whose window the readings do not sustain -- the receiver sitting inside the bar of its own baseline across the whole window anom-001's episode seeds -- is undecided rather than a fault, because a threshold crossing that the window does not bear out is not evidence about an instrument. It accounts for the undecided dismissals in the measurement: 8 on coverage-gap runs, 3 on gnss-degradation, 3 on rf-sensor-fault, 1 on ambiguous.

Correct non-detection on a normal-baseline run. Input: a completed normal-baseline scenario run with no injected deviation. Output: zero anomalies of any type. Constraints: this is a required positive behaviour of the detection engine, not an absence of behaviour; it is asserted for every detector, not only in aggregate. Failure case: any anomaly raised on a clean run fails the spec, because the false-positive rate reported in eval-002 becomes meaningless if the engine is noisy on clean data. Refs: FR-308, US-R5, AC-04, scn-002, eval-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 14. Amended 2026-09-14, before any detector was written against it, on measuring the corpus. The constraint that a normal-baseline run produces zero anomalies of any type is scoped here to the reportable ones -- the fused rules an analyst is actually shown, being anom-005's possible_interference_zone, anom-006's possible_data_source_issue and anom-007's possible_sensor_fault. It does not count the intermediate findings those rules consume. The measurement that forces this: a quiet run contains roughly 138 aircraft, of about 530 seen, whose reported position staleness exceeds 100 s, and about 8 intervals between consecutive reports exceeding 100 s before filtering. Those are real properties of real replayed data, not defects in the detector and not artefacts of the pipeline, and a rule requiring the track detector to emit zero of them would be requiring it to be wrong. Read the other way, the unamended constraint would be satisfiable only by a detector that failed to notice genuine discontinuities in its input. The control's purpose is unchanged and is what the scoping protects: on a run with nothing staged, nothing reaches the analyst, and the false-positive rate in eval-002 is computed from that. Two obligations are added rather than dropped. The rate of intermediate findings on quiet runs is recorded alongside the reportable count, because it is the number that would move if the corpus or the generator changed underneath the detectors and nothing else would show it. And the assertion stays per detector rather than in aggregate, as this item already requires -- for an intermediate producer the assertion is that its findings are within the recorded background rather than that there are none. Failure cases amended. A reportable anomaly of any of the three fused types raised on a clean run still fails the spec, unchanged. A detector reporting zero intermediate findings on a quiet run now also fails it, because the corpus is known to contain them and silence means the detector did not look. Recorded as a threat to validity: this scoping makes the false-positive rate a statement about the fused layer only, and a reader could mistake it for a statement about detection as a whole. The evaluation reports both numbers for that reason. Refs adds: anom-010, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, dal-001. Refined 2026-09-29, before writing tests, on reading the rules this control has to grade. Five changes, four of them found by reading. First, the register of producers is a constant keyed on the (rule_id, finding_type) pair ai-001 defines, and a producer not in it is refused rather than skipped. Rule id alone does not identify: anom-012 borrows anom-010's rule id, so a rate excess and a continuity gap are the same key by rule id while making different claims -- the collision ai-008 resolves on and eval-007 groups on. Second, the control takes an account of every registered producer and refuses a run where one is absent, rather than grading whatever it was given. This is the mechanism behind this item's own 'silence means the detector did not look', generalised: on the reportable side zero is the required answer, so an empty input and a correct run are indistinguishable by counting, and a control that passes when nothing ran is not a control. A registered producer missing from the account is refused and an unregistered one supplied is refused; both are caller errors rather than run properties, so both raise instead of returning a verdict. Third, 'zero fails' is carried by the measured band and is not asserted for every intermediate producer. The amendment of 2026-09-14 justified the non-zero requirement entirely from replayed track data, and it does not hold on the RF side: the RF grid is synthetic, a quiet run has nothing injected into it, and anom-014 measured anom-001 raising at least one episode on only 14 of 100 unstaged runs. A blanket non-zero rule would therefore fail about 86 per cent of quiet runs for being right. The band's lower bound is measured per producer instead, so the track side's silence fails because its measured floor is above zero and the RF side's passes because its measured floor is zero, and neither is a special case. Fourth, a registered producer with no implementation is reported as not exercised and never as clean. anom-006 has no rule: it was attempted twice, measured, and closed on the corpus as generated. A control reporting zero possible_data_source_issue across forty quiet runs would be quoting the absence of a rule as the accuracy of one. The false-positive figure eval-002 takes from here therefore states how many reportable types it actually covers, being two of three, since read as three it overstates the layer's coverage by exactly the rule that does not exist. Fifth, the input is a declared normal-baseline run and nothing else. A run of a staged type that staged nothing is eval-002's exclusion, counted and reported there, and is not a quiet run for this control -- the two are different facts, and folding them together would put a run the generator failed on into a figure about the detectors. Recorded as a threat to validity, in addition to the one already here: the background band is measured on the quiet runs of this corpus and applied to them, so it cannot fail on the data that produced it. It is a drift tripwire for a later corpus or a changed generator, which is the purpose this item already states for it, and not an independent test of the present figures. The band is the minimum and maximum observed over the runs it was measured on, with n recorded beside it, so a new run from the same distribution falls outside it at roughly 2/(n+1). Failure cases added: a control returning a verdict for a run in which a registered producer was not accounted for fails the spec; a producer reported as clean whose rule has no implementation fails it; and a false-positive figure quoted without the count of reportable types it covers fails it. Refs adds: anom-001, anom-004, anom-012, anom-014, ai-001, ai-008, eval-007.

Detection latency measurement. Input: an anomaly and its scenario run ground truth. Output: latency as the simulated-time delta between injected event onset and anomaly emission. Constraints: simulated scenario time only, never wall clock; the definition is fixed before any measurement code exists, per the Track 0 item in docs/implementation.md; the unit is recorded alongside the value. Failure case: a latency that changes when the same run is replayed on faster hardware fails the spec, because it proves wall-clock time leaked in. Refs: FR-309, FR-1002, NFR-601, scn-001, eval-002. DEFINITION FIXED 2026-09-28, closing the Track 0 item in docs/implementation.md, and before any measurement code exists as that item requires. **Detection latency is the simulated-time interval from the ground-truth onset of a staged incident to the earliest simulated instant at which every piece of evidence the claiming rule requires was available.** The obvious definition -- when the detector noticed, minus when it began -- has no second term in this system, and that is the whole difficulty: detection is batch. The rules read a completed run from the store; there is no instant at which a rule 'emits'. Written without settling this, the measurement would have reached for whichever timestamp was nearest, produced a plausible number, and measured nothing -- and the nearest one is evidence_bundles.created_at, which is wall clock in disguise and is precisely the failure case this item already names. What is real is how much of an incident must elapse before the evidence a rule demands is complete. That is a property of the rule's design rather than of its implementation, it is the same quantity a streaming version would face, and it is therefore the right figure for a thesis about deterministic rules -- provided it is never described as how fast the software is. Four rejected alternatives, recorded because each is defensible until examined. The start of the claimed window minus onset measures how well a rule **reconstructs** a window, is frequently zero or negative since anom-007 takes its window from the readings, and is worth reporting separately as window reconstruction error rather than as latency. The first cited observation minus onset is approximately zero by construction, since the first deviating reading is usually the first reading after onset, and would report instant detection truly and vacuously. Wall clock is forbidden by this item and by NFR-601. A stored row's created_at is wall clock wearing a simulated-time costume. CONSEQUENCES, all four load-bearing on how the figure may be reported. (1) The value is **quantised to the run's sampling interval**, 10 s on this corpus, so the smallest non-zero latency representable is 10 s and no single measurement may carry sub-interval precision; the interval is reported beside the figure. (2) A rule's minimum evidence requirement **is** its latency floor: anom-014's 10 s minimum episode duration contributes 10 s by construction, which is a measured cost of that threshold and not an artefact to subtract out. (3) The value is **signed and never clamped**: a negative latency means the rule's evidence begins before the staged onset, which is evidence it swept in readings from outside the incident, and clamping to zero would hide exactly the defect worth finding. (4) It is **per reported claim and not per run**, matched to its staged incident by subject, since anom-013 gives one event one zone and a run may stage two; an incident that was never reported has no latency, is excluded, and the exclusions are counted in the report on eval-002's own rule. IMPLEMENTATION CONSEQUENCE: the decidable instant is **declared by the rule that made the claim** rather than reconstructed by a measurement script, because each rule knows what evidence it required -- an episode reaching its minimum duration, a neighbour reading measured nominal, a second receiver's episode overlapping the first -- and a script inferring it from stored output would be a right number about the wrong object, which is the defect ai-004's payload module exists because of. Failure case added: a latency figure reported without its sampling interval, or with negative values clamped, or without the count of unreported incidents excluded, fails the spec. Refs adds: anom-001, anom-007, anom-013, anom-014, eval-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5. DESIGN REFINED 2026-09-28, on reading the rules before writing the tests, and the refinement is to *where* the decidable instant is declared rather than to what it means. The fixed definition above says the claiming rule declares it. Two facts about the built rules make a field computed at construction the wrong shape. First, **the rules do not retain the evidence they rest on**: a SensorFault carries which neighbours were asked and how far each sat from its baseline, and an InterferenceZone carries a rate excess and a corroboration verdict -- derived evidence, deliberately, because these objects carry conclusions rather than readings. Neither holds the anom-001 episodes underneath, so neither can compute when its evidence became sufficient without three dataclasses starting to carry raw readings they were built not to carry. Second, and the fact that makes this more than a plumbing question, **anom-005's zone window is the union of its receivers' windows** -- min of the starts to max of the ends -- so `window start + minimum duration` is correct for anom-007 and **wrong** for anom-005: at the union's start only the first receiver has begun, while the rule's whole claim is that more than one deviated together, so it cannot commit until the *second* receiver's evidence is sufficient. One formula for both rules would have understated interference latency by however long the receivers were staggered, silently and plausibly. So the declaration is a **registry keyed on rule id** stating how many receivers' evidence that rule requires -- one for anom-007, two for anom-005 -- and the decidable instant is the nth earliest qualification among the contributing receivers, where a receiver qualifies at its first episode's start plus the minimum episode duration. A rule with no entry is **refused**, never defaulted, which is anom-013's own rule that a claim whose rule has no declared position is refused rather than appended; a default would silently measure a new rule as though it needed one receiver. The minimum duration is **imported from anom-014's own module** and never retyped, because two copies of a threshold drift and the drift would move every latency figure at once. Failure case added: a claim whose rule has no declared receiver requirement is refused. Failure case added: a claim with fewer contributing receivers than its rule requires is refused rather than measured, since the evidence the rule says it needs was never present and a number computed anyway would describe nothing.

Track continuity rule, rule ID TRACK-GAP. Input: aircraft position observations for one scenario run, a staleness threshold, and the run's simulated time window. Output: a track_continuity_gap anomaly per affected aircraft, carrying the gap's onset and end in simulated time, its duration, the last known position as the anomaly's location, and the observation IDs either side of the gap. Constraints: staleness is the simulated-time interval between consecutive reports for one pseudonymised aircraft, never wall clock, consistent with anom-009; the threshold is configuration, not a literal in the rule; the rule is deterministic, so the same observations always give the same anomalies. Failure cases: an aircraft whose last report is the final one before the run window closes must raise nothing, since every track still in flight is stale at the end of every window and a rule that fires there fires on all of them at once; an aircraft that leaves the bounding box or lands must raise nothing, because ceasing to report is correct behaviour in both cases and neither is a discontinuity; and a gap one interval below threshold must raise nothing while one interval above raises exactly one. Refs: FR-304, FR-301, FR-306, adp-001, adp-004, anom-002, anom-004, anom-006, anom-008, db-004, scn-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3.
