Written 2026-09-14, on picking up Phase 8, because FR-304 had no spec item at all. Nine anom items covered eight of the nine detection requirements; anom-004 clusters track-continuity anomalies and anom-006 consumes track dropout clusters, and nothing in the backlog produced one. The rule the fusion pair is built on was the one rule nobody had written down. Two decisions. First, the unit is the gap rather than the aircraft: one anomaly per discontinuity, not one per stale track, because anom-004 clusters discontinuities by location and an aircraft with two gaps in different places is two pieces of spatial evidence rather than one. Second, and the reason this item cannot be written as a bare threshold: the corpus contains genuine dropouts, and normal-baseline replays the corpus. The coverage acceptance check of 2026-08-19 measured 10 of 948 tracks (1.05 per cent) carrying a genuine interior airborne dropout, with seven of the ten falling in the 100-300 s band that scenario type 4 injects into. A staleness rule over a normal-baseline run will therefore fire on real corpus gaps, and anom-008 requires that run to raise zero anomalies of any type. The conflict is settled here rather than discovered as a failing anom-008 test. Raising the threshold above 300 s is rejected: it would blind the detector to exactly the band the injected gaps occupy, buying a clean false-positive rate by disabling the measurement it is the control for. Relaxing anom-008 to anomalies attributable to injection is rejected: FR-308 makes correct non-detection a required behaviour, and a control that permits known firings is not a control. The accepted answer is the exclusion already owed by the Track 0 residue -- the generator refuses the ten identified tracks as corpus-window content, using the coverage report to identify them -- extended from injection sites, where it was owed, to baseline windows, where it is equally needed and was not previously noticed. Added failure case: a normal-baseline run raising a track_continuity_gap from a genuine corpus dropout fails this item as well as anom-008, because it means the exclusion was not applied. Recorded limitation: the exclusion removes real data to make a false-positive rate measurable, so the reported rate is conditional on it, and the measured rate with and without the exclusion is owed to the evaluation. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, after measuring the corpus rather than reasoning about it. The corpus-dropout decision written into this item that morning was wrong by about two orders of magnitude and is corrected here rather than quietly replaced. It assumed the ten tracks adp-008 names were the whole false-positive problem. Measured across the twenty normal-baseline runs in the development database, the background is this: of roughly 530 aircraft seen per run, 137.7 reach a peak reported position staleness above 100 s, 19.3 above 300 s, and 1.0 above 600 s. The equivalent gnss-degradation figures are 141.1, 20.7 and 0.6 -- so the staged signature is about 3.4 aircraft per run against a background of 137.7, and above 600 s the quiet runs are higher than the staged ones. No threshold separates them at any value. The cause is not a tuning error: the injection stages disruptions of 100-300 s because that is what a plausible real coverage failure looks like, and it is also what a real one is, so the staged effect was designed into the densest part of the distribution it has to be told apart from. Five decisions follow. First, this item's output is an intermediate finding and not a reportable anomaly. It is computed for anom-004 to cluster and is never shown to an analyst, for the reason anom-008 is amended alongside: a quiet run genuinely contains of the order of 138 track discontinuities that are real properties of real data, so a control requiring zero of them would require the detector to be wrong. What the rule detects is staleness; what it cannot do is attribute it, and attribution is spatial and cross-modal by design -- the background gaps are scattered across 309,000 square kilometres while a staged one sits inside a zone about 20 km across with a raised noise floor over it. Second, there are two detection mechanisms because the two scenario types stage differently, and a rule with only one of them is blind to one type. gnss-degradation rewrites the reported position staleness and the rows keep arriving; aircraft-coverage-gap suppresses the rows entirely, so nothing arrives to read a field from. The rule therefore reports a frozen_position finding from a reading whose position staleness exceeds the threshold, and a not_heard finding from an interval between consecutive reports of one aircraft that exceeds it. The shape is carried on the finding, because it is exactly what anom-005 and anom-006 need to tell interference from a data-source failure. Third, the frozen_position mechanism additionally requires contact to be fresh, and this is a measured decision rather than a tidy one. Requiring fresh contact alongside stale position -- the two-clock discriminator dal-001 documents -- narrows the quiet-run background from 137.7 aircraft per run to 24.6 while leaving the staged margin unchanged at 3.4, so the signal-to-background ratio improves from about one in forty to about one in seven. It is the single largest improvement available to this rule and it costs nothing. Fourth, two filters apply, and they are the same two the bounding-box sweep and adp-008 both needed. An aircraft on the ground is excluded from both mechanisms, because a parked aircraft stops reporting for the uninteresting reason that it has been switched off. A not_heard finding additionally requires both ends of the gap to lie inside the corpus bounding box by a margin, because an aircraft that flies out of the box and back leaves an interval with nothing in it and nothing went wrong; the interior test does not apply to frozen_position, which has no gap to bracket. Measured on the quiet runs: 164 intervals exceed 100 s, 32 survive the airborne filter, 23 survive both, and those 23 belong to four aircraft every one of which is on the adp-008 list, with none unlisted. Omitting the two filters would mean four-fifths of the findings were artefacts of having drawn a box and of aircraft being switched off. Fifth, the exclusion list stays the generator's responsibility and is not duplicated here. The measurement above is an independent validation of adp-008 from a different code path -- built at corpus-build time from raw archive rows, checked here against pseudonymised observations in PostGIS after a full replay -- and it also confirms the list is not being applied to baseline windows, which is owed work on the generator rather than a defence to add to the detector. Failure cases added. A reading whose position is stale but whose contact is equally stale must not raise a frozen_position finding, because that shape is an aircraft not being heard from rather than one reporting a frozen position. A gap whose either end lies outside the bounding-box margin must raise no not_heard finding. A gap either of whose ends has the aircraft on the ground must raise nothing. The superseded failure case about a normal-baseline run raising a track_continuity_gap no longer applies and is withdrawn: a quiet run raises many, by design, and anom-008 is amended to say what the control actually counts. Refs adds: adp-008, dal-001, anom-005, anom-006. Amended 2026-09-19, on the evb-002 traceability measurement, and the amendment is about what a finding cites rather than what it detects. A finding carries two kinds of time and this item had conflated them: the window is the rule's conclusion, and the reports it read are its evidence. For a not_heard gap the two coincide, because the window ends ARE the reports either side of the silence. For a frozen_position gap they cannot coincide: started_at is the first stale report's timestamp minus the staleness that report declares, a reconstruction of when the position went stale, and that instant is by definition the one moment in the whole window at which nothing was recorded -- the position had stopped updating, which is what the finding is about. Measured over 24 real bundles from 40 runs: of 1,021 cited coordinates 91 resolve to zero rows, every one of them a frozen_position start, with every RF coordinate and every not_heard coordinate resolving cleanly; a focused check over three runs put it at 48 of 48 frozen starts unresolvable and 3 of 3 not_heard findings clean at both ends. The finding therefore gains observed_at, the timestamps of the first and last report the rule actually read, which equal the window for not_heard and do not for frozen_position. started_at is unchanged and deliberately so: when the position went stale remains the right answer to the question the window asks, and moving it to the first stale report's own timestamp would make every frozen finding shorter than the event it describes, which would quietly change anom-012's during-window counts. Note what nearly hid this -- a test written over a coverage-gap finding passes, because both of its ends are real rows, so the fixture would have proved traceability working on the only shape that cannot break it. Same class as the baseline test that had to be rebuilt because it could not fail. Failure case added: a frozen_position finding whose observed_at start equals its started_at fails the spec, because that is the reconstruction being written back into the citation. Refs adds: evb-002, db-008.

Track-gap detection sensitivity, and the recall figure the fusion rules depend on. Input: the stored scenario runs with their ground truth, and the TRACK-GAP rule from anom-010. Output: a per-aircraft recall figure for each staged scenario type, measured against the answer key rather than against a control, together with an account of where the undetected staged aircraft are lost -- the perturber's choice of which records to touch, the rule's airborne filter, its interior-to-box filter, or the requirement for a bracketing report either side of an absence. Constraints: measured on at least two independently seeded batches before any figure is reported as a property of the detector, because the figures here come from one; the answer key is the ground truth recorded at generation time by scn-002, never derived from the detector's own output; the investigation changes no detector behaviour by itself, so any fix it motivates is a separate item with its own tests. Failure cases: a recall figure quoted without the batch and policy it was measured under fails the spec, per the project's rule that a measurement without its conditions is a memory; and an account that attributes the loss without measuring it -- naming a filter as the cause rather than counting what each filter removes -- fails it too. Written 2026-09-15, on measuring anom-004 before writing it. The measurement that forces this item: across the seed-matched runs, 119 aircraft were actually staged on and 25 produced a finding, a recall of 21 per cent, 19 per cent for aircraft-coverage-gap and 25 per cent for gnss-degradation. The shapes are correctly assigned in every case, frozen_position for the degradation runs and not_heard for the coverage gaps, so the two-mechanism design of anom-010 is wired correctly and this is a sensitivity result rather than a wiring one. It is also not a tuning artefact: sweeping the staleness threshold across 60, 100, 150 and 200 s and the contact-freshness discriminator across 10, 30, 60 and 90 s and disabled entirely leaves recall flat at 19 to 26 per cent throughout. The injected disruption is 300 s beginning 120 s into the window, comfortably above every threshold tried, so the loss is not the threshold. This gates anom-005, anom-006 and anom-007. Measured across the twenty rf-sensor-fault runs, whose truth is a broken sensor and which stage nothing on the track side, a background track cluster lies within the fusion radius of the faulty sensor on 70 per cent of them at 60 km and 75 per cent at 85.7 km -- so anom-005 as specified would report possible_interference_zone on most of the runs whose correct answer is possible_sensor_fault, and anom-006 being mutually exclusive with it for the same cluster means the false fusion removes the run from the rule that would have been right. Requiring three or more members in a cluster cuts that exposure from 70 to 25 per cent and cannot be used, because at 21 per cent recall a staged run yields one to three findings in total and only one measured run produced three detections on staged aircraft: the threshold that suppresses the background suppresses the signal, because they are the same size. The conclusion is one number rather than three problems -- the background is not too large, the recall is too small -- and the fusion rules must not be built until it is understood, or three items will pass their unit tests on constructed fixtures and fail together at evaluation time with the cause two layers below where the failure appeared. One interaction found on the way and not to be fixed by weakening anom-010: the aircraft-coverage-gap runs produce fewer findings than their own controls, because suppressing rows can remove the reports that would have bracketed a natural gap, and anom-010's refusal to extrapolate a gap from a track's final report is correct and stays. Refs: FR-304, FR-305, FR-306, FR-308, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, anom-008, anom-010, scn-002, adp-008, eval-002, docs/phase8_detection.md. Discharged 2026-09-16 for the recall half, on three batches rather than the two this item asks for. Batch 1 at the original generator gives 25 per cent overall and 37 for gnss-degradation; batch 2 after scn-006, base seed 20260916, gives 69 and 81; batch 3, base seed 20260917, gives 81 and 95. Parked aircraft in the answer key fall from 209 of 381 to 1 of 62 and then to 0 of 74. The loss account the item asks for is also settled: with the generator repaired, on ground accounts for 11 of the 14 remaining misses in batch 3 and below threshold for 3, with nothing at all lost to the interior filter, to an absent aircraft, or to an unbracketed absence. The on-ground remainder is aircraft that took off or landed during the window rather than aircraft parked throughout, which is the detector being correct. The staging yield across both repaired batches is 58 staging runs of 80, or 72.5 per cent, which is the figure eval-002's campaign sizing rests on. Re-measured and closed 2026-09-29. The discharge of 2026-09-16 above was taken on corpus v1, which was destroyed on 2026-09-19 by a database-tier test run pointed at the application database, and **no log of any of those three batches survived** -- the figures existed only as prose on this item and in thesis_notes.md, with nothing to re-derive them from. That is the failure this item's own constraint was written against, arriving from the direction nobody watched: not a figure quoted without its conditions, but a figure whose conditions were recorded and whose data was not. Corpus v2 held one generated batch until today, so the two-batch constraint was unsatisfiable on it; wave 2 was generated at base seed 965530111 (100 runs, ids 181-280) and the measurement re-run per batch and combined, with the log committed. Per-aircraft recall, threshold 100 s, contact fresh within 30 s, interior margin 0.25 deg: batch 1412660662 gives 83 per cent for gnss-degradation and 64 for each suppression arm, 70 overall; batch 965530111 gives 81, 59 and 59, 66 overall; combined over 600 staged aircraft, 82 / 62 / 62 and 68 overall. The figures replicate within a few points across independent seeds, which is what this item asked for and what corpus v1's three batches could no longer be used to claim. The loss account is complete and nothing is unattributed: 81 on ground, 88 below threshold, 21 contact not fresh, and **zero** to the interior filter, zero to an aircraft absent from the run, and zero to an unbracketed absence -- so of the four places the item named as candidates, two account for everything and two account for nothing. The on-ground remainder is aircraft that took off or landed inside the window rather than aircraft parked throughout, which is the detector being right. 10 of 600 answer-key aircraft were parked, against 209 of 381 before scn-006. No run staged nothing, so scn-007's floor holds and eval-002's exclusion count is zero on this corpus. One thing the measurement makes plain and which is not a second result: aircraft-coverage-gap and ambiguous-mixed-evidence are byte-identical in every column, because tracks.py gives them the same SUPPRESS mode and at a shared seed their track findings are the same findings -- one measurement reported twice rather than two, and it is recorded here so nobody reads the agreement as replication. The measurement script was also corrected: it selected batches by RUN_LO/RUN_HI id range, which was how a batch was addressed before scn-008 put the base seed on the row, and an id range is correct exactly until a corpus is regenerated -- the hazard measurements/corpus/_corpus.py exists to prevent. It now selects by base seed through that module and prints which corpus it read. Refs adds: scn-007, scn-008, ops-004. Wave 3 generated the same day (base seed 655209063, 100 runs, ids 281-380), completing corpus v2 at 300 runs and freezing it before eval-002 computes anything, so the headline metrics are taken once rather than recomputed after results are visible. Final figures over three independently seeded waves and 900 staged aircraft: 82 per cent for gnss-degradation and 59 on each suppression arm, 67 overall. **The third wave separated two things the two-wave figure hid, and this is the result worth reporting rather than the average.** The navigation arm replicates almost exactly -- 83, 81, 83 -- so 82 per cent is a property of the frozen-position mechanism. The suppression arms spread eleven points -- 64, 59, 53 -- and account for the whole of the drift in the combined row, so the not-heard mechanism's recall varies with which aircraft a wave happened to stage on and a single-wave figure for it is worth about plus or minus five points. One wave would have reported either as a fact, which is what this item's two-batch constraint exists to prevent and is now demonstrated rather than asserted. The loss account closes at 136 on ground, 132 below threshold and 33 contact not fresh, with zero to the interior filter, zero absent and zero unbracketed, and 16 of 900 answer-key aircraft parked.

Local discontinuity rate excess, the track evidence the fusion rules consume. Input: one scenario run's track-gap findings from anom-010, a centre and radius, and a reference time window. Output: the rate of findings inside the disc during the window and the rate inside the same disc outside it, both per unit time, and their ratio as the excess. Constraints: the comparison is within one run and within one place, so it controls for the two things that defeated cluster size -- air traffic is not uniform, so a busy place is always busy, and runs differ from one another; the centre and window come from a detected RF episode (anom-001) and never from ground truth, per api-009; the rate is per unit time rather than a count, because the window and its complement have different durations; the excess is a number the consuming rule thresholds, and this item sets no threshold of its own. Failure cases: a run whose window covers its whole span has no reference period and must say so rather than dividing by zero; a disc containing no findings at all gives an excess of zero rather than an error; and a count used in place of a rate fails the spec, because a 300 s window against a 600 s remainder would report an excess of two where there is none. Written 2026-09-16, after measuring it rather than before. This replaces cluster size as the track side's contribution to anom-005 and anom-006, and the reason is measured: over 20 seed-matched pairs in batch 2, the largest cluster on a staged run beats its own control in 1 to 3 pairs at every radius from 5 to 60 km, which is no signal at all, while this excess separates them. The separation is real and modest, and both halves are reported here because the item should not be built on the flattering half alone. At a 30 km radius the best threshold catches 5 of 20 staged runs and fires on 2 of 20 controls; at 45 km, 10 of 20 and 5 of 20; at 60 km, 16 of 20 and 9 of 20. As a standalone detector that is poor. What makes it worth building is the comparison with what it replaces: anom-005 as specified fires when an RF anomaly has any co-located track cluster, and a background cluster lies within the fusion radius on 70 per cent of the runs whose truth is a sensor fault, so the rule would misattribute most of them. At 30 km this excess fires on 10 per cent of those same controls. The improvement is in false attribution rather than in sensitivity, which is the failure that mattered. Two decisions. First, the form is the straight ratio of rates and not a difference-in-differences against the rest of the box. The naive form is confounded -- the window sits mid-run, where a gap is easiest to bracket because it needs reports either side, so even control runs score a ratio above one -- and dividing by the same ratio computed over the rest of the box cancels that. Measured, it makes no difference: separation is +0.35 by Youden's J for both forms at 60 km and +0.25 for both at 45 km. The correction only rescales, so the simpler form is kept and the confound is recorded rather than engineered around. Second, the radius is a parameter with a stated trade-off rather than a chosen value, because the three measurements above are a curve and not a maximum, and which point on it is right depends on whether a missed incident or a misattributed one costs more -- a question for the evaluation and not for this item. Refs: FR-301, FR-305, FR-306, api-009, anom-001, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-008, anom-010, anom-011, eval-002. Statistics added 2026-09-16, immediately after the figures above were first quoted and before any of them was built on. The counts in this item are from 20 seed-matched pairs and the intervals are wide enough that only one point is distinguishable from chance. Two-sided Fisher's exact on staged against control: p=0.407 at 30 km, p=0.191 at 45 km, p=0.048 at 60 km. Wilson 95 per cent intervals on the rates: recall 25 per cent [11-47] at 30 km, 50 per cent [30-70] at 45 km, 80 per cent [58-92] at 60 km; false alarms 10 per cent [3-30], 25 per cent [11-47] and 45 per cent [26-66] respectively. The claim that this item cuts false attribution from 70 per cent to 10 per cent is therefore overstated as first written and is corrected here: the 70 per cent is 14 of 20 with an interval of [48-85], the 10 per cent is 2 of 20 with an interval of [3-30], and although those intervals do not overlap, so the direction holds, the separation between the rule and its control at that radius is not itself significant on this sample. What is supported is that the reduction is substantial and that the effect reaches significance only at the wide radius. Two consequences. First, no threshold is to be fixed from these numbers alone: the curve is estimated from one batch and each point carries roughly plus or minus twenty percentage points, so choosing a radius from it would be choosing from noise. Second, this item is not to be reported as a detector in eval-002 without its intervals beside it, per the project's rule that a measurement without its conditions is a memory -- and its Youden's J of 0.15 to 0.35, against a scale where zero is a coin flip and a screening instrument anyone would act on wants better than 0.6, is the honest summary of its standalone strength. For contrast within the same system, anom-001's radio side separates an 8 dB elevation from a baseline spread of about 1.5 dB, which is beyond five sigma. The two halves of the fusion evidence are not remotely comparable in strength, and anom-005's design should reflect that rather than treating them as two equal votes. A second batch at a different base seed is required before any of these figures is quoted as a property of the method, on the same terms anom-011 already sets. Replicated 2026-09-16 on a third batch, base seed 20260917, 60 runs, generated after scn-006 and measured against the pre-registration recorded in thesis_notes before it ran. Batch 3 was scored at the thresholds batch 2 chose rather than at thresholds refitted to itself, because a threshold chosen on the data it is scored against is fitted to that data and would make any batch read as confirmation. Out of sample: 11 of 20 staged and 5 of 20 controls at 30 km, 13 and 5 at 45 km, 15 and 6 at 60 km, for Youden's J of 0.30, 0.40 and 0.45. Five of the six rates fall inside the Wilson intervals batch 2 gives and the ordering across radii is preserved; the sixth, recall at 30 km, comes in at 55 per cent against a predicted interval of 11 to 47 and is recorded as a miss rather than waved through, because it missed in the favourable direction and that is when a pre-registration is most worth honouring. Pooled over 40 matched pairs: 16 of 40 against 7 of 40 at 30 km, 23 against 10 at 45 km, 31 against 15 at 60 km, with two-sided Fisher's exact of 0.047, 0.006 and 0.001. That supersedes the statistics recorded above on one batch: the finding there that only the widest radius separates the rule from its control was a property of the sample size and not of the method, and all three radii separate once the batches are pooled. What does not change is the strength: pooled Youden's J is 0.23 to 0.40, so the rule is now reliably better than chance and still far from anything that could be acted on alone, and the eight-decibel radio signal remains incomparably stronger. The trade-off curve is therefore now supported well enough to choose a radius from, and the choice still belongs to the evaluation rather than to this item, because which point is right depends on whether a missed incident or a misattributed one costs more -- and on the ordering between anom-005, anom-006 and anom-007, which is unsettled. Amended 2026-09-17, after anom-007 was built and measured, and the amendment is in part a correction to how the figures above were obtained. Six decisions. First, the centre and the window come from anom-007's assessment of a zone rather than from an anom-001 episode directly. api-009 is untouched -- neither is ground truth -- but an episode is not an incident, which anom-007 established: the injected elevation dips below anom-001's threshold about one tick in six, so one 300 s incident arrives as a median of six episodes. Measured over batches 2 and 3, the longest episode on a run has a median length of 90 s against a staged 300 s, while anom-007's window, seeded by the episodes and bounded by the readings, has a median of 320 s. The consequence here is direct, because the window and its complement are the two halves of the ratio: a window a third of the true length puts two thirds of the incident's own findings into the reference period it is being compared against, which is the one place they must not be. This also makes anom-013's ordering load-bearing in a second way -- step one's output is step three's candidate -- rather than only a precedence between answers. Second, a window of zero length is refused, on the same argument as the whole-run case already recorded here. A single-reading anom-001 episode has its start equal to its end, and the rate divides by that length: measured, 6 of 86 runs produce such an episode as their longest. The existing failure case covers a window that leaves no remainder; this covers one that leaves no window, and both are a caller handing this rule something no measurement can be taken over. Refusing rather than clamping, because a clamped zero-length window would return a number computed over one reading and nothing would distinguish it from a measurement. Third, the figures recorded above were obtained with the centre and window taken from ground truth. That was a property of the measuring script rather than of this rule, and it is recorded here rather than left implicit because a curve measured on inputs the rule will never receive is not a curve about the rule. Re-measured with the window the rule will actually be given, over the same 40 matched pairs and at the same pre-registered thresholds of 1.79, 1.79 and 1.58: 18 of 40 at 30 km, 21 at 45 and 26 at 60, against 15, 20 and 28 from the ground-truth windows. The curve survives and flattens. No figure above is withdrawn -- they remain the correct account of the signal's size -- but the re-measured row is the one any threshold is chosen from. Fourth, the radius is 60 km. This item previously declined to fix it and can now do so because the question it was waiting on has been answered, exactly as anom-013 said it must be. Two independent reasons, and neither is the height of the curve. The first is that the specificity half of the trade-off is no longer the relevant half: measured over batches 2 and 3, the runs reaching a fusion decision at all are 40 of 40 gnss-degradation, 0 of 40 aircraft-coverage-gap and 1 of 40 rf-sensor-fault, because anom-007 claims the rest. The control arm every earlier figure here was measured against -- the sensor-fault run -- is removed by the ordering before fusion sees it, and the arm that could actually produce a false interference call, a coverage gap with a spurious radio anomaly beside it, does not occur once in 40 runs. With no false-positive pressure at this step the curve is read at its sensitive end, which is what anom-013 predicted from the ordering and is now measured rather than assumed. The second reason is independent of any measurement: 60 km is scn-002's own configured incident radius, so the disc matches the scale of the zone it measures. That is configuration rather than per-run ground truth, and it is the same principled basis anom-004 used for its own default. Fifth, and consequently, ExcessPolicy gains a default radius of 60 km, which reverses a decision recorded on this item and tested for. The original argument was that every measured point is a different trade-off and a default would make that choice quietly on the caller's behalf. That argument is discharged rather than overturned: the choice has now been made in the open, with the reasons above, and a named default carrying them in one place is more discoverable than the number repeated at every call site -- which is the arrangement anom-004 and anom-007 already use for the same kind of value. The test asserting the absence of a default is replaced by one asserting the value and citing the reasons, rather than deleted. Sixth, what this still does not settle, stated because the measurement makes it visible for the first time. At the pre-registered threshold and the chosen radius the excess reaches that threshold on 26 of 40 interference runs, so used as a necessary condition it would lose 14 of them. Whether anom-005 should gate on this quantity at all, or carry it as evidence strength in the bundle while firing on the radio pattern, belongs to anom-005 and not here -- but it cannot be decided without these numbers, and the asymmetry recorded above, an 8 dB radio signal against a Youden's J near 0.3, is what makes it a real question rather than a rhetorical one. Refs adds: anom-007, anom-014, scn-002. Qualified 2026-09-17, by a measurement taken while building anom-005, and this qualifies the figures above rather than withdrawing them. Of the 40 staged zones reaching the fusion step, 26 have an excess at or above the pre-registered threshold -- but only 6 of those 26 hold at least one finding in both the window and its complement. In the other 20 the reference period is empty, so its rate is nothing but this item's smoothing constant and the ratio is a function of the period lengths rather than a comparison of two observed rates. That is why the distribution is so wide, with a median of 3.87 and a 75th percentile of 11.47 on a quantity whose null value is 1. What this does not do is invalidate the separation recorded above. The control arm is subject to the same mechanism at the same traffic densities, since a control is the same corpus window with the same aircraft, so the comparison between arms remains like for like and the pooled Fisher's exact results stand. What it does mean is that the ratio must not be read as a rate comparison in the majority of cases where it fires, and that any consumer wanting to claim an observed excess has to check both counts, which is what anom-005 now does. Recorded here so that a reader of the trade-off curve above does not infer more from it than it supports.

Reportable rule precedence. Input: one scenario run's RF anomalies from anom-001, its track-gap findings from anom-010 and their clusters from anom-004, and the rate excess from anom-012. Output: at most one reportable anomaly per candidate zone per run, chosen by a declared order rather than by whichever rule happens to be evaluated first. Constraints: the three reportable rules partition one decision rather than testing independently, and the order is anom-007 first, then anom-006, then anom-005. anom-007 decides on the RF pattern alone -- one sensor abnormal with its spatial neighbours nominal -- and consults no track evidence at all; anom-006 applies where there is track evidence and no RF anomaly co-located with it; anom-005 applies only to what remains, an RF anomaly spanning more than one sensor with co-located track evidence. A zone claimed by an earlier rule is not offered to a later one, which is what makes anom-006's existing mutual-exclusion constraint enforceable rather than aspirational. Failure cases: two reportable anomalies of different types for the same zone in the same window fails the spec; a sensor-fault run raising possible_interference_zone fails it, which is anom-006's existing failure case restated where it can actually be checked; and an implementation that evaluates the rules in source order rather than in the declared order fails, since that would make the outcome a property of the file. Written 2026-09-16, because the ordering had never been written down and because anom-012's threshold cannot be chosen without it. The measurement that forces it: with fusion reading co-located track evidence and no precedence, a background track cluster lies within the fusion radius on 14 of 20 runs whose truth is a sensor fault, so the rule would claim most of anom-007's runs and, being mutually exclusive with anom-006 for the same cluster, take them from that rule too. Deciding the fault first removes the question rather than answering it with weaker evidence. The asymmetry of evidence is the reason and is measured: anom-001 separates an 8 dB elevation from a baseline spread of about 1.5 dB, beyond five sigma, while the track side's rate excess reaches a Youden's J of 0.40 pooled over 40 matched pairs. Asking the weaker signal to arbitrate what the stronger one already settles is the error. The consequence for anom-012 is recorded here: once anom-007 claims the sensor-fault runs, anom-005's remaining discrimination is between interference and nothing rather than between interference and a fault, so anom-012's radius is read from the sensitive end of its curve -- 31 of 40 at 60 km -- rather than the specific end. That choice is not fixed by this item and must not be until anom-007 exists and its own catch rate on sensor-fault runs has been measured, because the argument above assumes it claims them and that assumption is untested. Refs: FR-305, FR-306, FR-307, anom-001, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, anom-008, anom-012, evb-001, docs/phase8_detection.md, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Amended 2026-09-17, before tests, after anom-007 and anom-012 landed and after measuring what actually reaches each step. Seven decisions. First, the unit this item resolves is a claim and not a rule. It takes zone-bearing claims from whatever rules ran, orders them by a declared constant, and returns at most one per zone with a ledger of what was suppressed and by whom. That is what makes the item completable before anom-006 and anom-005 exist: their only obligation to this one becomes emitting a claim, and nothing here changes when they arrive. The alternative -- a resolver that calls the three rules itself -- cannot be built before them and would have to be tested against stubs, which is the arrangement that let anom-007 pass thirty-six tests and a mutation pass while being wrong. Second, the order comes from a declared constant and a claim whose rule is not in it is refused rather than appended. An unknown rule has no declared position; giving it one implicitly, whether last or by arrival, is exactly the third failure case above -- an outcome that is a property of the file rather than of the declaration. Third, suppression is between rules and never within one. Two claims from the same rule are two events: two broken receivers are two broken receivers, and a run may legitimately hold both. The mutual exclusion this item exists to make enforceable is anom-006's with anom-005, which is cross-rule by construction. Fourth, two claims are the same zone when their centres lie within a configured radius of each other and their windows overlap. The default is the layout's own discrimination radius, which scn-005 validates as the distance over which one cause can reach two receivers and which anom-007 already uses for that reason. Deliberately not anom-012's 60 km, which answers a different question -- how wide a patch to count dropouts over, not whether two candidates are one event. Recorded as provisional: an anom-005 zone may span a centre and its neighbours, up to about 120 km across, and two claims at opposite ends of one incident would then fail this test. Revisit it when anom-005 produces a zone rather than guess now what shape that zone will have. Fifth, an undecided verdict is not a claim. anom-007 is three-valued, and a zone it could not decide passes to the next step untouched -- the only reading consistent with undecided meaning what it says. A rule that cannot tell must not thereby block the rules that might. Sixth, window overlap is inclusive at both endpoints, on anom-007's argument: a window's end is its last contributing reading rather than the first quiet one, so two windows meeting at an instant shared it. Seventh, the gap this item ships with, stated rather than left to be discovered. Only anom-007 produces claims today, so the tests here exercise the resolution mechanism and not the ladder end to end, and no measurement over the corpus is possible until anom-005 lands. What is already measured and belongs here: of the 120 runs in batches 2 and 3, the runs reaching a fusion decision at all are 40 of 40 gnss-degradation, 0 of 40 aircraft-coverage-gap and 1 of 40 rf-sensor-fault, because anom-007 claims the rest. The ordering therefore already does the work this item was written to do, before the mechanism that enforces it exists -- which is an argument for building it rather than against, since that separation is currently a property of what the rules happen to produce rather than of a declaration anything checks. The end-to-end measurement is recorded here when the third step exists. Refs adds: anom-014, scn-005. Corrected 2026-09-17, same day, by the measurement recorded on anom-005: the description of the third step above says anom-005 applies to an RF anomaly spanning more than one sensor with co-located track evidence, and the track evidence is no longer a condition of it. The ordering is unchanged and so is every failure case; what changes is that the third step's trigger is the RF pattern alone, with the track excess carried as confidence. The mutual exclusion this item makes enforceable is therefore between a zone with a co-located RF anomaly and one without, which is a discrimination made on the strong signal rather than on the weak one. Measured end to end 2026-09-18, once anom-005 existed, which this item shipped without. Over all 240 stored runs the ladder decides 60 of 60 rf-sensor-fault runs as possible_sensor_fault, 60 of 60 gnss-degradation as possible_interference_zone, 20 of 20 ambiguous-mixed-evidence as a sensor fault, and is correctly silent on 75 of 80 aircraft-coverage-gap and 19 of 20 normal-baseline runs. No zone in any run received two answers, which is this item's first failure case and it does not occur. Six runs that stage nothing on the RF grid raise a sensor fault, and five gnss-degradation runs plus one rf-sensor-fault run carry a second anomaly of the other type in a different zone -- both are properties of anom-001's false-positive rate and of the per-zone guarantee being per zone rather than per run, not of the ordering. anom-006 remains unbuilt, so the aircraft-coverage-gap arm can only produce a correct non-detection here and must not be reported as a test of the ladder's second step. Amended 2026-09-18, on the anom-006 closure, and the amendment is about this item's evidence rather than its behaviour. The ladder measures 60 of 60 on all five arms with zero zones given two answers, and that result must be read precisely: it is not evidence that the ordering resolves conflicts, because on every arm of this corpus exactly one rule bids. anom-007 returns a fault verdict on the single-receiver types and an environmental one on the multi-receiver type, and anom-005 consumes only the environmental verdict, so SENSOR-FAULT and FUSION-SPATIAL never contest the same zone. The arm built to create a genuine conflict is ambiguous-mixed-evidence, which stages one receiver and a track gap together, and its track half is invisible because anom-006 is unbuilt. So the second bidder this item was ordered against does not exist on this corpus. The ordering itself is proved, by unit tests and by a mutation pass over measurements/mutation/mutate_anom013_precedence.py; what has never happened is the corpus presenting two claims for one zone. Record this separately from the detection results: an untested suppression path that passes because it is never reached is not a passing suppression path. Refs adds: anom-006, eval-002. Further to the amendment above, and recorded so the gap is not read as larger than it is: the arm that would supply the second bid, ambiguous-mixed-evidence, is measurably the right vehicle for it. Its RF stream is identical to the matched rf-sensor-fault run in 60 of 60 pairs and it additionally removes five aircraft, so the moment a track-side rule exists the arm presents two claims over one place with everything else held constant. Nothing about this item needs changing to accommodate that; what is missing is a second producer, not a different design. Measured 2026-09-19 by measurements/corpus/ladder_suppression.py, which closes the amendment above with a number rather than an inference. Across corpus v2, 188 claims are bid and 0 are suppressed. The breakdown matters more than the total: gnss-degradation bids exactly 60 claims over 60 runs, one each, while rf-sensor-fault and ambiguous-mixed-evidence bid 64 each, so four runs of each type produce two claims. Two claims in one run is therefore not rare -- what has never happened is two claims contesting the same zone, which is what suppression requires. The ordering and the merge are both exercised; the suppression path is not. So this item's 60 of 60 with zero conflicting runs should be read as evidence that the ladder correctly declines to merge separate events, and not as evidence that it correctly arbitrates competing ones. The second claim is proved by unit tests and by mutate_anom013_precedence.py, and is owed a corpus demonstration that only a second producing rule can supply.

Minimum episode duration for anom-001. Input: the existing RF-NOISE episodes and a configured minimum duration. Output: the same episodes with those shorter than the minimum reported as a distinct kind of non-finding rather than as anomalies, so that nothing downstream reads a single-reading threshold crossing as an event. Constraints: the minimum is configuration and not a literal; a suppressed episode is reported in the same channel anom-001 already uses for cells it could not judge, because a rule that silently drops what it has seen reopens the failure anom-008 exists to prevent; the change is to anom-001 and therefore to every figure measured through it. Failure cases: an episode exactly at the minimum must be kept, since the boundary belongs to the configured value and not to the comparison; and suppressing an episode without recording it fails the spec. Written 2026-09-17, unbuilt and deliberately so, which is the part of this item worth reading. The problem is real and measured: anom-001 raises at least one episode on 14 of 100 runs that stage nothing at all on the RF grid, and 6 of 86 staged runs produce a single-reading episode whose start equals its end -- a window of no length, which anom-012 divides by. But the harm is already caught twice downstream. anom-007 refuses an episode whose window its own readings do not sustain, which took the promoted false-positive rate from 14 of 100 to 6 of 100; and anom-012 refuses a zero-length window outright. Building this would remove the cause rather than the symptom, and it would also invalidate every measurement taken through anom-001 -- anom-007's 60 of 60, anom-012's trade-off curve on 40 matched pairs, anom-011's recall figures and the batch 3 replication scored against a pre-registration. That is the whole detection evidence base, traded for tidiness at the source of a harm that is already contained. The decision is therefore to specify it, record the reasoning, and leave it unbuilt until something depends on it that the downstream refusals do not cover -- at which point the batches are regenerated and re-measured together rather than one item at a time. Refs: FR-301, FR-303, anom-001, anom-007, anom-008, anom-012, eval-002. Amended 2026-09-18, when the item was taken off the shelf to be built, and the amendment settles one ambiguity and adds one constraint. The ambiguity: the original wording said a suppressed episode is reported 'in the same channel anom-001 already uses for cells it could not judge', which reads as though it should join the unjudged cells. It should not. An unjudged cell is the statement 'I had no baseline, so I did not look', and a suppressed episode is the statement 'I looked, I saw a crossing, and it was too brief to be an event'. Those are the same distinction anom-007's three-valued verdict and anom-005's three-valued corroboration are both built on -- silence separated from evidence of absence -- and folding the second into the first would discard the episode's own window, which is the only thing that makes a suppression checkable. So the findings gain their own field for suppressed episodes, each carrying the cell, the window it spanned, how many readings it held, and the minimum it failed; unjudged cells keep their existing meaning untouched. The added constraint: a negative minimum is refused rather than clamped, because a policy asking for a minimum duration below zero has no meaning and silently treating it as zero would turn a configuration error into a rule that quietly stopped suppressing anything. A minimum of exactly zero is legal and is the pre-anom-014 behaviour, which keeps the old behaviour representable and therefore testable. The value of the minimum itself is deliberately NOT fixed by this amendment: it is measured on the two populations it has to separate -- episodes on a cell the answer key names inside the staged window, against every other episode -- by backend/measurements/corpus/rf_noise_episode_duration.py, and the default is set from that measurement with the figure recorded beside it, in the same arrangement anom-012's radius and anom-007's 2 dB bar use. That measurement is valid across the regeneration this item lands in, because scn-007 changes the tracks and not the RF grid. Built and verified on the regenerated corpus 2026-09-18. The minimum is 10 s, measured on the two populations it separates before the number was written down, and the downstream effect matches the prediction exactly: every one of the 80 false episodes was a single reading, and every one of the 17 spurious sensor faults they were promoting is gone -- across all five arms -- with the catch rate unchanged at 60 of 60 on both staged types. On corpus v2 the false episode population is empty by construction and no episode anywhere has zero length, so anom-012's zero-length refusal now guards a case that cannot arise from anom-001.

Evidence bundle builder. Input: a group of related anomalies from one scenario run, grouped on three axes: simulated time window, spatial proximity, and frequency adjacency. Output: a bundle containing anomaly_type, time_window, affected_area, affected_channels, data_mode, an evidence list where each item has source, finding, and rule_id, and a known_uncertainties list. Constraints: this bundle is the only input the AI layer ever receives; raw observations never reach a model; anomalies on adjacent channels of the same sensor within the same window group into one bundle rather than several; the bundle carries no ground-truth field, per api-009. Failure case: an evidence item lacking a rule_id, or a bundle built with an empty evidence list, fails the spec. A second failure case: a broadband event spanning eight channels producing eight single-channel bundles, which fragments one finding into eight and hands the AI layer an incoherent picture. Refs: FR-401, FR-402, FR-404, FR-108, US-R1, AC-05, ai-003, api-009, scn-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.4. Amended 2026-09-19, before any test, on writing docs/phase8_evidence_bundles.md with the inputs known rather than anticipated. Three corrections, all of which change what the bundle is made of and none of which changes what it is for. First, data_mode cannot be a single value on this object. RF observations are ingested as SYNTHETIC and replayed tracks as REPLAYED, so every scenario run holds both, and a FUSION-SPATIAL bundle draws its evidence from both by definition, since that is what makes it a fusion. One value would have to be wrong and the wrong one is the one telling an analyst which half of the picture is invented. data_mode therefore belongs on the evidence item, with the bundle carrying the set its items span. This reaches further than tidiness because op-001's SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA badge is specified to reflect the data rather than a UI constant, and a bundle flattening two modes makes that badge wrong exactly where it matters. Second, the grouping constraint reads as a builder responsibility and mostly is not one. Grouping on simulated time window and spatial proximity already exists, in anom-013, which merges claims into zones on the layout's discrimination radius and inclusive window overlap because one zone per dismissal gave 160 zones for 60 events. A second implementation of near-in-time-and-space in this builder would be a second copy of a rule that already exists, which is the trap this repository recorded once already over distance being nearly measured in two places. The builder consumes anom-013's Resolution.reported and does not re-group. Frequency adjacency remains genuinely this item's, because nothing upstream merges anom-001's per-cell episodes across channels. Third, the unit of a bundle is one reported claim, not one run and not one finding. This item's phrase a group of related anomalies from one scenario run predates the ladder, which did not exist when it was written and is now the mechanism that decides which findings constitute one event; a run staging two broken receivers is two events and anom-013 already refuses to merge them. Two further constraints, both measured rather than assumed. A quiet run produces zero bundles and not one empty bundle: anom-008 requires zero reportable anomalies and this item independently requires an empty evidence list to fail the build, and the way those agree is that no bundle is created. And the known_uncertainties list has real content rather than being aspirational, because the detection layer already emits uncertainty as typed output: anom-005's not_measurable corroboration on 41 of 60 reported zones, anom-007's undecided verdict, anom-001's unjudged cells, anom-014's suppressed episodes and scn-007's floor shortfall. The 41 of 60 is the most important figure this object carries, because the project's fusion claim is weaker than it sounds and the bundle is what must say so to the thing writing the explanation. Corpus limitation recorded here rather than discovered later: the second failure case above, a broadband event fragmenting into eight single-channel bundles, cannot be provoked by any run available. All 300 runs of corpus v2 are narrowband, as all 240 of v1 were. The frequency axis must still be proved, by unit tests over constructed findings as the per-channel baseline granularity was in phase 8, but a unit test proves the mechanism and not that the mechanism matters; the corpus-level demonstration is owed to a broadband generation arm that does not exist and which anom-007's Medium and Low confidence bands also wait on. Refs adds: anom-013, anom-005, anom-014, anom-008, op-001, db-008. Composition agreed 2026-09-19, and it is the last thing gating tests. The governing principle, which each of the three decisions below is an instance of: every absence in a bundle is typed. Not applicable, could not be measured, and measured and found nothing are three different statements, and a bundle must never let a consumer collapse them -- the whole point of the object is that the thing reading it cannot tell the difference unless the bundle says. Note first that both compositions are almost entirely a projection of values the rules already emit rather than new computation: SensorFault already carries SpatialEvidence and SpectralEvidence, each with its own unjudged list, and InterferenceZone already carries sensors, corroboration, confidence and an optional RateExcess. A bundle for possible_interference_zone carries, as evidence: the anom-001 episode for each deviating receiver with its severity, peak deviation and triggering readings as refs; anom-007's environmental verdict, which is itself the finding that more than one receiver deviated together and is why the zone is environmental rather than a fault; anom-012's rate excess with its during and outside counts and its ratio, when it is measurable; and the anom-010 discontinuities inside the disc that excess was computed over. Its known_uncertainties carry, when corroboration is not_measurable, the reason stated in full rather than the flag alone -- the reference period held no discontinuities, so the ratio consists of nothing but anom-012's smoothing constant -- which is the 41 of 60 case and the most consequential uncertainty this system produces; plus anom-001's unjudged cells and anom-014's suppressed episodes. A bundle for possible_sensor_fault carries, as evidence: the anom-001 episode or episodes on the named receiver; each neighbour that was measured and found nominal, with its margin in dB, taken from SpatialEvidence.elevations against nominal_within_db, and these are positive evidence items rather than an absence because a nominal neighbour is the discriminating observation that makes this a fault and not the environment; the channel-adjacency check from SpectralEvidence as a second and independent reason, along the frequency axis rather than the spatial one; and the verdict with its confidence, which qualifies the attribution and not the deviation, whose severity anom-001 already carries. Its track side is explicitly not-applicable and must be stated as such: a single-receiver fault verdict never reaches anom-005, so there is no track evidence by design rather than by measurement, and an absent field would read as not_measurable, which would be a false uncertainty claim and the mirror image of the corroboration problem above. Its known_uncertainties carry spatial.unjudged and spectral.adjacent_unjudged, the neighbours and channels that existed and could not be judged. Third, suppressed claims. A claim suppressed by anom-013 is by construction another rule's competing conclusion about the same place, so the two rules disagreed and the ladder resolved it. It must never enter the evidence list, because the likeliest misreading is that co-occurrence is concurrence: a consumer handed both writes that two independent rules flagged this area, which inverts the truth exactly and is the misattribution docs/phase8_detection.md section 6 names as the error a fluent model makes unprompted. Nor may it simply be dropped, because a competing explanation that was considered and rejected is a genuine uncertainty and omitting it makes the bundle assert more confidence than the system has. So it goes in its own superseded field, outside the evidence list, phrased as a resolved competition naming the rule that won and why, never as a bare co-occurring fact. That choice has a consequence for ai-008 rather than for this item, and it is amended there: a grounding check that verifies a cited rule id exists in the bundle would certify a hypothesis citing a superseded explanation as support, which is the precise error the safeguard exists to catch. Refs adds: ai-008, anom-012, anom-010. Mutation pass 2026-09-19, over 34 sites, and the first pass is the part worth recording. It killed 22 of 34, and all 10 genuine survivors were the same kind of defect: a scoping rule. Evidence from another receiver, from outside the window, from another zone; a suppression a different rule won; an unjudged cell on a receiver this bundle is not about. The suite had tested thoroughly what goes into a bundle and barely tested what must be kept out of one, which is the more dangerous half, because a bundle carrying a neighbouring event's evidence is not malformed -- it is wrong, and it is wrong in a shape no schema check can see. Two of the tests it exposed were themselves weak rather than missing: the data-mode test keyed a dict on rule_id alone, so the rate excess and the discontinuity collapsed into one entry and one of them was never asserted at all -- the anom-012 identity ambiguity recorded above, biting the test written to check for it -- and the unjudged-cell test asserted a loose count of at least two, which the spatial and spectral sources satisfy on their own, while putting its cell on a receiver the builder correctly ignores, so the cell never reached the bundle. Seven tests added and two tightened; 34 of 34 now killed. The window tests deliberately place the excluded item BEFORE the window rather than after it, because an overlap comparison written from one side only still excludes a late item and wrongly admits an early one, so a test using a late item passes against a half-written comparison. Amended 2026-09-19, on evb-002's composition measurement, and the amendment adds one field to the evidence item. Of 332 evidence items across 24 real bundles, 260 cite raw observations and 72 cite nothing at all: a fault verdict, a nominal neighbour, a channel-adjacency check, an interference verdict, a rate ratio. Those 72 are not defective. They are judgements a rule made over readings, and there is no row for a judgement -- a nominal neighbour is in the bundle precisely because no episode was raised for it. But carrying no refs must not be a state an item can drift into, because a traceability check that skips items with no refs passes by default on any item that forgot them, which is the same defect as a sort key that does not exist sorting everything equal, recorded three times in this project already. So an item declares its kind: OBSERVED, which must carry at least one ref and every ref must resolve to exactly one stored row, or DERIVED, which must carry none. Both mismatches are refused at construction -- an OBSERVED item with no refs, and a DERIVED item with refs -- so the declaration cannot be a lie in either direction and a new item type cannot acquire the weaker treatment by omission. This is the typed-absence principle this item already applies to uncertainties, applied to citations: not applicable, not measurable and measured-and-found-nothing are three statements there, and cites-a-row against makes-a-judgement are two here. It is what makes evb-002's check total -- every item is checked, and the only way an item escapes a database lookup is by declaring that it makes no observational claim. Failure cases added: an item declaring OBSERVED with an empty refs tuple, and an item declaring DERIVED with a non-empty one. Refs adds: evb-002.

Evidence traceability. Input: a candidate evidence bundle. Output: a built bundle in which every evidence item resolves to a stored anomaly or observation ID. Constraints: resolution is checked at build time against the database, not asserted by the builder; the resolved IDs are persisted with the bundle so the grounding check in ai-008 has something to verify against. Failure case: a bundle containing an item whose rule_id or source reference matches no stored record must raise and must not persist a partial bundle. Refs: FR-403, US-R1, AC-05, evb-001, ai-008. Amended 2026-09-19, before any test, on measuring the question this item's design turns on. DetectionFinding.evidence_refs carries a coordinate and not an identifier -- an RF finding cites sensor_id, channel_index and timestamp, a track finding cites aircraft_id and a timestamp -- so resolving an evidence item to a stored observation is a query, and a query is a resolution only if it returns exactly one row. A resolver silently matching two rows would be worse than one that fails, because the bundle would cite whichever row the heap returned first, which is the unordered-result failure this project has now recorded three times. Measured by measurements/corpus/evidence_ref_uniqueness.py over both corpora: within one scenario run, RF observations are unique on sensor_id plus channel_index plus timestamp and track observations are unique on aircraft_id plus timestamp, across 20.7 million rows, with a worst collision of one and zero colliding coordinates on all four combinations. The ISO round trip is also exact -- refs store timestamps as ISO strings because findings.py must, and a stored string re-matched its own row on 2000 of 2000 sampled observations -- so a resolver may compare the string directly without normalising. This decides the item: resolution is by coordinate and no rule adapter changes. The alternative considered and not taken was recording row ids at finding time, which would have touched every from_* function; findings are derived and regenerable so the stored corpus was not the obstacle, but it buys nothing now that the coordinate is proved unique. One cost is recorded rather than hidden: a single resolution takes 64.7 ms, running as an index scan on ix_observations_scenario_run_id and then removing 38,424 rows by filter, because db-010's index narrows to the run and nothing narrows further. That is acceptable for a bundle carrying a handful of items and is not acceptable for one carrying hundreds, so the composite index is a candidate item to be decided once this item's evidence-list composition is fixed -- an index changes no data and no answer, only cost, which is what makes it safe to add later. Refs adds: db-010. Composition agreed 2026-09-19, on measurements/corpus/bundle_ref_cost.py, which closed the two questions this item left open and found one defect. Resolution is BATCHED, not per ref. 24 real bundles over 40 runs cite 1,021 coordinates -- a median of 26 per bundle and 105 at the worst, with a possible_interference_zone bundle citing a median of 79 and a possible_sensor_fault bundle 23. One query per ref costs 194.5 ms at the median and 748 ms at the worst, because db-010's index narrows to the run and the 38,424-row filter is then paid once per ref. One query per coordinate shape per bundle costs 10.5 ms at the median and 131.5 ms at the worst, 18.6x faster, because that filter is paid once. This closes the composite-index question this item deferred: the index is NOT owed before this item and stays a candidate, since batching removes the cost the index would have removed, and an index changes no answer. The coordinate shapes are a CLOSED SET OF TWO, matched by name and never by whatever keys happen to be present. RF is {sensor_id, channel_index, timestamp} and track is {aircraft_id, at}; the two spell the time differently, so a resolver reading timestamp alone silently misses every track ref while appearing to work. A ref matching neither shape is refused by name: from_track_cluster emits {aircraft_id} with no time, which as a predicate matches every report that aircraft made, and a resolver assembled from whatever keys are present would build an empty predicate for an empty ref and match the entire run. Every query is SCOPED TO THE SCENARIO RUN. The uniqueness established in evidence_ref_uniqueness.py is uniqueness within one run; the same coordinate exists in every run of the corpus, so an unscoped resolver would match 300 rows and cite whichever came back first. Resolution succeeds on exactly one row: zero is a citation of nothing, more than one is a citation of whichever row the heap returned first, and both raise. ATOMICITY IS PER RUN, not per bundle. Every bundle for the run is resolved in full before anything is written, and the write is one transaction replacing the run's bundles, following db-008's replace-rather-than-append -- a bundle is derived from findings which are derived from the seed, so appending would leave a superseded bundle beside a current one with nothing on either to say which is which. A failed resolution writes nothing at all, which is this item's must-not-persist-a-partial-bundle constraint read at the only unit where it is meaningful. The RESOLVED IDENTIFIERS ARE PERSISTED PER ITEM, inside the evidence JSON, rather than in a join table. The alternative considered was a bundle-to-observation join table with a real foreign key; not taken, because the foreign key would re-guarantee exactly what the resolver has just proved, observations are never deleted under db-007 so the guarantee has nothing to defend against, and ai-008 needs the identifiers attached to the item that cites them rather than pooled across the bundle. ONE MIGRATION, reversible. evidence_bundles was created by 0001 carrying an anomaly type, an evidence blob, an uncertainties blob and a created_at, and it predates everything this object turned out to be: no scenario run, no rule id, no subject, no window, no affected area, no affected channels, no superseded field. The revision adds them, with the affected area a Point at SRID 4326 under a GiST index following db-001 and db-008, and a btree index on scenario_run_id following db-010. Failure cases, each measured or constructible: a ref resolving to zero rows; a ref resolving to more than one; a ref whose shape is in neither known form; an item declaring OBSERVED and carrying no refs; a resolver not scoped to the run, which is the ambiguity case in disguise; and a failed resolution leaving rows behind. The defect this measurement found is recorded on anom-010 and db-008 rather than here, because the fix belongs to the finding that emits the citation rather than to the checker that caught it: 91 of the 1,021 cited coordinates resolve to zero rows, every one the start of a frozen_position track finding, whose window start is reconstructed from the reported staleness and is by definition the one instant in the window at which nothing was recorded. It belongs here as the reason this item is not a formality -- the first time every citation in this system was checked, one in eleven pointed at nothing. Refs adds: db-007, anom-010.

Hypothesis output schema. Input: a candidate hypothesis object from any generator. Output: a validated Pydantic model with hypothesis_title, confidence, summary, supporting_evidence, evidence_against_or_uncertainty, alternative_explanations, and recommended_human_action. Constraints: confidence is an enum of exactly Low, Medium, High; all fields are required; the same schema serves all three generators and is the source from which the hosted JSON schema and the local grammar are derived. Failure case: a hypothesis with confidence 87% or 0.87 must be unrepresentable, and one with a missing alternative_explanations field must fail validation rather than defaulting to empty. Refs: FR-501, FR-715, NFR-203, ui-001, ai-002, ai-004, ai-005. Composition agreed 2026-09-19, before any test. Field names are canonical here and the hypotheses table is wrong rather than this item: the table calls three of them uncertainty, alternatives and supporting_evidence, and has no column at all for summary or recommended_human_action. That is the same defect evidence_bundles carried -- a table written in 0001 before the object it stores existed -- and it is owed before any hypothesis is persisted, which is db-002's item and not this one. Recorded here so it is found at ai-004 rather than discovered there. First, a supporting-evidence item is a STRUCTURED CITATION and never a sentence. It names rule_id AND finding_type, plus the generator's own statement about it. Free text cannot be checked against anything, so a citation that is prose makes ai-008 unimplementable rather than merely awkward. Both identifiers are required because one does not identify: anom-012 defines no rule id and borrows anom-010's, so a rate-excess citation and a discontinuity citation carry the same rule id while making different claims -- measured, in every interference bundle the corpus produces. This is the loose end recorded on evb-001 as owed before ai-008, and it is closed here because the schema is what the model is instructed with: deciding it at ai-008 would mean changing the instruction after the campaign that used it. At least one supporting-evidence item is required, since a hypothesis supported by nothing is the thing this whole layer exists to prevent. Second, ALTERNATIVE_EXPLANATIONS REQUIRES AT LEAST ONE ENTRY, which is stronger than the field merely being present. A system built to stop a fluent model overclaiming must not accept 'there are no alternatives' as an answer, and the requirement is satisfiable rather than decorative: a fault bundle and an interference bundle are each other's competing conclusion, so the template generator can always name the one it did not pick. evidence_against_or_uncertainty is deliberately NOT given the same floor -- it must be present and may be explicitly empty, because 'nothing speaks against this' can be true while 'nothing else could explain this' essentially cannot. Whether a hypothesis carries the uncertainties its bundle carried is a completeness question about content, which is ai-008's, not a shape question, which is this item's. Third, NOTHING DEFAULTS. No field has a default value, including the two list fields. A list that becomes empty because the generator omitted it makes 'weighed the alternatives and found none' and 'never mentioned alternatives' arrive identically, which is evb-001's typed-absence principle at the next layer. Text fields are rejected when empty or whitespace, because a zero-length string satisfies a str type and is not a title. Extra fields are forbidden and the model is frozen, following the DAL's own base model. Fourth, and this is the test that is not obvious: THE RULE MUST SURVIVE DERIVATION. The item already says this schema is the source the hosted JSON schema and the local grammar are derived from, and the derived artefact -- not the Python model -- is what actually constrains a hosted generation. So the three-value confidence enum, the required-field set and the at-least-one floors are asserted on the DERIVED JSON schema as well as on the model. A derivation that silently widened confidence to a free string would pass every local test and lose the guarantee at precisely the boundary the guarantee exists for. Recorded as a limitation rather than solved: this schema stops a numeric confidence in the confidence FIELD and cannot stop a generator writing 'High (about 87% sure)' into the summary. FR-715 is a rendering rule as well as a schema rule and the UI carries the other half. The module lives at backend/app/ai/, not the repository-root ai/ placeholder: root ai/ is outside the backend package and therefore outside the test suite, the coverage gate, ruff and mypy, and a schema that nothing type-checks is the wrong place to put the one object three generators must agree on. Refs adds: db-002, anom-012, evb-001, ai-008.

Template hypothesis generator. Input: a resolved evidence bundle. Output: a schema-valid hypothesis assembled deterministically from the bundle contents, with no model call, and identical output for identical input. Constraints: no network, no API key, no model server, enforced by an import-graph test rather than by comment, because this is the correctness fallback for a model failure and a fallback sharing a dependency with the thing that failed is not one; confidence is read from the bundle's own verdict item -- the item whose finding_type is the bundle's anomaly_type -- rather than computed by a second scoring scheme, and is translated between the detection vocabulary (low) and the ai-001 vocabulary (Low) by enum member name, so an unrecognised word is refused rather than laundered by .title(); supporting evidence is grouped on the (rule_id, finding_type) pair ai-001 defines as a citation's identity, one citation per distinct kind in first-appearance order, with rule_id and finding_type copied verbatim and only statement composed; alternative explanations are the bundle's superseded claims, falling back to the standing fault/interference pair when there are none; every known uncertainty reaches evidence_against_or_uncertainty untruncated, in bundle order, because dropping the tail loses the distinction between measured-and-negative and never-looked that evb-001 exists to carry. Every emitted citation is copied from the bundle and is therefore grounded by construction, which makes a template hypothesis a test of ai-008 rather than of this generator. Failure cases: emitting a claim absent from the bundle invalidates the baseline; citing a superseded claim as supporting evidence inverts the ladder's meaning, since a suppressed claim is a competing conclusion and never support; a bundle carrying no item matching its own anomaly_type, or a verdict item whose confidence is missing or unrecognised, is refused rather than defaulted. Refs: FR-501, FR-502, FR-715, US-R1, AC-06, ai-001, ai-007, ai-008, anom-013, evb-001, eval-004, docs/implementation.md Phase 9.

Provider-agnostic hypothesis service interface. Input: an evidence bundle; the provider, dated model ID and frozen generation parameters come from configuration that SELECTS AND CONSTRUCTS the adapter rather than travelling per call, because parameters varying per call would invalidate the campaign comparison with no visible failure. Output: a generation result -- the validated hypothesis plus what produced it (generator kind, and for a model arm the model ID, the frozen parameters, the verbatim pre-parse response and usage). A bare hypothesis is insufficient and was an error in this item as first written: ai-004, ai-005 and db-002 each require that provenance, so an interface returning only a hypothesis forces every arm to invent its own carrier, which is exactly the leak this item forbids. The model-call record is a TYPED ABSENCE -- omittable only when the generator is the template, refused in both directions at construction -- rather than four nullable fields, which moves db-002's guarantee from the repository boundary to the point the result is made, so a model arm cannot construct a result missing its own raw response. Constraints: defined before either provider is written, so no provider's request or response shape appears in the signature, enforced by an AST purity check over app/ai/ that is fired once at a real violation because a check that finds nothing when it passes finds nothing when it is broken; the configuration CARRIES NO CREDENTIAL, since the parameters are persisted verbatim beside every hypothesis and a key held there would be written to the database once per row; the ai-002 template generator is registered through this interface, so the port has two implementations on the day it lands and cannot be shaped around a single case, and ai-007's correctness fallback becomes 'ask the registry for the template' rather than a special case carved into each model arm; two failure categories are named here, provider-unavailable and generation-refused, because ai-006 and ai-007 must remain distinct paths in code and in the write-up and a single exception type makes them indistinguishable to the code that chooses between them -- the template's own refusal is deliberately in neither, since falling back from the fallback has nowhere to go; adding a provider touches one adapter module and one registry line, and that cost is MEASURED rather than claimed, as the second data point for the RQ1 extensibility argument alongside adp-003. Failure cases: a provider-specific type in the interface signature; a caller branching on provider; a credential reachable from the persisted parameters; a model-arm result constructible without its verbatim raw response; an unknown provider name resolving to a default rather than being refused. Refs: FR-503, FR-508, US-E2, US-R6, AC-06, adp-003, ai-001, ai-002, ai-004, ai-005, ai-006, ai-007, db-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10. Amended 2026-09-25, found while building ai-011 and the second composition defect this item has surfaced by being used. ProviderFactory is Callable[[GenerationConfig], HypothesisGenerator] -- config in, generator out -- and that signature cannot carry a construction argument which is not a generation parameter. ai-004's per-1k prices are exactly such an argument: they are economics rather than anything the model is called with, they cannot travel in GenerationConfig.parameters because those are splatted verbatim into the provider request and an unrecognised key there is a rejected request, and they belong to one arm rather than to the port, since a local model costs nothing per call and has no price to give. So a caller assembling a run through build_generator silently loses them, and silently losing them is not a visible failure: cost evaluates to None on every call, ai-009's spend ceiling enforces nothing while reporting itself as configured, and eval-005's actual-cost result comes back empty. build_generator therefore forwards construction keywords to the factory it selects, and ProviderFactory widens to Callable[..., HypothesisGenerator] accordingly. The alternative considered and rejected was a prices field on GenerationConfig, which would put one arm's economics into the object all three arms share and into the row persisted beside every hypothesis. The registry's rule is unchanged and is what this preserves: it stays the only module that knows a provider by name, and the assembler goes through it rather than importing an adapter directly.

Hosted AI generator, the primary arm. Input: an evidence bundle, a pinned dated model ID, and frozen generation parameters. Output: a validated hypothesis persisted with generator=hosted, model_id, generation_params, and verbatim raw_response.
