Constraints: uses the provider's native JSON-schema-constrained output so schema conformance is a generation-time guarantee; the model ID is dated, never a moving alias; tests mock the provider and never make a real call. Failure case: a configuration naming a moving alias rather than a dated ID must be rejected at startup, since an alias changing mid-campaign would invalidate the comparison with no visible error. Refs: FR-504, FR-506, FR-507, FR-508, US-R3, US-R4, db-002, ai-001, ai-003. Precondition added 2026-09-19: a reasoning document, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md, is written BEFORE this item and not before ai-001. The pattern is established twice -- docs/phase8_detection.md and docs/phase8_evidence_bundles.md -- and both earned their keep by finding defects in their own specifications before a line was written, three in evb-001's case. ai-001 is a schema and needs no such document; this item is where the design questions actually land, and they are not small: two model arms plus a deterministic one and what it means for them to be comparable, two different kinds of fallback that must not be confused (availability in ai-006, correctness in ai-007), a spend ceiling whose realistic failure is a retry loop rather than a price rise, a pinned dated model id and frozen parameters as the reproducibility claim, and what a hosted provider receiving an evidence bundle means for NFR-405, which forbids a real aircraft identifier reaching one. Recorded on this item rather than in a session note because a handoff is overwritten and a specification is not. Amended 2026-09-22, provider chosen and four things settled or corrected while planning the build. Provider is OPENAI, on native structured outputs (response_format json_schema, strict true), chosen because dated model identifiers are its norm so the moving-alias guard works exactly as this item specifies. (1) WHAT LEAVES THE MACHINE IS NOW A MODULE, NOT A MEASUREMENT SCRIPT. Section 4 of docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md measured the egress payload field by field, and that measurement is what closed the Track 0 data-egress gate and what NFR-405 rests on -- but it was taken against a payload dict hand-written inside measurements/corpus/bundle_payload.py, and nothing in app/ serialises a bundle at all. Unless the adapter ships that exact serialiser, the thing measured is not the thing sent. The serialiser therefore lands in app/ai/payload.py, inside the package that lint, mypy and the coverage gate see, and the measurement re-runs against it. The superseded field IS sent, labelled as rejected: it is what lets a model write honest alternatives, and it creates precisely the trap ai-008 exists to catch, which is also what makes ai-008's second failure case testable on real data rather than only on constructed bundles. (2) THE PROMPT IS THE EXPERIMENT'S LARGEST VARIABLE AND IS PINNED BY FINGERPRINT. Written once as a module constant, reviewed before any call, and shared verbatim with ai-005 if that arm is ever built. Its SHA-256 is recorded in generation_params on every row -- the pattern the corpus manifest already uses for PSEUDONYM_SEED -- so a row identifies which instructions produced it and drift is detectable, without writing the text into every row. The prompt deliberately carries no glossary of anomaly types (the package's own prose already states each rule's conclusion, and a glossary adds a variable to an experiment trying to hold everything but the generator still) and never names the scenario type. (3) A CONSTRAINED SCHEMA DOES NOT CARRY EVERY GUARANTEE, WHICH CORRECTS THIS PROJECT'S READING OF SECTION 10. The claim recorded on ai-007 was that schema conformance is a generation-time guarantee for the hosted arm, so a validation failure cannot happen in the ordinary course and therefore means the provider broke its own constraint. That is true of STRUCTURE -- fields, types, the three-value confidence enum, additionalProperties false -- and NOT of QUANTITY. Structured-output strict mode does not honour the minLength and minItems constraints ai-001 relies on, so an empty supporting_evidence list or a blank summary is conformant to the provider and invalid to us. Those guarantees therefore MOVE from generation time to parse time: still enforced, by the Pydantic model, but as a refusal rather than as an impossibility. Consequence for ai-007: a malformed refusal from this arm is not automatically the alarming event section 10 described, and the adapter's refusal message distinguishes a structural failure from a constraint the schema could not express. The exact set of unsupported keywords is provider documentation rather than something this repository can verify without a real call, so it is a named constant, every guarantee is re-asserted on the NARROWED schema, and the three-bundle smoke test on the Phase 8.5 gate is what confirms it against the live API. (4) COST IS AN ESTIMATE AND MAY BE ABSENT. The provider returns token counts, not money, so Usage.cost_usd is None unless the adapter is supplied with prices -- which means ai-009's spend ceiling is inert on THIS arm too, not only on the local one as recorded when ai-009 was built. That sharpens rather than breaks the design: the call ceiling was always the guard. Prices are constructor arguments on the adapter and deliberately NOT part of GenerationConfig, because they are a fact about billing rather than about generation and would otherwise be persisted as generation parameters. A computed cost is an estimate; the provider console remains the authority, which is consistent with ai-009 reporting a lower bound. The API key is read from the environment by the adapter and never travels in GenerationConfig, whose parameters are persisted verbatim (ai-003); OPENAI_API_KEY is added to backend/.env.example with no default and the adapter fails loudly without it, following PSEUDONYM_SEED. Second failure case, added: a hypothesis persisted without the fingerprint of the prompt that produced it fails the spec, since two arms or two days given different instructions are not one comparison and nothing else in the row records which instructions ran. Refs adds: ai-007, ai-009, eval-004, eval-005, NFR-405, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md sections 2 and 4.

Local AI generator, the second arm and availability fallback. Input: an evidence bundle and the same frozen generation parameters as ai-004. Output: a validated hypothesis persisted with generator=local, model_id, generation_params, and raw_response. Constraints: schema enforced by a grammar compiled from the same JSON Schema as ai-004, so one schema has two enforcement mechanisms and an identical guarantee; the model server runs on the host and is reached over HTTP as a config value, never as a Compose service. Failure case: the local and hosted arms diverging in accepted schema, or generation parameters differing between arms, fails the spec and would make the comparison meaningless. Refs: FR-505, FR-506, FR-1102, ai-001, ai-003, ai-004, ai-006. DEFERRED 2026-09-21, with a trigger rather than a date: build ai-004, record how often the hosted arm is actually unavailable in development use, and revisit. Deferral is normally the wrong answer to a Phase 8.5 gate item and the reason it is safe HERE is narrow and is the whole justification -- the local arm is NOT SCORED. The pre-registration in docs/scoring_rubric.md covers hosted-versus-template only, so adding a second model arm afterwards costs nothing in validity, unlike every other item on that gate, which is expensive-to-impossible after the campaign precisely because it IS inside the pre-registration. What cutting it would lose is also smaller than it looks, for two reasons that only became true recently: the offline demonstration survives because ai-002 needs no network and produces a real explanation, and ai-003 named the two failure CATEGORIES, so losing the local arm does not collapse the two fallbacks -- they keep different causes and different log records and only the destination coincides. What would genuinely be lost is one schema enforced two ways, by a hosted provider's constrained decoding and by a locally compiled grammar, which is a real portability finding and costs a time-boxed day. Reasoning in docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 7.

Availability fallback, hosted to local. Input: a generation request while the hosted provider is unreachable, unauthenticated, or rate limited. Output: a hypothesis generated by the local arm, persisted with generator=local, and the fallback event logged. Constraints: no error state reaches the analyst; the fallback is a distinct code path from the correctness fallback in ai-007 and must remain distinct in code and in the write-up; it is deliberately exercised with the network off, not assumed. Failure case: a hosted timeout surfacing as an error in the UI, or falling through to the template generator instead of the local arm, fails the spec. Refs: FR-509, FR-511, NFR-103, NFR-105, AC-07, ai-005, ai-007, ai-010. DEFERRED 2026-09-21, with a trigger rather than a date: build ai-004, record how often the hosted arm is actually unavailable in development use, and revisit. Deferral is normally the wrong answer to a Phase 8.5 gate item and the reason it is safe HERE is narrow and is the whole justification -- the local arm is NOT SCORED. The pre-registration in docs/scoring_rubric.md covers hosted-versus-template only, so adding a second model arm afterwards costs nothing in validity, unlike every other item on that gate, which is expensive-to-impossible after the campaign precisely because it IS inside the pre-registration. What cutting it would lose is also smaller than it looks, for two reasons that only became true recently: the offline demonstration survives because ai-002 needs no network and produces a real explanation, and ai-003 named the two failure CATEGORIES, so losing the local arm does not collapse the two fallbacks -- they keep different causes and different log records and only the destination coincides. What would genuinely be lost is one schema enforced two ways, by a hosted provider's constrained decoding and by a locally compiled grammar, which is a real portability finding and costs a time-boxed day. Reasoning in docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 7.

Correctness fallback, model arm to template. Input: a model response that fails Pydantic validation or the grounding check in ai-008. Output: a bounded number of retries, then a template-generated hypothesis persisted with generator=template and the fallback reason logged. Constraints: the retry ceiling is explicit with no unbounded recursion, because a retry loop is the realistic route to an unexpected bill; retry rate is logged per arm; this path applies identically to the hosted and local arms. Failure case: unbounded retry on persistently invalid output, or falling back to template without recording that a fallback occurred, fails the spec. Refs: FR-510, FR-511, NFR-103, ai-002, ai-006, ai-008, ai-009. Amended 2026-09-21, three changes: the first is owed from docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 10, the other two were found while planning the build. (1) THE TWO TRIGGERS ARE NOT OF EQUAL STANDING. ai-004 uses the provider's native schema-constrained output, which makes schema conformance a generation-time guarantee, so for the hosted arm a validation failure cannot happen in the ordinary course. If one does, the provider broke its own constraint -- a more alarming event than an ungrounded claim, and one that must be recorded as its own category rather than folded into a retry count. The ceiling still bounds every attempt, since no unbounded recursion is unconditional, but the record distinguishes the two and in practice the ceiling is about grounding failures. They are told apart BY ORIGIN rather than by a flag the arms and the check would have to agree on: a refusal raised by the generator is malformed, a refusal raised by the injected grounding check is ungrounded. (2) A RETRY SENDS THE IDENTICAL REQUEST, AND ai-004 PINS TEMPERATURE 0 WITH A FIXED SEED. If the serving stack is deterministic the retry returns the identical answer and fails the identical check, so it is a second payment for the same refusal and the ceiling multiplies the cost of a failure by N for no benefit. The measurement that settles this is already scheduled: section 8's non-scored N=3 probe asks whether the provider is actually deterministic at temperature 0, which many are not, because of batching and floating-point non-associativity in the serving stack -- the same class of problem this project has hit three times in its own results. Until that probe reports, the recommended ceiling is 2 attempts, CHOSEN AND NOT MEASURED, on asymmetric arithmetic: being wrong upwards costs at most about 20 extra calls against ai-009's 200-call run budget, while being wrong downwards throws a recoverable hypothesis to the template and understates the model arm in a pre-registered comparison. The value is stated in one place and the ceiling itself carries NO DEFAULT, because a retry count is a spending decision and one made by omission is one nobody chose. (3) THE TWO CATEGORIES LEAVE RECORDS OF DIFFERENT STRENGTH, and the spec states the asymmetry rather than leaving it to be discovered. An ungrounded hypothesis parsed, so it is a storable row carrying grounding FAILED beside the template row that replaced it -- db-002 appends and never replaces for exactly this case. A malformed response never becomes a hypothesis, so it leaves NO ROW at all, only a log line and a counted call, which is a second reason it must be logged distinctly. Second failure case, added: catching ProviderUnavailable here fails the spec. That is ai-006's, and asking a different model the same failed question is the wrong response to an answer that was wrong; the two fallbacks ending at the same destination is what makes this the likeliest error in the item. Third failure case, added: a ceiling reached without the template being produced, or a template produced without the attempts that led to it being recoverable, fails the spec -- the fallback and the record of why it fired are one deliverable. Refs adds: ai-003, ai-004, db-002, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md sections 3, 8 and 10.

Automated grounding check. Input: a schema-valid hypothesis and the evidence bundle it was generated from. Output: a per-item grounded or ungrounded determination, a grounding_passed flag on the hypothesis, and a logged catch rate per generator arm. Constraints: this is the load-bearing safeguard, because constrained decoding guarantees shape but says nothing about whether the rule IDs inside the items exist in the bundle; the catch rate is a reportable evaluation result, not merely a safety net. Failure case: a hypothesis citing rule ID RF-NOISE-999, which is absent from the bundle, must be caught and flagged or rejected rather than passing on the basis of well-formed structure. Refs: FR-512, NFR-202, US-R1, AC-06, evb-002, ai-007, eval-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.5. Amended 2026-09-19, on agreeing evb-001's composition, and the amendment adds a failure case this item cannot currently catch. evb-001 now carries superseded claims -- a claim anom-013 suppressed because a higher rule had already claimed the zone -- in their own field outside the evidence list, because such a claim is a competing explanation that was rejected and dropping it would make the bundle assert more confidence than the system has. That honesty creates a hole here. This item verifies that a cited rule id exists in the bundle; it verifies existence and not appropriateness. So a hypothesis citing a superseded explanation as supporting evidence would pass grounding on the basis that the rule id does appear in the bundle, and the safeguard would certify the exact error it exists to catch -- reading two rules' disagreement as two rules' agreement. The check must therefore distinguish citable evidence from contextual content: the evidence list and the superseded field are both in the bundle and only the first may be cited in support. Second failure case, added: a hypothesis whose supporting evidence cites a claim from the superseded field must be caught and flagged or rejected, rather than passing because the identifier resolves. Recorded as untestable on the current corpus if the companion measurement shows anom-013's suppression never fires, in which case this is proved by unit tests over constructed bundles and the corpus demonstration is owed to a second producing rule. Refs adds: evb-001, anom-013. The companion measurement has been taken and the condition above is met: measurements/corpus/ladder_suppression.py records 188 claims bid and 0 suppressed across corpus v2, so no bundle built from this corpus carries a superseded field at all. This item's second failure case is therefore proved by unit tests over constructed bundles, and its corpus demonstration is owed to a second producing rule alongside anom-013's arbitration itself. Amended 2026-09-25, on reading what this item has to plug into, and the amendment pins five things. (a) The generator arm must be declared where the check is wired in and never inferred from the hypothesis, which carries no record of what produced it -- the same argument ai-009 settled for a refused call, which has no result to read an arm off either. (b) A catch rate over zero checks is not zero: never-caught-anything and never-ran must not arrive identically, so the rate is three-valued and an unmeasured arm says so, which is evb-001's typed-absence principle applied to a reported result. (c) The check must derive its citation key independently of ai-002, because ai-002 is the oracle: the template groups its citations on the (rule_id, finding_type) pair and this item resolves on the same pair, so a shared derivation would make a defect in that key invisible -- the template would emit wrongly-keyed citations, the check would resolve wrongly-keyed citations, the two would agree, and both would be wrong. Asserted by walking the import graph rather than promised in a comment, following ai-007. (d) Near misses are reported alongside the verdict, which they do not change: a citation whose rule id is present in the bundle under a different finding type -- the exact confusion the two-identifier citation exists to catch, anom-012 borrowing anom-010's rule id -- and a citation that would have matched but for case or spacing. Matching is exact, because normalising would silently repair model output and understate a catch rate eval-005 reports as a result; "14 catches" and "14 catches, 11 of them one rule's findings mistaken for another's" are different findings and only the second says anything. (e) Third failure case, added, and it is one this item does not catch: a citation naming a real finding with a false sentence attached passes, because the statement is prose and only the two identifiers are resolved. Recorded as a property of the item rather than left for an examiner to find -- judging whether a statement is true of the finding it names is eval-004's scoring, not this. Two smaller decisions settled here: only the evidence list is citable and not the bundle's own top-level rule id, since citing the claim as support for itself is circular; and where a pair appears in both compartments the evidence wins, the superseded verdict being reached only when the pair is genuinely absent from the evidence. Refs adds: ai-002, ai-009, eval-004.

Run-level call budget. Input: a configured maximum number of model calls or maximum spend for a run. Output: the run aborts with a clear reason when the budget is exceeded, and the calls made so far are recorded. Constraints: this is in-code and independent of the provider-console hard cap, which is the backstop; per-call token and cost logging is in place from the very first call, not retrofitted. Failure case: a retry loop exhausting the budget without aborting, or aborting without recording what was already spent, fails the spec. Refs: FR-513, FR-514, ai-007, eval-005. Amended 2026-09-22, three changes, all found while planning the build. (1) "A MAXIMUM NUMBER OF MODEL CALLS OR MAXIMUM SPEND" NAMES TWO THINGS OF UNEQUAL STANDING, and the "or" makes it possible to configure a run with no working guard at all. A call count can be checked BEFORE a call is made, so the ceiling refuses the call rather than noticing it; spend cannot, because cost is not known until the answer comes back, so a spend ceiling fires one call late by construction. Worse, the number is not always there: ai-003's Usage.cost_usd is float | None precisely because a locally hosted model genuinely costs nothing per call, so a spend ceiling on the local arm silently enforces nothing. The call budget is therefore THE guard and is required; the spend ceiling is an optional secondary tripwire and is documented as late and possibly inert rather than presented as an equal alternative. Both are stated explicitly by the caller, neither defaults, following ai-007's ceiling and GenerationConfig.model_id. (2) HOW THE RUN ABORTS IS THE PART THAT WOULD HURT IF LEFT UNSAID. Both fallbacks catch generation failures -- ai-006 on ProviderUnavailable, ai-007 on GenerationRefused -- so a budget exhaustion shaped like a generation failure would not stop the run: it would quietly finish the campaign on template output while the run reported itself as hosted, which is exactly the failure ConfigurationError was carved out of the GenerationError tree to prevent. BudgetExceeded is therefore NOT a GenerationError, and a test asserts that neither fallback catches it. Second failure case, added: a budget exhaustion that either fallback converts into a template hypothesis fails the spec. (3) WHERE THE BUDGET SITS RELATIVE TO ai-007 IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN A DETAIL. The ceiling exists for a retry loop, so the budget must wrap the ARM and the correctness fallback must wrap the budget; the other order counts one call per bundle and misses every retry, which is the only failure mode the item names. Third failure case, added: a budget that counts one call per bundle rather than one per attempt fails the spec. Two consequences follow for the record it keeps. A refused call still consumed tokens, so the ledger takes its usage from GenerationRefused's model call; and an UNPRICED call is unmeasurable rather than free, so total spend is a stated LOWER BOUND whenever any call reported no cost and the ledger says how many did -- a spend figure that quietly omits the calls it could not price is worse than none, and eval-005 reports actual cost as a result. One budget instance spans a whole run and therefore both model arms, because ai-006's hosted-to-local fallback is still one run; each arm's wrapper declares its own GeneratorKind, because a refused call has no result to read the generator from and that is precisely the call eval-005 has to attribute. The template arm is not wrapped: it makes no call and costs nothing, and counting fallbacks against a model budget would abort a run for doing the safe thing. Recommended values, numbers rather than principles: 200 calls per run, five times the largest plausible scored run and still trivially cheap, against a provider-console cap of GBP 20 which is the backstop that works when the code is the broken thing. Refs adds: ai-002, ai-003, ai-006, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 5.

Generator provenance surfaced in the UI. Input: a hypothesis carrying its generator field. Output: a visible indicator on the hypothesis card and detail view naming the producing generator. Constraints: a hypothesis produced by either fallback path is visibly distinguishable from a primary-arm one; degradation is shown, never hidden. Failure case: a template-fallback hypothesis rendering identically to a hosted-arm one fails the spec, because the analyst would not know the AI layer had degraded. Refs: FR-713, NFR-204, US-A8, ai-006, ai-007, hyp-001, api-004.

Run assembly for a model arm. Input: which arm to build (a GeneratorKind and the provider name behind it), a dated model id, the frozen generation parameters, the call ceiling, an optional spend ceiling, optional per-1k prompt and completion prices, a retry ceiling, a shared CallBudget and GroundingLedger, and an injected provider registry. Output: one object holding the generator a caller hands a single bundle to -- the arm wrapped in ai-009's budget, wrapped in turn by ai-007's correctness fallback with ai-002's template as the replacement and ai-008's GroundingChecker as the injected check -- together with the budget and the grounding ledger, which are read after the run because eval-005 reports both as results. Constraints: the wrapping order is fixed and asserted, budget inside fallback, because outside it the budget counts one call per bundle and misses every retry, which is the only failure ai-009 names, and both arrangements produce hypotheses so a wrong one has no symptom. The arm is named once and the three components that need it -- the budgeted wrapper, the grounding checker, and the provider looked up in the registry -- all derive it from that single argument, because a GenerationResult does not carry an arm that a refused call could be read from and nothing else can detect a disagreement; spend attributed to one arm and catches to another is a silently wrong reported result rather than an error. The template is never budgeted and never wrapped, following ai-009: it makes no call, and counting a fallback against a model budget would abort a run for doing the safe thing. One budget and one grounding ledger span a whole run and therefore both model arms, so both are inputs rather than things this creates per arm. Nothing here reads the environment except through ai-004's own credential lookup: the model id, the parameters and the prices are campaign facts persisted verbatim beside every hypothesis, so a value taken from the environment would let two machines run different campaigns with nothing in the results saying so -- the failure the dated-model rule already exists to prevent, arriving by another route. Failure case: supplying exactly one of the two prices is refused, because cost then silently evaluates to nothing on every call while a configured spend ceiling reports itself as enforced -- ai-009's unpriced-is-unmeasurable rule applied where the configuration is made rather than where it is read. Second failure case, agreed 2026-09-25: the spend ceiling stays optional, but a spend ceiling supplied with no prices at all is refused for the same reason and is the commoner shape of it -- this is the only place that sees the ceiling and the prices together, since ai-009 never learns whether the arm it wraps can price a call and ai-004 never learns whether a ceiling was set. Third failure case: a GeneratorKind of template is refused, since the template makes no call, needs no credential, and is the thing both fallbacks fall back to. Deliberately excluded: this assembles and does not run. Iterating bundles, storing results through db-002 and reporting through eval-005 is a separate job, and keeping them apart is what lets the pre-flight three-bundle smoke test need nothing that does not already exist. Refs: FR-501, NFR-202, ai-002, ai-003, ai-004, ai-007, ai-008, ai-009, db-002, eval-005, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 12. Corrected while building, same day: the input list above names both the ceilings and a shared CallBudget, and those are the same thing said twice -- the ceilings live inside the budget, which spans the run. The budget and the grounding ledger are the inputs; the ceilings arrive within the budget. This is also what makes the second failure case checkable at all, since CallBudget exposes max_cost_usd and this is therefore the one place that can see a spend ceiling and the absence of prices at the same moment. And the first failure case is met by construction rather than by a check: the two prices are a single frozen pair requiring both, so exactly one price is unrepresentable rather than refused, following ai-003's preference for making the bad state unconstructible. A price of zero or less is refused, because a zero price makes every call cost 0.00 and that is a number standing in for unknown, which is what ai-009 forbids. Amended 2026-09-27, on building ai-012. AssembledArm.generator is typed as ai-003's port, and the port's generate returns the delivered hypothesis and DROPS the refusals -- so an ungrounded refusal, which carries the parsed hypothesis db-002 appends beside the row that replaced it, is lost at precisely the caller that cannot afford to lose it. The recorded path is therefore exposed on the assembled arm as its own member rather than reached by narrowing the port type at a call site: the three-bundle smoke test reached generate_recorded through the narrowed attribute and got away with it because measurements/ sits outside mypy, and ai-012 in app/ would not. Failure case added: an assembled arm that can only be asked through the lossy method fails the spec, because the loss has no symptom -- every bundle still gets a hypothesis and the catch rate still reports a number, with no rows behind it.

Hypothesis Detail header. Input: a hypothesis from GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}. Output: title, status, confidence pips, affected area, and time window rendered in the detail header, with a zone map thumbnail and a mini timeline. Constraints: confidence renders through the ui-001 primitive; status is one of New, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Inconclusive; the map thumbnail goes through the MapView boundary. Failure case: an unknown hypothesis ID rendering an empty header rather than an explicit not-found state fails the spec. Refs: FR-711, FR-715, ui-001, map-001, api-004, nav-001.

Supporting evidence with traceability markers. Input: a hypothesis supporting_evidence list and its grounding results from ai-008. Output: one row per evidence item showing source, finding, a rule-ID chip, and a grounded marker. Constraints: grounded state is exposed non-visually so tests assert on it rather than on styling; an ungrounded item is displayed and marked as ungrounded, never silently removed. Failure case: hiding an ungrounded evidence item fails the spec, because concealing it removes the analyst's ability to judge the failure. Refs: FR-711, NFR-202, NFR-204, US-A4, ai-008, hyp-001.

Uncertainty and alternative explanations. Input: a hypothesis evidence_against_or_uncertainty and alternative_explanations fields. Output: both sections rendered on Hypothesis Detail, adjacent to supporting evidence rather than behind a disclosure. Constraints: both are always rendered; an empty list renders an explicit none recorded state so absence is visible rather than ambiguous. Failure case: collapsing alternatives behind a hidden accordion, or omitting the section when empty, fails the spec, since the point is to prevent anchoring on one interpretation. Refs: FR-711, NFR-201, US-A5, ai-001, hyp-001.

Decision-support disclaimer. Input: none. Output: the text Decision support only, analyst judgement is final, rendered on Hypothesis Detail. Constraints: always present, not conditional and not dismissible; consistent with the framing in the README and on every screen. Failure case: the disclaimer absent from the rendered detail view, or present only in a tooltip, fails the spec. Refs: FR-712, NFR-303, NFR-304, hyp-001.

Analyst verdict submission. Input: an analyst activating confirm, reject, needs more evidence, or false positive on Hypothesis Detail. Output: a POST to /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}/feedback, a persisted feedback row, an updated hypothesis status, and the new status reflected in the UI. Constraints: exactly four verdicts; the change survives a reload, because a verdict that is not persisted is not human-in-the-loop validation; status transition follows the documented state set. Failure case: a failed POST leaving the UI showing the new status while the database still holds the old one fails the spec. Refs: FR-601, FR-602, US-A6, AC-09, api-005, hyp-001.

Analyst note and verdict validation. Input: a verdict with an optional free-text note. Output: the note persisted alongside the verdict and shown in the hypothesis feedback history. Constraints: the note is optional and never required to submit a verdict; input is validated at the API boundary. Failure case: an unrecognised verdict value must be rejected with 422, must persist no feedback row, and must leave hypothesis status unchanged. Refs: FR-603, FR-604, NFR-402, api-005, fbk-001.

Batch runner. Input: a scenario type, parameter distribution, base seed, and run count between 20 and 30. Output: N completed runs per type, each with recorded parameters, seed, ground truth, and detector output, executed unattended. Constraints: the entire batch is reproducible from the base seed; a single failing run is recorded and skipped rather than aborting the batch. Failure case: a batch that cannot be reproduced from its recorded base seed fails the spec, since every downstream metric would then be unverifiable. Refs: FR-1001, FR-205, US-R2, scn-001, scn-003. Amended 2026-09-30, before any code, on measuring what this item already has and reading what it asks for. Five findings, and the item closes on a measurement rather than on new behaviour. First, three of the four output clauses are satisfied by scn-003 as built: a batch takes a scenario type, a parameter set, one base seed and a run count bounded at 20 and 30, produces that many runs unattended, and each run row carries its recorded parameters, its own seed and the answer key scn-002 wrote. Second, the reproducibility constraint holds and is now PROVED, which it could not have been when this item was written. Measured over the live database: 380 of 380 runs re-derive their own seed exactly from the base seed, batch index and batch size recorded on their own row, across five separate batches -- the three base seeds behind corpus v2, the development batch, and a batch generated from the screen on 2026-09-30. Zero runs carry no batch provenance. What made the measurement available is scn-008 and nothing here: before it the base seed was printed by the batch summary and never stored, and of the base seeds behind the first 240 runs exactly one survives anywhere, so this item's only failure case was UNTESTABLE RATHER THAN FAILING for the whole time it read as outstanding. That is the useful shape of the finding -- an item whose single failure case cannot be evaluated is not a passing item, and nothing in the backlog said so. Third, the 'detector output' clause is MOVED TO anom-015 rather than withdrawn, and the distinction matters because dropping it would bury a real gap. Four grounds for moving it off this item. (a) The clause predates the detection layer: this item's refs name scn-001 and scn-003 and no anom item at all, so it specified an output that had no producer when it was written. (b) Running detection inside generation would couple a corpus to the detector policy. eval-003 records thirteen detector settings beside the seeds precisely because changing one moves every catch rate, precision and latency on the same hours -- so a corpus generated under a 6 dB threshold could not be re-scored under 8 dB without regenerating 300 hours of observations, and the two-stage split is what makes the same hours re-scorable. (c) Findings are derived and regenerable by design, which is why db-008 replaces per run per rule and why db-007's never-delete rule deliberately does not reach them; a batch that stored them would persist the cheap half of the pipeline while coupling the expensive half. (d) It is moved and not dropped because nothing else owns it, and the consequence is visible: the detection chain is composed only inside measurements/corpus/detection_metrics.py, and no route serves what it produces, so the application cannot display an injected anomaly or a detection of one at all. Fourth, an observation recorded here rather than fixed, because it belongs to anom-015. detection_findings currently holds rows left by whichever measurement script ran last over whichever runs it touched, with nothing on the row recording which, and NO COLUMN FOR THE DETECTOR POLICY IN FORCE. It is harmless today for a specific reason: findings_for_run is read only by tests, and every figure of record re-derives the chain from the observations rather than reading stored rows. It stops being harmless the moment a screen reads them, which is exactly what api-012 would do. Fifth, what this item still needs is one test and one measurement, not new behaviour. scn-008 already asserts that a constructed run spec re-derives its own seed; nothing asserts that what was PERSISTED re-derives, and those differ -- the parameters go through a JSON round-trip, the base seed comes back as text to be cast, and the batch index indexes a list. That is a database-tier test and it is what this item's failure case is actually about, which is the record rather than the function. Beside it, a committed measurement and log carrying the figure above, so the proof is repeatable rather than quoted from a session. Added failure cases: a run row recording a base seed that its own seed does not derive from fails the spec; and this amendment must not be read as putting detection outside the build -- an amendment removing the detector-output clause without anom-015 existing would fail the spec, since the requirement it serves (FR-1001, a corpus ready to be evaluated) would then be met by nothing. Refs adds: scn-008, db-008, db-007, eval-003, anom-015, api-012, api-002.

Detection metrics. Input: batch run outputs and their recorded ground truth. Output: precision, recall, F1, false positive rate, false negative rate, and detection latency per scenario type. Constraints: latency is in simulated time per anom-009; normal-baseline runs contribute to the false positive rate, which is why anom-008 must hold; metric definitions are documented alongside the numbers. Failure case: a batch with zero true positives must produce a documented undefined or zero precision rather than dividing by zero. Refs: FR-1002, US-R2, US-R5, AC-10, anom-008, anom-009. Amended 2026-09-16, on measuring the staging yield after scn-006. Two additions the campaign plan depends on. First, sizing: with parked aircraft no longer eligible, 10 of 40 runs in the second batch staged nothing at all, against 3 of 80 before. At a 75 per cent yield the target of 100 to 150 staged incidents needs roughly 200 runs rather than 150, and at about 2.1 staged aircraft per staging run that gives some 315 staged aircraft, which is ample for the per-aircraft figures. The extra cost is compute and is small. Second, and more important than the count: a run of a staged scenario type that staged nothing is a baseline run wearing the wrong label, and it must be excluded from every metric rather than only from recall. anom-011's measure_recall already refuses it, but counting it as a staged run in precision or in the false-positive rate would be worse than counting it in recall, because a rule that correctly reports nothing on it would be scored as having missed something. The exclusion is recorded with the metrics, as a count, so a reader can see how many runs were dropped and why. Failure case added: a metrics report that does not state how many runs were excluded for staging nothing fails the spec. Refs adds: scn-006, anom-011, anom-012. Amended 2026-09-18, on anom-006 closing for the second time, and the amendment constrains how these metrics may be reported rather than how they are computed. Of the five scenario types, three produce positive detections and two produce correct silences. rf-sensor-fault, gnss-degradation and ambiguous-mixed-evidence are decided 60 of 60; normal-baseline and aircraft-coverage-gap are silent 60 of 60. So every recall, precision and F1 figure this item produces is computed over three arms and not five, and must say so. Three constraints follow. First, the aircraft-coverage-gap arm contributes no true positives and must never be counted as a tested positive: its correct non-detections are correct only because no rule judges that arm. Second, that arm is nonetheless not redundant with normal-baseline and should be reported as a discriminating negative rather than as a missing positive, because it tests something the baseline cannot -- that the RF rules stay silent while something real is happening on the track side, which is a specificity test against cross-modal leakage. research_scope.md scoped it that way from the outset, calling scenarios 3 and 4 deliberately negative discriminating cases where correctly not claiming interference is a first-class evaluation result. Third, ambiguous-mixed-evidence must not be reported as an independent third positive arm without the qualification that it is currently indistinguishable from rf-sensor-fault in reportable output, for the reason recorded on anom-006. A per-scenario-type table that lists five rows without these three notes overstates what was tested. Refs adds: anom-006, anom-013. Corrected 2026-09-18, later the same day, on measuring whether ambiguous-mixed-evidence is actually redundant. The amendment above said that arm must not be reported as an independent third positive arm without qualification, and that stands, but it understated what the arm contributes and the correction matters for how the evaluation chapter reads. Measured by measurements/corpus/arm_rf_identity.py over all 60 shared seeds: rf-sensor-fault and ambiguous-mixed-evidence stage the same receiver, the same elevation and the same window in 60 of 60, and their RF observation streams are identical byte for byte in 60 of 60. The only staged difference is that the ambiguous arm also removes five aircraft. The pair is therefore a controlled comparison differing in exactly one variable, and both arms being decided possible_sensor_fault 60 of 60 is a positive result rather than a null one: a simultaneous track-side disturbance does not perturb the RF verdict. rf-sensor-fault alone cannot establish that, having no disturbance to be immune to. So the arm is a negative control living inside a positive one and must not be dropped as a duplicate. Report it as such: not as a third independent positive arm, and not as redundant, but as the immunity check, quoting the identical-stream figure so a reader can see the comparison is controlled. The arm's other intended role, supplying anom-013 with a second competing claim, remains unavailable while anom-006 is closed. Amended 2026-09-30, before building it, and the amendment settles what the figures are indexed by rather than adding outputs; six changes and one guard. First, THE WORD RECALL MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS IN THIS PROJECT AND THEY DIFFER BY MORE THAN TWENTY POINTS. anom-011 measures recall per staged aircraft on the track side -- 82 per cent for gnss-degradation, 59 on each suppression arm, 67 over 900 staged aircraft. This item measures recall per run over reportable output, which the 2026-09-18 amendment above already frames as a per-arm count over 60 runs. Different questions, different denominators, one word: unlabelled in the write-up a reader can quote either for the other. Both are reported, labelled by their denominator, and neither is averaged into the other; anom-011 is referenced here for its exclusion rule -- a staged-type run that staged nothing -- and never as a source of a recall figure. Second, recall is indexed by truth and precision by prediction. Recall's denominator is the runs of a scenario type; precision's is the runs given an anomaly type. A per-scenario-type row carrying both puts two denominators under one label, and the two coincide only where no arm is ever reported as another, which is a result to state rather than an assumption to build on. F1 is emitted only where an arm and a reportable anomaly type correspond one to one and the report names where they do not -- which today is everywhere, rf-sensor-fault and ambiguous-mixed-evidence both being decided possible_sensor_fault. Third, the classification is ONE MULTI-CLASS CONFUSION over the reportable anomaly types and not three independent binary problems. anom-013 guarantees at most one claim per zone, so a run reported as the wrong type is two events -- a false negative for the type staged and a false positive for the type claimed -- and three binary tests would count it once and lose half of it. Fourth, there are TWO false-positive rates and they are never pooled. A report on normal-baseline is invention from nothing; a report on aircraft-coverage-gap is cross-modal leakage, something real happening on the track side that no reportable rule judges, which is the specificity test the 2026-09-18 amendment already argued that arm exists for. Both arms are correct-silence arms and they fail in different ways, so one pooled figure over 120 runs cannot say which failed; they are reported as from-nothing and cross-modal, each over its own 60. Fifth, latency is CONDITIONAL ON DETECTION and must say so. anom-009 gives a value per claim and this item aggregates, so the aggregate exists only over the runs that produced a claim: printed beside a recall below one it reads as a property of the arm when it is a property of the successes. It is therefore reported per arm over the claims that were made, carrying the count it was taken over. Sixth, EVERY RATE IS None OVER AN EMPTY POPULATION, which answers this item's original divide-by-zero failure case with the convention eval-005 and ai-008 already use rather than with the documented zero that wording permitted: a precision of 0.0 on an arm nothing was ever claimed for reads as a measured failure, and 0.0 is the value that destroys the distinction the failure case was written to protect. The original wording is superseded, not extended. The guard: this item REFUSES TO REPORT A FALSE-POSITIVE RATE FOR A CORPUS WHOSE QUIET RUNS DID NOT PASS anom-008's CONTROL, which makes the constraint above -- 'normal-baseline runs contribute to the false positive rate, which is why anom-008 must hold' -- mechanical rather than a sentence in a document; a rate computed over runs whose detectors may never have run is a measurement of the pipeline and not of the rules. Failure cases added: computing a from-nothing false-positive rate without a passing anom-008 verdict fails the spec; and reporting either false-positive rate without stating anom-008's coverage figure -- two reportable types of three, anom-006 being registered as not exercised -- fails it too, since a rate quoted over the types that exist reads as a rate over the types the system claims to have. The arithmetic and the classification bookkeeping live in app/evaluation/metrics.py over outcomes the caller has already read, touching no database, following the rest of that package. Refs adds: anom-011, eval-005, research_scope.md.

Metrics export. Input: computed metrics from eval-002 and eval-005. Output: CSV and JSON files suitable for direct use in thesis tables and charts, including the run parameters and seeds that produced them. Constraints: exports are self-describing, so a table in the write-up can be traced back to the exact runs behind it. Failure case: an export omitting the seeds and parameters fails the spec, because the numbers would then be unreproducible. Refs: FR-1003, NFR-601, AC-10, eval-001, eval-002. Amended 2026-09-30, before building it and after building eval-002, and the amendment is mostly about what 'self-describing' has to mean to be checkable. Six changes and three failure cases. First, SEEDS DO NOT REPRODUCE THESE NUMBERS. The failure case above names 'the seeds and parameters', and for the detection figures the parameters that matter are not the scenario's but the DETECTORS': anom-001's 6 dB threshold, anom-014's 10 s minimum episode, anom-010's 100 s gap threshold and 30 s contact freshness, anom-012's 60 km radius, anom-004's cluster radius, anom-005's corroboration threshold and the corpus bounding box. Change the threshold from 6 dB to 8 and every figure in the table moves with the base seed unchanged, so an export carrying seeds alone satisfies this item as first written and is not reproducible. Both are exported and the distinction is stated: a seed reproduces the hours, a policy reproduces the figures. Second, there are TWO provenance records and they do not flatten into one field. The detection figures rest on a corpus identity, its base seeds, its run count and the detector policies; the campaign figures rest on a model id, the frozen generation parameters, the prompt digest and eval-004's sample seed and population. A single seeds list makes neither reproducible, and the two are separately dated besides -- the corpus was regenerated on 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29, the campaign ran on 2026-09-28 against the dev batch. Third, traceability is a RESOLVABLE KEY and not a header comment. A comment line breaks a CSV parser, and the thing that actually travels into a write-up is one row pasted into a table, which loses every line above it. So a short digest over the provenance record is the first column of every exported row and one file resolves it, following the pattern `ai-004` already uses for the prompt: change any provenance field and the digest changes, so a stale row fails to resolve rather than quietly citing the wrong corpus. Fourth, NO RATE IS EXPORTED WITHOUT THE COUNTS IT WAS COMPUTED FROM in adjacent columns. `eval-002` is careful that a rate over an empty population is None and never 0.0, and a CSV writes None as an empty cell, which a spreadsheet and a dataframe both read as zero -- so the convention dies exactly at the export boundary, which is `anom-008`'s `as_json` dropping its band population one item along. A sentinel token was rejected because it makes a numeric column non-numeric and the item asks for charts; the counts beside the rate are `eval-005`'s own rule and leave a blank cell unambiguous, since the denominator says whether it is zero or unmeasured. Fifth, THE EXPORT COMPUTES NOTHING: no rounding, no percentages, no column totals, every exported value appearing verbatim in the metrics handed to it. `eval-007`'s governing rule for the scoring pack, applied here for a different reason -- an exporter that rounds makes the quoted number differ from the computed one, and the CSV is what gets quoted. Sixth, CSV COLUMN NAMES ARE DERIVED FROM THE EXPORTED KEYS rather than retyped, because a hand-written header is precisely where `recall_per_run` becomes `recall` and `eval-002`'s two-recalls guard evaporates at the one boundary that guard exists for. Failure cases added: a CSV carrying a rate without its numerator and denominator fails the spec; an export recording scenario seeds but not the detector policies fails it, since the figures are not regenerable from what it carries; and an exported row whose provenance digest resolves to nothing fails it. The export is `app/evaluation/export.py`, pure like the rest of that package: computed metrics and an assembled provenance in, named files as text out, no path and no filesystem, so a measurement script decides where anything lands. A provenance record that is missing a field is REFUSED AT CONSTRUCTION rather than exported incomplete, which is what turns this item's failure case from something to check into something that cannot happen. Refs adds: eval-005, eval-007, anom-008, ai-004, scn-008.

Anonymised two-arm hypothesis export for blind scoring. Input: a stratified sample of evidence bundles (approximately 5 per anomalous scenario type, ~20 total) processed by the hosted and template generators, one scored generation per arm per bundle. Output: a scoring pack containing the rendered hypothesis pairs in randomised within-bundle order with identical formatting across arms, the arm key written to a separate file, and a blank score sheet per rater carrying the dimensions defined in docs/scoring_rubric.md. Constraints: the arm is not inferable from the exported text, including from formatting artefacts, field ordering, or whitespace; the corpus and the rubric are fixed before the campaign runs, not adjusted after seeing results; the local arm is excluded from scoring and its exclusion is recorded rather than silent. Failure case: an export in which the template arm is identifiable by its phrasing or layout invalidates the blind comparison and fails the spec. Refs: FR-1004, US-R3, ai-002, ai-004, eval-006, docs/scoring_rubric.md, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.9. Amended 2026-09-21, per docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 9: the stratification as written cannot be satisfied, and the reason is a fact about the built system rather than about the plan's intent. Five scenario types exist but they produce TWO KINDS OF BUNDLE -- gnss-degradation gives possible_interference_zone on 20 of 20, rf-sensor-fault gives possible_sensor_fault on 21 of 21 and ambiguous-mixed-evidence gives the same on 20 of 20 by design, aircraft-coverage-gap produces nothing on 75 of 80 because its rule was closed as unbuildable on this corpus, and normal-baseline produces nothing by design as anom-008's control. Five per anomalous scenario type would require bundles from a type that produces none. The sample is therefore STRATIFIED ON BUNDLE KIND -- 10 interference and 10 fault, keeping the planned 20 bundles and 40 hypotheses -- and the producing scenario type is recorded on every sampled bundle, so the rf-sensor-fault against ambiguous-mixed-evidence split can be examined afterwards without having been stratified on. Two consequences the scorer's briefing must carry. Size: interference bundles are 3.2x larger, so balancing by kind gives a scorer roughly equal numbers of long and short documents where stratifying by scenario type would have given three-quarters short ones. Constancy: the template arm emits exactly four citations on all 41 bundles, because both bundle kinds happen to carry four kinds of evidence, so its length does not vary with the event where a model's does, and any dimension rewarding completeness or concision is scored against a constant for one arm. N is fixed at 1 scored generation per bundle per arm at temperature 0, with a separate non-scored N=3 determinism probe held outside this pack -- see section 8 and the Phase 8.5 gate. Amended 2026-09-27, after the three-bundle trial, and this amendment changes a PRE-REGISTERED PLAN rather than an implementation detail, so it is argued for here and recorded in docs/scoring_rubric.md's change log rather than made quietly. (1) THIS ITEM IS TWO PASSES SEPARATED BY THE CAMPAIGN, AND NOTHING IN THIS BACKLOG PRODUCES ITS STATED INPUT. The sample is written here as an input and no item draws it, so the selection is this item's FIRST deliverable, executed and committed BEFORE any scored request is made -- which is what the pre-registration claim actually rests on, the instrument predating the results being worth nothing if the corpus does not. The export of rendered pairs is the second pass, after ai-012 has run. Selection is a seeded draw over the stored bundles, stratified 10 possible_interference_zone and 10 possible_sensor_fault per the amendment above, recording the chosen bundle ids, the seed and the rule, because a sample nobody can redraw is a sample nobody can check. (2) N IS RAISED TO 3 GENERATIONS PER BUNDLE PER MODEL ARM, OF WHICH THE FIRST IS SCORED and the other two are never scored. N was fixed at 1 on the ground that temperature 0 with a fixed seed returns the identical answer, so a second generation would add nothing to score; the trial measured that premise FALSE -- 4 of 5 comparable repeated pairs differed, one changing the set of cited evidence kinds and one losing an alternative's falsification test between runs -- so a single generation is one draw from a distribution, and the observed variation lands on dimensions 1 and 3, the two the study cares most about. Scoring all three was considered and rejected on a ground that is not cost: it takes one rater from 280 values to 840 and from about 90 minutes to four and a half hours, and 280 is quoted in the participant information sheet and on the ethics approval form, so raising it is a re-consent rather than a configuration change. The human corpus therefore stays at 20 bundles x 2 arms = 40 items and 280 values, and the two unscored generations become eval-005's grounding-variance population, which that item already asks for and which was previously to be supplied by a separate probe over a handful of bundles. The template baseline is still generated once, and that N=1 is safe for exactly the reason the model arm's was not: there is no provider in it, so its repeatability is a property of the code rather than a claim about someone else's serving stack. (3) THE SCORED GENERATION IS THE FIRST AND IS NOT SUBSTITUTED WHEN IT FELL BACK. A first generation the model failed and ai-002 answered is what the hosted arm DELIVERED on that bundle, and substituting generation 2 would delete every fallback from the scored corpus and flatter the arm under test -- the flattering-by-omission failure, chosen after the fact, which is why the rule is fixed now. Consequence for Part A, which must reach the scorer before scoring begins: two hypotheses under one pack may be identical or nearly so, and that is expected rather than an error in the pack. Failure case added: a scored pack whose sample was drawn, or whose scored generation was chosen, after any generation had been read fails the spec. Refs adds: ai-007, ai-012, docs/scoring_rubric.md change log. Both passes built 2026-09-28. The SAMPLE is app/evaluation/sampling.py (17 tests) and the EXPORT is app/evaluation/pack.py (17 tests), each at 100% and neither touching a database -- bundles, hypotheses and scenario types all arrive as the caller has already read them, so the corpus decision and the rendering are both checkable without Docker. Three decisions made while building. The A/B shuffle is keyed PER BUNDLE from one seed, so the whole pack is reproducible and no bundle's draw depends on the one before it. The scored row is found by ORDINAL and never by position, since taking it by row order would silently export a different generation on any bundle whose rows were written in another order -- and on a bundle whose first generation fell back, that is exactly the substitution this item forbids. And the arm-vocabulary check reads GeneratorKind rather than a spelled list, deliberately EXCLUDING the words 'model' and 'baseline': an explanation may honestly say 'a propagation model', and a check forbidding it would fail on real prose while catching nothing a marker could use. Failure cases added, all refusals rather than blanks: a bundle with only one arm in the record (an unpaired item scores one arm with nothing to subtract it from), a bundle with no evidence pack supplied (nothing to judge evidence use against), and a missing hypothesis (rendered blank it becomes a missing section, which the rubric tells a marker to score 1, so an absent item would score its arm at the floor).

Per-arm AI statistics. Input: all hypothesis generations from a campaign, across every generator that ran. Output: grounding catch rate, grounding variance across N generations per bundle, retry rate, actual cost, and wall-time, each broken down by generator arm. Constraints: recorded per arm rather than in aggregate, because the comparison between arms is the result; computed over all N generations, which is a separate and larger population than the one-generation-per-arm corpus that eval-004 exports for human scoring; the local arm is reported here when it ran as a fallback even though it is not blind-scored, since fallback frequency is itself a reliability result; cost and wall-time are write-up material and make the deliberate-spend claim concrete. Failure case: reporting a single pooled grounding catch rate across arms fails the spec, since it hides the very difference being measured. Refs: FR-1005, US-R3, ai-008, ai-009, eval-003, eval-004. Amended 2026-09-27, while building it, and the amendment widens one output rather than changing the item. GROUNDING VARIANCE ACROSS N IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THE WRONG THING TO MEASURE ALONE: the three-bundle trial passed every citation of every generation and held confidence stable on every comparable pair, so that figure will report 1.0 and say nothing. What actually moved was the free prose and, on one bundle, the SET of evidence kinds cited -- which is the finding that raised N from 1 to 3 in the first place. Agreement is therefore computed over the three things that can vary across a bundle's N generations -- the grounding verdict, the confidence, and the set of (rule_id, finding_type) pairs cited -- and over the SET rather than the sequence, because two answers citing the same kinds in another order have not disagreed about anything this study asks. Agreement is undefined over a single generation and is computed only over bundles asked more than once, so the template arm, always N=1 by design, reports None rather than a perfect score it did not earn. Two additions on the same argument. FALLBACK RATE PER ARM is reported, because how often a model arm had to be replaced is a reliability result in its own right and is only measurable at all since db-002 recorded which arm was ASKED beside which generator answered. And RETRY RATE IS A RATE OVER ATTEMPTS, not over generations or bundles: the question is what fraction of the calls this arm made produced an answer nobody could use, which is comparable across arms and against the spend, where over generations it would be an average number of retries wearing the word rate and could exceed 1.0. Every rate is None over an empty population rather than 0.0, following ai-008's ledger -- a fallback rate of 0.0 on an arm nobody asked reads as perfect reliability. cost_is_complete is also PER ARM, since a local arm prices nothing while a hosted one prices everything and one flag for the run would call the hosted figure incomplete on the strength of the other's. Input adds: the stored hypotheses, as a mapping the caller has already read, so the join stays in the open and the arithmetic is checkable without a database -- eval-004's sampler takes scenario types the same way. Failure case added: a mapping missing any generation's hypothesis is refused rather than skipped, since dropping it would leave the agreement figures and the counts beside them describing different populations with nothing saying so. Refs adds: ai-007, ai-012, db-002. Measured 2026-09-30, running it end to end over the scored campaign for the first time, and the measurement SETTLES THE AMENDMENT ABOVE AGAINST ITSELF. That amendment predicted, from the three-bundle trial, that grounding agreement would report 1.0 and say nothing while the SET of cited evidence kinds would be the dimension carrying the result -- the trial having seen the cited set move on one of its three bundles. Over the scored twenty, asked three times each at temperature 0 with a fixed seed, all three dimensions report **1.000**: identical grounding verdict, identical confidence, identical set of cited evidence kinds, on every one of the twenty. The widening was still right to make -- a report carrying grounding agreement alone would have printed 1.0 and been unable to say whether anything else had moved -- but the prediction about which dimension would carry the result does not hold at twenty bundles, and the write-up must say so rather than quoting the three-bundle expectation. What that leaves is a sharper claim than the amendment expected: across sixty generations the only thing that differed between repeated answers was the **free prose**, which none of these three measures and which `eval-004`'s blind scoring is what actually examines. The rest of the figures: hosted 60 generations over 20 bundles, 60 checked, **0 caught**, 0 refusals and therefore a retry rate of 0.000, 0 fallbacks, 60 calls, $0.854364, 334.197 s; template 20 generations, 20 checked, 0 caught, 0 calls, 0.008 s; local never asked, and every one of its rates is `None` rather than 0.0 -- the first live demonstration of the rule this item is built on. Because nothing was refused and nothing fell back, this campaign says nothing about `ai-007`'s retry path: it reports that the path never fired, which is not the same as reporting that it works. A note on the instrument rather than the result: the campaign's own artefact does **not** round-trip into the object these figures are computed from -- `ai-012` serialises the budget and the ledger as figures rather than as contents, and this item needs the individual calls because it reports cost and tokens PER ARM while the stored budget is pooled across the run. The figures above are therefore computed from a record rebuilt in `measurements/corpus/campaign_statistics.py`, with each call's spend taken from the generation it produced and its model id, frozen parameters and verbatim response taken from the row `db-002` stored for it, so nothing is invented -- and then reconciled twice against what the campaign recorded at the time, the rebuilt calls having to sum to the stored pooled budget exactly and the rebuilt ledger having to match the stored per-arm counts, either failing refusing the whole report. A failed grounding check cannot be rebuilt at all, the artefact recording THAT a hypothesis failed and never WHICH citation did, so that path raises rather than inventing a finding; it is unexercised here because nothing failed. Serialising enough for the record to round-trip is owed on `ai-012` and is DELIBERATELY NOT BEING DONE, with a stated trigger rather than left as lingering debt: it would not help this artefact, which was written before it; re-running the campaign costs money and would replace a pre-registered corpus; and every benefit it carries -- a per-arm cost needing no rebuild, an unreachable call made visible, a catch explainable rather than counted -- is conditional on a second campaign, which requires `ai-005` and is not planned. The trigger is exactly that: DO IT FIRST IF A SECOND CAMPAIGN IS EVER RUN. What is kept instead is the finding, which is the part with thesis value -- an artefact designed to be readable is not automatically one the next stage can consume, and two items passed independently with the join between them never exercised. One exposure is closed rather than argued away: the rebuild depends on the eighty stored rows, and this project has lost a corpus once, so the reconstructed per-call split is committed beside the record in `measurements/corpus/scored_campaign_calls.json` -- written only after the reconciliation passes, so it cannot exist in an unchecked state. The claim the write-up may make is therefore that these figures are regenerable from the artefact, the stored rows and the committed script, and not that they are regenerable from the artefact alone.

Blind-score ingest and inter-rater agreement. Input: completed score sheets from two independent raters over the eval-004 scoring pack, plus the separately held arm key. Output: per-dimension mean and distribution per arm, the hosted-versus-template difference per dimension, and quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa computed across the whole double-scored corpus. Constraints: the arm key is joined only after both sheets are ingested, so scores cannot be attributed to an arm during entry; every scored item carries two independent scores, so agreement is reported over the full corpus rather than a subset; the pre-registered adjudication rule is applied to disagreements rather than chosen after inspecting them; a rater who scored only part of the corpus is reported as partial coverage rather than silently averaged. Failure case: computing kappa over items scored by one rater only, or silently substituting a single rater's score where the second is missing, overstates agreement and fails the spec. Refs: FR-1004, FR-1006, US-R3, eval-003, eval-004, docs/scoring_rubric.md.

Docker Compose full stack. Input: docker compose up on a clean machine with Docker installed. Output: frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL with PostGIS running and reachable, with migrations applied and the app usable end to end. Constraints: no cloud account and no external service required; the local model server is a host process referenced by config through host.docker.internal, never a Compose service, because Docker Desktop on macOS does not pass Metal through. Failure case: a Compose file declaring the model server as a service fails the spec, and a first-run start that requires an undocumented manual step fails AC-12. Refs: FR-1101, FR-1102, NFR-105, AC-12, ai-005. Defect found 2026-09-14 by looking at what `make up` reported: the frontend container sits permanently unhealthy while serving correctly. The healthcheck probes http://localhost:8080/ from inside the container; nginx declares `listen 8080;`, which binds IPv4 only; and `localhost` inside that image resolves to ::1 first. Confirmed from inside the container: 127.0.0.1 succeeds, [::1] and localhost are both refused. The check is what is wrong rather than the server -- nginx has no reason to bind IPv6 behind Docker's bridge -- so the probe targets the literal address nginx actually binds. Why it matters beyond tidiness: a service that is always unhealthy can never report *becoming* unhealthy, so the signal was not merely wrong, it was unavailable, and `depends_on` conditions or any later orchestration would inherit that. Added failure cases: a healthcheck naming a host nginx does not bind fails the spec, and a healthcheck naming a port nginx does not listen on fails the spec. Both are asserted structurally against compose.yaml and frontend/nginx.conf together rather than against either alone, because the defect exists only in the relationship between them -- each file is individually correct.

CI pipeline. Input: a pushed commit or opened pull request. Output: backend pytest, frontend vitest and build, lint on both halves, and a basic dependency audit, each reported as a separate check. Constraints: no Trivy, no container scanning, no deployment step in v1; a failing test fails the pipeline rather than warning. Failure case: a commit that breaks a frontend test passing CI, or a lint failure reported only as a warning, fails the spec. Refs: FR-1103, NFR-404, US-E6, AC-12.

Root Makefile as the containerised command surface. Input: a make target run from the repo root. Output: generate runs a scenario batch in a container; demo runs generate then brings the stack up with a build; build builds all images; migrate applies the Alembic revisions against the running database (db-001); db-test-create provisions the disposable test database with the PostGIS extension, idempotently; test runs the backend pytest suite and the frontend vitest suite in containers; up starts the stack; down tears it down with orphans removed. Constraints: every target delegates to docker compose, so the root Makefile needs no host toolchain beyond Docker; backend/Makefile is retained unchanged for local venv work and the two are not merged; this item is blocked on ops-001, since the Compose file must exist first. Amended 2026-08-27: migrate added, and test-backend no longer runs with --no-deps, because db-001's tests need the postgis service healthy and --no-deps starts the backend container alone -- a test target that silently skipped every database test while reporting success would satisfy the letter of this item and defeat its purpose. The containerised run is therefore the authoritative coverage number, since it is the only one with a database. This item enumerates its targets, which makes it the thing that must be amended whenever one is added. Amended 2026-09-04: replay is added, running python -m app.replay in the backend service (adp-007). It deliberately does not use the pipeline service, whose command names a module that does not exist, so make generate is broken today and stays that way until scn-003 -- recorded here because a target that cannot work is this item's own first failure case, and it is being carried knowingly rather than fixed by pointing it somewhere convenient. Amended 2026-08-30 on two counts. First, db-test-create is added and test-backend depends on it: db-001's tests need a test_em_fusion database carrying the PostGIS extension, which was created by hand while db-001 was being built. A manual step nobody has written down is an undocumented first-run requirement, which is what AC-12 and ops-001's own failure case forbid, and it also produces this item's second failure case by a different route -- the tests skip, and the target reports success. Second, this text previously required the native backend/Makefile gate to omit live-database modules when their tests skip. That machinery was specified before db-001 was built and turned out not to be needed: alembic_config resolves paths and reads a committed ini, so it is provable in the unit tier, and app/db/migrations.py reaches 100 per cent natively with no omission at all. The omission set is therefore empty today and the clause has been removed rather than left describing something that does not exist; the rule returns with db-003, where the PostGIS repository genuinely cannot be exercised without a database. Failure case: a target that succeeds while the underlying compose command fails, or a test target that reports success when either suite had failures, fails the spec. A second failure case: migrate reporting success against a database where no revision was applied, or test reporting success while every database test skipped. Refs: FR-1104, US-E7, AC-12, ops-001, ops-002, db-001, adp-007. Amended 2026-09-12: generate is claimed by scn-003. That item creates app.pipeline -- the module the pipeline service has named since this file was written -- so the target stops failing on a missing module and runs a scenario batch, which is what this item's first sentence has always said it does. The carve-out recorded on 2026-09-04, that generate is knowingly broken and stays so until scn-003, is lifted when scn-003 passes and not before. PIPELINE_ARGS carries the scenario type, base seed and run count through to the container, mirroring REPLAY_ARGS on the replay target; the target set is unchanged, so the enumeration above needs no new member. Amended 2026-09-12 again, on landing scn-003: `generate` now runs `python -m app.pipeline` with PIPELINE_ARGS and the carve-out above is lifted. A target is added at the same time -- build-pipeline, which refreshes the pipeline image before a batch runs in it. It exists because the pipeline service builds its own image from ./backend rather than sharing the backend service's, so `build-backend` does not refresh it, and `generate` was the one target with no build prerequisite at all. Found by running it: the cached pipeline image predated SQLAlchemy becoming a dependency and the batch died on an import before reaching any code of its own -- this item's own first failure case, a target that fails while the compose command underneath it is fine. Measured on the first working run: 20 runs of aircraft-coverage-gap over ten simulated minutes each, 52.5 s wall time, about 510,000 rows. Amended 2026-09-19, adding `measure`. Every figure this project quotes comes from a script in backend/measurements, and every one of them has been run by hand-writing a docker compose invocation -- the same class of command that destroyed the corpus, since a hand-written invocation is where a wrong environment variable gets supplied. `measure SCRIPT=<path>` runs one of them in the backend container with PYTHONPATH set and the corpus selector passed through, so the run command lives in the Makefile beside every other one rather than in a reader's shell history. It takes --no-deps, because a measurement reads the database that is already running and must never start one, and it does not take a database URL at all: the only URL it can reach is the application's own, which is the correct target for a measurement and the catastrophic one for a test. Failure case: a `measure` recipe that accepts or sets TEST_DATABASE_URL fails the spec, because that is the variable whose misuse ops-004 exists to catch and a command surface must not offer a second route to it. Refs adds: ops-004, NFR-602.

The database test tier refuses to run against a database holding real data. Input: the TEST_DATABASE_URL the database-tier fixtures are pointed at, and the DATABASE_URL the application uses. Output: the fixtures run normally against a genuine test database, and abort before touching anything otherwise. Two independent checks, because they fail in different ways. First, an identity check: if the two URLs name the same host, port and database, the tier aborts. Second, a population check performed immediately before the DROP: if the target holds more scenario runs or observations than a test fixture could plausibly have created, the tier aborts and names the counts it found. The second is a heuristic with a stated threshold and it is the one that matters, because the first only catches URLs that are spelled identically -- the same database reached as 'localhost' and as a container hostname is two spellings of one disaster. Failure cases: a database-tier run pointed at a database holding a generated corpus must abort with the row counts in the message and must not execute DROP SCHEMA; and a legitimate empty test database, or one holding only the handful of rows a previous test in the same session created, must run normally. Written 2026-09-19, after I destroyed the corpus. conftest.py already carried the argument for this in a comment -- the test variable is deliberately not DATABASE_URL, so that the tier can never run a DROP against whatever database somebody happened to have configured, and two variables make that impossible by construction rather than by care. The construction was sound and I defeated it by hand, passing the application's own database as TEST_DATABASE_URL on a docker compose run to avoid waiting for make test-backend, which provisions a separate database for exactly this reason. Every targeted test run then dropped the schema and rebuilt it empty. 540 scenario runs and 20.7M observations across two corpora were lost; corpus v2 is regenerable because scn-008 and CORPUS_V2_PLAN.md record its three base seeds and no generator code has changed since, and corpus v1 is not, because its seeds were never written down -- which is the precise failure scn-008 was built to prevent and which has now cost the thing it was built to protect. Note what the lesson is not: it is not that the convention was wrong. A safety property that holds only while every command is typed correctly is a convention, and this item converts it into a check. It also breaks db-007's never-delete rule, which until now had never been broken by anything. Refs: db-007, scn-008, NFR-602, ops-003, docs/qa.md.

Collapsible navigation rail. Input: the analyst's stored collapse preference and the current route. Output: the rail rendered at one of two widths -- expanded at 280px with text labels, collapsed at 56px with icons only -- plus a control that toggles between them. All three entries and the current-page marker render in both states. Six decisions. First, collapsed is an icon rail rather than a hidden one. Fifty-six pixels keeps all three destinations one click away and keeps the current-page indicator visible; hiding the rail entirely reclaims 56 more pixels and costs both, since nothing then says which screen the analyst is on and every screen change becomes expand-then-choose.
