DESIGN.md already describes sidebar navigation as slim icons with labels, so the collapsed state is that line with the labels dropped rather than a new idea. The three icons are hand-authored inline SVG path data carried on the route declaration itself, which keeps nav-001's fifth decision intact -- the three screens stay declared once, so a fourth screen cannot be added in a place that has no icon. No icon dependency is added, consistent with TanStack Query and frontend coverage tooling both being deferred rather than taken mid-item. Second, the preference lives in browser storage rather than in the URL, and this does not contradict nav-001. The hash carries the route because the hash answers where you are, and a screen has to be linkable and nameable in a fault report. Rail width answers how one person likes their chrome. In the hash it would give a single screen two addresses and make every shared link impose one analyst's layout on the next reader. localStorage is per-viewer and survives a reload, which is the entire point of a preference. Every read and write is guarded, because storage throws in a private window and can return an absent or corrupt value. Third, expanded is the default -- on a first visit, and whenever the stored value is missing, unreadable or not one of the two expected values. That keeps nav-001's ten tests green without amendment, since they render the app and assert three labelled links, and it means a failed storage read degrades toward the state that shows more information rather than less. Fourth, the toggle is a button rather than a link. nav-001's entries are anchors precisely because they are navigation and carry addresses; the toggle changes no address and goes nowhere, so it is a button carrying aria-expanded and an accessible name stating what it will do. Rendering it as an anchor would be the mirror image of the error nav-001 avoided. Fifth, collapsing hides labels and never entries. FR-701 fixes the rail at three, and a collapsed rail that drops an entry or buries one behind an overflow changes the entry count in a state the analyst can reach. Each collapsed entry keeps its accessible name, so the rail reads identically to assistive technology in both states: the label is visually hidden, not removed. Sixth, this item constrains nav-002 rather than building it. nav-002 specifies the system-health strip in the navigation footer (FR-702) and is unbuilt. A collapsing rail hands it a question it would not otherwise have had: what the strip shows at 56px. The constraint this item places on it is that a collapse must not be the thing that hides system health, which is the same posture op-001 takes for the data-mode badge -- unconditional, not dismissible, not collapsible. That badge lives in the top status bar and is untouched here. Note also that nav-001 cites FR-709 for the health strip where the requirement is FR-702; nav-002 cites it correctly and is the authority. Out of scope, deliberately: auto-collapsing at narrow viewports, which needs a breakpoint decision and belongs to responsive layout rather than here; and the width transition, which is cosmetic and is not asserted. Scope note: DESIGN.md's Panels section states that sidebars have fixed widths, giving 280px for the primary nav. The expanded width is unchanged but fixed stops being true, so one sentence is added there as part of this item rather than leaving the design spec disagreeing with the build. Only the root DESIGN.md is amended; the per-screen copies under frontend/src/assets/Design are generated references. Failure cases. A collapsed rail offering no visible control to expand it, which is a state the analyst cannot leave, fails the spec. Fewer than three entries rendered while collapsed, or an entry reachable only after expanding, fails the spec. The current-page marker rendering only in the expanded state fails the spec. A stored value that is absent, corrupt or unreadable crashing the rail or blanking it, rather than resolving to expanded, fails the spec. Writing the preference into the URL hash fails the spec. Collapsed entries losing their accessible names, so the rail announces three unlabelled links, fails the spec. A toggle rendered as an anchor, or rendered without aria-expanded, fails the spec. Collapsing or expanding changing which screen is rendered fails the spec. Known limit, recorded rather than tested: that a collapsed label is visually hidden while remaining in the accessibility tree is not assertable from this project's test stack. jsdom performs no layout, and the testing convention forbids asserting on CSS classes in favour of analyst-visible behaviour, so the assertable half is the surviving accessible name and the visual half is proven by looking at the running interface. This is the third blind spot recorded on this project, after the frontend coverage gap and the caption defect scn-004 shipped. Refs: FR-701, FR-702, NFR-303, US-A1, nav-001, nav-002, op-001, scn-004, DESIGN.md sections Sidebar Navigation and Panels, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.7.

Frontend data access for scenario control. Input: a poll interval, the backend base URL, and a configuration the analyst submits. Output: the Scenario Control screen reading GET /api/v1/scenario/runs on a timer and posting to POST /api/v1/scenario/start, with the fixture retired from its runs table. Six decisions. First, the fetch goes in the one module that already reaches the network. api-003 made src/lib/api.ts the only module allowed to call fetch, and src/test/transport.test.ts holds it by scrubbing comments and string literals out of every other module's source and scanning what is left. A second module would be a second place the endpoint is known, and changing it would stop being a one-file change. The two scenario calls therefore join the picture's there. Second, the fixture had two halves and only one of them was pretending. scenarioControlMock carries a scenario library -- the five type ids with their names and descriptions -- and a list of runs. The runs were the problem: real seeds from a real batch, indistinguishable from what the database holds, which is what nav-001 had to put a sentence on screen about. The library is not data about the system's state at all: it is the closed set of five types the generator can produce, already parity-checked against the enum, with presentation copy attached, and no endpoint serves it. So the library moves to src/lib/scenarioLibrary.ts and becomes what the app imports, the mock imports it in turn and keeps its shape for the tests that already use it, and App stops importing a mock. Deleting the mock outright would have removed something nothing serves. Third, the table shows nothing until the first answer arrives, and never shows mock rows. This diverges from api-003 deliberately. The picture falls back to the example payload before its first response because a map with nothing on it cannot be developed against, and the degraded badge carries the warning. A runs table is different: an empty table is perfectly legible, and rows lifted from a real batch are not distinguishable from the database's own by anyone reading them. So the fallback here is emptiness rather than fiction, and the screen says which of the two states it is in. Fourth, a 202 has to say something. Start returns at once and the first row can take ten seconds to appear, so a control that changes nothing visible reads as a dead button -- the exact thing scn-004 avoided by disabling controls that were not wired. The acceptance is shown, and what it shows is the base seed the server used: the number an analyst needs in order to reproduce the batch, and one the server may have drawn rather than been given. Fifth, reset and replay stay unwired, for different reasons, and both keep their disabled control with its stated reason rather than acquiring a handler that does something adjacent. Reset has no endpoint at all: api-006 deferred it until there is an in-flight batch worth abandoning. Replay has an endpoint that cannot express it: start takes a configuration and a batch is between 20 and 30 runs (scn-003), so replaying one recorded run is not a request this API can make. Sixth, the poll mounts and unmounts with the screen. nav-001 moved the picture's poll into its own route so that it stops when the analyst is looking at something else; a second five-second poll running against an endpoint nobody is watching would undo that. Failure cases. The runs table rendering fixture rows at any point after this item fails the spec -- that is the whole point of it. A second module calling fetch fails the spec and transport.test.ts. Start reporting success without naming the seed the server used fails the spec, because a batch whose seed the analyst was never shown is a batch nobody can reproduce. A failed poll clearing the runs already on screen fails the spec: the posture is api-003's, which keeps stale truth over fresh nothing. The note on screen still claiming the runs are a fixture, once they come from the database, fails the spec. A screen importing the mock fails the spec, because App.tsx is the seam and no component may know where its data comes from. Scope: two functions in src/lib/api.ts, one hook, the App wiring, the library moved out of the mock, and the note's sentence rewritten. It builds no reset and no replay. Refs: api-003, api-006, scn-003, scn-004, nav-001, FR-806, FR-807, NFR-503.

One batch at a time. Input: POST /api/v1/scenario/start while a batch started earlier is still running. Output: 409 Conflict naming what is already in flight -- its scenario type, its base seed and when it started -- and no second batch, no run rows, no second thread. A start arriving when nothing is running behaves exactly as api-006 describes. Seven decisions. First, why this exists at all, measured rather than supposed. The backend was found hung on 'QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out', serving nothing -- not slow, unserviceable, with its container reporting unhealthy -- after several batches had been started from the screen in quick succession. Measured afterwards: one batch is harmless, adding a single connection while /health stays 200 throughout. So the fault is concurrency, not batches. Every start spawns another unbounded daemon thread (api-006's second decision) and every thread borrows the API's one engine (db-003: one Engine per process), so batches compete with request serving for a pool whose ceiling is SQLAlchemy's default fifteen, because nothing sets pool_size or max_overflow. Bounding the count at one removes the observed cause. It does not make the pool safe against arbitrary load, and this item claims only the former. Second, the state lives in the API process and is never written to the database, which looks like the lazy choice and is the correct one for db-007's own reason. A batch cannot outlive the process running it, so a persisted 'running' flag would be a claim no crash could retract: kill the container mid-batch and the row still says a batch is in flight, locking the button until somebody edits the database. db-007 rejected exactly this when it refused a three-valued status column, on the grounds that a process killed outright cannot record its own death. In-memory state has the property that argument wanted: a restart genuinely means nothing is in flight, and the state says so by not existing. Third, this is sound only while the API is one process. Uvicorn is started with no --workers flag in both the Dockerfile and the compose command, so there is exactly one worker today. Adding workers would give each its own guard and silently restore the defect, so a test asserts the single-worker invocation alongside the guard itself -- the guard and the condition it depends on are asserted together, because the guard alone would keep passing while becoming untrue. Fourth, the guard is released in a finally, always. A batch that raises must free it, or one failure disables the button until the container is restarted -- which would convert a recoverable error into an outage, and would be a worse defect than the one this item fixes. This is its sharpest failure case and it is tested by launching a batch that raises and then starting another successfully. Fifth, taking the guard is atomic. A check followed by a set lets two simultaneous requests both observe 'nothing running' and both proceed, which defeats the item entirely while passing any test that starts batches one after another. The guard is taken under a lock, and the test issues two starts concurrently and asserts exactly one 202 and exactly one 409. Sixth, the refusal says what is already running rather than that something is. An analyst who cannot tell which batch is in flight, or how long it has been, cannot tell whether to wait or to investigate -- and the information costs nothing, since the guard is holding it in order to exist. Ground truth is not among it, per api-009. Seventh, the screen surfaces the refusal in its own words. api-010 already shows what was accepted; refusing without telling anybody is the failure this project keeps recording, and a 409 that renders as nothing would look exactly like the defect that prompted this item. The message names the running batch and says the button will work when it finishes. Out of scope, and stated so the item is not mistaken for solving them. It does not cancel a batch -- reset remains deferred, and this item is what makes reset meaningful later by giving it something definite to cancel. It does not report a batch that *failed* after acceptance, which remains the open honesty gap: this item tells the analyst a batch is running, not that one died. It does not give batches their own engine, which stays available and unowned as the complementary fix. It does not set pool_size. Failure cases. Two simultaneous starts both accepted fails the spec. A batch that raises leaving the guard held, so no further batch can start without a restart, fails the spec. A 409 whose body does not name the running batch fails the spec. Persisting the in-flight state to the database, so a restart reports a batch that cannot be running, fails the spec. The screen receiving a 409 and rendering nothing, or rendering it as an indistinguishable generic error, fails the spec. Running the API with more than one worker fails the spec while every other test still passes, which is why the invocation is asserted. Scope: a small guard object with an atomic take-and-release, the route consulting it, the launcher releasing it in a finally, the 409 shape, one sentence of screen copy, and tests including a concurrent one. Refs: api-006, api-010, api-009, db-003, db-007, ops-001, FR-806, NFR-503. Amended 2026-09-30, before implementation, on six findings from reading the code this item describes. The scope line said "one sentence of screen copy" and that is the one part of it that was wrong. First, the screen has no channel for a backend refusal at all, so the seventh decision builds one rather than wording one. The scenario feed already computes an error value for exactly this purpose and the seam drops it: App.tsx destructures the feed without it, the screen declares no prop for it, and the screen's own error state is form validation only. The consequence is larger than this item -- every 422 the start endpoint returns today is invisible on screen, so an unknown scenario type or a batch outside the run bounds is refused by the backend and the analyst sees nothing at all. This item's fifth frontend failure case is therefore already failing, for a different status, and it is the same fix. Scope adds the prop, the wiring at the seam, and a test that a refusal reaches the rendered output. Second, the lease crosses the launcher seam, because the launcher cannot release what it has not finished. The item said the launcher releases the guard in a finally; launch_batch starts a daemon thread and returns within microseconds, so a release there would free the guard before the batch had opened a single run row -- which is not a weaker guard but the absence of one, since the second start would always be accepted. The release therefore belongs to the thread, so what the route takes is a lease and the lease travels to the launcher as an argument, changing BatchLauncher's signature. That keeps the seam honest in both directions: a recording launcher that never releases is a faithful simulation of a batch still running, and one that releases at once simulates a batch that finished, so both sides of the guard are testable without a corpus or a database, which is the property api-006 built that seam for. Third, the guard is taken in the handler body and never in a dependency. A dependency is resolved whether or not the body validates, so a guard taken there would be consumed by a request that never started a batch -- and this item's neighbours are exactly those requests: an unknown type, a batch outside the run bounds, an incident beginning after its run ends. Added failure case: a 422 that consumes the guard, so a valid start following an invalid one is refused 409 while nothing is running, fails the spec. Fourth, the 409 body carries facts and never prose. It names the in-flight batch's scenario type, base seed and start time as fields, and the sentence an analyst reads is composed on the screen. Two reasons. Every other piece of user-facing copy on that screen is already there -- the validation refusals, the acceptance note -- so a server-composed message would split the screen's voice across two codebases and make its tone depend on the API. And a body of fields is assertable field by field, where a sentence is assertable only by substring, which is the weaker test of the two. Ground truth is not among the fields, per api-009. Fifth, wall clock is the correct clock here, recorded because this project has the opposite defect on file. anom-009 exists because detection latency would otherwise have reached for created_at -- wall clock in a simulated-time costume -- and the rule that came out of it is that a time about the simulated world is taken from the simulated world. The start time here is not about the simulated world: it answers how long a real process on a real machine has been running, which is what tells an analyst whether to wait or to investigate. So it is the wall clock in UTC deliberately, and saying so here keeps it from reading later as a repeat of the mistake anom-009 was written about. Sixth, the single-worker invariant is asserted across three invocations rather than one. backend/Dockerfile carries two CMDs, development and production, and compose.yaml overrides both with a third; none passes --workers today, and an assertion covering one of the three would keep passing while the invariant became untrue in either of the others.

Record a run's batch provenance on the run row. Input: the base seed a batch was generated from, the run's index within that batch, and the batch's run count. Output: those three values stored in scenario_runs.parameters alongside the run's own derived seed, so that every run names the batch it came from. Constraints: the three values together must make the run's own seed re-derivable and therefore checkable -- derive_seeds(base_seed, batch_runs)[batch_index] must equal the stored seed -- because a recorded number nobody can check is barely better than a lost one, and scn-001's whole argument is that a run is reproducible from what its row records; they are provenance and not generation inputs, so RunSpec.from_record must accept and ignore them rather than refusing the row, and must not treat their absence as a fault, since every one of the 240 runs generated before this item has no batch recorded and those rows stay readable; a run generated outside a batch carries none of the three rather than inventing a batch of one, because a synthetic value here would be indistinguishable from a real one and the field exists precisely to be trusted. Failure cases: a row whose stored seed does not equal the seed re-derived from its recorded batch provenance fails the spec, and so does a from_record that refuses a row carrying these fields. Written 2026-09-18, and the reason it exists is a gap found while planning the corpus regeneration. BatchSummary has always carried base_seed and has always printed it in the batch report, and the value then reached nothing durable: scenario_runs holds each run's own derived seed and nothing holds the seed that produced it. Of the base seeds behind the 240 stored runs exactly one survives anywhere, in a pre-registration note that happened to quote it, which is why a run-for-run paired comparison across the regeneration is not available and the regenerated corpus has to be reported as a new corpus rather than a repeat. The cost of having recorded it would have been three integers per row. Refs: FR-205, NFR-601, scn-001, scn-003, scn-004, db-001, eval-002.

Index observations by the run that produced them. Input: the existing observations table. Output: a btree index on scenario_run_id, added by an Alembic revision like every other schema change. Constraints: it is an index and therefore changes no data, no query result and no behaviour -- only cost, which is why it can be added after the fact without invalidating anything measured before it; the revision must be reversible, because an index is exactly the kind of change that should be droppable without touching rows; and it belongs in a migration rather than applied by hand, since a schema the migrations cannot reproduce is a schema a fresh clone does not get. Failure cases: a query selecting one run's observations that still plans a sequential scan after the revision fails the spec, and so does a downgrade that leaves the index behind. Written 2026-09-18, found while re-measuring the regenerated corpus. observations holds 20.7 million rows in 12 GB and carries only a primary key and a GiST index on location, so scenario_run_id -- the column nearly every detection measurement filters on, and a foreign key declared ON DELETE CASCADE -- had nothing behind it. Every measurement in backend/measurements queries one run at a time, so a single pass over the corpus was performing three hundred sequential scans of the whole table, which is the difference between a measurement taking thirty minutes and taking seconds. The cascade has the same problem for the same reason. Refs: NFR-602, db-001, db-007, db-008, adp-002, scn-003.

Campaign run over a fixed bundle sample. Input: an ordered, explicitly supplied sample of stored evidence bundles; one assembled model arm (ai-011) and ai-002's template baseline behind ai-003's port; how many generations to take per bundle per model arm; and the session factory every result is written through. Output: one campaign record -- per bundle, per arm, per generation: the stored row id, the arm that was ASKED, the generator that ANSWERED, whether it fell back, ai-008's verdict, every refusal with its category and attempt number, and the usage -- together with ai-009's budget report and ai-008's ledger, which are what eval-005 reports and what ai-011 hands back for exactly this reason. Constraints: the sample is an INPUT and is never invented here, because docs/scoring_rubric.md fixes the corpus before the campaign runs and a runner that could choose its own bundles could choose them after seeing a result; an empty sample and a repeated bundle are both refused, the second because a bundle generated twice under one campaign would be counted twice in every per-arm figure while looking like two bundles. The model arm is asked through ai-007's RECORDED path and never through ai-003's port method, which returns the delivered hypothesis and drops every refusal -- and the refused-but-parsed ones are precisely the rows db-002 appends and never replaces, stored with grounding FAILED beside the hypothesis that replaced them. The template baseline is grounding-checked into the SAME ledger, because ai-002 is grounded by construction and so anything flagged on it is a defect in the check rather than in the baseline, and it is NEVER budgeted and never wrapped in a correctness fallback, per ai-009 and ai-011: it makes no call, and a fallback from the template to the template is not a fallback. The generation ordinal lives in this record and NOT in the schema, because it is a fact about the experiment rather than about the hypothesis and a deployed system generates once -- the record is therefore an artefact that must be serialised and kept, not a diagnostic. Failure cases: a per-bundle generation failure is recorded and skipped rather than aborting the campaign, following scn-003 and eval-001, because a campaign that dies on bundle 14 of 20 has spent the money and kept nothing; but BudgetExceeded and ConfigurationError abort the whole run, and a campaign that caught either per bundle would make the budget inert and finish every remaining bundle on template output while reporting itself as hosted -- the failure ai-009 carved BudgetExceeded out of the GenerationError tree to prevent, arriving one layer up. Second failure case: a run that stores the delivered hypothesis and discards the ungrounded ones fails the spec, since the catch rate would then be a number with no rows behind it. Third failure case: a run that records which generator answered but not which arm was asked fails the spec, since a fallback is then indistinguishable from the baseline. Deliberately excluded: drawing the sample (eval-004's first pass), rendering the scoring pack (eval-004's second), and computing the per-arm statistics (eval-005). Refs: FR-501, FR-508, FR-513, US-R3, NFR-602, ai-002, ai-003, ai-007, ai-008, ai-009, ai-011, db-002, eval-004, eval-005, docs/scoring_rubric.md, docs/phase9_hypothesis_layer.md section 12. Amended 2026-09-28, after the first scored campaign, and the finding cost two scored generations. A CAMPAIGN AGAINST A RATE-LIMITED PROVIDER MUST PACE ITSELF, or it silently shrinks a pre-registered corpus. The run made 60 calls as fast as it could against a 30,000 tokens-per-minute ceiling with prompts averaging 4,909 tokens -- about six calls a minute -- and the provider refused five of them. ai-004 maps a 429 to ProviderUnavailable, which is a GenerationError, which this item records and skips: correct handling for a provider that is down and wrong for one that is merely busy, since the refusal itself says 'try again in 5.09s'. Two of the five were GENERATION 1, so two of twenty bundles came out with no scored hosted generation at all -- taking the marking corpus to 18 bundles, 36 items and 252 values, against the 20/40/280 quoted in the participant information sheet and on the ethics approval form. A silently smaller corpus is the worst shape this failure could take: everything succeeded, every figure reported, and the shortfall appears only when the pack is built. The remedy is a pause between model calls, REQUIRED and with no default on ai-007's max_attempts rule -- how fast a run may ask is a decision about the provider it is pointed at, and one made by omission is one nobody chose. It is deliberately NOT a retry: retrying inside this item would blur ai-006's availability fallback into ai-007's correctness one, which the whole layer is built to keep apart, and pacing prevents the condition rather than recovering from it. The sleeper is injected, so the suite can assert the pacing without waiting for it. The template baseline is never paused: it makes no call. Failure case added: a campaign that outruns the provider and records the refusals as skipped generations fails the spec, because the corpus it reports is smaller than the one that was pre-registered and nothing says so.

Readable evidence pack. Input: the same EvidenceBundle and paired PackItems eval-004 already renders; no new data. Output: hypotheses.md in which every block a marker reads is valid Markdown. Six requirements. (a) No space-aligned plain text: the current pack indents its findings two spaces, which is neither a fence nor a code block, so a Markdown renderer reflows nineteen lines into one paragraph and collapses the alignment the layout depends on -- the pack is legible only in a raw editor. (b) The bundle's own claim leads, identified as the evidence item whose finding_type equals the bundle's anomaly_type, required to exist exactly once, which is ai-002's rule and evb-002's exactly-one-row rule one layer up. (c) Remaining findings are grouped on the (rule_id, finding_type) citation key ai-001 defines -- the same pair ai-008 resolves and ai-002 groups on, so this invents no new vocabulary. (d) Every finding row carries its subject, which the current renderer drops: a hypothesis citing 'RF-06:4' cannot be checked against a pack that never says which sensor a deviation belongs to, and evidence use is dimension 1 of five. (e) Repeated known uncertainties are de-duplicated with a count rather than repeated verbatim. (f) Each pack states its position (N of M) and is separated from the next by a rule. Constraint, and the item's hard one: grouping must not replace detail with summary. Every finding stays listed individually beneath its counted heading, because a pack that pre-digests its own findings has done part of the work dimension 1 scores, which would deflate the difference between arms in the direction that flatters the weaker one. Constraint: one renderer for both arms, no branch on PackItem.arm anywhere, BLINDING_GIVEAWAYS unchanged -- eval-004's blinding argument is that a formatting difference is a perfect classifier where prose style is only a hint, and a restructure is exactly where such a difference could be introduced by accident. Failure case: a bundle whose verdict item is absent, or appears more than once, is refused rather than rendered with an arbitrary lead. Failure case: a finding whose subject is empty renders its group without inventing one. Refs eval-004, eval-006, ai-001, ai-002, ai-008, evb-001, FR-402, docs/scoring_rubric.md Part A. AMENDED 2026-09-28, after the first restructure was read by a human and was still a wall: valid Markdown was necessary and nowhere near sufficient. Fourteen table rows repeating 'power_dbm deviated by X dB at its peak' and fifteen repeating 'reporting from this aircraft broke during the window' carry one sentence and N values between them, and the sentence is what the eye has to re-read. So a group of findings is rendered by **factoring the text they share**: the common prefix and suffix become the group's heading, stated once, and each row carries only what differs, gathered under its source. Where the texts are byte-identical the varying part is empty and the group becomes one sentence plus its list of sources. The same factoring applies to known uncertainties within one kind, which is where six sentences differing in one sensor name each became six lines. Factoring fires only when the shared text is substantial, and never mid-word; otherwise the statements are listed, deduplicated with a count. This REPLACES the earlier 'group but never summarise' constraint, whose stated reason was wrong in direction: the template baseline's own citations are summaries, so a pack that summarises makes the baseline read as pure restatement and scores it **lower**, widening rather than narrowing the arm difference, while also lowering the model for the same reason -- the net effect is not predictable in advance, which is exactly why the pack must not be in that business at all. The constraint that replaces it is mechanical and testable: **the pack re-organises values and computes none.** Every measurement rendered must appear verbatim in a finding, an uncertainty or the bundle's own metadata; a count of items the pack itself lists is permitted, because the reader could count them, and is the only arithmetic allowed. No minimum, maximum, mean, range, ratio or total may be introduced, since each of those is a synthesis an explanation could otherwise be credited for. Failure case: a rendering that introduces a number absent from its sources is refused by test rather than reviewed by eye. Refs eval-004, eval-008, ai-001, ai-002, docs/scoring_rubric.md Part A.

The scorer's workbook. Input: the same PackItems, DIMENSIONS and JUDGEMENTS eval-004 writes to CSV. Output: score_sheet.xlsx -- one row per item in pack order, a frozen header, the seven columns headed as the rubric words them rather than as field names, a validated 1/3/5 dropdown on each of the five pass-one dimensions, validated lists on the two pass-two judgements, each column carrying the rubric's own anchor wording as a note, the identifier columns locked, and a second sheet carrying all five dimensions' anchors in full so the handout does not have to be open beside it; and arm_key.xlsx as its own separate workbook, never a tab on the file the marker opens. Constraint: the CSV remains the archival and machine-readable form, and both are written from the same rows in one pass, so the workbook cannot drift from the sheet eval-006 ingests. Constraint: no cell, sheet name, note, header or document property in the marker's workbook may name an arm -- the blinding check that covers hypotheses.md covers this too, or the leak simply moves to the file nobody scanned. Failure case: a dimension with no anchor entry is refused rather than exported with an empty dropdown, since a dropdown offering nothing reads to a scorer as a broken file and to a reader of the results as an unscored dimension. Failure case: a validated list that does not match the rubric's 1/3/5 scale is refused, because a sheet accepting a 4 collects values the pre-registered analysis has no anchor for. Adds openpyxl. Refs eval-004, eval-006, eval-007, docs/scoring_rubric.md.

A glossary in the scoring pack. Input: the bundles eval-004 is exporting. Output: a terms section at the head of hypotheses.md and a matching sheet in score_sheet.xlsx, so the term is reachable both where the evidence is read and where the score is entered -- a scorer working through forty explanations should not have to stop and ask what a track gap is. Covers three kinds of term: the rule ids and finding types that appear as citation keys, which a marker must understand to check a citation at all; the conclusion labels a pack is about; and the recurring domain words in the findings' own prose (baseline, channel, dB, power_dbm, nominal, disc, discontinuity, reference period, rate ratio, smoothing constant, corroborate). Only terms actually present in the exported pack are rendered, so the scorer meets no definition for something they will never see. THE GOVERNING CONSTRAINT, and the reason this item is risky enough to need one: a definition says what a term **denotes** and never what it **implies**. 'An aircraft stopped sending position reports' is a definition; 'an aircraft stopped sending position reports, which can indicate interference' hands the marker the causal link that evidence use -- the first scored dimension -- exists to test, and cause correctness in pass two exists to test again. This is the same failure as a summarising evidence pack (eval-007) in its most dangerous form, because it is reasoning in prose rather than arithmetic. Enforced by a named constant of causal connectives that no definition may contain, on BLINDING_GIVEAWAYS' pattern: the list is the argument, kept in one place, and asserted against every entry. Failure case: a (rule_id, finding_type) pair present in an exported bundle with no glossary entry is **refused**, not omitted -- a silently missing definition is how a marker meets an undefined rule mid-flow, and a rule added later must be defined rather than quietly inherit silence. Failure case: a definition containing a causal connective is refused. Failure case: a definition naming an arm is refused, since the glossary is a third artefact the marker reads and an unscanned one relocates the blinding leak rather than weakening it. Refs eval-004, eval-007, eval-008, ai-001, docs/scoring_rubric.md Part A, docs/qa.md.

Detection pass over one completed run -- the stage missing between generation and everything that reads a finding. Input: a completed scenario run id, the detector policies in force, and a repository. Output: every finding the rules produce for that run persisted through db-008, the reportable claims left after anom-013's ladder, and a record of the policy the pass ran under. IT COMPOSES AND DOES NOT DECIDE: each rule keeps its own logic and is called rather than reimplemented, and what this item owns is the order, which is anom-013's, plus the wiring between one rule's output and the next one's input. The argument for it being an item at all is that the composition exists today ONLY inside measurements/corpus/detection_metrics.py -- baselines, RF episodes, faults, gaps, clusters, fusion, then the ladder -- and measurements/ sits deliberately outside make lint, make type-check, make test and the coverage gate. So the ordering that produces every detection figure this project quotes is the one part of the chain nothing checks, while all eight rules sit at 100% coverage individually. Same class of defect as ai-004 records, where the egress payload was measured against a dict hand-written inside a measurement script while nothing in app/ serialised a bundle: a right number about the wrong object, harder to notice than a wrong number because every check you could run on the measurement passes. ai-011 exists because by the time five parts worked separately, three ways of joining them produced a system that runs perfectly and reports something false; the detection layer has no such item, and this is it. ITS OWN STAGE, NEVER INSIDE GENERATION AND NEVER ON READ. Not inside generation, on eval-001's amended argument: the corpus and the detector settings must stay separable or the same hours cannot be re-scored under a different threshold. Not on read, because the picture is polled every five seconds (api-003) and the chain reads a whole run's observations, so computing it per request would recompute the chain per tick. The cost of one pass is NOT MEASURED, and that figure is what settles whether this stage can be triggered automatically when a batch completes or must stay a separate command -- measured before choosing, on the same footing as anom-014's minimum, scn-007's floor and anom-012's radius. FINDINGS RECORD THE POLICY THAT PRODUCED THEM, and detection_findings has no column for it, so this item carries a migration. Without it a stored finding is unprovenanced: a screen would show figures taken under one threshold while the settings in the repository say another, with nothing able to detect the disagreement. eval-003 settled the same point at the export boundary -- a recorded setting that is not the one in force is worse than none, because it looks like provenance -- and a screen is a second boundary with the same property, so eval-003's REQUIRED_POLICIES is the floor here too. A RUN NOT KNOWN TO HAVE FINISHED IS REFUSED RATHER THAN SCORED: db-007 records the absence of a completion stamp as not known to have finished, which covers a run still going and a run that died, and scoring either gives findings over partial observations that change when the run completes -- so a figure read off the screen would not be the figure the run produces. THE WRITE REPLACES PER RUN PER RULE (db-008): appending would leave a stale set beside a new one with every count including both, which is the defect db-008 was written to prevent and which a re-run under a new policy would trigger every time. Failure cases. A pass that reimplements a rule's logic rather than calling it fails the spec, since the rule and the copy then drift and the measured figures describe neither. A pass that stores findings with no record of the policy in force fails, because a later reader cannot tell whether what is on screen came from the settings it claims. A pass that appends rather than replaces per run per rule fails. Scoring a run with no completion stamp fails. And a pass that silently scores zero rules because a producer was not registered fails, on anom-008's own argument: detectors that ran and found nothing, detectors that never ran and detectors pointed at the wrong observations all produce an identical empty result, so an account of every registered producer is what answers did this look, and never the count. Refs: anom-001, anom-002, anom-004, anom-005, anom-007, anom-008, anom-009, anom-010, anom-012, anom-013, anom-014, ai-004, ai-011, db-007, db-008, evb-001, eval-001, eval-003, api-002, api-003, api-012, FR-1001, FR-301, FR-306. Amended 2026-10-01, before tests, on reading the chain this item lifts and measuring what it costs. Seven findings. First, THE COST, which the item said to measure before choosing the trigger. One run is 1.04-1.29 s, median 1.22 s, across all five arms -- and about 1.0 s of that is READING the run's observations, the rules themselves taking 0.11-0.23 s. The baseline is 11.2 s over 60 quiet runs, once per pass session rather than per run. A 20-run batch is therefore about 35 s end to end, against a batch's own ~105 s, so the answer is that the stage CAN be triggered automatically when a batch completes. It still cannot run per request, and the reason is the baseline rather than the pass: 1.22 s would fit inside api-003's five-second poll, but 11.2 s recomputed every tick would not. The I/O dominance is the figure to carry forward -- this stage is 85% reading and 15% detecting, so anything that makes it faster is a query and not a rule. Second, THE PASS CANNOT COMPUTE ITS OWN BASELINE, so the baseline is a fourth input beside the run, the policies and the repository. anom-002 measures normality per sensor per channel over the corpus's QUIET runs across a trailing window -- 60 of them here -- and not over the run being scored. The item's input list omitted it, which would have produced either a pass that silently baselined against the run it was judging, or one that could not run at all. Third, and following from that, A STORE WITH NO QUIET RUNS CANNOT BE SCORED AND THE PASS MUST REFUSE. Generate one batch of interference runs into a fresh database and there is nothing to baseline against; inventing one from staged runs would measure the incident as normal and report the arm clean, which is worse than refusing because it looks like a detection result. This is anom-008's own argument -- zero is also what a broken pipeline gives -- reached from the other direction. Fourth, THE POLICY RECORD MUST NAME THE QUIET RUNS THE BASELINE WAS TAKEN OVER, not only the thresholds. Two passes under identical settings and different baselines produce different findings and would be indistinguishable in the record, which defeats recording the policy at all. The record's vocabulary is eval-003's REQUIRED_POLICIES verbatim rather than a second spelling, so a pass's provenance satisfies the export's floor by construction and the two cannot drift. Fifth, PERSISTING IS LOAD-BEARING MID-CHAIN AND NOT A FINAL STEP. anom-004 and anom-012 are PostGIS queries over stored rows, so the TRACK-GAP findings must be written BEFORE anom-005 runs -- the shape 'compute everything, then store' is not available, and a pass written that way would find no track evidence and report it as absent rather than as unwritten. Sixth, THE REPORTABLE CLAIMS ALREADY HAVE A PERSISTED FORM AND IT IS NOT THE TABLE BUILT FOR THEM. The `anomalies` table has existed since 0001 and NOTHING HAS EVER WRITTEN TO IT -- no application module, no measurement script -- while evb-001's one-bundle-per-reported-claim is already the established unit, already stored through evb-002, and 103 of them exist. So this stage stores findings and bundles, inventing no third representation, and `anomalies` is recorded as dead rather than quietly adopted; retiring it is a migration this item does not take. Seventh, THE OBSERVATION READER IS ALSO ONLY IN A MEASUREMENT SCRIPT, AND IT INVENTS FIVE FIELDS. `detection_metrics.py` and `bundle_end_to_end.py` each hold their own `obs_for` with raw SQL that hardcodes `source_id="o"`, derives source type and data mode from the observation type rather than reading them, asserts `validation_status=VALID` without checking, and builds a `Provenance` from scratch. `app/db/repository.py` already has `_observation`, which reconstructs all five from the row and picks the payload class by type. The hardcoded mapping happens to agree with what the generator writes, so it is a right answer from a wrong source -- ai-004's defect exactly, and this item's own argument applied to its input rather than its ordering. evb-001's `data_mode` is per item and read off the observations, so a bundle built through the script's reader takes its data mode from a mapping rather than from the record. Scope therefore adds one repository read, `observations_for_run`, reusing `_observation`, which is where FR-904 puts the SQL. Added failure cases: a pass that baselines against the run it is scoring fails the spec; a pass that scores a store holding no quiet runs rather than refusing fails; a policy record naming the thresholds but not the baseline's source runs fails; and a pass that reconstructs observations itself rather than reading them through the repository fails (FR-904). Refs adds: anom-002, api-003, db-004, db-009, evb-002, FR-904. Amended 2026-10-02, after reading this pass from the far side of the API boundary while specifying api-012. Two findings, and both are about what the pass leaves BEHIND rather than what it computes. First, THE PASS PERSISTS ITS EVIDENCE AND NOT ITS CONCLUSIONS, so from any other process its conclusions do not exist. It writes TRACK-GAP and RF-NOISE findings because anom-004 and anom-012 read those rows back, which is the fifth finding above; the two rules at the end of the ladder -- SENSOR-FAULT's attribution and FUSION-SPATIAL's zone, the reportable claims this whole chain exists to produce -- are returned on the Assessment and written nowhere. Inside one process that is invisible, and the sixth finding above is why it was not noticed: it recorded the bundle as the reportable claim's persisted form, which was true of the 103 rows a measurement script had stored and was never true of this pass, since the implementation withdrew bundle storage on eval-004's argument that a pre-registered sample names its twenty bundles by id. So the premise expired between the amendment and the code. THE REPORTABLE CLAIMS ARE THEREFORE WRITTEN AS db-008 FINDINGS, one row per reported claim, replaced per run per rule like every other. That is not the third representation the sixth finding refused: db-008 is one shape every rule becomes with what is rule-specific in details, SENSOR-FAULT and FUSION-SPATIAL are rules, and the reason they had no rows was incidental -- only the rules something later QUERIES were written down. The dead `anomalies` table stays dead. ONLY THE CLAIMS anom-013 REPORTED ARE WRITTEN, never the suppressed ones: a suppressed claim is a competing conclusion and evb-001 carries it in `superseded` precisely so co-occurrence is not read as concurrence, and a suppressed claim stored beside the claim that beat it would be read as two events by every count taken over the table. The consequence is recorded rather than glossed: with bundles unstored, a suppression is not persisted anywhere, so the ladder's own workings are reconstructible only by re-running the pass. Second, NOTHING RECORDS THAT A PASS HAPPENED, and that is unrecordable in the findings table by construction. The write replaces per run per rule INCLUDING AT ZERO, so a run examined and found clean leaves no rows, which is byte-for-byte what a run nobody examined leaves -- and an unprovenanced finding was the thing this item's migration was taken for. This item's own last failure case says an account of every registered producer is what answers did this look and never the count; the account needs somewhere to live. So THE PASS STAMPS THE RUN with when it was examined and the policy record it was examined under, two nullable columns on scenario_runs in a second migration, null meaning not known to have been scored. Nullable and parallel to db-007's completion stamp for db-007's own reason, and the policy beside the stamp rather than only on the findings because a quiet run has no findings to carry it -- a pass recording thresholds nowhere is exactly the case anom-008's measured bands were taken under. Stamped LAST, after every write the pass makes, so a pass that dies midway leaves a run that is not known to have been scored rather than one claiming an examination it did not finish; db-008's replace semantics make re-running the whole recovery, which this item already records. Added failure cases: a pass that returns its reportable claims without persisting them fails the spec, since the conclusions are then unreadable outside the process that computed them and api-012 has nothing to serve. A pass that persists a claim anom-013 suppressed fails. A pass that leaves no record that it ran fails, because a clean run and an unexamined run are then indistinguishable, which is the one thing anom-008 exists to prevent. And a pass that stamps the run before its writes complete fails, since a partial pass would then claim a completed examination. Refs adds: db-002.

The operational picture carries detection. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture for a run anom-015 has scored. Output: detectionSummary carrying anomaly counts per category and an overall severity as Low|Medium|High, rfSensors carrying each receiver from scn-005's layout with its state, and timelineEvents carrying the reportable claims' windows oldest to newest -- the three collections api-002 has always served empty. THIS IS WHERE api-002'S JUSTIFICATION IS RETIRED rather than left reading as current. That item records the collections as empty 'because no detector, RF source or generator exists', with the principle beside it that an empty section is honest while a populated one would be invented data reaching an analyst. The principle stands and the condition has expired -- eight detection rules, the synthetic RF source, the generator, 103 stored evidence bundles, 155 stored hypothesis rows -- and nothing noticed, because three items consume these fields (op-003 takes detectionSummary, op-006 takes timelineEvents, api-007 filters both) and no item produced them. Closing a producer-less field is what this item is for. A RUN WITH NO DETECTION PASS MUST NOT PRODUCE THE SAME PAYLOAD AS A RUN THE PASS FOUND NOTHING IN. This is the sharpest constraint and it is anom-008's argument arriving at the API boundary: zero is the answer a quiet run gives and also the answer a pipeline that never ran gives, and most of those cases are failures no property of the output can separate. So an unscored run is reported as unscored and a scored run holding nothing is reported as clean -- api-002's honest-empty rule kept, and made two-valued rather than one. NO SCORE, EVER: severity and signal integrity are Low|Medium|High strings and nothing here serves a percentage or a decimal (FR-715, NFR-203, AC-11, ui-001), api-002's own amendment having renamed anomalyScore to anomalyLevel after the screen rendered '74.2%' and '0.92'. NO GROUND TRUTH, and this is the response api-009's failure case actually names: neither the scenario type of the active run nor the injected event may appear, whether as a field, a label or an inferable artefact. The scenario type is legitimate on Scenario Control, which is the harness's own face (FR-714); it is not legitimate here, where a detector's output is being shown to an analyst. NO SQL IN THE HANDLER (FR-904, db-006): reads go through a repository function, following api-002. Failure cases. Any percentage or decimal reaching the screen fails (AC-11). An unscored run and a genuinely quiet run producing the same payload fails, because it makes a broken pipeline indistinguishable from a correct non-detection, which is the one thing anom-008 exists to prevent. The scenario type or the injected event appearing in the payload fails (api-009). A summary computed in the handler rather than read through the repository fails (FR-904). And an overall severity derived by pooling rules of different kinds -- an RF episode's severity averaged with a fault attribution's confidence -- fails, because anom-007 is explicit that confidence qualifies the ATTRIBUTION while severity qualifies the DEVIATION, so a single number over both describes neither. Refs: api-002, api-003, api-007, api-009, anom-007, anom-008, anom-013, anom-015, op-003, op-004, op-006, ui-001, db-006, scn-005, FR-707, FR-710, FR-714, FR-715, FR-904, NFR-203, AC-11. Amended 2026-10-02, before tests, on reading what the detection pass actually leaves in the store and what this endpoint already serves. Four findings. First, THE TWO-VALUED DISTINCTION HAS NO MECHANISM AND NOW HAS ONE. The item requires an unscored run and a quiet run to produce different payloads and names no means, and there was none: findings are replaced per run per rule including at zero, so a scored-clean run and an unexamined run leave an identical empty table. The mechanism is anom-015's amended run stamp, and the payload shape follows it rather than inventing a parallel flag -- detectionSummary becomes NULLABLE, null meaning no pass has run, which is the same shape scenario already carries for no run and db-007's nullable completion stamp one layer along. A boolean beside a list would be two representations of one fact that can disagree. Second, THE SUMMARY CARRIES AN ACCOUNT AND NOT ONLY TWO LEVELS, which is a contract change on both sides and the reason op-003 could never have been built: op-003's input is counts per category and the contract declares no counts at all, only anomalyLevel and signalIntegrity. DetectionSummary gains one entry per producer in anom-008's REGISTER, keyed on the (rule_id, finding_type) pair for anom-012's borrowed rule id, carrying the kind so a screen can tell an intermediate finding from a reportable one -- a quiet run genuinely holds about 138 track discontinuities (anom-010) and an analyst shown that figure as an anomaly count would read a correct non-detection as a storm. EVERY ABSENCE IN THE ACCOUNT IS TYPED, three states and not two: no summary means nobody looked, an entry whose count is null means that rule does not exist (anom-006 is registered and unbuilt, and a zero there would quote the absence of a rule as the accuracy of one -- anom-008's own words), and a number means the rule looked and found that many. The inner levels stay nullable for the same reason one layer down: a pass that could judge no cell at all must not report Low or High, since anom-001 reports the cells it cannot judge precisely so that a clean verdict cannot be satisfied by not having looked. Third, THE HEADLINE ALREADY CARRIES THE ANSWER KEY. api-002 serves scenario.name from the run's scenario_type, so the operational picture's h1 reads `gnss-degradation` -- api-009's named failure case, live, in every screenshot of that screen. It survived because ScenarioRunSummary was deliberately built with no ground_truth field and the check stopped there: the type is not the injected event, it is the LABEL for it, and it discloses everything the event would. name becomes the run's own label and nothing read off the type. Fourth, WHAT STAYS EMPTY AND WHY, stated so the next reader does not take silence for completion. hypotheses stays an empty list: 155 rows exist, serving them is its own item with its own questions (which arm, which grounding verdict, what a FAILED row may show an analyst), and visibly unbuilt is better than half-served. And NOTHING FIRES THE PASS -- at 1.22 s a run plus 11.2 s of baseline it belongs at the end of a batch and not inside a five-second poll (api-003), so until that item exists every run honestly reports as unexamined and this endpoint's scored path is exercised by scoring a run by hand. rfSensors is served from scn-005's layout whether or not a pass has run, with health carrying the state and `unknown` when there is none: the seven receivers and their positions are configuration the generator itself reads, not invented data, so serving them is not the thing api-002's honest-empty rule refuses -- what would be invented is a health reading, and that is exactly the field the stamp governs. Added failure cases: a payload that reports a producer anom-008 registers as unbuilt with a count of zero fails. A summary carrying levels but no account fails, since op-003 cannot be built against it and the account is what answers whether a detector looked. An intermediate finding type presented to an analyst as an anomaly count, with nothing in the payload distinguishing it from a reportable one, fails. And scenario.name carrying the run's scenario type fails (api-009). Refs adds: anom-002, anom-006, anom-010, anom-012, db-007, db-008. Amended 2026-10-02, second pass, before tests: one correction to the amendment above, found by designing the assembly against what the store actually holds. THE INNER LEVELS ARE NOT NULLABLE AND THE SUMMARY'S OWN ABSENCE IS THE ONLY ABSENCE. The note above kept anomalyLevel and signalIntegrity nullable so that a pass which could judge no cell at all could not report Low, on anom-001's rule that a clean verdict must not be satisfiable by not having looked. That reasoning is sound and the data cannot carry it: anom-001's unjudged cells are a list of cells and not findings, nothing persists them, so from the findings table 'judged everything, found nothing' and 'judged nothing' are the same empty result -- a nullability whose meaning no stored value can establish is worse than none, because it reads as a distinction being made. One absence with one meaning instead: no summary means no pass ran, and inside a present summary every value is a reading. Two things make that honest rather than convenient. anom-015 REFUSES a run with no RF observations, so a stamped run is a run whose radio side was read, and the account's own RF entry reports whether the rule produced anything. RECORDED AS A LIMITATION rather than closed: this endpoint cannot distinguish a receiver measured and nominal from one whose cells had no baseline, and the fix belongs to whatever persists anom-001's unjudged cells rather than here. ONE MORE CONSEQUENCE OF THE SAME CHECK, and it is why the account needs a second kind of absence. Two registered intermediate producers leave no rows at all: anom-004's clusters are deliberately not persisted (`from_track_cluster` is a declared non-resolver, so storing them would put citations evb-002 refuses by name into the store for no reader) and anom-012's rate excess is internal to the fusion decision. So an entry's count is absent for TWO different reasons -- the rule does not exist, or the rule ran and its output is not persisted -- and collapsing them would report a built detector as a missing one. The payload carries which, exactly one of the count and the reason being present, refused at construction in both directions on EvidenceItem.grounding's rule. And the set of persisted producers is asserted STRUCTURALLY against the pass rather than declared twice: a test parses anom-015's chain and requires the rule ids it hands save_findings to be exactly that set, so a rule that starts persisting its output cannot leave this endpoint reporting it unpersisted. Levels cross the vocabulary boundary by ENUM MEMBER NAME following ai-002, the detection layer spelling a level `low` where the contract demands `Low`: an unfamiliar word is refused rather than laundered by .title() into something that merely looks valid. And timelineEvents carry the finding type VERBATIM rather than a sentence -- api-011's facts-and-never-prose rule, so the screen composes its copy where the rest of that screen's copy lives. Added failure cases: a count of null whose reason is absent, or a count and a reason both present, fails. An entry reporting a producer whose output is not persisted as though it were unbuilt fails. A level derived by capitalising whatever string the row holds fails. Refs adds: anom-004, evb-002, ai-002.

Firing the detection pass when a generation batch completes -- the trigger that makes a run examined without somebody scoring it by hand. Input: a batch that has finished generating, and the runs it produced. Output: every completed run of that batch passed through anom-015, each one stamped under 0009's columns with the settings it was read through; a batch whose scoring cannot be attempted left generated, stored and honestly recorded as unexamined. The argument for it is that anom-015 and api-012 between them built a pass and a screen that can show its output, and nothing calls the pass: the 300 stored runs carry findings and no stamp, so every one of them reads as unexamined, which is correct and is also why nothing on screen changes until a run is scored by hand. THE INTERACTIVE PATH ONLY, AND THE MECHANISM IS PLACEMENT RATHER THAN A FLAG. app/pipeline.py's main() calls run_batch directly and app/scenario/batch.py's run_batch_now calls it too, so the scoring goes in run_batch_now after run_batch returns and `python -m app.pipeline` -- the Compose pipeline service and make generate -- is unscored by construction rather than by a parameter somebody must remember to pass. Two paths that differ is usually a smell; here it is eval-001's amended argument, that the corpus and the detector settings must stay separable or the same hours cannot be re-scored under a different threshold, and the 300 hours behind every figure this project quotes were built by the command that must not fix the settings. So the difference is asserted in both directions: nothing reachable from app/pipeline.py's entrypoint imports app/detection/, and run_batch_now does. INSIDE api-011'S LEASE, BEFORE IT IS RELEASED. The guard is claimed for the whole of launch_batch's work() and released in its finally, so scoring placed in run_batch_now is covered by it without a second mechanism. That is not incidental: the pass opens its own sessions against the one Engine db-003 provides, which is exactly the pool exhaustion api-011 was written for, and the measurement that shaped that guard covered generation only -- so scoring outside the lease would reintroduce the observed cause in the one place nothing has measured. It also means a second batch cannot start while the first is still scoring. ONLY THIS BATCH'S COMPLETED RUNS. BatchSummary.runs carries a run_id and a completed flag per run and those are the ids scored. Never a store-wide sweep: 300 runs is about six minutes, and it would rewrite every figure-of-record run's findings under whatever settings are current, which is the coupling eval-001 moved off itself. A run the batch recorded as not completed is not offered to the pass, which is a cheap check rather than the only one -- anom-015 refuses it anyway on db-007's absent completion stamp. THE SETTINGS OF RECORD MOVE INTO app/, AND WHAT MOVES IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS. Every detection figure was measured under measurements/corpus/detection_metrics.py's POLICIES, with a second copy in tests/test_anom_chain.py annotated as exactly those. Most of that record is already inside the package: FaultPolicy, FusionPolicy, PrecedencePolicy and ClusterPolicy are taken at their defaults, so what exists ONLY OUTSIDE app/ is ThresholdPolicy's five required fields, GapPolicy's two, and the corpus box's four coordinates -- eleven numbers, of which app/ holds none, app/corpus/build.py carrying the box as a CLI metavar and nothing else. One definition, in app/detection/settings.py; the measurement script and the suite import it rather than restating it. A third copy declared here would put figures on a screen taken under settings that can differ from every quoted number with nothing able to notice, because each copy is internally consistent -- eval-003's 'a recorded setting that is not the one in force is worse than none', and anom-015's own argument one step along: that item moved the ORDER the rules run in, this moves the SETTINGS they run under, and the reason is identical. ONE DEFINITION PLUS ONE PIN, WHICH ARE DIFFERENT THINGS. The eleven values are also written out verbatim in a test, and that is not the duplication this item removes: a definition is what something runs under, a pin is an assertion about it. Changing any of them then fails a test that names the figures they were measured under, which makes a drift loud instead of silent -- ai-004's prompt digest and eval-003's provenance digest, in the one place a digest is unavailable because the values themselves are what is being pinned. NORMALITY IS MEASURED OVER THE STORE'S QUIET RUNS, AND SELECTING THEM IS THE HARNESS'S DECISION. anom-002 measures it over the corpus's quiet runs and never over the run being scored, so the trigger builds one baseline per batch from the store's normal-baseline runs and hands every run of the batch the same Normality. Selecting them reads scenario_type, which is the answer key's label -- permitted because the selection happens outside the detectors and what crosses the boundary is run IDS, which is anom-008's rule and api-009's reason: an observation carries no scenario type for an engine to recognise staged data by. That boundary is asserted rather than assumed, nothing in app/detection/ reading a scenario type. A STORE WITH NO QUIET RUNS REFUSES, AND THE REFUSAL DOES NOT FAIL THE BATCH. A fresh database always is one: generate twenty interference runs into it and there is nothing to measure normal against. anom-015's Normality already refuses an empty tuple, so what this item owns is the consequence -- the hours are generated and stored, which is what was asked for, and every run of the batch is left unstamped. Visibility needs no new mechanism: an unstamped run is served detectionSummary null and api-012's panel says in words that nothing has examined it, which is the state the run is actually in. A logged refusal naming the reason beside it, since nothing on screen distinguishes a refused pass from one never attempted. A PASS THAT FAILS ON ONE RUN IS RECORDED AND SKIPPED, which is scn-003's posture toward a run that dies inside a batch and eval-001's toward a campaign that dies at bundle 14 of 20: the remaining runs are still examined, and the failed one is left unstamped rather than stamped under a pass that did not finish -- which anom-015 already guarantees by stamping last, after every write it makes. COST, measured under anom-015 rather than here: 11.2 s for the baseline once per batch and 1.22 s median per run, so about 35 s on a twenty-run batch against the batch's own seventy seconds or so, which is api-006's figure and the only one on record. This item spends that figure; it does not re-measure it. It is also why the trigger is not api-003's five-second poll, and the baseline rather than the pass is the reason. NO RETRY AND NO SCHEDULE. Nothing in this project runs on a timer and that stays true; a batch completing is the only trigger. Re-scoring the existing 300 runs is a command run once and is deliberately not behaviour specified here. LIMITATION, recorded rather than fixed: a normal-baseline batch is scored against a baseline that includes its own runs. The same self-reference anom-008's measured bands carry -- they are taken on the quiet runs they grade, so they cannot fail on the data that produced them -- and it is the honest consequence of the baseline being a property of the store rather than of the batch. Failure cases. Scoring inside run_batch fails the spec, because the corpus-building command would then fix the detector settings onto the hours it generates and the same hours could not be re-scored under another threshold. A scoring failure that propagates out of generation and makes a completed batch report as failed fails, the hours having been generated and stored. Scoring a run the batch did not produce, or the whole store, fails. Baselining against the batch's own staged runs because the store holds no quiet ones fails, and refusing is the required behaviour rather than a tolerated one. A second declaration of the settings of record, here or anywhere, fails. Handing a detector a run's scenario type fails (api-009). Scoring outside api-011's lease fails. And a run left stamped after a pass that raised fails. Refs: anom-015, anom-002, anom-008, anom-013, api-003, api-006, api-009, api-011, api-012, scn-003, db-003, db-007, db-008, eval-001, eval-003, FR-205, FR-308, FR-707, FR-1001.

The health signal refuses when the database schema is behind the code. Input: a running backend and the database DATABASE_URL points at. Output: GET /api/v1/health reports which of three states the schema is in -- at the revision the code expects, drifted from it, or not determinable -- and **refuses with 503 naming both revisions** when it has drifted. THE ARGUMENT IS A LIVE DEFECT THAT LASTED A DAY. api-012 added two columns to scenario_runs in 0009 and the migration was applied to the *test* database by the fixture that brings it to head before every database-tier test, and never to the application's. So /api/v1/operational-picture returned 500 from the moment that item landed until 2026-10-03, while 1,874 tests passed over the columns, `docker compose ps` reported the backend **healthy**, and /api/v1/health answered 200 throughout because it touches no table. The shape generalises and is the reason this is an item rather than a line: a suite that creates its own schema is testing the migration AND hiding whether anybody has applied it anywhere else, and those two facts are indistinguishable from inside the suite. Nothing in the project compares the running database's revision against the migrations on disk. IT CANNOT BE A STARTUP GATE, and that is the constraint that shapes everything else. db-005 and the lifespan deliberately open no connection at startup, so that a database which is *down* does not stop the service coming up -- an outage presents as a degraded database and not as an unreachable service. Determining the schema version requires a connection. A gate at startup would therefore reverse a decision made on purpose, and would make a database outage indistinguishable from a deployment mistake, which is the exact conflation this item exists to remove. So the check runs where a connection is already in hand and is **reported rather than asserted**. THE PLACE THAT WAS SILENT IS THE PLACE IT GOES. The health route is what the Compose healthcheck probes and what said healthy for a day, so it is where the fact belongs; a second readiness route was considered and rejected as a new concept for a project whose API is minimal by scope, and because the probe that misreported is the one already wired. THREE STATES AND NOT TWO. at-head answers 200. **drifted** -- behind, ahead, an unversioned database, or a migration graph with more than one head -- answers 503 and names the revision found beside the one expected. unknown, meaning the database could not be reached, answers **200** and says it could not tell. That third state is the whole of what keeps api-001's guarantee: an outage is not a misconfiguration, and refusing on an outage would turn a degraded database into an unreachable service, which is the failure api-001 was written to avoid. Ahead is refused as well as behind, because a database carrying a revision this code does not know means somebody deployed newer code and rolled back, and the code may now read columns that were dropped. THE EXPECTATION COMES FROM THE MIGRATIONS ON DISK AND NEVER FROM THE DATABASE. Reading what to expect out of alembic_version -- the same table being checked -- makes the check agree with itself on every database, which is a guard that cannot fail and therefore is not one. The on-disk head is read once at import, because it cannot change without restarting the process; the database's revision is read on every probe, because applying the migration against a live stack must flip the container back to healthy on the next probe rather than needing a restart. THE SQL LIVES IN THE REPOSITORY, NOT THE HANDLER (FR-904, db-006). Stated because the obvious implementation imports the Alembic configuration into the route, and db-006's check forbids a route module naming `alembic` at all -- 'a migration run from a request handler is the same mistake wearing a different hat'. The allowlist of app.db modules a route may name must also NOT widen a second time: anom-016 added a guard asserting every entry on it is a repository module, and app/db/migrations.py is configuration rather than a repository. So the comparison is a repository function the handler calls, the expectation is imported into the repository from the migration module, and the route names one already-allowed module. The guard doing its job by forcing the function to where the rule already said it belongs is worth recording rather than smoothing over. COST. One single-row read per probe against a one-row table, at the healthcheck's five-second interval. The alternative of caching the result is refused by the live-recovery requirement above. A CONSEQUENCE ACCEPTED DELIBERATELY, AND THE MAKEFILE CHANGE THAT PAYS FOR IT. Nothing applies migrations when the stack starts: `up` and `demo` are plain `docker compose up`, and `migrate` is its own target (ops-003). So without a change this check would leave a freshly started stack unhealthy until somebody runs migrate, which is correct and is also a new failure mode on every first run -- and a guard that fires routinely is one somebody switches off, which is api-003's recorded argument about the GenerationConfig credential guard in a different costume. So `up` and `demo` apply the migrations first, amending ops-003. Idempotent: `alembic upgrade head` against a database already at head is a no-op. Auto-migrating from the container's own entrypoint is **refused** -- db-001 keeps migration a deliberate act, and an image that migrates on boot runs schema changes from however many instances start at once. AMENDS api-001 in its output clause and not in its failure case. That item says 'Output: 200 with a JSON body' and the output is now 200 or 503; its failure case 'requiring a database connection to answer' is UNVIOLATED and the distinction matters -- this endpoint still answers without a database, which is what the unknown state is, and it consults one when there is one. The clause was written so health stays truthful before persistence exists, and that remains true. api-001 stays passing: every property it asserts is still asserted. Failure cases. A database one revision behind while health reports healthy fails the spec -- that is the defect of record and the reason the item exists. Refusing while the database is merely unreachable fails, because it reverses api-001's guarantee and reports an outage as a deployment mistake. Reading the expected revision from the database fails. An alembic_version table that exists and holds no row reported as at-head fails, since that is a database nobody has migrated. A migration graph with more than one head reported as at-head fails, the comparison being meaningless when 'head' names two things. A route handler holding the SQL, constructing a session, or naming the migration machinery fails (db-006), and so does widening the app.db allowlist to admit a configuration module. A check that caches the database's revision, so that applying the migration against a live stack never clears the refusal, fails. And a first-run `make up` that leaves the stack permanently unhealthy fails, which is what the ops-003 amendment is for. Refs: api-001, api-003, api-012, db-001, db-005, db-006, ops-001, ops-003, ops-004, anom-016, FR-801, FR-904, AC-12, docs/qa.md section 144.

The picture serves a named hour, and an index of the hours it will serve. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture?run=<id>, and GET /api/v1/operational-picture/hours. Output: for the first, 200 with the SAME payload shape api-002 already serves, built for the named run instead of the newest; for the second, 200 with a list of selectable hours, newest first, each entry carrying the run id (the value the run parameter takes), the replayed window in simulated time (observedFrom/observedTo, from what the run row records), and whether a detection pass examined it. Constraints. (1) WHAT THE INDEX MUST NOT CARRY is the item. No entry may carry the scenario type, the seed, the incident dials, or anything from which the injected event can be inferred -- api-009, and the guarantee is STRUCTURAL rather than disciplinary, following ScenarioRunSummary's own argument that a shape with no field for the answer cannot leak it on any run. This endpoint exists BECAUSE /api/v1/scenario/runs already serves the list the screen wants and carries scenarioType legitimately -- Scenario Control is the harness's own face, where naming gnss-degradation is correct, and the analyst's screen is where it is disqualifying. api-012 found that exact string in the picture's heading after a year, and it survived because a repo-wide search for it finds a justified use and stops; reusing the harness listing here replaces a structural guarantee with a convention somebody has to know. Asserted the way api-012 asserts it: serialise the whole index and search it for all five scenario-type names across a store holding all five, because a check on one field only ever proves the field somebody thought of. (2) THE INDEX CARRIES NOTHING THE DETECTORS CONCLUDED -- no finding count, no severity, no claim type, no 'interesting' flag. Not because it would leak the answer key (a detector's conclusion is precisely what an analyst is meant to see, and is served in full for the hour actually selected) but because on this corpus precision is 1.000 and recall is 60/60 on every positive arm, so a count of reportable findings is empirically a near-perfect proxy for whether anything was staged. A chooser that ranked hours by what was found would make any future exercise in which a person reads this screen un-blind, and eval-006 is still outstanding. What it DOES carry is examined-or-not, which is api-012's own distinction -- whether anybody looked is answered by the presence of the account and never by a number in it -- so selecting an hour that nothing has examined is not a surprise after the fact. (3) An unknown run is 404 and NEVER a fall back to the newest, which is the sharpest failure here: silently serving a different hour than the one asked for is indistinguishable from the feature working, and is exactly what 'default to the latest' does. A non-integer run value is 422, following api-007's rule that an unrecognised parameter value never silently defaults. (4) With no run parameter the behaviour is UNCHANGED -- the newest completed run, falling back to the newest (db-007) -- so api-002's guarantee, its parity test and the frontend contract are untouched, and the payload shape is one shape rather than two. (5) The index lists runs KNOWN TO HAVE COMPLETED while the run parameter accepts any run in the store, and the asymmetry is deliberate: the index is the set of whole hours worth offering a person, the parameter is the addressing mechanism, and a half-generated hour stays reachable because diagnosing a batch that partly failed is a legitimate thing to do from the screen. (6) The index is bounded and ordered by the run's start, newest first, like the harness listing: an unbounded list over a growing store is a payload with no ceiling, and an unordered one takes its order from the heap, which this repository has had to fix three times.
