(7) Reads go through the repository (FR-904); the route holds no SQL and the index's shape lives in the schemas module beside the picture's. Failure cases. An unknown run id served as the newest run rather than refused. An index entry carrying the scenario type, the seed, the incident parameters, or any field from which the staged event is inferable -- and a test that checks only the named fields rather than the serialised payload across all five types. An index entry carrying a finding count, a severity, a claim type or any other property of what the detectors concluded. A requested-run payload whose shape differs from the default payload, which would split the contract in two. A non-integer run value resolving to the newest run rather than 422. An index that lists every run in the store with no bound. Refs: FR-811, FR-802, FR-904, NFR-604, AC-13, AC-04, api-002, api-007, api-009, api-012, db-007, anom-015, anom-016, op-009, eval-006. Amended 2026-10-03, before tests, three refinements found while writing them. (a) observedFrom and observedTo are NULLABLE. The replayed window is knowable only from what the run row records in its parameters, and a replay run records none -- so a run that cannot name its hour says so, which the selector renders as the run number alone. Deriving the window from started_at instead is the failure to avoid: that is the wall-clock minute the generator ran, and labelling a replayed 2022 hour with it is anom-009's recorded mistake, wall clock in a simulated-time costume. Failure case adds: an entry whose window is filled in from the run's own start or completion timestamps rather than from the recorded simulated window. (b) The bound is GENEROUS and exists as a ceiling rather than as a trim -- 500 against a store holding 400. A bound of 50, matching the harness listing, would list hours 371-420 and therefore almost none of the 240 that hold a claim, which is the entire thing this item exists to reach; and because the index carries nothing the detectors concluded (constraint 2), a short list cannot be the interesting part of a long one. (c) An empty store is 200 with an empty list, never 404, on api-002's own argument.

The hour selector on the Operational Picture. Input: the index of selectable hours from api-013, and the analyst's selection. Output: a control listing the selectable hours, the selection driving which hour the whole screen shows, and a visible statement of whether the screen is FOLLOWING THE NEWEST hour or PINNED to a chosen one, with a way back to following. Constraints. (1) Each hour is rendered by its replayed window and its run number and nothing else. No scenario type, which is structurally unavailable because api-013's index has no such field -- asserted here as well as there, by scanning the rendered screen for all five type names, because the same string reaching this screen from any source at all is the failure api-009 names. (2) The source of the list is api-013's index and NOT /api/v1/scenario/runs, which carries the scenario type for Scenario Control's own legitimate use. Asserted structurally: no module reachable from the Operational Picture may import the scenario-runs fetcher or the scenario-control contract. The fetch itself goes through the one module allowed to reach the network (api-003). (3) The default is to follow the newest, which is today's behaviour, so the screen always has a selection and a reader who ignores the control sees exactly what they see now. (4) FOLLOWING AND PINNED MUST BE VISIBLY DIFFERENT. An analyst pins an hour, a batch lands, and the screen goes on showing the pinned hour while looking identical to a live one -- which is the same class of defect as a health signal reporting healthy through an outage (ops-005) and a summary reading clean when nothing examined it (api-012): the screen must not present stale data in the costume of current data. (5) Polling continues while pinned, and asks for the PINNED hour rather than the newest. Continues, because a historical hour's detection state can still change under it -- re-examining a run restamps it, and the re-score of 2026-10-03 changed 380 runs' findings in six minutes; asks for the pinned hour, because a poll that keeps requesting the newest would revert the screen under the analyst between selections, which is a worse failure than not having the control. (6) An hour the index marks unexamined still renders, through the sentence api-012 already composes. The control neither hides nor disables such hours: an unexamined hour is a legitimate thing to look at, and hiding it would make a batch whose scoring was refused invisible -- the one condition anom-016 reports only through that sentence. (7) Confidence and severity continue to render through ui-001; nothing about selection introduces a number (FR-715, AC-11). Failure cases. The control naming the scenario type of any hour, from any source. A pinned hour rendering identically to a live one, or no way back to following the newest. The poll continuing to request the newest hour while the control shows another hour selected, so the screen reverts on the next tick. The selectable hours taken from the scenario-control runs listing rather than from api-013's index. An unexamined hour hidden or disabled in the control. An empty index rendering as a blank control rather than as an explicit statement that the store holds no completed hour. Refs: FR-719, FR-716, FR-715, AC-13, AC-11, api-013, api-003, api-009, api-012, ui-001, op-001, op-008, anom-016, ops-005. Amended 2026-10-03, before tests, two refinements found while writing them. (a) The index is fetched ONCE PER MOUNT and never polled. It changes only when a batch completes, an entry is a handful of fields over 400 rows, and following-the-newest does not depend on it at all -- the picture endpoint with no run parameter always serves the actual newest, so a stale list affects which hours are OFFERED and never which hour is SHOWN. Recorded as a limitation rather than fixed: a batch completing while the screen is open does not appear in the list until the screen is remounted. (b) The selection is component state and NOT the URL hash, which was considered and deferred. A pinned hour in the hash would make an hour shareable and survive a reload, which is worth having for a demonstration -- but screenFromHash is nav-001's machinery and it resolves a bare screen id today, so a parameterised hash is its own item with its own failure case (an unrecognised run in a hash must resolve the way an unrecognised screen does). Deferred deliberately, and named here so it is not re-derived as a defect.

The scenario block stops carrying a health field. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture. Output: the payload's `scenario` object carries `id`, `name` and `dataMode` and no `health`, and `frontend/src/types/operationalPicture.ts` matches. Why a removal rather than a producer. The field is hard-coded to `unknown` in the builder, with a comment recording that no health monitoring exists -- which was true when written. What has changed is not that a producer arrived but that **another field took the job**: `api-012` added `detectionSummary.signalIntegrity`, which is the state of the receiver layout, has a producer, and is the run-level health signal this field would have carried. Two health fields where one works is worse than one, because the broken one reads as a second fact that never arrives. This is `api-002`'s producer-less-field lesson resolved by its THIRD route. That amendment named two -- produce the field, or record that the reason it is empty is still true -- and both assume the field is wanted. A field whose job another field already does is neither produced nor justified: it is deleted, and the deletion is the thing that has to be visible, because a nullable-looking field nobody writes is exactly what hid `detectionSummary`'s own gap for a year. Constraints. **`rfSensors[].health` is NOT removed** and the distinction is the whole risk here: that field has a producer (`_receiver_health`), carries per-receiver state, and is what the screen renders for each of `scn-005`'s seven receivers -- a removal that took both would delete a working signal alongside a broken one. Parity is proved in both directions by the existing contract parser, which is what makes a removal as checkable as an addition: the field must be gone from the response model AND from the TypeScript interface, and leaving it on either side fails. No consumer may read it afterwards -- the Operational Picture header rendered it as a bare `unknown`, which `op-001`'s amendment replaces with the labelled data-mode readout, and `nav-002` no longer wants it. The fixtures that carry it are updated rather than left with an extra key, since `Scenario` forbids extra fields and a stale fixture key would fail at construction. Failure cases. The field removed from the response model and left in the TypeScript contract, or the reverse -- caught by the parity test in whichever direction, and the reason that test exists. `rfSensors[].health` removed with it. A consumer still reading `scenario.health` and rendering `undefined` where it used to render `unknown`. The removal done by making the field optional rather than absent, which leaves the contract able to express a value nothing produces. And `signalIntegrity` being asked to mean service health as well as receiver-layout health, which is `nav-002`'s job and a different layer. Refs: FR-802, FR-715, api-002, api-012, op-001, nav-002, ops-005, scn-005, AC-11.

A derived-data stage may not replace an evidence bundle a hypothesis cites. Input: a call to the bundle write (evb-002) for one scenario run. Output: the write proceeds exactly as before when no bundle of that run is cited by a hypothesis row, and is refused -- nothing deleted, nothing inserted, nothing resolved -- when one is. WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A FEATURE. The write replaces per run: DELETE then INSERT, which is db-008's rule for derived data and correct for a bundle, which is derived from findings which are derived from a seed. But hypotheses.bundle_id is declared ON DELETE CASCADE and is that table's ONLY link to a run -- there is no scenario_run_id column on hypotheses at all -- so a replace over a cited run deletes the hypothesis rows citing it SILENTLY: the DELETE succeeds, the cascade fires, nothing raises, and the failure is observable only as rows that are no longer there. Measured on the store of record: 155 hypothesis rows, the whole scored campaign, hang off 20 bundles on runs 102-175 -- eval-004's pre-registered sample. That is what eval-005's per-arm figures and the Evaluation chapter rest on, and it is the one population in this project that cannot be regenerated: db-002 appends rather than replaces precisely because a model call consumed money and produced one specific response. Nothing in app/ calls that write today (the 103 stored bundles were written by measurements/corpus/bundle_end_to_end.py), so the path is unguarded rather than live; it becomes live the moment the detection pass stores what it builds, which is evb-003, and the obvious implementation of that item trips it. Constraints. (1) THE REFUSAL IS IN THE REPOSITORY AND NOT IN THE SCHEMA. Changing the foreign key to RESTRICT was considered and rejected: deleting a scenario run SHOULD take its bundles and their hypotheses with it, a hypothesis having no other route back to a run, so a restriction there would block a correct delete in order to prevent an incorrect one. What must be refused is REPLACEMENT BY A DERIVED-DATA STAGE, which is a different act from deletion of the hour: a cascade on a delete is the schema working, and a cascade on a REGENERATION is data loss wearing the costume of a refresh. (2) Refused BEFORE anything is written and before anything is resolved, which sharpens evb-002's own atomicity rule -- that item resolves in full before writing so a single unresolvable citation leaves the database as it was, and a refusal decidable from the store alone must not first cost a query per citation. (3) DECIDED FROM THE STORE AND NEVER FROM AN ARGUMENT. A caller flag saying 'this run is protected', or a module-level list of protected run ids, is a convention somebody has to know -- which is what api-013 rejected for the hour chooser, on the grounds that it downgrades a structural guarantee. The fact lives in hypotheses.bundle_id and is read from there, so a twenty-first cited bundle protects itself. (4) The refusal names the run, the cited bundle ids and how many hypothesis rows cite them, so a reader can tell a protected population from a bug. (5) WRITING AN EMPTY SET IS THE SAME ACT and is refused on the same terms: evb-002 makes a zero-bundle write clear what was there -- the replace rule at zero, and the case a run re-detected as quiet produces -- which on a cited run is the identical cascade with nothing inserted afterwards. (6) A run with no cited bundles is UNAFFECTED, including at zero, so evb-002's existing suite and its two committed measurements keep their behaviour. Failure cases. A replace over a cited run that succeeds and takes hypothesis rows with it. A guard that counts hypothesis rows AFTER the delete, which is a report and not a guard. A guard implemented as a caller-supplied exclusion list, which protects exactly the runs somebody remembered. A guard that also refuses deletion of the scenario run itself, which is a correct cascade this must not touch. A check that runs inside the same transaction as the delete but after it, so the rollback is the only thing standing between the cascade and the store. A guard asserted only over a non-empty bundle list, leaving the zero case to cascade. Refs: FR-907, FR-901, FR-904, NFR-602, db-001, db-002, db-007, db-008, evb-002, evb-003, eval-004, eval-005, ai-012, anom-015, api-013.

The screen can ask why: one endpoint serving the evidence behind an hour's reported claims. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture/evidence?run=<id>; with no parameter, the same hour /operational-picture serves with no parameter -- the newest completed run, falling back to the newest (db-007) -- so the two endpoints cannot disagree about which hour is current. Output: 200 with null when no detection pass has examined the hour, otherwise an object carrying the run id and TWO LISTS which together account for every reported claim the store holds for that hour: `explained`, one entry per claim that has a stored bundle, carrying that bundle; and `unexplained`, one entry per claim that has none, carrying the claim's rule id, finding type, subject and a TYPED reason. An unknown run is 404. WHY TWO LISTS RATHER THAN A LIST OF BUNDLES. This is api-012's nullable-summary argument one layer along, and the same three states must stay apart: an hour with nothing to explain (quiet, and correct), an hour whose claims are explained, and AN HOUR WHOSE CLAIM WAS NEVER BUNDLED -- which is a gap in the pipeline and must not read as the first. Measured on the store of record all three are live and none is hypothetical: 160 runs quiet, 100 with a claim and its bundle, 140 with a claim and NO bundle, 0 with a bundle and no claim. The hour index lists newest first, so every hour a person opens today is in the 140. Served as a bare list of bundles, all three states are the empty list, which is exactly the dash op-003 had to replace with a sentence. Constraints. (1) THE TWO LISTS PARTITION THE HOUR'S REPORTED CLAIMS. Every reportable finding the store holds for the run appears in exactly one of them, and this endpoint is the only place that join is made. That is what makes a dropped conclusion unconstructible rather than merely refused: it cannot vanish by omission, because its omission breaks a count. Reportable is derived from anom-008's register and never spelled here, following api-012, so a rule that becomes reportable needs no edit. (2) EVIDENCE IS SERVED GROUPED, ON ai-001's PAIR. A real interference bundle holds about 34 items -- roughly 11 RF deviations and roughly 13 aircraft dropouts repeating one sentence with a different pseudonym each time -- and eval-007 already learned on the scoring pack that a flat list of those is a wall rather than a document. The key is (rule_id, finding_type) and never the rule alone, because anom-012 borrows anom-010's rule id, so a rate excess and a discontinuity are identical by rule id in every interference bundle this corpus produces: the fourth place that collision has had to be handled, after ai-008's resolution, eval-007's grouping and anom-008's register. (3) THE GROUPING RE-ORGANISES VALUES AND COMPUTES NONE -- eval-007's replacement constraint, stated mechanically and tested rather than judged. Every value on a group appears VERBATIM on one of its items or on the bundle's own metadata; the only arithmetic permitted is a count of the items the group itself lists. A group's span endpoints and its largest deviation are therefore SELECTIONS of values present, not aggregates: no mean, no total, no rounding, no re-derived severity. (4) GROUPING HAPPENS SERVER-SIDE, so there is one implementation inside the coverage gate rather than one per consumer, and hyp-002 gets the same shape when it needs it. (5) EVERY ABSENCE KEEPS ITS KIND. evb-001's three uncertainty kinds cross the boundary by ENUM MEMBER NAME following ai-002, not by title-casing a word into something that fails a layer later, and each statement crosses verbatim and untruncated -- the kind says what sort of not-knowing it is and the statement is the only part a person can weigh. A bundle's `superseded` crosses too, labelled a competing conclusion that did not win and NEVER inside the evidence list, which is ai-008's third verdict at the screen boundary and the co-occurrence-read-as-concurrence error evb-001 names. (6) OBSERVATION ROW IDS DO NOT CROSS, excluded by name following ai-004's rule for its egress exclusions: a row id is not something an analyst can act on, the check that needs them is ai-008's and ran before anything was stored, and evb-002 already refused the whole bundle if any ref failed to resolve. What does cross is each group's sources -- the receiver-and-channel, or the aircraft pseudonym. (7) AIRCRAFT IDENTIFIERS ARE PSEUDONYMS AS STORED AND NOTHING REVERSES THEM. The substitution is the DAL's at ingest, so this endpoint holds no seed and performs no lookup, and NFR-405 is satisfied for a screenshot of the panel because what is on it was never the real identifier. (8) NO BUNDLE IS BUILT HERE. anom-016 records that the detection pass does not fire per request and that the baseline, at 11.2 s, is the reason; so an hour with no stored bundle is reported as unexplained and never scored on demand. Serving a bundle built under current settings beside findings stored under the recorded ones would be two sources for one event, which is the conflation anom-016 removed from the other direction. (9) A non-integer run value is 422 and an unknown run is 404 and never the newest hour -- api-013's two refusals, repeated because they are the same mistake available at a second endpoint, and the second is the one that looks like the feature working. (10) A SEPARATE ENDPOINT RATHER THAN A FIELD ON THE PICTURE: it is read on demand rather than every five seconds, it is an order of magnitude larger than the picture, and the picture's shape is a contract two parity tests hold in both directions. (11) Reads go through the repository (FR-904); the route holds no SQL. Failure cases. All three states served as an empty list. A reported claim appearing in neither list, or in both. Reportable spelled in this module rather than derived from the register. A grouped value appearing nowhere on an item -- a mean deviation, a total, a rounded figure, a recomputed severity. Grouping on the rule id alone, which collapses anom-012's rate excess into anom-010's discontinuities. An uncertainty crossing as a bare `not_measurable` with its statement dropped, or with its kind title-cased. `superseded` served inside the evidence list. Observation ids served. An unknown run answered with the newest hour's evidence. A bundle built on demand for an hour that has none. An unexamined hour and a quiet hour serving the same payload. Refs: FR-812, FR-802, FR-904, NFR-202, NFR-405, AC-05, AC-14, api-002, api-009, api-012, api-013, db-007, db-011, evb-001, evb-002, evb-003, ai-001, ai-002, ai-004, ai-008, anom-008, anom-010, anom-012, anom-016, eval-007, op-003, op-010, hyp-002. Amended 2026-10-04, before any test, on measuring the join against the store of record. THERE IS NO KEY JOINING A BUNDLE TO ITS CONCLUSION, and the item was written as though there were. `evidence_bundles` carries no reference to `detection_findings` and cannot: findings are replaced per run per rule, so a foreign key would cascade-delete the bundles on every re-score -- `db-011`'s argument one table along, which makes the omission correct rather than an oversight. The two rows are therefore matched on fields, and measurement settled which. (a) SUBJECT CANNOT BE IN THE KEY. A fusion bundle's subject is the receivers that deviated together, joined ('RF-05, RF-06, RF-07'), while the claim's is the one representative receiver ('RF-05') -- so a key including it misses every interference bundle in the store, 41 of 103, while matching all the faults: the shape of a bug that looks like a feature on half a corpus. (b) THE KEY IS (run, rule id, type, window), measured UNIQUE ON BOTH SIDES -- zero duplicate groups among 103 bundles and zero among 249 reported claims. (run, rule, type) alone is not unique, three runs carrying two fault claims each, and nor is adding the subject back, those two claims being on the same receiver. (c) A THIRD LIST, because exact matching leaves four bundles over. Measured: 99 of 103 stored bundles match a reported claim exactly, and the four that do not differ by ONE OR TWO SAMPLING INTERVALS at one end of the window (bundles 220, 237, 242 and 251, on runs 54, 71, 76 and 105) -- the same event with a boundary that moved. They were written by a measurement script on 19 and 28 September, before `anom-007`'s window derivation settled, and the findings beside them were written later by the pass. None of the four is cited by a hypothesis, so `eval-004`'s twenty are all consistent. The plan had been to REFUSE such a bundle on `api-012`'s precedent for a stored value the payload will not serve, and that is WITHDRAWN: the state is live on the corpus rather than hypothetical, and a 500 on four hours is worse than a sentence about them. So `unclaimed` carries them and the guarantee becomes TWO-SIDED COMPLETENESS -- `explained` plus `unexplained` account for every reported claim, `explained` plus `unclaimed` account for every stored bundle, so nothing in the store is dropped in either direction. The widened match that would absorb the four -- overlap, or nearest window -- is rejected for the reason this project rejects every such repair: it would pair a bundle with a conclusion it was not built for, and the pairing would be invisible. (d) An explained claim's `subject` is THE BUNDLE'S, being that bundle's own record of which receivers deviated together, which is what the panel has to name; the claim's own representative subject already reaches the screen through `api-012`'s timeline, so carrying both here would put two differing values for one word in front of a reader. An unexplained claim's subject is the claim's, there being no bundle. Failure cases add: a key including the subject, which misses every interference bundle. A key not unique on both sides. A stored bundle matching no claim and silently dropped, which makes an hour read as fully explained when some of its evidence was discarded. A match widened to overlap or proximity. Amended again 2026-10-04, still before any test passed, on reading the two constructors rather than only the rows. The previous amendment concluded the subject cannot be in the key, which is half right: the RAW subject cannot, and its HEAD can and must. `findings.py` files a fusion claim under `zone.sensors[0]` and a fault under `fault.sensor_id`, while `bundle.py` writes `", ".join(producer.sensors)` and `producer.sensor_id` -- so the claim's subject IS the first of the bundle's joined list, by construction in both rules rather than as a property of this corpus. The key is therefore (run, rule id, type, first of the joined subject, window). It matches the same 99 of 103, is unique on both sides with zero duplicate groups, and is the better key for a reason the four-field one cannot cover: two broken receivers are two events (`anom-013`) and `anom-007` derives each window from the readings, so two faults staged in one window would share a four-field key and neither claim could be told which bundle was its own. That occurs zero times on this corpus and is entirely legitimate, which is the class of thing not to leave to a measurement. The ambiguity is CHECKED rather than assumed away all the same -- `evb-002`'s exactly-one-row rule one layer up -- so two bundles or two claims sharing the key is refused: a bundle attributed to whichever row came back first is the unordered-result failure this repository has recorded three times. The head relationship is asserted against both constructors rather than against stored rows, since what makes it safe is that it is built that way. Failure cases add: a key on the raw joined subject, which misses every interference bundle. A key dropping the subject entirely, which cannot attribute a bundle on a run holding two claims in one window. A duplicate key resolved by taking the first match. Amended 2026-10-04, after the first green run, ON LOOKING AT THE RUNNING SCREEN -- the third kind of blind spot this project records, and its second instance. Uncertainties were specified to cross verbatim and untruncated, which they must; what was not specified is that they cross ONE PER SUPPRESSED EPISODE. Run 102 renders `a deviation on channel 4 of RF-07 lasted 1 reading(s), under the 10 s minimum` three times identically, and the store holds bundles carrying the same sentence 28 times. That is `eval-007`'s wall in its own words -- fourteen rows repeating one sentence are a wall whether or not each sits in its own row -- and the fix is the one already applied to the evidence: identical entries collapse to one carrying a COUNT. Collapsed on the whole (kind, statement, subject) triple and never on the statement alone, since the statement is the only part a person weighs and two kinds of not-knowing that happen to be worded alike are still two claims. Verbatim is unaffected -- no sentence is shortened, merged or rewritten, and the count is a count of the items collapsed, which is the only arithmetic this endpoint performs. It belongs HERE and not in the panel for the reason the evidence grouping does: one implementation, inside the coverage gate, and `op-010` renders what it is given. Failure case adds: identical absences served one per episode, which puts the same sentence in front of an analyst up to 28 times.

The conclusion says why. Input: the evidence account for the selected hour (api-015), fetched on demand rather than polled. Output: for each reported conclusion the detection summary lists, the evidence it rests on -- the subject and the window in simulated time; the receivers that deviated together, each with how far above its own normal it went and in which metric; whether the aircraft side corroborated and, when it could not, the stated reason; the judgements the rules made, marked as judgements rather than measurements; and every absence as its own kind of absence. Constraints. (1) A CONCLUSION WITH NO STORED ACCOUNT RENDERS A SENTENCE SAYING SO, never an empty panel and never silence. This is op-003's own correction one layer along -- a dash meaning 'nothing to report' could not be told from a dash meaning 'nobody looked' -- and on the store of record it is the state of 140 of the 240 claim-bearing hours, so it is the common case and not an edge. (2) A MEASUREMENT AND A JUDGEMENT ARE VISIBLY DIFFERENT THINGS. evb-001 declares per item whether it cites observations or states a judgement, and that declaration is the one part of a bundle that cannot be inferred from the rest: a nominal neighbour is in the bundle PRECISELY BECAUSE nothing was raised for it, and rendered unmarked beside a deviation it reads as a second deviation -- which inverts the fault verdict it is evidence for. (3) THE THREE KINDS OF ABSENCE ARE THREE DIFFERENT SENTENCES, exposed non-visually so tests assert on the kind and not on styling (hyp-002's rule). Not-applicable, not-measurable and measured-negative are the distinction evb-001 exists to keep, and collapsing them here undoes it at the last boundary before a person. (4) NO PERCENTAGE AND NO DECIMAL SCORE (FR-715). A deviation in dB is a measurement rather than a score, so it carries its unit and names its metric; confidence and severity continue to render through the ui-001 primitive. (5) COPY FOR A FINDING TYPE COMES FROM THE ONE VOCABULARY MODULE (op-003) and is not written again here, or one conclusion acquires a second wording with nothing to catch the drift. (6) THE PANEL RENDERS WHAT IT IS GIVEN AND GROUPS NOTHING: the grouping and the re-organisation are api-015's, server-side, and a second implementation here is the duplication this repository has recorded over distance once already. (7) AIRCRAFT ARE SHOWN BY PSEUDONYM AND THE COUNT LEADS -- 'reporting broke from 13 aircraft inside the zone during the window' is the claim an analyst can weigh, and the identifiers are traceability beneath it (NFR-405, NFR-202). (8) A COMPETING CONCLUSION THE LADDER REJECTED IS SHOWN AS REJECTED, never among the support. Measured: 0 of 103 stored bundles carry one, so this path is unexercised on this corpus and is a limitation to state rather than a case to claim coverage of. (9) The account is fetched for the hour the screen is showing, so pinning an hour (op-009) changes it, and a failed fetch keeps what is on screen rather than emptying the panel (api-003's rule). Failure cases. An empty panel where a claim has no stored account. A judgement rendered indistinguishably from a measurement. Three absence kinds rendered as one sentence, or an absence dropped because its statement was empty. A deviation shown as a percentage or a 0-1 score. Copy for a finding type written a second time in this panel. Grouping, counting or arithmetic performed on the client. A superseded claim listed as supporting evidence. A list of thirteen identical sentences differing only in a pseudonym. A panel that empties itself when a poll fails. Refs: FR-720, FR-707, FR-711, FR-715, NFR-202, NFR-204, NFR-405, AC-08, AC-14, api-003, api-015, op-001, op-003, op-009, ui-001, evb-001, hyp-002, eval-007. Amended 2026-10-04, before any test passed, on building the fetch. CONSTRAINT 9 IS WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED. It said a failed fetch keeps what is on screen rather than emptying the panel, citing `api-003`'s rule -- and that rule does not transfer here. `api-003` governs POLLING ONE THING: a failed poll of the picture keeps the picture, because the next answer would have been about the same hour. This fetch is keyed on the hour, so a failure after a successful one can only follow a change of hour, and keeping what is on screen would then show ONE HOUR'S EVIDENCE UNDER ANOTHER HOUR'S CONCLUSION -- which is precisely the conflation this item exists to remove, arrived at by following a rule from the wrong context. So a failed fetch says it could not load this hour's evidence. THE ABSENCE OF AN ANSWER AND AN ANSWER OF NULL ARE THEREFORE TWO STATES, not one: null is the server saying no pass examined this hour, and no answer is the client having none -- `api-012`'s own distinction moved onto the client, where the panel has four states rather than three and each says a different sentence. Failure cases add: a failed fetch rendering the previous hour's evidence. A failed fetch rendering the sentence for an unexamined hour, which reports a transport failure as a fact about the store. Amended 2026-10-06, by the mutation pass. THE PANEL HAS FIVE STATES AND NOT FOUR. The previous amendment separated *no answer* from *an answer of null*, which was right and not far enough: `undefined` was then carrying BOTH **loading** and **failed**, so the panel says *the evidence could not be loaded* for as long as a fetch is in flight -- a sentence that is false at the moment it is shown, and the same class of error as reporting a transport failure as a fact about the store. Three mutants survived the pass and all three were this one gap: disabling the catch and removing the clear-on-hour-change each left the suite green, because with the two states merged either mechanism alone satisfies the test, and neither could be shown load-bearing. The states are therefore NAMED rather than carried on the absence of a value -- `loading`, `failed`, `null` (no pass examined this hour), and an account whose lists may be empty (a quiet hour) or populated. `undefined` no longer appears in the contract at all, which is what makes the five distinguishable by construction instead of by convention. Failure cases add: a panel that says the evidence could not be loaded while it is still loading. A previous hour's evidence left on screen while the next hour's request is in flight. And one more the same pass found: a response that is not an account -- another endpoint's payload, or an error body -- rendered rather than refused, which the hour index's own fetcher already guards and which reaches the panel as an object whose lists are undefined. Amended 2026-10-06, before tests. THE PANEL IS COLLAPSIBLE, with one constraint that is the whole of it: COLLAPSED, THE HEADER STILL STATES WHAT IS INSIDE -- how many conclusions this hour holds and how many have no stored evidence. A collapse that hides *140 of the 240 claim-bearing hours report their conclusion as unexplained* turns the gap this item exists to expose into a thing an analyst has to go looking for, which is `op-003`'s dash in a new costume. Expanded by default, because the panel is the project's own subject and a collapsed-by-default panel is one nobody opens. The preference persists in guarded `localStorage` following `nav-003`'s rail, with every read and write wrapped and anything unexpected resolving to EXPANDED -- the safe direction being the one that shows more, which is the opposite of the rail's default and for the opposite reason. The state is the analyst's chrome preference and not the route, so it does not touch the hash. Failure cases add: a collapsed header that says only *Evidence*, so an hour with an unexplained conclusion is indistinguishable from a quiet one. A default of collapsed. A collapse that also hides the unclaimed-evidence note, which is a fact about the hour whatever the conclusions look like. Refs add: FR-721, nav-003.

The pass stores the account it builds, and the hours holding a claim with none are filled. Input: a completed detection pass over one run (anom-015), and a one-off fill over the runs the store already holds. Output: the pass writes the bundles it builds through evb-002's write -- after its findings and before its stamp -- and the fill writes bundles, AND ONLY BUNDLES, for every run holding a reported claim and no bundle. WHY THE PASS STOPPED SHORT. anom-015 persists its evidence and, since api-012, its conclusions, and throws away the account that joins them: the bundles are built in the same function and returned on the Assessment, where they are complete inside one process and do not exist to a web request. The recorded reason is eval-004's -- the pre-registered sample names its twenty bundles BY ID, so a pass rebuilding them corpus-wide renumbers that population and stops the draw reproducing itself. That reason is sound and NARROWER THAN THE BEHAVIOUR IT BOUGHT: it protects twenty bundles on twenty runs, and was implemented as 'store none, ever'. db-011 makes the protection structural and decided from the store, after which storing is safe for every run nothing cites -- 380 of 400. Constraints. (1) THE FILL WRITES BUNDLES AND NOTHING ELSE: not findings, not the examination stamp. The findings on those runs are figures of record; db-008 replaces per run per rule and a rewrite that is byte-identical is still a rewrite, while the stamp means WHEN the hour was examined and that answer has not changed. This is what makes the fill not simply 'run the pass again', and it is eval-001's unprovenanced-rather-than-wrong distinction read from the other side. (2) THE FILL CHECKS AS IT FILLS. Building a bundle needs the rule outputs, not the stored rows, so the detectors run -- and the reported claims they produce are compared against the claims already stored, run by run, on rule id, finding type, subject and window. A disagreement REFUSES THAT RUN rather than writing its bundle, because filing today's conclusion under an hour that recorded a different one is worse than leaving the hour unexplained. Which makes the fill a second, independent validation of anom-015's byte-identical claim over a population the first one did not cover. (3) THE PASS PROPAGATES db-011's REFUSAL rather than swallowing it. A run whose account may not be replaced is a run somebody must be told about; scn-003 and eval-001's recorded-and-stepped-over rule applies at the batch, which already records a per-run failure and continues, so the refusal reaches a log and a record without stopping the batch. (4) ORDER INSIDE THE PASS IS LOAD-BEARING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: bundles AFTER the findings they cite, because evb-002 resolves every citation against stored rows and a bundle written first cites rows that are not there yet; and BEFORE the stamp, because the stamp means the pass finished everything it writes, which is the whole argument for stamping last. (5) The fill is a measurement-tier script with its log committed, like every other corpus-wide operation, and it NAMES ITS RUN RANGE EXPLICITLY rather than defaulting to the whole store -- a default of 'everything' is how a protected population gets reached by a script nobody re-read. (6) A QUIET RUN WRITES NO BUNDLE and that is not an absence to report: anom-008 requires zero reportable findings of one and evb-001 refuses an empty bundle, and the way those two agree is that nothing is created. api-015 then serves two empty lists, which is the quiet state and distinguishable from the other two. Failure cases. A pass that stores bundles over a cited run and takes 155 hypothesis rows with it -- which is db-011, and the reason it is a separate item gating this one. A fill that re-writes findings or re-stamps the examination, moving provenance on figure-of-record runs for no gain. A fill that writes a bundle for a run whose rebuilt claim disagrees with its stored one. Bundles written before the findings they cite, which evb-002 refuses one citation at a time and which leaves a run partly written. The stamp written before the bundles, which makes a crash indistinguishable from a complete pass. A fill defaulting to the whole store, or taking its run range from the store's own bounds. A pass that logs db-011's refusal and reports the run as examined. Refs: FR-907, FR-901, AC-05, AC-14, db-002, db-008, db-011, evb-001, evb-002, anom-008, anom-015, anom-016, api-012, api-015, eval-001, eval-004, scn-003. Amended 2026-10-04, before any test, from the same measurement. THE FILL'S SCOPE IS TWO CONDITIONS AND NOT ONE. 140 runs hold a reported claim and no bundle, which is what this item was written for; and four hold a bundle matching no reported claim, off by one or two sampling intervals at one end of the window, written by a measurement script before `anom-007`'s window derivation settled (`api-015`'s own amendment carries the measurement). Left out of scope those four disagree with themselves forever, since `evb-002` replaces per run and a fill scoped to 'runs with no bundle' never reaches them. They are in scope; none is cited, so the replace is permitted by `db-011`. THE TWO COMPARISONS STAY DISTINCT and conflating them would be the defect: the fill's own rebuilt claim against the stored claim decides whether the detectors still agree with the figures of record, and refuses that run if not; an existing bundle against the stored claim decides only whether that bundle is stale, which is a reason to rewrite it rather than to refuse. Failure case adds: a fill scoped to runs with no bundle at all, which leaves a store that disagrees with itself in four places and no way to reach them. Amended 2026-10-04, before any test, on reading `evb-002`'s resolver. CONSTRAINT 4's FIRST HALF IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. It said bundles must be written after the findings they cite, because `evb-002` resolves every citation against stored rows -- true, and the rows are **observations**, not findings. A citation is a coordinate into the observation stream, written at generation time, so it exists long before any pass runs and there is no ordering dependency on `save_findings` at all. The second half stands unchanged: bundles before the stamp, because the stamp means the pass finished everything it writes. WHAT REPLACES IT IS THE OPPOSITE ORDER, for a better reason. The bundle write is the only one of the three that can REFUSE (`db-011`), so it goes FIRST: a protected run then leaves the store exactly as it was, where written last a refusal would leave new conclusions beside bundles belonging to the old ones. That buys run-level atomicity out of ordering rather than out of a second guard, which is `evb-002`'s own argument for resolving in full before writing. It is not total and the limit is worth stating: the track findings are written mid-chain, before the rules that read them back run, so a refusal still leaves those replaced -- harmlessly, since that write is idempotent and happens on every pass, but it is a partial write and saying otherwise would be the overclaim. Order is therefore bundles, then the reported claims, then the stamp. Failure case replaces: a bundle write placed after the findings write, so a run `db-011` protects ends the pass with this hour's conclusions beside the previous hour's evidence. Amended 2026-10-06, while building the fill. CONSTRAINT 1 IS UNACHIEVABLE AS WRITTEN AND IS REPLACED. It said the fill writes bundles and ONLY bundles -- not findings, not the examination stamp -- so no figure-of-record row is rewritten. Building a bundle needs the rule outputs, and two of the rules (`anom-004`'s clusters and `anom-012`'s rate excess) are PostGIS queries over **stored** track findings, which is exactly why `anom-015` persists mid-chain. A pass that writes no findings therefore cannot reach the fusion decision at all, and an in-scope run's track findings are replaced the moment the rules run, whatever the fill does afterwards. The constraint was written against a model of the chain in which persistence was a final step, and it is not. WHAT REPLACES IT KEEPS THE GUARANTEE AND DROPS THE MECHANISM. The fill RUNS THE PASS -- the same code path, so there is no second implementation of the chain to drift -- and the figures of record are protected by the COMPARISON rather than by withholding a write: each in-scope run's stored reported claims are read before the pass runs, compared against what the pass then stored, and a disagreement STOPS THE WHOLE FILL rather than skipping that run. Stopping rather than skipping is the part that matters: a skip would carry on rewriting 139 further runs under settings just shown to disagree with the ones every quoted figure was measured under, which is `eval-001`'s recorded-and-stepped-over rule applied where it does not belong -- that rule is for a run that FAILED, not for a run that came back with a different answer. TWO COSTS ARE ACCEPTED AND STATED. `detection_pass_at` moves to the day the fill ran, which is true rather than a loss: the hour was re-examined, and `detection_policy` is rewritten beside it, which is the provenance the comparison checks. And the track findings are replaced without being compared -- the comparison is over the REPORTED CLAIMS, since those are what the bundles explain and what `eval-002`'s table is indexed by, while `anom-010`'s intermediate output is neither. Failure cases replace: a fill that reimplements the chain rather than calling it. A disagreement that skips the run and continues. A comparison made only after every run has been written, which cannot say which run disagreed. MEASURED 2026-10-06, and the fill is BLOCKED by what it found -- which is the item working rather than failing. It reached run 71 of 144 and stopped: the rebuilt claim's window begins at 12:22:13 where the stored one begins at 12:22:33, twenty seconds and two sampling intervals apart. The cause is not the detectors and not the thresholds, which are identical. It is the BASELINE. `measure_normality` takes `quiet_run_ids`, every quiet run the store holds, so the normality a run is scored against depends on how large the store was when the pass ran -- and the store now holds findings written under TWO baselines: **378 runs at 60 quiet runs and 22 at 100**, by the recorded policy. `anom-016` named this exact hazard when it put the quiet runs on the record (*two baselines under identical thresholds give different findings and are otherwise indistinguishable*), and `eval-003`'s policy column is what made it visible here; what neither does is PREVENT it, and nothing on the screen or in `eval-002`'s table reports which baseline a figure was taken under. It also inverts this item's own earlier reading: the four bundles matching no claim are not stale. Run 71's bundle, written in September, agrees with today's rebuild to the second, and it is the stored FINDING that was produced under the other baseline. So the half of this item that is built and green is the pass storing what it builds; the fill is written, has run, refused, and waits on a decision that is not a code decision: whether to re-score the corpus under one baseline, which rewrites every detection figure of record, or to leave two baselines in the store and report which is which. The two runs the fill wrote before stopping (54 and 71) were restored from a dump taken beforehand, so the store is byte-for-byte as it was. `passes` stays false: the pass stores its bundles and 140 hours still report their conclusion as unexplained. Amended 2026-10-07, to close. THE FILL IS SUPERSEDED, AND ITS OUTCOME IS MET ANOTHER WAY. The decision this item waited on was taken as `anom-017`: the baseline population was pinned (one hundred quiet runs, each with its seed) and every completed run re-scored under it by `rescore_baseline.py`, which runs the shipped pass and therefore stores every bundle it builds. That re-score is the fill's job done under the conditions the fill exposed, and it records the change the fill refused to make silently -- every run whose reported claims moved is listed before and after (11 of 440, all window edges by 10-30 s, no claim gained or lost). The twenty runs `db-011` protects were refused by the guard and left on the 60-run baseline, where their claims, bundles and stamp already agreed. MEASURED 2026-10-07 against the store of record, both directions of `api-015`'s two-sided completeness are now empty: 0 runs and 0 reported claims with no matching bundle, and 0 bundles matching no reported claim -- including the four on runs 54, 71, 76 and 105 that this item's first amendment brought into scope, all of which the re-score replaced. So the outcome this item was written for holds, and the half of it that is code -- the pass storing what it builds, bundles first, the refusal propagated, the stamp last -- has been built and green since 2026-10-06. `backfill_bundles.py` stays committed with its log as the measurement that stopped and produced `anom-017`; it is not to be run again, the re-score having superseded it. Constraint 5's explicit run range survives in that script and is not carried over, since the re-score's scope is every completed run by design and its protection is `db-011`'s, decided from the store. Refs add: anom-017.

The baseline population is declared, not discovered. Input: the detector settings module. Output: the quiet runs a baseline is measured over are a CONSTANT read from `app/detection/settings.py` beside the other eleven, and `measure_normality` takes that constant; the corpus is then re-scored under it once, and the figures of record re-measured. WHY. `measure_normality` takes `quiet_run_ids`, every quiet run the store holds, so the normality a run is scored against depends on HOW LARGE THE STORE WAS WHEN THE PASS RAN. Measured 2026-10-06 while `evb-003`'s fill ran: the store holds findings written under two baselines, 378 runs at 60 quiet runs and 22 at 100, and on run 71 the same code over the same hour under the same thresholds puts the claim's window 20 s -- two sampling intervals -- apart. `anom-016` NAMED this hazard when it put the quiet runs on the record (*two baselines under identical thresholds give different findings and are otherwise indistinguishable*) and `eval-003`'s policy column is what made it diagnosable; neither prevents it, which is the gap this item closes. It is `eval-003`'s own argument one layer up: a recorded setting that is not the one in force is worse than none, and a setting that is in force but chosen by the store is not a setting anybody decided. Constraints. (1) THE POPULATION IS ALL 100, and the choice is measured rather than preferred: the 60-run set is a STRICT SUBSET of the 100 (set difference empty), every one of the 100 is corpus v2 by `scn-008`'s base-seed discriminator, and all are 900 s -- so this is one homogeneous population measured twice, once with 40 fewer runs, and not two populations to choose between. More of the same data is a better estimate of normal and there is no countervailing measurement. (2) IT IS A LIST OF IDS AND NOT A RULE FOR FINDING THEM. `quiet_run_ids` stays, and is what the constant was derived from, but a rule evaluated against the store is the thing that moved; `eval-004`'s sample is named by id for the same reason. The derivation is recorded beside the constant so a later corpus can repeat it deliberately. (3) A RUN IN THE CONSTANT THAT IS NOT IN THE STORE IS A REFUSAL, not a silently smaller baseline -- a baseline measured over 97 of its 100 runs is a different baseline, and the whole point of pinning is that it cannot vary without somebody saying so. (4) THE RE-SCORE IS PART OF THIS ITEM and not a consequence of it, with its own measurement script and its own confirm variable, because the store is inconsistent TODAY and pinning alone leaves it inconsistent under a name. It runs the shipped pass over every completed run, and -- unlike `evb-003`'s fill, which refuses on disagreement -- a changed claim is the EXPECTED outcome here and is RECORDED: the committed log carries every run whose reported claims moved, before and after, because that count is the result. It subsumes the fill, since re-scoring every run stores every bundle. (5) `detection_metrics.py` IS RE-RUN AFTERWARDS and its log re-committed. It re-runs the detectors rather than reading `detection_findings`, so its figures are not invalidated by the re-score -- they are something narrower and worse, figures taken under a baseline the store no longer has. Any figure that moves is reported rather than quietly superseded. (6) The order is PIN, re-score, re-measure, report. Re-scoring before pinning re-introduces the variable at the moment of the operation meant to remove it. Failure cases. A constant that is still a query against the store, which is the defect wearing a name. A missing run silently narrowing the baseline. A re-score whose log records only that runs changed and not WHICH, so the delta cannot be read. `detection_metrics.py` left un-re-run, leaving every quoted detection figure taken under a baseline nothing holds. A re-score run before the pin. Refs: NFR-605, NFR-601, anom-002, anom-016, anom-015, eval-001, eval-003, eval-004, evb-003, db-008, scn-008. Amended 2026-10-06, before tests, on measuring the store. (7) THE TWENTY RUNS THE SCORED CAMPAIGN CITES ARE REFUSED, NOT RE-SCORED. `db-011` forbids replacing a bundle a hypothesis cites, runs 102-175 hold twenty such bundles, and all twenty are stamped with the 60-run baseline. The re-score lets the guard fire, records each refusal by run id, and leaves those twenty runs on the 60-run baseline -- where their claims, their bundles, their stamp and the hypotheses that explain them all agree. They are the ONE STATED EXCEPTION to a consistent store, tellable apart by their stamp. Re-scoring their claims while keeping their bundles is rejected because it recreates the claim/bundle disagreement `evb-003`'s fill stopped on; filtering them out in advance is rejected on `evb-003`'s own argument, that a guard routed around is a guard nobody has seen work. (8) THE CONSTANT PINS EACH RUN'S SEED BESIDE ITS ID. An id names a row in one store and not a content: another database generates its own run 21, which may be quiet with a different seed or not quiet at all, and a baseline over it is a different baseline under the same name -- the defect this item removes, arriving by a different door. `scn-001` regenerates a run byte-identically from its type, parameters and seed, so the seed is what identifies the content. A pinned run is accepted only if it EXISTS, is COMPLETED, is `normal-baseline` and carries the PINNED SEED; anything else is refused, naming every run that failed and why, before any observation is read. (9) THE REFUSAL SITS IN `measure_normality`, so every caller inherits it -- the batch trigger (`anom-016`), the re-score and `detection_metrics.py` -- and the batch trigger passes the constant rather than `quiet_run_ids`. The consequence is stated rather than discovered: on a freshly generated database the pinned runs are absent, so the batch trigger refuses and new runs are served unexamined until the constant is re-derived deliberately for that corpus. That is the item working, and it is cheaper than a baseline that varies with whichever store it lands in. (10) Measured 2026-10-06: the store holds 460 completed runs, not 400 -- 421-480 were generated from Scenario Control on 6 October and were already scored under all 100 quiet runs. The 100 come from five base seeds, twenty each: the corpus of record's three (1412660662, 965530111, 655209063), 695081452 for runs 21-40 and 1284648146 for runs 381-400. `anom-016`'s `rescore_corpus.py`, which baselines over `_corpus.quiet_runs`' sixty and rewrites every stamp, moves to `measurements/superseded/` so the one script that does that can no longer do it under the old population; the re-score is a new script with its own confirm variable, `RESCORE_CONFIRM`. Failure cases add: a pinned id that exists in the store as a different run, accepted. A refused run whose claims or stamp moved. A re-score that skips the protected runs without the guard firing. A batch trigger still reading `quiet_run_ids`. Refs add: db-011, scn-001, anom-016. Amended 2026-10-06, after the re-score, on re-running the results table. (11) A MEASUREMENT WRITES NOTHING. `detection_metrics.py` runs the detection pass, and the pass has written as it goes since `anom-015` (findings, re-stamping every run it touched) and stores bundles since `evb-003` -- so constraint (5) could not be met: the run stopped at run 102, the first cited run, on `db-011`'s refusal. The table needs the pinned-baseline answer for all 300 corpus runs, the twenty cited runs among them. `assess_without_storing` provides it: it runs the shipped pass with every write inside one database transaction that is ALWAYS rolled back, so the rules that read stored track findings back still see them, and the store is byte-for-byte as it was afterwards -- findings, bundles and stamps. Inside that transaction, and only there, the bundle write is skipped, which is what lets a cited run be measured without the guard firing: the guard exists to stop a REPLACEMENT, and a rolled-back transaction replaces nothing. The skip is not a parameter of `assess` -- a public flag to skip the bundle write would recreate, outside a rollback, the claim/bundle disagreement constraint (7) refuses -- and is held structurally: only `assess_without_storing` reaches it. `detection_metrics.py` uses it, which also ends the results table re-dating every run's examination stamp. Failure cases add: a measurement that changes the store. A cited run the measurement cannot score. A failure part-way through a measured pass that leaves its earlier writes behind. A way to skip the bundle write that does not roll back.

Each aircraft track carries the state this run's findings put it in. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture, and the run's stored `TRACK-GAP` findings. Output: every entry of `aircraftTracks` carries a `state`, and `frontend/src/types/operationalPicture.ts` matches. WHY IT IS NEEDED NOW. `op-004`'s panel labels a tab *Tracks (n degraded)* and `api-007` filters a payload on whether a row is anomalous -- and `AircraftTrack` carries `id`, `name`, `altitudeFt`, `lat` and `lon` and nothing about degradation, so both the count and the filter have no property to read. Built without this, the tab is a tab with an invented number in its label, which is `api-002`'s producer-less field reaching an analyst rather than sitting empty. Constraints. (1) THE STATE IS DERIVED FROM STORED FINDINGS AND NOT RE-DETECTED. `anom-010`'s continuity gaps are persisted per run (`api-012`'s `PERSISTED_PRODUCERS`), keyed on the aircraft pseudonym, so this is a join and not a detector -- `anom-016`'s rule that the pass does not fire per request. (2) THREE STATES AND NOT TWO, following `_receiver_health`: `nominal` is a track this run's findings say nothing about, `interrupted` is one `anom-010` raised a continuity gap for, and `unknown` is every track on a run NO PASS HAS EXAMINED. The third is `api-012`'s distinction again: a run nobody looked at must not report 432 nominal tracks, which is a claim nothing established. (3) `interrupted` AND NOT `degraded`, which is what `op-004`'s tab label says: the finding is that reporting from that aircraft broke, and *degraded* is a judgement about the aircraft that nothing here makes. The tab label is `op-004`'s own wording and is amended to match rather than the state being renamed to fit it. (4) A TRACK-GAP FINDING IS INTERMEDIATE AND THIS DOES NOT PROMOTE IT. A quiet hour holds about 138 of them and run 420 holds 17; what this field says is *this aircraft's reporting broke*, which is a fact about a track, and never *an anomaly was reported*, which is the ladder's to say. The detection summary continues to count it as intermediate and the state is not a reportable claim. (5) THE JOIN IS ON THE PSEUDONYM AS STORED, and nothing reverses it: `anom-010` keys its findings on the same substituted identifier the observation carries, so the match needs no lookup and NFR-405 is untouched. (6) A track with several gaps is `interrupted` once; the state is a state and not a count. Failure cases. A `degraded` boolean, which collapses *examined and clean* into *not examined*. A state derived by re-running the detector inside a request. A state that promotes an intermediate finding into the summary's reportable counts. A join on a resolved identifier rather than on the stored pseudonym. A track on an unexamined run reported nominal. Refs: FR-813, FR-802, FR-708, FR-716, NFR-405, api-002, api-007, api-012, anom-010, anom-012, op-004, op-007, scn-005.

A hot-reloading frontend dev server inside Compose. Input: `make dev` from the repo root. Output: postgis, the backend (already bind-mounted and running with --reload) and a new `frontend-dev` service running `pnpm dev --host 0.0.0.0` on port 1234, built from the frontend Dockerfile's existing `build` stage with `./frontend` bind-mounted, so a saved edit reaches the browser without an image rebuild. WHY. The `frontend` service is nginx serving a production build frozen at image build time, so a frontend edit is invisible on :8080 until a rebuild, while the backend reloads on save -- the two halves of the stack had different development loops, and a reviewer looking at :8080 after an edit sees the old screen (docs/qa.md 153). Constraints. (1) THE PROXY TARGET COMES FROM THE ENVIRONMENT. `vite.config.ts` reads the address `/api` is forwarded to from an environment variable, defaulting to http://localhost:8000 so `pnpm dev` on the host is unchanged, and the container sets http://backend:8000. (2) NODE_MODULES IS ISOLATED FROM THE MOUNT. The host's node_modules holds macOS-native binaries (esbuild, rollup, Tailwind's oxide engine); the container keeps its own Linux install in a volume over /app/node_modules, so the mount cannot shadow it. (3) PROFILED. The service sits in a `dev` profile, so plain `docker compose up` and `make up`/`make demo` do not start it; the nginx service stays the demo path (ops-001, AC-12). (4) Vite does not try to open a browser when it runs in the container. Failure cases. A container forwarding /api to its own localhost: every call fails, and because the operational picture falls back to its mock on first paint (api-003) the screen looks healthy while showing invented data -- the sharpest of the three. The host's node_modules shadowing the container's. A saved edit that never reaches the browser because file-change events do not cross the macOS bind mount -- polling is then opt-in and its use recorded. Proof: tests on the Vite config's proxy target with and without the variable, and on the Compose service declaration (profile, port, mount, node_modules volume, proxy variable); plus one recorded check that an edit to a component reaches a running dev server without a restart. Refs: ops-001, ops-003, api-003, AC-12, docs/qa.md 153. Amended 2026-10-07, before tests. Three things found reading the configuration. (1) NOT THE `build` STAGE. That stage runs `pnpm run build`, which is `tsc -b` first, so a dev server built from it could not start while the working tree fails to type-check -- which is the normal state of a tree mid-edit. The Dockerfile gains a `deps` stage (corepack, manifests, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) that `build` now starts from, and `frontend-dev` targets `deps`; the production image is unchanged. (2) THE VARIABLE IS `API_PROXY_TARGET` AND NOT `VITE_`-PREFIXED. Vite publishes `VITE_*` variables into the client bundle, and the proxy address is server configuration. The address is read through one helper beside `vite.config.ts`, which refuses a value that is not an http(s) URL, naming the variable, and treats an empty value as unset. (3) `make dev` RENEWS THE `node_modules` VOLUME. An anonymous volume outlives the container, so after a dependency change it would keep serving the previous install while the image held the new one; the target passes `--renew-anon-volumes`. Vite's own `BROWSER=none` covers constraint (4). Failure cases add: a dev server that will not start because the tree does not type-check. A proxy variable published into the browser bundle. A stale node_modules volume after a lockfile change.
